payload.answer:
COMPLETE EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN — "GPT-2 vs CodeLlama-7b-Python on RepoBench Python cross_file_first (next-line auto-completion)"

Status: DESIGN ONLY. No experiment was run. Any number below is a plan assumption or predicted budget, never a measured result.

════════════════════════════════════════════
0. RESEARCH QUESTION → TESTABLE FORM
════════════════════════════════════════════
RQ: How does a small general-text LM (GPT-2 family) compare with a large code-specialized LM (CodeLlama-7b-Python) on repository-level NEXT-LINE completion in the cross_file_first setting of RepoBench Python?

Testable decomposition (all zero-shot):
- Q1 (capability at equal context): mean Exact Match and mean Edit Similarity difference when both models receive ≤1,000 tokens of cross-file context (matched condition). Primary estimand: ΔEM = EM(CodeLlama-7b-Python) − EM(GPT-2-<size>) and ΔES analog.
- Q2 (system-level with native windows): same comparison when each model uses its own max context (GPT-2 ≤1,024; CodeLlama ≤16,384 minus completion budget). This is the "deployed-system" comparison.
- Q3 (sensitivity): does the ordering or conclusion change between matched and native? Reported explicitly as an interaction, never collapsed into one number (Research suggestion #3).
- Q4 (exploratory, secondary): pass@k on a subsample; token-overlap and chrF partial-credit; effect of retrieval-order permutation (baseline).

════════════════════════════════════════════
1. FIXED TASK REQUIREMENTS vs ASSUMPTIONS
════════════════════════════════════════════
FIXED (task-defining, not negotiable):
- Dataset: official released RepoBench Python benchmark, setting = cross_file_first (RCF), i.e., completion must be predicted from cross-file context (other files of the same repo) with NO same-file/previous-line context. Use the retrieval context SHIPPED with the dataset (standard BM25, provided top-K files); no re-retrieval — retrieval is not a variable.
- Official splits: use the official test split as released; report train/valid only if a fine-tuning condition is ever added (it is NOT in this design).
- Official metrics: Exact Match (EM) and Edit Similarity (ES) computed with the released official evaluation script. EM and ES are CO-PRIMARY here (Rationale: single-line EM in code completion is typically very low, so ES/partial-credit carries most signal — Research suggestion #1; both are official so no extra burden).
- The question's mention of pass@k is honored ONLY as a clearly-labeled, secondary, non-official addition.

ASSUMPTIONS (stated, testable at execution):
- A1 Dataset provenance: canonical copy = official RepoBench repo / its HuggingFace artifact for Python; test ≈4,000 instances (approximate count to verify at download).
- A2 Models = HuggingFace checkpoints: gpt2, gpt2-medium, gpt2-large, gpt2-xl; codellama/CodeLlama-7b-Python-hf. If budget forces a single "small" model, default gpt2-large (774M).
- A3 Zero-shot inference; NO fine-tuning (keeps pipeline clean; fine-tuning is a separate study).
- A4 Budget: one 40 GB-class GPU-machine run (full test set greedy; subsample for sampling/pass@k). CPU-only is a documented fallback only.
- A5 "Performance" = next-line completion quality, primarily EM & ES; secondary metrics labeled non-official.
- A6 Execution environment is NOT this workspace (here: no network, no GPU, no ML libs, no data/weights — verified). Design executes on a provisioned networked+GPU box.

════════════════════════════════════════════
2. EXPERIMENTAL UNITS, FACTORS, CONDITIONS
════════════════════════════════════════════
Units: the official test instances (i = 1..N, N≈4,000). Paired design — every model/condition sees the SAME instances in the SAME order.

Factor A — Model (5 levels): gpt2, gpt2-medium, gpt2-large, gpt2-xl, CodeLlama-7b-Python. (GPT-2 family = size sweep so "small model" is a curve, not one arbitrary point.)
Factor B — Context policy (2 levels per model):
   • matched: truncate prompt to first 1,000 tokens for ALL models (≤ GPT-2 window; equalizes information actually feedable).
   • native: use each model's own window (GPT-2: 1,024−budget; CodeLlama: up to 16,384−budget). For GPT-2, matched and native are nearly identical (1,000 vs ~924 usable); the meaningful matched-vs-native difference is on CodeLlama.
Factor C — Decoding (2 modes): greedy (primary, deterministic) and sampling (secondary).
Baseline/control conditions: empty prediction; frequency baseline; retrieval-order permutations (random, reverse) on a subset and for at least CodeLlama-native + gpt2-large-matched to quantify sensitivity to the provided ordering.

Cross-product: greedy run = 5 models × 2 context policies (10 pipelines) over N instances. Sampling/pass@k = subsample S≈400–500 stratified instances × n=5 samples × {gpt2-large, gpt2-xl, CodeLlama} × both policies (bounded budget).

════════════════════════════════════════════
3. DATA PIPELINE & PROMPT CONSTRUCTION
════════════════════════════════════════════
P0 Download & hash: record dataset commit/version, HF artifact hash, transformers/torch versions; freeze them in the report.
P1 Prompt builder: replicate EXACTLY the official RCF template from the official retrieval_based_autocomplete.py — concatenate retrieved files each prefixed by a "# Path: {path}" header, followed by the official sentinel line naming the target file (e.g., "# The code you need to complete is located in the file: {target}"). Reconstruct from the official source at implementation time; do NOT re-derive from memory (template exactness is a required sanity check, §6).
P2 Tokenization per model (each model's own tokenizer — this is part of the model system; no cross-model tokenizer sharing).
P3 Truncation: matched → keep first 1,000 tokens; native → keep first (max window − completion_budget) with completion_budget = 100 tokens. Truncate from the END, preserving earliest (repository-overview) context, consistent with official behavior.
P4 Record per instance: prompt_length_tokens, truncated_flag, num_retrieved_files_actually_used, retrieved_token_count, and whether the gold completion line (or its distinctive tokens) appears in the retained context (context-quality proxy). These feed stratified analysis and truncation reporting.

════════════════════════════════════════════
4. INFERENCE & DECODING
════════════════════════════════════════════
- Greedy: max_new_tokens = 100; extract the FIRST COMPLETE LINE of the generation as the prediction (official comparison is line-level). Record raw generation too.
- Sampling (pass@k): top-p = 0.8, temperature = 0.8, n = 5 samples/instance, fixed distinct global seeds (logged). Same line-extraction.
- Precision: CodeLlama fp16/bf16; GPT-2 fp32 or bf16. Batch size tuned to VRAM (CodeLlama bsz 4–8 at matched; smaller at 16k native).
- Log per instance: wall time, tokens/sec, VRAM peak, generated tokens, truncated/empty flags.

════════════════════════════════════════════
5. METRICS & EVALUATION (official eval script)
════════════════════════════════════════════
Primary (official):
- EM[i] = 1{extracted_line == gold_line}; report mean EM and per-instance vector.
- ES[i] = official edit similarity (1 − normalized Levenshtein) between extracted line and gold line; report mean ES and per-instance vector. ES is CO-PRIMARY, computed by the same official script for both models.
Secondary (all labeled NON-official):
- token-window overlap: |pred_tokens ∩ gold_tokens| / |gold_tokens| (and Jaccard) for partial credit.
- chrF (character n-gram F-score) for character-level partial credit (Research suggestion #1).
- pass@k: line-level exact match over n=5 samples (pass@1..5, ES@5 = best ES over samples) on the subsample.
- Diagnostic rates: empty-prediction rate, truncated-completion rate, mean/median prediction length, per-repo means.
All metrics computed by the SAME script for both models (no per-model eval variants).

════════════════════════════════════════════
6. SANITY CHECKS BEFORE FULL RUN (viability)
════════════════════════════════════════════
(S1) Template fidelity unit test: for 3 hand-crafted instances, assert the builder output byte-matches the official script output (golden-file diff). Fail ⇒ stop.
(S2) Smoke test: 10–20 instances × every model×condition; verify no crashes, VRAM fits, output lengths sane, empty-rate not pathological, gold line is achievable (manual review of ≥5 outputs per model).
(S3) Performance probe: measure tokens/sec and s/instance on the smoke batch; EXTRAPOLATE to N≈4k and validate the budget in §9 with ≥2× margin; adjust batch size if needed.
(S4) Determinism: rerun greedy on the smoke set twice; assert identical outputs (same hardware/seed) before trusting paired comparisons.
(S5) Baseline sanity: empty/frequency baselines computed — EM of baselines should be ~0 and ES small but >0; if a model matches baseline EM it is flagged as non-informative.
(S6) Truncation audit: verify matched condition truly yields ≤1,000 tokens for 100% of instances and report native truncation rates (how often CodeLlama's 16k window is exhausted).

════════════════════════════════════════════
7. STATISTICAL ANALYSIS PLAN (pre-specified)
════════════════════════════════════════════
- Estimates: mean EM, mean ES, and differences ΔEM, ΔES for (a) matched and (b) native, for every GPT-2 size vs CodeLlama. Report all four model sizes (never only one) to show the small-model size trend.
- Uncertainty: 95% paired bootstrap CIs over the instance index (10,000 resamples). Paired tests: McNemar on per-instance EM; paired difference test / permutation on ES. Report Cohen's h effect size for EM.
- Stratified (mechanism): split instances by (i) retrieved-context length (low/mid/high cross-file need), (ii) context-quality proxy (gold tokens present in context or not), (iii) repo size. Report ΔEM/ΔES within strata to test whether any CodeLlama advantage concentrates in high-context-need slices.
- Matched-vs-native reporting protocol (Research suggestion #3): report THREE headline numbers, never one: (1) Δ(EM, ES) matched; (2) Δ(EM, ES) native; (3) the within-model change Δnative−matched for CodeLlama (the "context-window dividend" attributable to 16k window). State the conclusion under each condition and explicitly state whether the model ordering is stable; if they differ, the report must say the conclusion is condition-dependent rather than pick one.
- Sensitivity bounds: recompute ΔEM for the retrieval-order permutations (random/reverse) to bound how much the provided ordering alone explains any gap.
- Sample retention: log any dropped instances (empty gold, decode failure, OOM) and re-run the paired analysis on the intersection.

════════════════════════════════════════════
8. COMPUTE/BUDGET & FEASIBILITY
════════════════════════════════════════════
- This workspace CANNOT run it (verified: no network, no GPU, no torch/transformers/datasets, no data/weights). Execution requires a provisioned box.
- Target hardware: 1× A100/H100 40 GB (CodeLlama fp16 ≈14–16 GB VRAM; bsz 4–8). GPT-2 needs ≤3 GB.
- Predicted budget (to be validated by S3, not measured yet): full-test greedy ≈ 2–5 GPU-hours (CodeLlama dominated; native-16k prompts dominate; GPT-2 negligible). Sampling/pass@k subsample 500×5 adds ≈1–3 GPU-hours. Total ≈ 0.5–1.5 A100-days.
- Software: pip install torch transformers datasets accelerate evaluate huggingface_hub; git clone official RepoBench for scripts/eval; pins recorded.
- Reduced-budget fallback (documented, lower fidelity): stratified n=500, gpt2-large only, matched-greedy only, CodeLlama 4-bit CPU (llama.cpp) only if no GPU — flagged as non-headline.

════════════════════════════════════════════
9. REPORTING / DELIVERABLES
════════════════════════════════════════════
- Main table: per model×condition: mean EM, mean ES, secondary metrics, empty/truncated rates, mean context tokens.
- Difference table: ΔEM/ΔES with 95% CI and p-value (matched and native rows) for each GPT-2 size vs CodeLlama; the matched-vs-native interaction row.
- Figures: ES distribution (box/violin) per model; EM by strata; ΔEM vs GPT-2 parameter count (size trend).
- Transparent artifacts: seed list, dataset/model/library versions + hashes, full config JSON, per-instance result CSV, reproduction script.
- Explicit statement in conclusion: no claim of measured results from this design; all numbers are to be generated at execution time.

════════════════════════════════════════════
10. LIMITATIONS & UNCERTAINTIES
════════════════════════════════════════════
- Inherent confound: size + code-specialization + model family co-vary; controls (equal context, greedy, same eval/instances) remove the context-window and decoding explanations but attribution to "scale" vs "specialization" vs "family" is NOT identifiable from this design — the conclusion is about MODEL SYSTEMS (small general vs large code-specialized), wording chosen accordingly.
- Exact official template/instance JSON layout reconstructed from official source at implementation (not from memory; S1 guards it).
- Dataset canonical artifact/size approximate (~4k test) until download.
- pass@k/chrF/token-overlap are non-official additions (labeled).
- Single-line EM may be near-floor; this is why ES is co-primary and partial-credit metrics are included (Research suggestion #1).
- Budget numbers are predictions to be validated by the S3 probe, not measurements.

payload.answer:
【一、输入端调研】(依据领域文献与官方文档；工作区无网络/无GPU/无数据集，故以下标记“待核”者为无法本地核实项)

1) RepoBench 整体结构（Liu et al., arXiv:2306.03091, 2023）
- 组成：RepoBench-P(代码自动补全)、RepoBench-R(相关代码检索)；本任务只用 Python 子集的补全部分。
- Python 子集：由约 1,000 个公开 Python 仓库构建（待核：确切仓库数与样本总数）。
- 设置差异：
  - Cross-File First (CFF)：给定 (i) 目标函数的签名/前缀 与 (ii) 与目标文件有依赖关系的仓库文件（“依赖文件”作为 oracle 上下文，无检索环节），模型需补全目标函数体。CFF 强调跨文件依赖利用。
  - “single-file” 类对照：(等价于 CFF 去掉跨文件上下文、仅给自身前缀) 常见于作为无上下文的基线对照；官方数据/HF 卡中该命名是否就叫 single_file 需核实（待核）。
  - RAP(检索增强管线) 不在本任务范围内，仅 CFF。
- 每个 CFF 样本大致包含：cross_context(依赖文件内容)、target(目标函数体=金标)、target_signature/前缀；确切 JSONL 字段名与文件拼接顺序需按官方仓库核实（待核）。
- 评测指标：官方为 Exact Match (EM) 与 Edit Similarity (ES=1−Levenshtein/max(len_gold,len_pred))；官方不以 BLEU 为主，BLEU/CodeBLEU 只能作补充（待核：官方脚本是否还输出其他指标）。
- 官方对输入截断/随机种子/采样的规定：基线通常将输入截到固定最大 token 数（我记得默认约 1024），生成多用 greedy(temp=0)+固定种子；确切默认值需查官方 `config`（待核）。

2) 两模型基线信息
- GPT-2（建议用 gpt2/small, 124M）：上下文 1024 token；字节级 BPE 分词(≈50,257 词表)；原始因果 LM 接口直接做前缀续写（无 fill 特化 token）；未经代码微调。参考既有结果（近似，待核）：在 RepoBench-P CFF 上 GPT-2 的 EM 接近 0、ES 偏低；在 CodeXGLUE 单行/单 token 补全上有 EM 约 30–45% 量级的历史基线。
- CodeLlama-7B（建议 base 版，代码续写，不用 Instruct/Python 变体以对齐“代码补全”能力）：上下文 16,384 token（RoPE 外推）；SentencePiece BPE 词表 32k、偏向代码；因果接口。CodeLlama(2023-08) 晚于原 RepoBench 论文，官方表里没有它，参考数字来自后续文献：HumanEval pass@1≈30.5%、MBPP≈44.5%，以及后续工作对 RepoBench-P 的 CodeLlama-7B 结果（待核）。内存：FP16≈14GB，GPT-2 仅≈0.5GB。

【二、工作方法概要】(仅要点)
(a) 规模：优先官方 CFF 全量测试集（约 1.4 万样本，待核）；若算力受限则固定种子(42)抽 1,000 样本，两模型用同一子集（配对设计）。生成主用 greedy（确定性，1 轨）；可选 3–5 轨 temp=0.8 采样用于方差估计/Pass@1。重复性通过“配对 bootstrap 重采样样本”而非重复跑。
(b) 统一任务格式：两模型均用“依赖文件(官方顺序) + 目标签名前缀”拼接成 prompt，统一用普通左到右因果续写（都不引入 FIM/填充特化 token），各自用自己的分词器；max_new_tokens 统一（如固定 256 或“min(金标长度, 上限)”两个口径）；输出后统一规范化（去首尾空白/缩进、切到金标长度）再打分，避免长度优势。
(c) 评测与显著性：主指标=官方 EM+ES（配对样本）；补充 BLEU/CodeBLEU（可选）。显著性：配对 bootstrap(≥1 万次，固定种子) 给出 ES 均值差的 95% CI；ES 用 Wilcoxon 符号秩，EM(Binary 每样本是否命中) 用 McNemar；均报告效果量。
(d) 消融/对照：
- 上下文长度混杂：把两模型都截到公共 token 预算(如 1,024)做“等长”比较；再单独跑 CodeLlama 16K 全上下文，以量化“上下文越长”本身的收益；注意分词器不同→1,024 token 不等价，需按字符/等长口径做稳健性检查。
- 代码特化 vs 规模混杂：算力允许时，加入“用 RepoBench-P 训练切 CFF 格式微调后的 GPT-2”作对照（把 GPT-2 非代码特化混淆出来）；并可在 CodeLlama 上用单文件(无跨文件上下文)控制。
- 解码/评分控制：greedy 与采样对照；预测统一切到金标长度后再算 EM/ES。

【三、关键假设与不确定性】
必须做出的假设(对结论的影响)：
1. “小模型”取 gpt2/124M、CodeLlama 取 7B base（非 Python/Instruct 变体）→ 影响“代码特化收益”的解释范围。
2. max_new_tokens 与输入截断预算（如输入统一裁到 1,024 token、输出裁到金标长度）→ 直接影响两模型相对差距大小。
3. 评测用官方脚本 vs 自建：官方 ES/EM 定义明确；若无法拿到官方脚本需自实现 Levenshtein/EM，须用单元测试对齐定义（对绝对分数有影响，对相对比较影响小）。
4. 部署：执行环境当前无 GPU/无网络/未装 ML 依赖；CodeLlama-7B 在纯 CPU(224 核)上推理极慢→假设在带 GPU 的执行环境跑，或对 CodeLlama 做一致的 int8/4bit 量化（量化的精度损失须说明且两模型保持一致处理）。
5. 采样/种子：主结果 greedy+固定种子 42，保证可复现。
6. 若算力不足：从全量抽样 1,000 是否代表总体（置信区间会偏大，结论稳健性下降）。

尚缺资料/需澄清：
- 官方数据字段名、依赖文件拼接顺序、CFF 样本总数与“single_file”命名的确切定义（网络禁用，无法拉取官方 repo/HF 卡核实）。
- 原论文确切的截断/采样默认值与官方 EM/ES 脚本细节。
- 后续文献中 CodeLlama-7B 在 RepoBench-P CFF 的具体数值（作复现对照用）。
- 执行阶段是否具备 GPU、能否联网下载模型/数据集、以及 CodeLlama 是否允许量化——这些决定“全量 vs 抽样”和部署方式。

# 实验设计书：GPT-2(small) vs CodeLlama-7B 在 RepoBench-P Cross-File-First 设置下的性能对比

状态声明：本文为纯实验设计，未运行任何实验；其中所有结论性数字均为"待执行验证/待核实"项。本设计书不声称已运行实验。

---

## 0. 目标与范围
- 研究问题：在小模型 GPT-2(124M, 非代码特化) 与大代码特化模型 CodeLlama-7B 之间，RepoBench-P Python 子集的 **cross_file_first (CFF)** 设置下，谁更好、好多少、在何种条件下差距收窄。
- 范围：仅评估补全(CFF)环节；不涉及 RepoBench-R 检索任务、不涉及 RAP 检索增强管线本身（我们使用 oracle 提供的依赖文件，即 CFF 的原始设定）。
- 主比较为配对设计：两模型在**完全相同样本、相同 prompt 构造、相同解码与评测口径**下逐样本对比。

---

## 1. 输入端调研与"待核"项的处置（核实方式 / 转假设 + 敏感度）

基于公开文献（RepoBench, Liu et al., arXiv:2306.03091; OpenAI GPT-2; Meta CodeLlama, arXiv:2308.12950）建立的知识基线；因本工作区无网络、无 GPU、无数据集，以下每个"待核"项均给出【核实方式】或【转假设+敏感度】。

### 1.1 RepoBench 结构知识基线
- RepoBench-P：Python 子集，由约 1,000 个公开 Python 仓库构建，含补全样本；CFF 测试集约 1.4 万条(近似值)。【核实：官方 GitHub `Leolty/repobench` 的 README/`data/` 目录行数与 HF 数据集卡的分裂统计】
- CFF 设定：输入 = (依赖文件的全部内容) + (目标文件的前缀，到目标函数签名为止)；金标 = 目标函数体。无检索，依赖文件为 oracle 上下文。
- "single_file"：官方数据中是否以此命名待核【核实：HF 卡 split 名与官方 README】。若不存在官方切分，则将其**转假设**为"CFF 去掉跨文件上下文、仅给目标前缀"的对照变体，由我们自己构造（prefix-only 模板）。敏感度：该变体仅用于消融解释，不影响主比较结论（主比较只发生在 CFF 设置下）。
- 官方指标：Exact Match (EM) 与 Edit Similarity (ES，基于 Levenshtein 距离，ES=1−dist/max(len_gold, len_pred))。官方不以 BLEU 为主要指标；本项目以 EM+ES 为主，BLEU/CodeBLEU 仅作补充。【核实：官方 `evaluate.py` 是否还输出其他指标】

---

## 2. 工作方法（正式版）

### 2.1 实验规模与配对设计
- **数据集**：RepoBench-P 官方 CFF 测试集，默认**全量**（约 1.4 万样本，待核 U1）。
- **配对**：两模型在相同样本、相同 prompt、相同解码设置下逐样本评分；样本级匹配是后续配对统计的前提。
- **重数/随机性**：
  - 主结果：greedy（temp=0）单轨，确定性。随机性由固定 seed 控制，并通过**对样本**做配对 bootstrap（10,000 次，seed 42）估计 CI 与 p 值——即"重数"体现在重采样统计而非重复生成。
  - 可选（预算允许时）：每样本生成 k=3~5 轨 temp=0.8、top-p=0.95 采样，报告 pass@1 以及解码鲁棒性分析。
- **抽样决策（算力受限时）**：固定 seed 42 做简单随机抽样 n=1,000，导出被抽样本 id 列表（存 JSON）供审计；若仍不足则 n=300 探索性子集并**明确标注"仅初步证据"**。报告中注明抽样导致 CI 变宽并附功效说明。

### 2.2 统一任务格式（prompt 构造与两模型对齐）
- **公共模板（两模型共用）**：
  - CFF 主轨：`concat(依赖文件按官方顺序) + <分隔> + 目标文件前缀(至签名行)`。
  - 对照轨（prefix-only）：仅目标文件前缀。
  - 分隔符用普通换行/文件路径注释头；**不使用任何模型的特殊 fill token**（两模型均标准前缀续写接口，避免 InCoder 式 FIM 带来的不可比）。
- **模型接口**：GPT-2 用 `GPT2LMHeadModel`（`gpt2` 官方权重，124M）；CodeLlama 用 `AutoModelForCausalLM` 加载 `codellama/CodeLlama-7b-hf`（base 版，非 Instruct/Python 变体，理由：对齐"原生气代码补全"能力并在 §5 列为假设）。两者均用各自 tokenizer + `generate` 前缀续写。
- **输入长度对齐**：统一输入预算 B=1,024 token（对两模型一致——GPT-2 窗口上限即 1024）；CodeLlama 另跑 B=16K 全上下文轨（消融 A）。由于两者分词器不同，"1,024 token"实际覆盖字符数不同，故**双口径复核**：按「token 数」与「字符数」各做一次等长对齐，报告两者结果。
- **输出长度对齐**：`max_new_tokens` 主口径 = min(256, 金标 token 数)，并在评分前把两模型预测都截到金标长度（见 §2.3）；另设"不截断（上限 256）"次口径（消融 E）。

### 2.3 评测管线细节（打分管线）
1. **输出归一化（对两模型一致）**：
   a. 去除生成文本首尾空白与多余尾随缩进/换行；b. 行尾统一为 LF(CRLF→LF)；c. 截取预测到金标 body 长度（字符级为主口径）；d. 规范化 EM＝去除所有空白后精确相等；同时记录原始精确 EM。
2. **指标**：主指标 = per-sample ES（字符级 Levenshtein 归一化）+ 规范化 EM；补充 = BLEU/CodeBLEU（注明非官方指标，仅参考）。
3. **官方脚本 vs 自建（对齐方式）**：
   - 首选：若能获得官方 `evaluate.py`，直接调用并锁定其版本（记录 hash），官方怎么算就怎么算。
   - 否则自建：实现 EM（规范化与原始两种）与 ES（Levenshtein），将实现锁定在仓库内，并用**手工样例单元测试**对齐官方定义（例如给定 gold=`return a+b`，对若干预测变体断言期望的 ES/EM 值）。两模型共享同一套打分函数，保证相对比较零偏差。
   - 无论哪种，报告声明口径；自建时在报告中给出"与官方定义的差异列表"。

### 2.4 统计与显著性检验
- 配对 bootstrap（10,000 次，seed 42）→ 两模型 ES 均值差/中位数差的 95% 百分位 CI。
- ES：Wilcoxon 符号秩检验（配对）；EM：McNemar 检验（每样本命中与否的 2×2）。
- 报告效果量（如 Cohen's d / 差中位数 / 胜率差）为主，p 值为辅；多指标/多口径说明多重比较的处置（默认不校正并注明，或附加 FDR 校正的敏感性行）。

### 2.5 消融 / 对照设计
- **A. 上下文长度隔离（最关键）**：CodeLlama@16K vs CodeLlama@1,024 vs GPT-2@1,024。把"CodeLlama 赢"拆成"代码特化/规模收益"与"更长上下文收益"两部分。若 CodeLlama@1,024 已显著优于 GPT-2，则结论与上下文长度无关；否则上下文长度是主要混淆。
- **B. 有无跨文件上下文**：CFF vs prefix-only（对两模型各测一次），量化跨文件上下文的边际价值。
- **C. 代码特化 vs 规模（可选，算力允许时）**：用 RepoBench-P 训练切 CFF 格式微调 GPT-2（LoRA，固定 seed），对比"未微调 GPT-2"，把"非代码特化"这一混淆显式拆出。
- **D. 解码**：greedy vs temp=0.8/top-p 0.95，检验结论对解码不敏感。
- **E. 输出截断口径**：截到金标长度 vs 不截断(上限 256)，检验评分口径的影响。
- 每个消融均保持其余环节与主实验完全一致（只动一个变量）。

---

## 3. 可复现性块
- **全局种子**：Python/`random`/`numpy`/`torch` 各自 `.manual_seed(42)` 且同值；GPU 下启用 `deterministic` 并关断 benchmark 模式，说明残余非确定性的处理。
- **模型配置**：GPT-2 = `gpt2` 官方权重；CodeLlama = `codellama/CodeLlama-7b-hf` 官方权重；量化时记录量化方案与位宽（见 §4）。权重 sha256 记录在案。
- **数据与代码版本**：HF 数据集 commit hash、transformer/torch/Python 版本、评测脚本版本全部记录；无网络环境先预下载并校验。
- **抽样**：完整记录 seed、抽样函数与被抽样本 id 列表（存 `sample_ids.json`）。
- **输出落盘**：每样本 prediction/gold/两模型 logits 元数据存 JSONL，支持事后重评与审计。
- **运行脚本**：单入口脚本 + 固定参数文件（config.yaml），一键复现主实验与全部消融。

---

## 4. 可行性
- **当前执行环境事实**（已勘察）：无 GPU（无 /dev/nvidia*）、无网络（DNS 失败）、未装 torch/transformers/datasets 等 ML 包；224 CPU 核；约 2TB RAM（可用约 1.2TB）；工作区可用磁盘约 24GB。
- **内存**：GPT-2 124M FP16 权重≈0.25GB；CodeLlama-7B FP16≈14GB 权重；KV cache 随上下文增长——B=1,024 时整机峰值约 15–17GB，B=16K 时约 24–40GB（随 batch 变化，按需降 batch）。
- **部署方案（按优先级）**：
  1. 首选：具备 GPU（≥24GB，如 A100/4090）的执行环境，两模型均 FP16 全精度。
  2. 若显存 <16GB：CodeLlama 用一致的 4-bit 量化（bitsandbytes/GPTQ），同一量化跑完全部样本；并在 200 样本子集上用 FP16 对照量化误差，量化损失在报告中说明，且不把量化版与全精度 GPT-2 的差异直接当成"模型能力差异"。
  3. CPU 回退（本机 224 核/1.2TB RAM 理论上可跑）：CodeLlama-7B CPU 推理约每样本 30s–数分钟，14k 样本不可行；仅建议作为 300 样本探索性验证，并标注"初步证据"。
- **时间粗估（假设 1×A100）**：CodeLlama-7B greedy、B=1,024、约 100 token 输出、bs=8：约 1–3s/样本 → 1,000 样本约 0.5–1h/轨，14k 全量约 4–12h；B=16K 轨约 2–4× 更慢；GPT-2 快约两个数量级，可忽略。
- **全量 vs 抽样决策规则**：默认全量（约 14k）；若 GPU·时预算 < 约 12h → 抽样 1,000（seed 42）并报告 CI 与功效；< 约 2h → 降级 300 探索性子集并明确标注。

---

## 5. 关键假设汇总与敏感度
| 假设 | 内容 | 若违背/偏离的影响 |
|---|---|---|
| H1 模型选择 | GPT-2 取 124M `gpt2`；CodeLlama-7B 取 base（非 Instruct/Python） | 改变"代码特化收益"的解释范围——若用 Instruct 会混入指令微调能力 |
| H2 输入预算 | 主比较统一 B=1,024 token（对 GPT-2 是窗口满额，对 CodeLlama 是截断） | 若 CodeLlama 靠长上下文取胜，主比较会低估它——故设消融 A 显式隔离 |
| H3 输出截断 | 评分前预测截到金标长度；max_new_tokens=min(256, gold) | 影响 ES 分母与 EM（长度优势被消除）；消融 E 量化其影响 |
| H4 归一化口径 | 规范化 EM(去空白)+字符级 Levenshtein ES；自建时用单元测试固定 | 影响绝对分数，相对比较不敏感；报告中声明口径 |
| H5 评测实现 | 优先官方 `evaluate.py`，否则自建并单元测试对齐；两模型共用同一打分函数 | 保证两模型等口径即可，实现差异只影响绝对分 |
| H6 部署 | 需 GPU 执行；或 CodeLlama 一致量化并在子集上对照全精度 | 量化会引入精度损失，已用子集对照+声明处理 |
| H7 抽样 | 全量优先；受限时 seed 42 抽 1,000 并报告 | 抽样放大 CI、降功效；结论方向不变 |
| H8 single_file 命名 | 若无官方切分，按 prefix-only 自建 | 仅影响消融 B 的解释措辞，不影响主比较 |

---

## 6. 交付物与收尾
- 主报告：EM/ES 表（全量或抽样规模标注）+ 配对 CI + 检验 + 效果量；消融 A–E 表；可复现脚本/种子/样本清单；局限性与假设清单（H1–H8、U1–U7 的处置记录）。
- 明确不声称已运行实验；所有数字待执行时以记录的事实/输出为准。

---

## 7. 尚需在执行阶段澄清（按优先级）
1. 执行环境是否提供 GPU、能否联网下载 HF 权重/数据集（决定部署方案与全量/抽样）。
2. CodeLlama 是否允许量化（决定 H6 的 1 或 2 方案）。
3. 官方 repo`evaluate.py` 与 JSONL schema 的可获得性（决定 U2/U5 走"核实"还是"假设+自建"）。
4. 是否需要把 GPT-2 微调（消融 C）纳入范围（影响算力预算约数小时/轨）。

1) Inspect the available inputs. This is a design-only task (no execution required), so just survey what is present in /workspace and any provided documents, and summarize what source-supported details they contain about RepoBench, the 'cross_file_first' setting, and the evaluation contract.

2) Propose an approach in outline form (a few bullets is fine): how you would structure an experiment comparing GPT-2 (small) vs CodeLlama-7b (larger, code-specialized) on RepoBench Python 'cross_file_first'. Please indicate your planned choices for (a) data/subset and split, (b) prompt/input construction specific to cross_file_first (e.g., cross-file context retrieval or gold-file context, context window limits), (c) model setup (tokenizer, max tokens, decoding, sampling vs greedy), (d) evaluation metric(s) suitable for this benchmark, (e) controls to make the comparison fair and isolate the model-size/specialization factor, and (f) the analysis plan (effect sizes, error breakdowns, sensitivity checks) and feasibility.

3) List the consequential assumptions and uncertainties you would rely on, and how you would validate or flag each. In particular: how the RepoBench cross_file_first input is formed and scored, what "performance" should mean operationally (e.g., exact-match/F1/code-bleu, pass@k not being feasible without execution), and resource/runtime constraints. Note that any of these not confirmed by the documents remains an assumption, not a fact.

I will review your proposed outlines and assumptions before authorizing the full design.

Design-only task. Workspace contains only /workspace/task.json; the only document (track.md, embedded in task.json) says "Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required." No datasets, no model weights, no RepoBench files, no torch/transformers/numpy, no network, no GPU, 224 CPUs, ~2TB RAM. Therefore all RepoBench-specific claims are external-knowledge assumptions unless the researcher confirms them.

PROPOSED OUTLINE:

(a) Data/subset/split: official RepoBench Python TEST split (assumed to exist); deterministic seeded subsample N≈300–500 stratified by repo, pre-filtered so the FULL prompt (cross-file context + target-file prefix + marker) fits GPT-2's 1024-token window — both models then see byte-identical full text (removes truncation as confound). Small N≈50 qualifier subset first.

(b) Prompt construction (cross_file_first): prepend gold cross-file context files (the cross_file_first contexts, i.e., files referenced/imported by the target) + target file content up to a line-boundary marker; model must generate next ground-truth line(s). Context budget computed in each model's own tokens; no mid-context truncation in the primary design; separate truncation sensitivity check (front-truncate to shared budget).

(c) Model setup: gpt2 (124M) vs codellama/CodeLlama-7b-hf (7B), off-the-shelf, no fine-tuning; each model's own tokenizer (byte-BPE vs Llama SPM); primary decoding = greedy (T=0); max_new_tokens sized for 1 gold line (primary) and 3 lines (secondary); bf16/fp32 on CPU.

(d) Metrics: Primary = Exact Match (EM) on next line(s) (official RepoBench-Code metric, with specified normalization). Secondary = Edit Similarity (normalized Levenshtein) + optional token/char F1 and CodeBLEU. Execution-based pass@k explicitly NOT feasible (no execution/coverage contract; would need running repo environment) — "performance" is defined operationally as text-match completion metrics.

(e) Controls/fairness: identical template, context, subset, greedy decoding, and scorer for both models; same-N paired framing; a cross_file_random-style/no-context control condition to verify each model actually uses cross-file context (so gap in cross_file_first isn't a formatting artifact); no truncation design isolates model-size/specialization factor.

(f) Analysis/feasibility: per-model EM + Edit-Sim with bootstrap CIs; PAIRED differences via McNemar (EM) and paired t/Wilcoxon (Edit-Sim) with effect sizes (Cohen's h/d); error breakdowns (context size, target-line type, repo); sensitivity checks (temperature/top-p, 1-line vs 3-line targets, truncation policy, subset seed). Feasible on 224 CPUs for N≤500 (CodeLlama-7B CPU greedy is slow but tractable); BLOCKERS for any future run: no network (must provision weights+data offline) and no ML libs installed (Python 3.14 wheel compatibility unverified).

payload.answer:
# FINAL EXPERIMENT DESIGN (deliverable)

**STATUS: Design specification only. No experiment has been executed. All compute-, data-, and result-related statements below are a protocol to be followed in a future run, not observations. Statements labeled [ASSUMPTION] are external-knowledge claims about RepoBench (Liu et al., ICLR 2024; github.com/amazon-science/repo-benchmark) that are NOT confirmed by any provided document; each is paired with a validation step or flag in Section 6.**

---

## 1. Rationale and hypotheses

**Rationale.** RepoBench tests repository-level code completion where a model must continue a target file using cross-file context. Comparing a small general-purpose LM (GPT-2 small, 124M, byte-level BPE trained on English text, 1024-token window) with a 7B code-specialized LM (CodeLlama-7b, SentencePiece/Llama tokenizer, 16k window, pretrained on code) isolates the joint factor "capacity + code specialization." CodeLlama is expected to dominate on surface-level code fluency and on using cross-file context, but a controlled measurement (identical inputs, decoding, and scoring) is needed to (i) quantify the gap, (ii) test whether the gap is really driven by cross-file context usage vs simple memorization of Python scaffolding, and (iii) characterize where (which line types / context sizes) each model fails.

**Pre-specified hypotheses (falsifiable, directional):**
- **H1 (primary):** CodeLlama-7b achieves higher Exact Match (EM) than GPT-2 small on RepoBench Python `cross_file_first` next-line completion on the evaluable subset (paired, one-sided, α=0.05).
- **H2:** CodeLlama-7b achieves higher Edit Similarity than GPT-2 small (paired, α=0.05).
- **H3 (context-use test):** the `cross_file_first` minus random-context (control) delta in EM is larger for CodeLlama than for GPT-2, i.e., CodeLlama derives more benefit from the gold cross-file context (interaction test; H3 is secondary/exploratory).
- **H4 (exploratory):** the relative gap is smaller for short-context, single-line targets and larger for long-context or structural targets (e.g., `return`/control-flow lines after imports), consistent with GPT-2's short-window and weak code induction limits.

**Operational definition of "performance."** Performance = text-match code-completion quality: Exact Match (primary) and Edit Similarity (secondary) on the next line(s), computed identically for both models. **Execution-based `pass@k`/runtime-correctness is explicitly out of scope**: no execution sandbox, no test harness, and the benchmark's code-completion contract is text-based [ASSUMPTION-3]. Results will be worded as "predicted-text matches the gold next line exactly / approximately," never as "code runs."

---

## 2. Full protocol

### 2.1 Data, split, subsampling, filtering
- **Source [ASSUMPTION-1]:** official RepoBench Python `cross_file_first` test split (must be provisioned offline; see §5). Repository/data files are not present in the workspace and must be supplied before any run.
- **Qualifier phase:** draw a seeded **N=50** sample and run the entire pipeline end-to-end; verify (a) prompt assembly parses, (b) per-model token budgets are respected, (c) scorer reproduces EM/Edit-Sim on hand-checked cases. Fix protocol bugs here; do not report these 50 in final results.
- **Fitness filter (applied to test split):** an example is eligible iff the FULL assembled prompt (context files + target prefix + marker, see §2.2) fits within **GPT-2's 1024-token window** using GPT-2's tokenizer. This guarantees both models see byte-identical complete text (no truncation → removes truncation as a confound). Record the eligibility rate and (for the analysis §4.5) the difficulty-coverage tradeoff this induces.
- **Final sample:** from eligible examples, **N=400** drawn with **seeded stratified sampling**: stratify by repository, draw proportionally, cap per-repo. Seeded across two seeds (0 and 2026) as a robustness pair; primary report = seed 0, seed 2026 used in §4.5 sensitivity.
- **Control condition (same 400 samples):** the "no/random context" variant uses the same target-prefix/marker but with the cross-file context REPLACED by a matched-size set of random files from the same repo (`cross_file_random`-style) [ASSUMPTION-2]. This is an ablation of context usefulness, not an extra dataset.

### 2.2 Prompt assembly for `cross_file_first` [ASSUMPTION-2,4]
Assembled prompt template (identical for both models; only per-model token budget checks differ):
```
<path:context_file_1>
<text of context_file_1>

<path:context_file_k>
<text of context_file_k>

<path:target_file.py>
<target file text up to the line-boundary marker>MARKER_START
<target line(s) to generate>MARKER_END
```
- **Context-selection rule:** use the example's `cross_file_first` context exactly as provided by the benchmark [ASSUMPTION-2]; preserve the official file ordering (no re-ranking) to avoid introducing our own retrieval into the comparison. Number of context files and total context size are recorded per example for the error breakdown (§4.4).
- **Separators:** a header line `<path:...>` above each file, blank line between files (mirrors the benchmark's stated concatenation convention; exact separators to be locked to the official eval script when available — flagged, see §6).
- **Marker:** single line-boundary sentinel placed immediately before the first gold target line; the model never sees gold text past the marker.
- **Token budgets:** GPT-2 budget = 1024 tokens (its full window); CodeLlama budget = 16,384 tokens. The fitness filter (§2.1) ensures both budgets are satisfied with no clipping. `max_new_tokens` is computed from the gold target block (see §2.3), not from a fixed count.

### 2.3 Model and decoding configuration
**Shared across both models:** off-the-shelf pretrained checkpoints, **no fine-tuning** (factor = pretraining + size only). Greedy decoding (temperature=0, `do_sample=False`) as the primary configuration. `pad_token_id` set explicitly; generation batched (see §5).
- **GPT-2 small (`gpt2`, 124M):** its byte-level BPE tokenizer; window 1024; prompts must pass the fitness filter.
- **CodeLlama-7b (`codellama/CodeLlama-7b-hf`, ~7B):** its Llama SentencePiece tokenizer; window 16,384; same prompt strings, no reformatting.
- **`max_new_tokens`:** primary = tokens needed for **1 gold line** (computed with the generating model's own tokenizer from the gold reference, so each model emits "one target line"); secondary = **3 gold lines**. No sampling in primary runs. Stop at the newline(s) terminating the gold line block per the contract [ASSUMPTION-2,5].
- **Precision/loading:** bf16 (fallback fp32) on CPU; no quantization in primary runs (a quantization sensitivity run is optional, §4.5, to check robustness of the 7B results).

### 2.4 Evaluation pipeline
1. Generate greedy continuations from the marker for both models on exactly the same 400 prompts (plus 50 qualifier).
2. Extract the generated block: text from after the marker up to the configured stop (1-line or 3-line condition).
3. **Normalization (identical for both models, applied to model output and reference):** strip trailing newlines/whitespace; normalize line endings to `\n`; do NOT dedent or strip leading indentation (indentation is part of matching); do NOT strip the final partial line.
4. **Metrics (code-tokenization-free; computed on strings, so tokenizer mismatch cannot distort scoring):**
   - **EM** (primary): exact string equality of normalized generated block vs normalized gold block → 0/1 per sample. Also reported as **line-set EM** (all generated lines matched, order-preserved) for the 3-line condition.
   - **Edit Similarity** (secondary): 1 − (Levenshtein / max(len(ref), len(gen))) on the normalized block.
   - Optional tertiary: character-level F1 and CodeBLEU (needs a Python tokenizer such as tree-sitter — flagged as optional/dependency-gated).
5. Every result row stores the per-model generated text so all metrics, breakdowns, and error audits are reproducible from the same artifacts.

---

## 3. Controls and threat mitigation

| Threat | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| **Truncation confound** (GPT-2 window < long contexts) | Fitness filter guarantees byte-identical full prompts for both models in the primary analysis; separate §4.5 truncation-sensitivity check front-clips context to a shared token budget and reports the delta. |
| **Difficulty-coverage tradeoff** (filter keeps only ≤1024-token prompts) | Reported explicitly: (i) eligibility rate of the test split, (ii) comparison of sample vs full-split difficulty using GPT-2's own performance as a proxy where computable, (iii) length strata in breakdown §4.4. No claim is made that results generalize to longer-context examples. |
| **Prompt-formatting artifacts** (both models merely parrot the template) | Random/no-context control condition (§2.1, H3): if a model's `cross_file_first` gain over its own control is ~0, its absolute score is treated as format-driven, not cross-file-driven. |
| **Tokenizer mismatch** (byte-BPE vs SPM; different token counts) | (i) Metrics computed on normalized strings, never on tokens; (ii) token budgets computed per model; (iii) text is byte-identical; (iv) 7B window advantage is neutralized by the fitness filter in the primary design. |
| **Decoding stochasticity** | Primary = greedy (deterministic, seed-fixed). Sampling (T=0.2, top-p=0.9) as sensitivity (§4.5) with 5 seeds reported as median±spread, never conflated with greedy results. |
| **Context usefulness** (does the model actually use it?) | `cross_file_first − control` delta per model (§2.1, H3); also error audit that flags samples where predictions equal control predictions (no context effect). |
| **Scorer/implementation bias** | Identical scorer binary applied to both models; normalization locked before any run on the qualifier set; hand-audited on 10 hand-constructed cases during qualifier. |
| **Data/selection bias** | Seeded stratified sampling; two seeds; pre-registered N, filter, and analyses (all in this document). |

---

## 4. Analysis plan

### 4.1 Point estimates and CIs
Per model, per condition (`cross_file_first`, control), per target width (1-line, 3-line): **EM rate** and **mean Edit Similarity**, each with **95% percentile bootstrap CIs** (10,000 resamples, over the 400 samples, seeded).

### 4.2 Primary inference (paired, same 400 samples)
- **EM (binary, paired):** McNemar's test (two-sided for reporting; H1 tested one-sided). Report the discordant-pair table and the paired EM difference.
- **Edit Similarity (continuous, paired):** Wilcoxon signed-rank (primary, robust) and paired-sample t-test (reported alongside); report mean paired difference and its bootstrap CI.
- **Effect sizes:** Cohen's h for EM difference; Cohen's d (paired) for Edit-Sim difference. Interpret vs conventional benchmarks (small/medium/large), but emphasize the CI.
- **H3 interaction:** per-model control-adjusted scores; test whether `(EM_cross − EM_control)` differs between models (two-sample bootstrap test on the paired deltas).

### 4.3 Significance/power note
With N=400 binary paired outcomes, a McNemar test can detect a ~6–8% true discordance-rate difference with power ≥ 0.8 (α=0.05, one-sided) — this is a planning estimate, not a result; the design reports exact CIs regardless of significance.

### 4.4 Pre-specified error breakdowns (stratified EM and Edit-Sim with CIs)
- By **context length** (tokens needed: quartiles of total context tokens; plus a "≤256 / 257–1024" GPT-2-feasible bucket).
- By **number of cross-file context files** (1 / 2–4 / >4).
- By **target-line type** (assignment, `return`, `def`/`class` header, control flow, call/import — labeled by a lightweight static heuristic, not a full parser; dependency-gated refinement with tree-sitter optional).
- By **repository** (top-10 largest-repo strata + "other").
- By **gold-line length** (chars).
- By 1-line vs 3-line condition.

### 4.5 Pre-specified sensitivity checks
1. **Sampling:** T=0.2, top-p=0.9, 5 seeds; report median ± IQR of EM/Edit-Sim per model; check ordering stability.
2. **Truncation policy:** front-clip context to the largest shared token budget (e.g., 512) in both models; report EM delta vs the no-truncation primary — isolates whether the primary gap is truncation-sensitive.
3. **Subset seed:** seed 2026 vs seed 0 (same rules); report CI overlap and ranking stability.
4. **Target width:** 3-line condition vs 1-line.
5. **Optional:** CodeLlama quantization (e.g., int8) to check 7B results' stability under memory-saving loading.

### 4.6 Reporting contract
Pre-registered tables: (a) eligibility/filter stats, (b) main results table (both conditions, both widths, metrics with CIs), (c) paired-test table, (d) breakdown tables, (e) sensitivity table. Every claim will be phrased conditionally on this protocol; the word "we ran" will be avoided; all outputs will be labeled "simulated under the design" or "not yet produced."

---

## 5. Feasibility, compute and runtime estimates, provisioning blockers

**Observed environment (verified during exploration):** Python 3.14.4 system; **no** torch/transformers/datasets/numpy/pandas; **no network**; `gpu_enabled: false`; 224 CPUs; ~2 TB RAM; workspace contains only task.json.

**Provisioning blockers (must be resolved before any run):**
- **Weights:** GPT-2 (≈0.5 GB) and CodeLlama-7b (≈13–14 GB in bf16) must be present locally — network is disabled, so they must be provisioned offline into the workspace.
- **Data:** RepoBench Python `cross_file_first` split must be supplied offline (not present).
- **Dependencies:** a Python environment with torch + transformers must be installed; Python 3.14 wheel availability for these is **unverified** (flagged). A fallback is to use a compatible pinned Python 3.10/3.11 env, which may itself need provisioning.
- **Optional evaluator deps:** tree-sitter / sacrebleu for CodeBLEU and type-labeling; gated.

**Compute/runtime estimates (planning figures only, not measured):**
- GPT-2 small: ~15–40 tokens/s/sample on 1 CPU core; for ≤ ~1k prompt tokens + ~50 output tokens, ≈ tens of seconds per sample per core; trivially parallelized across 224 cores → the 400+50 GPT-2 runs complete in minutes.
- CodeLlama-7B greedy on CPU: ~1–5 tokens/s/sample on 1 core (realistically slower; large-model CPU inference), i.e., roughly **1–10 min per sample** on a single core. Parallelizing 200 samples across cores (batching on 4–8 cores each) gives an estimated **wall-clock range of ~1–8 hours** for the 7B side, dependent on achievable throughput — acknowledged as a wide estimate and a top execution risk (flagged, §6).
- Memory: 13–14 GB for CodeLlama bf16, far below 2 TB; batching of dozens of 7B decodes per node is memory-trivial, so the bottleneck is CPU compute throughput and memory bandwidth, not capacity.

4. **[ASSUMPTION-4] RepoBench cross-file prompt formatting convention** (header lines, blank-line separators, marker placement). Validation: mirror the official eval script exactly when available; currently flagged as the protocol's own locked convention pending that source.
5. **[ASSUMPTION-5] "Next line" scope (1 line primary / 3 lines secondary) and stop/newline handling.** Validation: researcher confirms the benchmark's target-width convention; default stays 1-line primary.

9. **[ASSUMPTION-9] CPU-only 7B inference for N≈400 (plus qualifier) is feasible (≈1–8 h est.), and Python 3.14/torch wheels install.**

**Non-blocking uncertainties flagged:** exact official separators/template (§2.2), exact scorer normalization (§2.4), eligibility rate of the test split (unknown until data provisioned), and achievable CodeLlama-7B CPU throughput (unknown until measured in the qualifier phase).

पहले /workspace repository और track.md दस्तावेज़ का निरीक्षण करो — देखो कि FuseLLM, Llama-2, और CommenSense (CS) benchmark के बारे में कोई सेटअप विवरण दर्ज है या नहीं। यह design-only कार्य है; कोई experiment run करने की ज़रूरत नहीं है और मैं run हुआ होने का दावा नहीं चाहता।

अभी पूरा solution मत दो। मेरे लिए ये तीन चीज़ें तैयार करो:
1. Repository/document inspection का सार — क्या उपलब्ध है, क्या गायब है (जैसे कौन-से model checkpoints, कौन-सी benchmark परिभाषा)।
2. प्रस्तावित approach — प्रायोगिक डिज़ाइन की रूपरेखा: CS benchmark के कौन-से घटक/benchmarks (जैसे BoolQ, PIQA, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-e/c, OpenBookQA, CommonsenseQA), FuseLLM और Llama-2 के कौन-से base sizes/variants और checkpoints, zero-shot evaluation protocol (prompt format, decoding params), controls (समान prompts, same seed/decoding, same harness), metric (accuracy), और analysis plan (trial/repetition count, error bars, कैसे निष्कर्ष निकालेंगे)।
3. Consequential assumptions और uncertainties — जहाँ source में कोई विवरण नहीं मिलता (setup_2, setup_9 केवल सवाल और "FuseLLM" तय करते हैं), वहाँ तुम जो choice मानोगे उसे assumption की तरह ही मार्क करो, confirmed fact की तरह नहीं, और उसका प्रभाव बताओ।

जवाब में यह भी स्पष्ट करो कि तुम्हारी proposed setup के तहत क्या feasibility है (कोई GPU/compute नहीं है)।

## 1. Repository / Document Inspection का सार

- `/workspace` में केवल `task.json` है — कोई FuseLLM codebase, कोई model checkpoint, कोई benchmark dataset, कोई harness नहीं।
- `task.json` में एकमात्र document entry है:
  - `track.md` → सामग्री: "Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required." (यह एक note है, अलग फ़ाइल नहीं — पूरे filesystem में `track.md` नाम की कोई फ़ाइल नहीं मिली)।
- `documents` में FuseLLM paper, setup_2, setup_9, benchmark-परिभाषा, या model-size जैसा कोई विवरण उपलब्ध नहीं है।
- Environment verification (execute_check का concrete output):
  - Python 3.14, pip मौजूद; पर परियोजना-संबंधी packages स्थापित नहीं: `torch`, `transformers`, `datasets`, `lm_eval`, `numpy`, `accelerate`, `safetensors` — सब `False`।
  - GPU नहीं (`nvidia-smi` driver communication fail), network disabled (कोई HF cache, कोई datasets mount नहीं), 224 CPU cores + ~2TB RAM उपलब्ध।

**क्या उपलब्ध है:** प्रश्न (question), context ("Design an experiment…", "Do not claim that an experiment was run"), track.md का design-only note, और researcher द्वारा पुष्टि कि setup_2 व setup_9 केवल सवाल और "FuseLLM" तय करते हैं।

**क्या गायब है:** model checkpoints की कोई list (FuseLLM कौन-सा size/variant, Llama-2 कौन-सा size), CS benchmark की आधिकारिक परिभाषा (कौन-से sub-benchmarks), evaluation protocol (prompt format, decoding params) — इनमें से कोई भी source में दर्ज नहीं है; इसलिए इन्हें assumptions घोषित करूँगा।

## 2. प्रस्तावित Approach (outline)

**उद्देश्य:** परीक्षण करना कि क्या FuseLLM, Llama-2 पर zero-shot CS benchmarks पर बेहतर प्रदर्शन करता है (reproduction/verification-type experiment — इसमें FuseLLM paper का headline result है)।

**Models (controlled comparison):**
- Treatment: FuseLLM-7B (paper का fused checkpoint; architecture = Llama-2-7B, इसी से initialize)।
- Baseline: Llama-2-7B (same architecture → matched param count; fusion training ही अकेला अंतर)।
- Control-तर्क: यही pair question का core है; architecture/scale match होने से प्रदर्शन अंतर fusion का effect माना जा सकता है। (Additional context के रूप में source models OpenLLaMA-7B, MPT-7B भी रख सकते हैं, पर primary comparison FuseLLM vs Llama-2 ही रहेगा।)

**CS benchmark घटक (proposed set, paper के "Commonsense Reasoning" suite पर आधारित):** BoolQ, PIQA, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-easy, ARC-challenge, OpenBookQA, CommonsenseQA (CSQA)। (Exact list — assumption; source में परिभाषा नहीं मिली।)

**Zero-shot protocol:**
- एक ही harness (EleutherAI lm-eval-harness, fixed version) सभी models के लिए।
- Multiple-choice tasks (PIQA, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-e/c, OBQA, CSQA): answer-choice log-prob ranking (no generation) — हर choice के token log-prob sum करके max वाला चुनना; HellaSwag के लिए primary metric `acc_norm` (length-normalized)।
- BoolQ: cloze/generation task → greedy decoding (temp=0), max_new_tokens छोटा (≈1–3), फिर True/False match करके accuracy।
- दोनों models पर समान prompt templates, same dataset splits (harness defaults), same seed, same precision (bf16/fp16), same batch settings।

**Metric & analysis:**
- Primary: प्रत्येक benchmark की accuracy; secondary: CS set पर average accuracy।
- Hypothesis (one-directional): FuseLLM-7B की CS-औसत accuracy > Llama-2-7B की।
- Analysis plan: per-benchmark comparison (कौन-से benchmarks पर जीत/हार), aggregate mean difference, और robustness के लिए (a) multiple prompt templates (≈3–5 description variants) से per-benchmark accuracy distribution + bootstrap CI (instances पर), और (b) अगर चाहें तो per-instance paired McNemar test। चूँकि zero-shot MC scoring deterministic है, repetition से नहीं बल्कि template-variation/instance-bootstrap से error bars आएँगे।
- निष्कर्ष का नियम: aggregate पर FuseLLM आगे और अधिकांश benchmarks पर consistent win → "FuseLLM outperforms Llama-2 on CS"; aggregate पर पीछे या मिश्रित नतीजे → "no clear outperformance"।

**Feasibility (मेरे environment में):** कोई GPU नहीं, torch/transformers/lm_eval स्थापित नहीं, network बंद, datasets/HF cache नहीं → इस workspace में experiment चलाना feasible नहीं है। डिज़ाइन ही deliverable है। बाहरी GPU-क्लस्टर पर दोनों 7B models (~14GB fp16 each) + 8 datasets (~22k instances) के लिए MC-eval pipeline ~1–3 GPU-hours (A100/H100) अनुमानित; CPU-only run ~50–200× slower और आज के environment में dependencies नहीं मिलने से अव्यवहारिक।

## 3. Consequential Assumptions & Uncertainties

**Assumptions (source में दर्ज नहीं — researcher-पुष्टि अपेक्षित):**
1. CS = FuseLLM paper का "Commonsense Reasoning" benchmark suite (BoolQ, PIQA, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-e, ARC-c, OBQA, CSQA)। प्रभाव: benchmark list अलग होने पर नतीजा (win margin) बदल सकता है।
2. FuseLLM variant = FuseLLM-7B; Llama-2 variant = Llama-2-7B (matched scale)। प्रभाव: दूसरा size चुनने पर यह conclusion केवल उसी size पर लागू होगा।
3. Evaluation harness = lm-eval-harness (paper की default setups) with zero-shot MC-likelihood scoring। प्रभाव: prompt template की sensitivity ही मुख्य noise स्रोत है — इसलिए template-variation को design में रखा गया है।
4. Dataset splits = harness defaults (e.g., HellaSwag/WinoGrande/CSQA/BoolQ/PIQA validation, ARC-e/c test, OBQA test)। प्रभाव: split बदलने से संख्याएँ बदलेंगी पर relative comparison पर असर कम।

**Uncertainties:**
- setup_2 / setup_9 का content मेरे पास नहीं है (workspace में unavailable) — researcher से पुष्टि की आवश्यकता कि वे वास्तव में केवल प्रश्न+FuseLLM तय करते हैं, या वे benchmark list/protocol भी दर्ज करते हैं।
- FuseLLM-7B checkpoint की availability/format (HF repo, safetensors आदि) नेटवर्क बंद होने से यहाँ verify नहीं हो सकती — checkpoint तक पहुँच बाहरी compute पर मानी गई है।
- क्या paper का "outperform" claim aggregate-average पर आधारित है या हर benchmark पर — इससे निष्कर्ष-नियम तय होगा (मेरा design दोनों रिपोर्ट करता है)।

payload.answer:
# अंतिम प्रायोगिक डिज़ाइन — "Will FuseLLM outperform Llama-2 on CS (zero-shot)?"

यह design-only deliverable है। **कोई experiment run नहीं किया गया और न ही किसी परिणाम का दावा किया गया है।** नीचे केवल डिज़ाइन, controls, analysis plan और feasibility है।

## 1. Rationale

- **Pair क्यों:** प्रश्न "FuseLLM vs Llama-2" का न्यूनतम controlled परीक्षण **FuseLLM-7B vs Llama-2-7B** है — दोनों एक ही architecture/scale; FuseLLM-7B Llama-2-7B से initialize होकर token-level distribution fusion (OpenLLaMA-7B, MPT-7B से) करता है। इस तरह दोनों के बीच एकमात्र अंतर fusion training है, इसलिए accuracy का अंतर fusion के effect के रूप में पढ़ा जा सकता है। यही question का core है।
- **Benchmark-set क्यों:** "standard benchmarks CommenSense(CS)" FuseLLM paper के Commonsense Reasoning suite से मेल खाता है, जो बहु-विध question types (binary QA, physical commonsense, common-sense inference, common-sense QA, science QA) को cover करता है — यानी एक single benchmark पर निर्भर नहीं रहता।
- **Protocol क्यों:** प्रश्न "zero-shot" तय करता है। MC tasks के लिए answer-choice **log-prob ranking** (generation नहीं) determinism देता है; BoolQ के लिए cloze/greedy generation. दोनों models पर एक ही harness/templates/seed → परिणाम पर्याप्त रूप से comparative।
- **Aggregate + per-benchmark क्यों:** question "outperform" है — एक साथ aggregate average (paper का headline) और per-benchmark breakdown से यह कहा जा सकता है कि win consistent है या कुछ benchmarks पर ही है।

## 2. Experimental Setup

**Models (primary comparison):**
- Treatment: **FuseLLM-7B** (paper का fused checkpoint; source = Llama-2-7B + OpenLLaMA-7B + MPT-7B से fused)।
- Baseline: **Llama-2-7B** (matched architecture/param count)।
- Optional context (अलग से, primary comparison बदले बिना): OpenLLaMA-7B, MPT-7B (source models) — fusion की upper/lower bound समझने के लिए।

**CS benchmark suite (components):** BoolQ, PIQA, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-easy, ARC-challenge, OpenBookQA, CommonsenseQA (CSQA)।
- Primary metric: प्रत्येक benchmark की accuracy (HellaSwag: `acc_norm` primary; `acc` secondary); BoolQ: True/False match accuracy।
- Secondary metric: CS suite पर average accuracy; per-benchmark और aggregate दोनों।

**Zero-shot protocol (एक ही, हर model और हर benchmark पर):**
- Harness: EleutherAI **lm-eval-harness** (fixed, pinned version; reproducibility के लिए commit hash lock)।
- MC tasks (PIQA, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-e/c, OBQA, CSQA): हर choice की token log-prob sum करके max वाला चुनना (**no sampling**); HellaSwag के लिए length-normalized (`acc_norm`) primary।
- BoolQ: cloze/generation — greedy (temperature=0), `max_new_tokens` ≈ 1–3, आउटपुट को "True/False" से match।
- Prompt template: harness के per-benchmark default template; robustness के लिए **3–5 description-variant templates** (e.g., बिना description, "The following are multiple choice questions…", आदि) भी run।
- Compute/precision: **bf16** (fp16 fallback) दोनों models पर समान; batch-size समान रखा जाए।
- Dataset splits: harness defaults (BoolQ/PIQA/HellaSwag/WinoGrande/CSQA → validation; ARC-e/c/OBQA → test)। Seed: fixed (e.g., 42), समान दोनों पर।

## 3. Controls (दोनों models पर समान रखी गईं, और क्यों)

| Control | विवरण |
|---|---|
| Harness version | एक ही lm-eval-harness commit — prompt/logit handling में भिन्नता समाप्त |
| Tokenizer/vocab | दोनों Llama-2 tokenizer share करते हैं — tokenization bias नहीं |
| Prompt templates | वही template list वही order — prompt-sensitivity fair खेल में |
| Dataset splits & instances | वही instances, वही order — instance-sampling bias नहीं |
| Decoding | MC: likelihood-only (no sampling); BoolQ: greedy दोनों पर |
| Precision/batch | bf16/fp16, same batch-size — batching determinism बरकरार |
| Seed | fixed, same — कोई stochastic भिन्नता नहीं |
| कारण | अकेला independent variable fusion training रह जाए — accuracy अंतर effect-प्रमाण के रूप में पढ़ने योग्य हो |

## 4. Analysis Plan (डेटा → निष्कर्ष)

1. हर model × हर benchmark × हर template पर accuracy निकालो → per-template per-benchmark table।
2. Primary per-benchmark: default template की accuracy दोनों models के लिए; फिर सभी templates पर mean ± SD।
3. Aggregate: CS-average (8 benchmarks का mean) दोनों models के लिए।
4. Uncertainty/error bars:
   - **Instance-level bootstrap** (e.g., 1000 resamples) → per-benchmark accuracy के 95% CI।
   - **Template-variation**: अलग-अलग template पर results से robustness spread (यही अधिकांश noise स्रोत है — zero-shot MC deterministic है, repetition से नहीं बल्कि template-variation/instance-bootstrap से error bars)।
   - वैकल्पिक: **per-instance paired McNemar test** प्रत्येक benchmark पर (aggregate से संदूषित नहीं)।
5. **निर्णय-नियम:**
   - "FuseLLM outperforms Llama-2 on CS" तब कहेंगे जब FuseLLM-7B का CS-average CI, Llama-2 के CS-average CI से ऊपर (non-overlap या bootstrap difference CI > 0), **और** 8 में से अधिकांश (≥6) benchmarks पर consistent win।
   - "No clear outperformance" तब जब aggregates overlap करें, या जीत मिश्रित (कुछ benchmarks पर FuseLLM, कुछ पर Llama-2) — भले किसी एक benchmark पर अंतर बड़ा हो।
   - Result को कभी single benchmark के अंतर से तय न करें।

## 5. Feasibility

- **इस workspace में:** कोई GPU नहीं (`nvidia-smi` driver-communication fail), `torch`/`transformers`/`datasets`/`lm_eval`/`numpy` स्थापित नहीं (सभी `importlib.find_spec` → False), network disabled, कोई HF cache/datasets mount नहीं। इसलिए यहाँ experiment चलाना **feasible नहीं है**; यह design केवल deliverable है।
- **बाहरी GPU क्लस्टर पर (अनुमानित):** दोनों 7B models fp16 ≈ 14GB VRAM each; 8 datasets ≈ ~22k instances (BoolQ ~3270, PIQA ~1838, HellaSwag ~10k, WinoGrande ~1267, ARC-e ~2376, ARC-c ~1172, OBQA ~500, CSQA ~1221 — सभी harness splits)। MC-eval pipeline दोनों models के लिए **~1–3 GPU-hours (A100/H100)** अनुमानित; template-variation (3–5×) और bootstrap के साथ ~2–4× तक। CPU-only run ~50–200× slower और आज के environment की तरह बिना deps के अव्यवहारिक।

## Assumptions (source में नहीं मिले choice — confirmed fact नहीं) & Uncertainties

- **[A1]** CS suite = FuseLLM paper का Commonsense Reasoning set (BoolQ, PIQA, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-e, ARC-c, OBQA, CSQA) — अलग होने पर win margin बदल सकता है।
- **[A2]** Models = FuseLLM-7B vs Llama-2-7B (matched scale) — conclusion इसी scale पर लागू।
- **[A3]** Harness = lm-eval-harness (pinned version), splits = harness defaults — संख्याएँ बदलेंगी पर relative comparison पर असर सीमित।
- **[A4]** FuseLLM-7B checkpoint की HF-availability/format बाहरी compute पर उपलब्ध मानी गई (यहाँ network बंद से verify नहीं हो सकी)।
- **[U1]** **setup_2/setup_9 के वास्तविक contents मेरे पास उपलब्ध नहीं हैं** (workspace में कोई दस्तावेज़ नहीं); researcher के अनुसार वे केवल प्रश्न + "FuseLLM" तय करते हैं — यदि वे benchmark list/protocol भी तय करते हैं, तो [A1]/[A3] को उनसे बदलना होगा।
- **[U2]** paper का "outperform" claim aggregate-average है या per-benchmark — design दोनों रिपोर्ट करता है, निर्णय-नियम section 4 में परिभाषित।
- **[U3]** कोई परिणाम नहीं बताया जा रहा — interpretation नियम ऊपर हैं (section 4), आँकड़े run होने पर ही मिलेंगे।

payload.answer:
PROPOSED APPROACH (design-only). Answer the zero-shot question "does FuseLLM outperform Llama-2 on CS?" with a controlled, matched-size, single-harness reproduction of the FuseLLM paper's zero-shot commonsense evaluation, then decide "outperform" primarily on the aggregate mean accuracy over a fixed CS sub-benchmark suite, with per-benchmark detail and optional item-level significance.

1) RECON RESULT (exact source materials): The workspace contains ONLY task.json; its track.md is a note ("Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required"), not source material. There is no FuseLLM code, no benchmark config, no checkpoints, no datasets, no harness anywhere on disk; Python has no torch/transformers/lm-eval; network is off. Therefore the design must be grounded in the public FuseLLM paper (arXiv:2310.06201) and standard zero-shot LM-eval conventions, and in the fixed requirement labels setup_2 / setup_9 (which are NOT defined in the workspace — see uncertainty U1).

2) DESIGN SKELETON:
- Model matrix (matched size, fused-vs-base): (A) FuseLLM-7B vs Llama-2-7B-hf; (B) FuseLLM-13B vs Llama-2-13B-hf. Compare ONLY within same size; never FuseLLM-7B vs Llama-2-13B. Optionally include OpenLLaMA-7B as a secondary source-model reference. Use the exact HF checkpoints the paper reports (fusellm/FuseLLM-7B, fusellm/FuseLLM-13B; meta-llama/Llama-2-*-hf), bf16/fp16, greedy decoding.
- Fixed CS sub-benchmark suite (candidate): HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-easy, PIQA, OpenBookQA, BoolQ, and (optionally) ARC-challenge and CommonsenseQA. A "primary set" of 6 (HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-e, PIQA, OpenBookQA, BoolQ) mirrored to the paper's Commonsense Reasoning group, plus a sensitivity analysis reporting what happens if ComonsenseQA/ARC-c are added or removed. This honors the question's listed candidates (HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-easy, PIQA, OpenBookQA, CommonsenseQA...) while flagging the set boundary as a decision point.
- Zero-shot protocol: EleutherAI lm-evaluation-harness (fixed commit), num_fewshot=0 on every CS task; multiple-choice log-likelihood ranking (choose highest-scoring option continuation); temperature=0/greedy (deterministic -> a single seed suffices for MC tasks; any non-MC task capped at max_new_tokens and also greedy); identical batch size, dtype, max context length, prompts/templates (harness defaults) for both models. No in-context examples, no CoT, no generation-time sampling.
- "Outperform" decision rule: PRIMARY = FuseLLM mean-CS accuracy minus Llama-2 mean-CS (same size) > 0, where mean = simple average over the fixed per-benchmark accuracies (not weighted by dataset size). SECONDARY = per-benchmark win/loss count and margin table. OPTIONAL = per-item stratified bootstrap 95% CI / paired difference test on mean CS (samples drawn within each benchmark then averaged) to quantify significance, since the 6-8 benchmark averages alone are too few for a meaningful paired test.

3) CONTROLS (what makes it a fair comparison): same harness version and task templates for both models; same hardware/dtype/batch; same max seq len; verify each model's tokenizer matches its evaluation setting; confirm dataset splits (HellaSwag/WinoGrande/ARC-e/PIQA/BoolQ on val, OpenBookQA on test, CSQA on dev); one run per model is deterministic (greedy), so no multi-seed averaging is required for MC zero-shot; note this explicitly.

COMPLETE EXPERIMENT DESIGN (design-only; nothing executed)

========================================================================
0. OBJECTIVE AND FIXED REQUIREMENTS
========================================================================
Question: "For commonsense evaluations, will FuseLLM outperform Llama-2 on standard benchmarks Commonsense (CS) (zero-shot)?"

Answer target: determine, under a controlled reproduction, whether a FuseLLM model strictly outperforms the same-size Llama-2 base model on a fixed zero-shot commonsense (CS) multiple-choice suite, using mean accuracy over a fixed six-benchmark suite as the primary decision statistic.

Fixed task-level requirements (taken as given, not modifiable):
- setup_2 and setup_9 (iclr2024/18013/1). Neither is defined in any file in /workspace (recon found only task.json, whose track.md is a note, not source). Per explicit instruction they are treated as fixed requirements and mapped to the paper's two primary comparisons; this mapping is an EXPLICIT ASSUMPTION (A1), not a confirmed fact.
- No execution: this is a design-only task; any "checks" below are design-level verification steps, not claims of having run anything.

========================================================================
1. FIXED DESIGN CHOICES (as confirmed with the researcher)
========================================================================
(1) Matched-size comparison only, fused-vs-base within each size, exact HF checkpoint IDs from the paper:
   - Comparison A (7B):  fusellm/FuseLLM-7B  vs  meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf
   - Comparison B (13B): fusellm/FuseLLM-13B vs  meta-llama/Llama-2-13b-hf
   - Optional reference (not a decision input): openlm-research/open_llama_7b_v2 (OpenLLaMA-7B), the second fusion source, to contextualize where the gain comes from.
   - Cross-size comparisons (FuseLLM-7B vs Llama-2-13B) are explicitly OUT of scope.
(2) Primary CS suite of six (fixed): HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-easy, PIQA, OpenBookQA, BoolQ. Sensitivity analysis (Section 5) covers adding/removing ARC-challenge and CommonsenseQA.
(3) Single pinned version of EleutherAI lm-evaluation-harness (fixed git commit, pinned at install time), num_fewshot=0 on every task, multiple-choice log-likelihood ranking, greedy/deterministic decoding; identical dtype/batch/max-length/templates for both models.
(4) Decision rule: primary = (FuseLLM mean CS) - (Llama-2 mean CS) > 0 on simple mean over the fixed six; secondary = per-benchmark win/loss margin table; optional = per-item stratified bootstrap 95% CI / paired-difference inference.
(5) Controls: same harness commit; same hardware/dtype/batch/max-seqlen; fixed per-dataset splits (Section 3).

========================================================================
2. RATIONALE FOR THE KEY CHOICES
========================================================================
- Matched size, fused-vs-base: FuseLLM is produced by continuing from a Llama-2 base under a distribution-fusion objective; the paper's claim is that the fused model beats the base it started from at the same size. Across-size comparison would confound capacity with fusion effect.
- Multiple-choice log-likelihood ranking, not generation: all six CS tasks are closed-form multiple choice (choose one of 2-4 options). The standard protocol scores each option continuation under the model and takes the max; this avoids decoding variance and makes scoring fully deterministic.
- Greedy/deterministic single run is sufficient (one of the confirmed fixed choices; state why): with num_fewshot=0 and log-likelihood ranking, the score is a deterministic function of the frozen weights and the fixed template. There is no sampling, hence no seed-induced variance, so a single run is the full run; any residual nondeterminism (kernel/order) is numerical noise at <0.01 accuracy level and should be controlled by running both models in the same process/hardware. Dataset sampling (e.g., HellaSwag's internal subsetting) is fixed by the harness/dataset files, not by an eval seed.
- Simple (unweighted) mean over six as primary: this is the paper's and the field's convention ("average over commonsense benchmarks"); it treats each benchmark equally and matches how the original tables were aggregated. Weighting by item count is reported as a robustness note but not used as the decision statistic.
- Exact checkpoint IDs: the HF repos fusellm/FuseLLM-7B and fusellm/FuseLLM-13B are the paper-reported released weights; Llama-2-hf are the base checkpoints the fusion continues from.

========================================================================
3. EVALUATION PROTOCOL (exact specification)
========================================================================
Harness: EleutherAI lm-evaluation-harness, ONE pinned commit (commit hash recorded), run identically for all four models on the same host. Task names (v0.4.x canonical, to be verified at design-check time — Section 6):
   - hellaswag        (dataset split: validation; ~10,042 items; harness evaluates the LC subset ~6,653) | metric acc_norm (length-normalized)
   - winogrande       (validation; 1,267)                                                               | metric acc_norm
   - arc_easy         (validation; 2,376)                                                               | metric acc_norm
   - piqa             (validation; 1,838)                                                               | metric acc_norm
   - openbookqa       (test; 500)                                                                       | metric acc_norm
   - boolq            (validation; 3,270)                                                               | metric acc  (binary true/false; harness metric differs from 4-way MC)
   Sensitivity-only (not decision): arc_challenge (validation; 1,172), commonsense_qa (validation; 1,221).

Protocol for both models on every task — identical:
   - num_fewshot = 0 on every task (zero-shot by construction; no in-context exemplars, no demonstrations).
   - Scoring: multiple-choice log-likelihood ranking (max over option continuations), with identical normalization mode as the harness default for the metric reported (record acc_norm vs acc per task and keep metric constant across models).
   - Decoding: greedy (temperature=0) / no sampling; no generation is used for MC scoring; any harness-internal or optional open-ended task would cap max_new_tokens; for the six fixed MC tasks no max_new_tokens applies (log-likelihood only), but set a uniform max_seq_len (e.g., 2048) for all models.
   - dtype = same for all models (bf16 where supported, else fp16); batch size identical (set by harness batch arg, e.g., batch_size=8 per device for 7B, smaller for 13B — but identical between the two models within a size comparison); same prompt templates (harness defaults for each task, unchanged); same truncation/max-length policy.
   - Both models in a comparison run in the same environment session to hold numerical/hardware state constant.

========================================================================
4. ANALYSIS PLAN / DECISION RULE
========================================================================
For each size s in {7B, 13B} compute:
   mean_CS(FuseLLM_s) = (1/6) * sum over the six fixed tasks of task accuracy
   mean_CS(Llama2_s)  = same over the identical task set/splits/metrics
   delta_s = mean_CS(FuseLLM_s) - mean_CS(Llama2_s).

Decision (primary): "FuseLLM outperforms Llama-2 on CS (zero-shot)" = delta_s > 0 for the size under test. Report delta to 3 decimals; a strictly positive mean is the pass condition (the paper's claim is a strict improvement on the average).

Secondary evidence (always reported): per-benchmark table of accuracies for both models, win/loss/tie count across the six tasks, and margin per task; also report weighted-by-item-count mean as a robustness check.

Optional statistical layer (design includes it; whether it gates the answer is a stated choice):
   - Per-item stratified bootstrap: resample items within each benchmark (stratified so each benchmark contributes its same weight), recompute the six-benchmark mean for both models per resample; form a 95% CI on delta via the bootstrap percentile. Report CI and the proportion of resamples with delta>0 (a paired-difference probability). With only six benchmark means, a paired test over benchmark-level numbers has n=6 and is underpowered, so item-level stratified bootstrap is the appropriate significance instrument; it is OPTIONAL because the zero-shot deterministic protocol is not stochastic, and the field's standard is a point-average comparison without formal significance testing.
   - State clearly: the primary decision is the deterministic mean comparison; the bootstrap is reported as confidence quantification and does not change the decision rule.

========================================================================
5. SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS (confirmed fixed choice)
========================================================================
Report the full fixed-six result, then repeat the mean computation under:
   (a) +ARC-challenge (six -> seven: HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-e, ARC-c, PIQA, OBQA, BoolQ) — mirrors the LLaMA-paper "Commonsense Reasoning" group;
   (b) +CommonsenseQA (six -> seven, replacing none: add CSQA);
   (c) +ARC-challenge + CommonsenseQA (eight).
State in the writeup whether delta_s sign/magnitude is robust across (six, seven-a, seven-b, eight). This guards the U2 boundary uncertainty (which sub-benchmarks constitute CS) by showing the conclusion's stability rather than asserting one canonical list. The fixed decision rule uses the six; sensitivity informs interpretation only.

========================================================================
6. FEASIBILITY CHECKS (design-level; NOT carried out, NOT claims of execution)
========================================================================
Listed steps that a real run must pass before trusting scores; each is a verification, not an experiment:
   (a) Harness task-name resolution: install pinned lm-eval, run `lm_eval --tasks hellaswag,winogrande,arc_easy,piqa,openbookqa,boolq ... --show_config`-style listing to confirm all six (plus arc_challenge, commonsense_qa) resolve to the intended tasks and report the intended metric (acc_norm/acc). Record the exact commit+task config as an artifact.
   (b) Split verification: confirm harness loads HellaSwag/WinoGrande/ARC-e/PIQA/BoolQ from validation, OpenBookQA from test, and confirm item counts approximately equal the values in Section 3 (they change with dataset version; record the versions). Mismatched splits would invalidate cross-model comparisons — both models must use identical splits.
   (c) Checkpoint correspondence: verify each HF repo ID resolves to the paper's released weights (FuseLLM-7B/13B from fusellm/*; Llama-2-7b/13b-hf from meta-llama/*), confirm config params/arch (7B: 32 layers/hidden 4096; 13B: 40 layers/hidden 5120), and confirm FuseLLM-13B's fusion source combination as reported in the paper (assumption A2: Llama-2-13B + OpenLLaMA-7B). If any checkpoint is unavailable (e.g., due to gated access/license), note it as a blocker in the writeup rather than substituting another model.
   (d) Determinism sanity: run a single model on a small task twice (same commit, same host) and confirm identical scores (to recorded precision) before the full matrix; this validates the "one deterministic run suffices" claim on the actual environment.
   (e) Resource budget estimate for the run (design note): ~15k log-likelihood items for the six-task suite per model; 4 models -> ~60k item evaluations; 7B/13B GPU or CPU inference with bf16. Record batch size and wall-clock expectation in the run card, but this is design context, not a result.

========================================================================
7. ASSUMPTIONS (explicit) vs FIXED REQUIREMENTS
========================================================================
Fixed (given, not open to change): setup_2 and setup_9 as task requirements; matched-size-only; six-benchmark primary suite; single pinned harness + num_fewshot=0 + log-likelihood ranking + greedy; mean>0 as primary decision rule; controls in Section 3/5; design-only (no execution).
Assumptions (my reading, to be re-confirmed only if new source appears):
   A1. setup_2 / setup_9 map to the paper's two primary zero-shot CS comparisons — FuseLLM-7B vs Llama-2-7B (setup_2) and FuseLLM-13B vs Llama-2-13B (setup_9). Not verifiable from the workspace; labelled per instruction as assumption, not fact.
   A2. FuseLLM identity and fusion sources as in arXiv:2310.06201 (FuseLLM-7B = Llama-2-7B + OpenLLaMA-7B; FuseLLM-13B = Llama-2-13B + OpenLLaMA-7B), and the 'Llama-2' comparator is the corresponding meta-llama/Llama-2-<size>-hf checkpoint.
   A3. The released HF checkpoints (fusellm/FuseLLM-7B, fusellm/FuseLLM-13B) are the faithful, paper-matched artifacts; no re-training is performed in this design.
   A4. CS = the six fixed multiple-choice commonsense benchmarks with the specified splits as the operative definition; the question's listed candidates are satisfied by this set, and boundary membership (BoolQ, ARC-c, CSQA) is handled by sensitivity analysis.
   A5. Zero-shot = zero in-context demonstrations via num_fewshot=0; 'standard benchmarks' refers to the released datasets as consumed by the pinned harness.

========================================================================
8. UNCERTAINTIES (do not block the locked design)
========================================================================
   U1. Exact content of setup_2/setup_9 is not present in the workspace (recon: only task.json). Binding rests on A1; if any file specifying them ever appears, A1 must be reconciled with it before the design is re-locked. Per instruction, A1 stands as the explicit working mapping.
   U2. CS sub-benchmark boundary (BoolQ/ARC-c/CSQA membership) — mitigated by the fixed-six primary rule + Section 5 sensitivity, so the answer is robust to this uncertainty.
   U3. Harness-version effects: different lm-eval commits change task names/metrics/num-fewshot defaults; fixed by pinning a single commit and recording its config (Section 6a).
   U4. Checkpoint availability/access: network is disabled in THIS sandbox, so nothing can be downloaded here; the design assumes the run would occur in a networked env with HF access. Documented as a blocker to flag, not a design change.
   U5. Whether 'outperform' must be formal-significance-gated for the task owner; design answers with deterministic mean>0 primary + per-benchmark secondary + optional bootstrap, and states which layer is decisive.

========================================================================
9. DELIVERABLE ARTIFACTS OF THE DESIGN (what a real run would produce)
========================================================================
(a) run card: harness commit, task list with split+counts+metric, model IDs, dtype, batch, seed policy (none needed - deterministic, justified in Section 2), date/host;
(b) per-model x per-task accuracy table (six + two sensitivity tasks) for all four models;
(c) delta_s for 7B and 13B on the fixed six with robustness across sensitivity variants;
(d) optional: stratified bootstrap CI on delta_s and P(delta>0);
(e) verdict per size using the primary rule, with the A1/A2 assumptions restated in the caption.

No experiment has been run; this is the complete locked design awaiting execution in an appropriate environment.

PLAN — Estructura del diseño experimental (sin diseño final completo, sin resultados inventados)

OBJETIVO
Responder SI/NO + cuánto: “¿El modelo fusionado FuseLLM supera a Llama-2, del mismo tamaño, en el benchmark de sentido común (CS) en zero-shot?”. Se define: (i) una comparación primaria, (ii) controles rigurosos, (iii) un plan de análisis con criterio pre-registrado de “supera”, y (iv) una evaluación de factibilidad.

COMPARACIÓN (estructura del experimento)
