DISEÑO EXPERIMENTAL COMPLETO (diseño-sólo; especifica el experimento tal como un tercero lo replicaría. No se ejecutó nada ni se reportan resultados.)

============================================================
1. OBJETIVO Y PREGUNTA OPERACIONALIZADA
============================================================
Pregunta del brief: "For commonsense evaluations, will FuseLLM outperform Llama-2 on standard benchmarks Commonsense (CS) (zero-shot)?"

Operacionalización (decisión binaria pre-registrada):
¿La accuracy promedio de FuseLLM-7B en el benchmark estándar de sentido común (7 tareas, zero-shot) es mayor que la de Llama-2-7B, bajo protocolo de evaluación idéntico y controlado?
- Variable de resultado primaria: Δ = mean_CS(FuseLLM-7B) − mean_CS(Llama-2-7B), donde mean_CS = promedio aritmético de la accuracy de las 7 tareas.
- Variable de resultado complementaria: vector de diferencias por tarea y test pareado a nivel de ítem.
- Unidades: ítems de los test sets estándar; n de tareas = 7 (agrupación de la media agregada).

Criterio de decisión pre-registrado (se escribe ANTES de correr):
"FuseLLM supera a Llama-2-7B en CS zero-shot" ⇔ se cumplen TODAS:
  (i)   Δ > 0;
  (ii)  FuseLLM-7B ≥ Llama-2-7B en al menos 5 de 7 tareas (mayoría no-negativa, de las cuales al menos 4 estrictamente positivas);
  (iii) el IC de bootstrap por ítem (90%) de Δ no contiene 0, O, si el poder no alcanza para (iii), el test de permutación por ítem sobre la media combinada da p ≤ 0.10 como criterio de robustez.
Resultado posible adicional: "evidencia insuficiente" (Δ>0 pero sin pasar (ii)/(iii)); esto NO cuenta como "supera".

============================================================
2. COMPARACIONES
============================================================
Primaria (responde la pregunta): FuseLLM-7B vs Llama-2-7B.
- Justificación de justicia: mismo tamaño (7B), misma arquitectura (Llama-2-7B) y misma inicialización — FuseLLM-7B es Llama-2-7B entrenado por fusión profunda. Es la comparación canónica del paper FuseLLM (ICLR 2024 / 18013) y elimina factores de tamaño/arquitectura.

Secundarias (contexto, no decisoras):
- Llama-2-13B: ancla de mayor capacity; permite situar "cuánto" sube FuseLLM-7B (p. ej. acercarse a 13B).
- OpenLLaMA-7B y MPT-7B (las otras dos fuentes): aislamiento del efecto. Si FuseLLM-7B > cada fuente y > Llama-2-7B, el efecto es atribuible a la fusión y no a que una fuente ya fuera mejor.
- Se reportan las 5 columnas (FuseLLM-7B, Llama-2-7B, Llama-2-13B, OpenLLaMA-7B, MPT-7B) en la misma tabla, mismas tareas/prompts.

============================================================
3. BENCHMARK CS Y AGREGACIÓN
============================================================
Tareas (set estándar de 7 usado para "Commonsense Reasoning" en el paper; supuesto A3):
1) HellaSwag (val, ~10K), 2) PIQA (~1.8K), 3) OpenBookQA (test, ~500), 4) ARC-Challenge (test, ~1.2K), 5) WinoGrande (val, ~1.3K), 6) SIQA (val, ~1.9K), 7) CommonsenseQA (CSQA, test, ~1.2K).
- Identificación por nombre canónico en la librería de evaluación (p. ej. hellaswag, piqa, openbookqa, arc_challenge, winogrande, siqa, commonsense_qa), con revisión de datos (revisions) fijadas (supuesto A4) para que los splits no varíen.
- Métrica por tarea: accuracy (promedio de aciertos sobre la tarea).
- Agregación principal: media aritmética simple de las 7 accuracies (mean_CS). Se reportan además: mediana, min–max, y la tabla por tarea con la diferencia por tarea.
- Elección: media simple (no ponderada por tamaño) = mismo criterio que el paper; se documenta para que un tercero pueda recalcular.

============================================================
4. PROTOCOLO ZERO-SHOT EXACTO (supuesto A4)
============================================================
- Harness: EleutherAI lm-evaluation-harness, versión pínneada a un commit exacto (se registra el commit SHA en el reporte; uso de cualquier actualización posterior queda prohibido).
- Formato: prompts por defecto de cada tarea del harness con num_fewshot=0 (sin ejemplos few-shot; zero-shot estricto). No se escriben prompts custom para no introducir sesgo por el autor.
- Selección de respuesta: choice-scoring por log-likelihood — se calcula logprob de cada candidato bajo el modelo y se elige el de mayor logprob (no generación libre, no sampling). Esto vuelve la evaluación determinística.
- Generación/aleatoriedad: al ser por logits, no hay temperatura; seed fijo (17) por si el harness usa cualquier RNG; corridas adicionales con 42 y 2024 solo si hubiera muestreo.
- Precisión: carga en BF16 (fp16 permitido si la GPU no soporta bf16) para AMBOS modelos; mismo máximo de secuencia y mismo tokenizador (Llama-2 tokenizer para FuseLLM-7B y Llama-2-7B; tokenizer nativo para MPT/OpenLLaMA).
- Inferencia: batch size fijo por hardware; max_length consistente (p. ej. 2048) para los dos modelos de interés.

============================================================
5. CONTROLES
============================================================
C1. Protocolo idéntico: mismo harness/commit, prompts, seed, precisión, hardware y splits para todos los modelos; correr ambos modelos en el mismo nodo/interleave para mitigar deriva térmica/placement.
C2. Fuga/contaminación: screening del corpus de entrenamiento de fusión contra los test sets de CS:
   - coincidencia exacta de secuencias (normalizadas) y solapamiento de n-gramas de token (p. ej. 8–13-gram, Jaccard/containment, hashes MinHash).
   - Reportar tasa de solapamiento por tarea. Si > umbral (p. ej. >0.5% de ítems con solapamiento ≥40%), re-evaluar excluyendo esos ítems y reportar ambos escenarios. Aclarar que los corpus de pre-entrenamiento de las sources quedan fuera de nuestro control (riesgo inherente, documentado).
C3. Checkpoint: regla pre-registrada, fija (p. ej. 1 epoch / número fijo de pasos con LR fijo); se guarda y evalúa SOLO el checkpoint final, sin seleccionar el mejor por validación. Si se usan pesos publicados por los autores, se usan tal cual, sin selección.
C4. Determinismo: fijar seeds (17/42/2024) y reportar cualquier componente estocástico; reportar mediana/rango de las corridas si la hay.
C5. Pre-registro del criterio de decisión (sección 1) y del plan de análisis (sección 6) antes de ver resultados.
C6. Almacenamiento de predicciones por ítem (JSONL) para ambos modelos de interés → permite reanálisis (McNemar, permutación, bootstrap por ítem) por terceros.

============================================================
6. PLAN DE ANÁLISIS
============================================================
A. Descriptivos: tabla de accuracy por tarea (5 modelos) + mean_CS + Δ por tarea.
B. Inferencia primaria (pareada por ítem, porque ambos modelos ven exactamente los mismos ítems):
   1. Bootstrap de dos niveles sobre Δ: muestrear ítems dentro de cada tarea y re-combinar, B=10,000; IC 90% (percentil) y p bootstrap.
   2. Test de permutación combinado: permutar las etiquetas de modelo por ítem dentro de cada tarea (10,000 permutaciones) sobre la media agregada → p global.
   3. McNemar por tarea (tabla 2×2 de aciertos pareados) como robustez por tarea; se reporta cuántas tareas dan p<0.05.
C. Reporte de tamaño de efecto: diferencia de proporciones agregada con IC; Cohen's h por tarea.
D. Potencia/limitación declarada: varias tareas son chicas (OBQA ~500, ARC-c ~1.2K, CSQA ~1.2K); el test global combinado tiene mucho mayor poder que tests por tarea — por eso (ii) es "mayoría" y no "todas las tareas significativas". Advertir que un efecto chico del orden de 1 punto porcentual puede exigir n grande; el criterio (iii) puede no pasar aun con Δ>0 → resultado "evidencia insuficiente" es un desenlace válido y honesto.
E. Artefacto final: tabla principal, Δ con IC, reporte de contaminación, decisiones (i)/(ii)/(iii) y veredicto conforme a la regla pre-registrada.

============================================================
7. FACTIBILIDAD, RECURSOS Y PASOS REPRODUCIBLES
============================================================
Alcance: diseño-sólo; aquí NO se corre nada. El ambiente (sin red, sin GPU, sin datasets) impide la ejecución; el diseño especifica todo para un tercero.

Software (versiones sugeridas a fijar): Python 3.10+; torch ≥ 2.1; transformers; accelerate; numpy/scipy; lm-evaluation-harness (commit SHA fijado); git para pinning. Se escriben requirements con hashes.

Hardware (estimación conceptual): 
- Evaluación: 7 tareas × 5 modelos = pocas GPU-horas con A100/H100 (inferencia BF16).
- Entrenamiento de fusión (solo si no se usan pesos publicados): corpus ~220K frases; 3 fuentes 7B + target 7B con alineación KL (token + secuencia). Memoria del orden de ~60-80 GB (4 modelos bf16 + optimizer Adam fp16); ~8×A100 80G, tiempo del orden de horas-1 día (el corpus es chico). Se especifica la schedule con pasos totales, batch y LR fijados y justificados por el paper (supuesto A1/A5).

Pasos:
1) Fijar repos/commits: pesos (HuggingFace con revisiones) y harness.
2) Construir/verificar corpus de fusión (si re-entrenamiento): muestrear ~220K frases de las fuentes del paper (C4, RedPajama, PILE, p. ej.), guardar hashes del corpus.
3) Screening de contaminación del corpus vs 7 test sets (C2) → guardar reporte.
4) Entrenar fusión con regla de checkpoint fija (C3) → guardar SOLO el checkpoint final.
5) Correr lm-eval zero-shot (num_fewshot=0, semilla 17) en los 5 modelos, mismo nodo/precisión (C1/C4); guardar JSONL por ítem (C6).
6) Correr script de análisis (fijo): descriptivos, bootstrap 2 niveles, permutación, McNemar, veredicto por la regla de la sección 1.
7) Emitir reporte con: tabla, Δ+IC, contaminación, versiones/commits, semillas, veredicto.

Checks factibles sin cómputo pesado (validaciones de diseño):
- Smoke test de harness: cargar cada tarea con 10 ítems y confirmar que los prompts/formatos son los canónicos y consistentes entre modelos.
- Verificación del script de contaminación sobre un submuestreo chico.
- Verificación de que FuseLLM-7B y Llama-2-7B comparten tokenizador/config.
- Chequeo de splits (mismas revisiones de datasets) entre corridas.

============================================================
8. SUPUESTOS (NO FIJADOS POR EL BRIEF — EXPLÍCITOS)
============================================================
A1. Variante FuseLLM = "FuseLLM: Fusing Large Language Models through Deep Fusion" (ICLR 2024, submission 18013): fusión profunda de 3 fuentes de 7B (Llama-2-7B, OpenLLaMA-7B, MPT-7B) por alineación de distribuciones (loss a nivel token y secuencia), inicializado en Llama-2-7B ⇒ FuseLLM-7B.
A2. "Llama-2" en la pregunta = Llama-2-7B (comparación justa por tamaño/arquitectura/inicialización); 13B solo como ancla.
A3. Benchmark CS = el grupo de 7 tareas (HellaSwag, PIQA, OpenBookQA, ARC-c, WinoGrande, SIQA, CSQA) con promedio aritmético.
A4. Protocolo zero-shot = prompts por defecto de lm-eval (commit fijado), num_fewshot=0, elección por logprob, BF16, seed fija.
A5. Datos de fusión = corpus del paper (~220K frases de C4/RedPajama/PILE); si los pesos publicados de FuseLLM-7B están accesibles, se usan directamente (ver A6).
A6. Disponibilidad de pesos/corpus/harness: se asume accesibles por un tercero con red; el diseño no puede descargarlos.
A7. Es tarea de diseño: el entregable es la especificación; no se ejecuta ni se reportan resultados acá.
A8. El poder estadístico puede ser bajo para efectos pequeños; se acepta "evidencia insuficiente" como veredicto válido.

Nota de motivación (dato del paper, NO resultado de este experimento): el paper FuseLLM reporta a FuseLLM-7B por encima del promedio de Llama-2-7B en el grupo de sentido común zero-shot; esto justifica la comparación primaria elegida, pero el experimento se diseña para verificar esa afirmación con controles propios.

## 0. 任务定位与资料状态【已确认设定】
- setup_2 的固定要求：在**零样本**场景下，于 Common Sense(CS) 基准上评估 FuseLLM 是否**优于** Llama-2；setup_9 的对象为 **FuseLLM**。
- 资料状态：/workspace 仅含 task.json，无 FuseLLM 配置、评估脚本、Llama-2 基线设定或 CS 任务清单；track.md 不存在，断网、无 GPU。因此 CS 任务清单、模型规模、提示措辞等在资料中不存在，一律作【假设】处理（见 §10），不视为事实。

## 1. 已确认设定（研究者确认，作为设计固定口径，非事实陈述）
1. **规模对比**：FuseLLM-7B（论文发布的融合 checkpoint）对 Llama-2-7B（meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf，base 非 chat）；OpenLLaMA-7B 作为额外源模型对照。
2. **CS 基准 = 标准 7 任务常识推理组**：HellaSwag、WinoGrande、PIQA、ARC-easy、ARC-challenge、OpenBookQA、BoolQ；指标按 lm-eval 惯例（acc_norm / acc）；**宏平均为主指标、逐任务明细为辅**。
3. **零样本** = 无 in-context 示例，采用单一锁定的 lm-eval-harness 版本默认模板；两模型完全同协议。
4. **两条模型均由我方在同一协议下实测比较**；论文公开数值仅作数量级健全性锚点。
5. **「优于」判定规则预先声明**：主指标宏平均差值 Δ>0 **且**多数任务方向一致（≥5/7）；bootstrap 95% CI 与配对检验为辅助证据。
6. **数据分割**用各基准标准评测分割（由 harness 内置）。
7. **环境无 GPU、断网、仅设计任务**：方案中注明执行阶段需要 GPU；本任务不实际运行。

## 2. 研究问题操作化
- **估量（estimand）**：Δ = mean_{t∈CS7} Acc(FuseLLM-7B, t) − mean_{t∈CS7} Acc(Llama-2-7B, t)，其中 Acc 为各任务在固定零样本协议下的标准指标（见 §4）。
- **假设检验（预先登记）**：H0: Δ≤0 对 H1: Δ>0（单侧）；同时在 7 任务层面记录每任务方向。
- 因 FuseLLM-7B 由 Llama-2-7B 与 OpenLLaMA-7B 融合而来，两条对比对象**共享大量领域信息**，故在统计上按“以任务为配对单元”的配对比较处理，而非独立样本比较。

## 3. 对照设定
- **处理组**：FuseLLM-7B（发布 checkpoint；HF 仓库确切 id/commit 于执行时记录，见 A4）。
- **基线组**：Llama-2-7B（meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf，base）。
- **额外对照（源模型）**：OpenLLaMA-7B——用于检验“融合相对两个源模型均提升”，并作为协议一致性对照（其得分应落在两模型之间或附近，若异常则提示协议问题）。
- **公平性要求（强制相同协议）**：同一 harness/版本、同一提示模板、同一解码参数、同一 dtype、同一 batch、同一 seed；任何差异须记录并作为限制说明。

## 4. 评估指标与协议细节
- **Harness**【已确认设定+假设】采用 EleutherAI lm-evaluation-harness；【假设】pin 到具体版本（建议发布 tag，如 v0.4.x，执行时记录 commit hash），以杜绝不同版本导致的提示/指标实现差异。
- **任务·数据分割·指标**（标准公共数据，数量为近似值，执行时以 harness 下载版本核对）：
  - HellaSwag：validation（≈10,042）· acc_norm
  - WinoGrande：validation（≈1,267）· acc
  - PIQA：validation（≈1,838）· acc_norm
  - ARC-easy：validation（≈2,376）· acc_norm
  - ARC-challenge：validation（≈1,172）· acc_norm
  - OpenBookQA：test（≈500）· acc_norm
  - BoolQ：validation（≈3,270）· acc
- **零样本**：num_fewshot=0；使用 harness 各任务默认模板【假设：确切措辞以所选 harness 版本为准】。
- **解码**：贪心（argmax，temperature 0，无采样；MC 任务用 lm-eval 默认）；max_new_tokens 统一（如 32，足以覆盖选项/Yes-No；BoolQ 只需 yes/no 判断）。
- **精度与版本**：dtype 统一 fp16（若硬件支持则 bf16）；torch/transformers 版本 pin 并记录；两模型用各自 tokenizer（如 lm-eval 默认）。

## 5. 随机性与可复现性控制
- 上述 MC/QA 任务在贪心解码下**近似确定性**；仍执行：
  1. 固定并记录全部随机种子（python/numpy/torch/random）。
  2. 每模型×任务重复 R=3 次（同一配置）验证确定性：报告均值与离散度（预期 0 方差；若出现非零则记录、诊断）。
  3. 【可选健全性】对选项顺序做多重 seed 扰动（ARC/OpenBookQA/PIQA/HellaSwag 若 harness 支持），检验对选项次序的敏感性。
  4. 记录模型仓库 commit sha、harness/torch/transformers 版本与补丁、硬件与 batch 信息。
  5. 同一批评估在同一环境会话内串行完成，避免并发引入差异。

## 6. 预设判定规则（pre-registered，不可事后修改）
- **主指标**：Δ（7 任务宏平均差值，FuseLLM − Llama-2）。
- **判定 FuseLLM 优于 Llama-2 需同时满足**：
  (a) Δ > 0；
  (b) 7 任务中 ≥5 个任务方向为正（简单多数一致）。
- **辅助证据**（不影响头条结论，仅作佐证与区间描述）：
  - Δ 的 bootstrap 95% CI（以任务为抽样单元，10,000 次），报告 CI 是否排除 0；
  - Wilcoxon signed-rank / paired t（n=7，功效低，仅作描述性提示，不作唯一判定依据）；
  - 每任务差异（百分点）与效应量。
- **边际情形**：若 Δ 接近 0（预声明容差，如 |Δ|<0.1pp），结论表述为“无充分证据显示优于/大致持平”，不作“优于”结论；避免过读。
- 所有规则先行声明，防止按结果挑任务/挑口径。

## 7. 结果分析方法
- 输出逐模型×逐任务准确率表（含 R=3 均值）、每任务 Δ、宏平均 Δ、bootstrap CI、方向一致性计数、配对检验 p 值。
- 敏感性：报告 (i) 完整 7 任务宏平均；(ii) 若移除任单个任务后判定是否翻转（识别“摇摆任务”）；(iii) macro 与加权平均（若需）对照。
- 一致性检查（数量级锚点）：若我方 Llama-2-7B 或 FuseLLM-7B 的 CS 数值与论文公开值偏差超过 ~2–3pp，则标记协议配置问题并排查，但**不以论文数值作为判定真值**。

## 8. 健全性检验
1. **协议再现锚点**：同协议重跑后，我方数值与论文公开数值数量级一致（±2–3pp 内）。
2. **确定性**：R=3 重复稳定。
3. **源模型对照**：OpenLLaMA-7B 得分与已知分布一致、且 FuseLLM-7B 相对两个源模型均不下降（可接受为“融合不劣于源模型”的支撑）。
4. **零样本泄漏规避**：确认全部任务 num_fewshot=0、无 in-context 示例，无训练/验证泄漏（使用标准评测分割）。
5. **选项顺序扰动**（可选）稳定。

## 9. 可行性说明（计算量估算与所需资源）
- 规模：7 任务合计约 ≈20K 条短序列（见 §4 近似值，执行时以实际下载版本核对）。
- 计算量：7B 模型推理 FLOPs≈2×N×tokens；每条序列约 50–100 tokens，全程约 1–2M tokens/模型/全套任务。单张现代 GPU（如 A100-40/80GB，或 2×24GB 消费级）上，贪心生成可在**数小时内**完成全套 3 模型×7 任务×R 次；无训练开销。
- 显存：7B @ fp16≈14GB 权重+KV cache，单卡 24GB 可容纳；Llama-2-7b-hf / OpenLLaMA-7B / FuseLLM-7B 相同，统一 bf16（若支持）。
- CPU-only 不可行（数十小时~数天），故**执行阶段需 GPU**——仅为执行前提，不影响本设计交付。
- 软件依赖：pin 的 lm-eval-harness + transformers + torch（执行阶段需联网安装；本环境断网，故仅在文档中注明）。
- 交付物：环境锁文件、评估运行脚本（runner）、任务配置 yaml、结果 CSV、分析 Notebook、含判定规则的预登记文件。

## 10. 假设清单与后果
- A1【假设】CS=上述 7 任务组。后果：若 CS 实为其他子集，绝对/相对结论可能变化；因逐任务结果全部输出，可随时在任意子集上重算宏平均。
- A2【已确认设定】规模=7B 对 7B。后果：结论限定 7B 口径，不推广至 13B/70B。
- A3【假设】零样本措辞=所选 lm-eval 版本默认模板。后果：不同措辞影响绝对值，可能微调 Δ；因两模型同模板+配对比较+数量级锚点，影响被大幅对冲。
- A4【假设】FuseLLM-7B 确切 checkpoint（HF 仓库 id/commit）待执行时确认并记录 sha。
- A5【假设】harness 具体版本待执行时 pin 并记录。
- A6【假设】数据分割/版本由 harness 内置，执行时记录。
- A7【已确认设定】两模型均由我方同协议实测；论文数值仅作锚点。
- 后果总述：提示/评测层面的**系统偏差对两模型近似同向**，配对的任务级比较使判定对这类共同偏差较稳健；最大不确定来源是 A1（任务清单）与 A3（提示措辞），均已通过完整逐任务输出+锚点检验缓解。

## 11. 明确不做的事
- 不引用任何“已运行的实验结果”；不虚构数值；本设计仅规定协议、判定规则与分析方法，供未来有 GPU/联网时执行。

payload.answer:
## Proposed approach outline (plan stage)

**1. Reframe the question as a falsifiable comparison.** The experiment tests whether FuseLLM (7B-class, fused checkpoint) achieves higher zero-shot accuracy than Llama-2 on standard commonsense-reasoning (CS) benchmarks. Deliverable = a pre-registered design: hypothesis, arms, benchmark set, fixed protocol, metric, controls, analysis, decision rule. No execution.

**2. Model arms (treatment vs. baseline).**
- Treatment: FuseLLM-7B fused checkpoint, defined per the FuseLLM (ICLR 2024, paper #18013) recipe — Llama-2-7B backbone structure fused with OpenLLaMA-7B and Mistral-7B teachers via probability-matrix (knowledge) fusion on a large text corpus.
- Baseline: Llama-2-7B (base/pretrained, non-chat), matched to FuseLLM backbone (same architecture/family/size/tokenizer) so the fused vs. unfused contrast is clean.
- Optional reference arms for context: OpenLLaMA-7B and Mistral-7B (teacher models), and/or Llama-2-7B-chat (secondary, explicitly not the primary baseline).

**3. Benchmark suite + zero-shot protocol.** Standard CS suite (proposed default set, confirm against source): HellaSwag, PIQA, Winogrande, OpenBookQA, ARC-easy, ARC-challenge, BoolQ, SocialIQA, COPA. All evaluated zero-shot with the same prompt template and scoring rule across both arms; generation greedy (temperature 0), per-task consistent max_new_tokens; one eval harness version pinned for both models.

**4. Metrics.** Per-task accuracy; primary outcome = macro-average accuracy across the CS suite; per-task breakdown table; secondary = number of tasks where FuseLLM ≥ Llama-2 and pooled item accuracy.

**5. Controls (design-only commitments).** Identical harness/prompt/decoding/config for both arms; pinned checkpoint identifiers and file hashes; single evaluation code path; record per-item correctness to support item-level uncertainty; pre-register primary metric and decision rule before analyzing; handle ties/malformed outputs explicitly.

**6. Analysis plan.** (a) descriptive per-task table; (b) primary inference: macro-average accuracy difference with 95% bootstrap CI over items/tasks plus a paired test (e.g., McNemar-style per task or paired permutation on items; sensitivity with t-test over task means); (c) robustness: 5-shot/few-shot contrast as secondary if the source protocol is only 0-shot; teacher arms to contextualize; (d) explicit "outperform" decision rule, e.g., FuseLLM − Llama-2 > 0 with CI excluding 0 at α=0.05 and materially positive effect; state both.

**7. Feasibility & resource envelope.** Design-only — no run required; if executed: CPU-only (224 cores, large host RAM ~1.9TB visible, no GPU, 39GB free disk), network disabled, no ML packages preinstalled (would need offline install). A full 7B eager eval over ~9 CS tasks on CPU is tractable but slow; 39GB disk is marginal for two ~13.5GB checkpoints — a stated constraint, not a blocker for the design.

Filesystem scan found no track.md, no ICLR/FuseLLM/Llama materials, no HF cache anywhere (find over /). Environment: Python 3.14.4; NO ML packages installed (pip list shows no torch/transformers/datasets/lm-eval-harness/accelerate); network disabled (HTTPS to huggingface.co times out); no GPU (nvidia-smi absent); 224 CPUs; host RAM ~1.9TB visible; /workspace is an NFS mount with ~39GB free (98% used). /home,/dev,/etc contain no data mounts or model/dataset env vars. Conclusion: nothing source-supported is physically present — the design must be built from domain knowledge of FuseLLM (ICLR'24) plus the fixed requirements in the question, with protocol details flagged for researcher confirmation via topics iclr2024/18013/1:setup_2 and setup_9.
assumptions: Baseline Llama-2 variant = Llama-2-7B base (non-chat), since FuseLLM is a 7B-class fused model built on a Llama-2-7B backbone; to be confirmed.
FuseLLM checkpoint = the official released FuseLLM-7B fused checkpoint (teachers OpenLLaMA-7B + Mistral-7B, Llama-2-7B backbone, per ICLR'24 paper #18013), used as-is rather than re-fused locally.

'CommenSense(CS)' refers to a standard commonsense-reasoning benchmark suite evaluated zero-shot (proposed default: HellaSwag, PIQA, Winogrande, OpenBookQA, ARC-easy, ARC-challenge, BoolQ, SocialIQA, COPA), matching the source setup if it defines an exact list.
Zero-shot protocol = lm-eval-harness-style fixed prompts, greedy decoding, per-task max_new_tokens, no few-shot examples; to be confirmed against source setup_2/setup_9.
Primary metric = macro-average accuracy across CS tasks; 'outperform' decided by a pre-registered statistical rule (CI excluding 0 at alpha=0.05) rather than raw point estimate alone.
Software approach = pin one eval harness version and identical configuration across both arms; offline install if execution ever happens.
Design can add teacher/Llama-2-chat arms and a few-shot secondary analysis provided the primary comparison stays 0-shot CS FuseLLM vs Llama-2.
uncertainties: Exact definition and composition of the 'CommenSense(CS)' benchmark set in the source materials (topics iclr2024/18013/1:setup_2 and iclr2024/18013/1:setup_9) — which tasks, how many, and the precise zero-shot prompt/eval protocol as defined by the source.
Whether the intended baseline is Llama-2-7B base, Llama-2-13B, or a chat variant; FuseLLM in the paper is 7B-class, so 7B base is the working default.
Whether the official FuseLLM checkpoint is available/expected or whether the design must specify local re-fusion (teacher set, fusion ratio, corpus size) — affects reproducibility and resource needs.
Whether 'outperform' must be a statistical claim (CI/significance) or a directional claim on reported numbers; the design will make the decision rule explicit either way.

Whether the source protocol permits any secondary arms (few-shot, chat variant, teachers) or requires strict 0-shot CS FuseLLM-vs-Llama-2 only; I default to permissive secondary arms, primary stays strict.
Resource ceiling for any hypothetical execution (CPU-only, 39GB disk) is tight for two 7B checkpoints; design treats this as a constraint note, not a blocker.

payload.answer:
# Experiment Design — Does FuseLLM outperform Llama-2 on Commonsense (CS) benchmarks at zero-shot?

## 0. Fixed requirements (approved facts — NOT assumptions)
- **F1 — Arms:** the comparison must be FuseLLM vs Llama-2 (both a FuseLLM treatment arm and a Llama-2 baseline arm are mandatory).
- **F2 — Domain:** commonsense evaluation on "standard benchmarks CommenSense (CS)".
- **F3 — Protocol:** zero-shot (no in-context demonstrations).
- **F4 — Deliverable:** design-only. No experiment may be executed and **no claim that an experiment was run** may be made. Deliverable = design with rationale, arms, controls, analysis plan, and feasibility.
- **F5 — Source dependency:** source-supported setup details (ICLR 2024 paper #18013 / FuseLLM) may be clarified by topic (`setup_2`, `setup_9`), but **the workspace contains no source materials** (only `task.json`; no `track.md`, no papers, no checkpoints, no datasets). Protocol specifics therefore remain unconfirmed and are marked as working assumptions below, not as confirmed source facts.

## 1. Rationale and falsifiable hypothesis
FuseLLM (ICLR 2024) fuses the knowledge of same-scale teacher LLMs (OpenLLaMA-7B, Mistral-7B) into the architecture of a backbone (Llama-2-7B) via a learned "probability-matrix" soft-label objective during continual pretraining on a large text corpus. The paper reports gains over the backbone on several evaluation families. The open scientific question addressed here is whether that fusion benefit persists in the **zero-shot commonsense-reasoning regime** — a stricter generalization test because there are no in-context examples to anchor or demonstrate the task.

- H0 (null): FuseLLM-7B zero-shot CS accuracy is not higher than Llama-2-7B's (population macro-average difference Δ ≤ 0).
- H1 (alternative): FuseLLM-7B zero-shot CS accuracy is higher (Δ > 0).
- This is a **pre-registered design**: hypotheses, metric, decision rule, and benchmark set are fixed *before* any numbers are examined; no post-hoc reselection of tasks or metrics is allowed.

## 2. Arms
**Primary arms (both mandatory, F1):**
- **Treatment — FuseLLM-7B.** Definition (provenance flagged, paper-recipe): fused checkpoint whose architecture/tokenizer = Llama-2-7B backbone; teachers = OpenLLaMA-7B and Mistral-7B; fusion performed via probability-matrix soft-label distillation over a large-scale text corpus (paper uses ~600K RefinedWeb samples), yielding a "FuseLLM" model roughly matching the backbone size. Preferred use: the official released FuseLLM-7B checkpoint, pinned by repo commit + checkpoint ID + SHA-256 hash. If unavailable offline, the design documents the exact re-fusion recipe (teacher set, corpus, epochs, LR) as a secondary provenance path.
- **Baseline — Llama-2-7B (base, pretrained, non-chat).** Matched to the FuseLLM backbone (same family, size, tokenizer) so the **fused-vs-unfused contrast is clean**; same hash pinning.

**Secondary arms (explicitly not part of the primary inference; for context only):**
- OpenLLaMA-7B and Mistral-7B — the teacher models, to contextualize the direction/magnitude of any gap.
- Llama-2-7B-chat — an instruction-tuned variant, useful sanity check but *not* the designated baseline.

## 3. CS benchmark composition and zero-shot protocol
**Working-assumption CS suite (9 standard tasks; must be flagged as assumption, not a confirmed source list):** HellaSwag, PIQA, Winogrande, OpenBookQA, ARC-easy, ARC-challenge, BoolQ, SocialIQA (SIQA), COPA. These are the widely used zero-shot commonsense-reasoning benchmarks in the lm-eval-harness family.

- **Substitution rule:** if the source topics (`setup_2`/`setup_9`) or researcher clarification define a different CS list, swap in that exact source list while keeping protocol, metrics, and analysis identical. The default 9-task list is used only to make the design concrete and executable today.
- **Prompt template:** lm-eval-harness-style task templates (choice-formatted contexts, no few-shot examples — zero demonstrations). For generation tasks, a fixed template with a task-appropriate cue. Identical template text for both arms; templates recorded in the design doc.
- **Decoding:** greedy (temp 0), no sampling seed dependence; per-task `max_new_tokens` set to cover the choice space (e.g., 1–8 tokens for fixed-choice tasks; sufficient budget for free-form tasks), equal for both models.
- **Scoring:** task-native metric from lm-eval-harness (e.g., normalized accuracy via log-prob over choices where the harness does so; exact-match for free-form), identical scorer for both arms; record **per-item correctness** (raw item id → prediction → correct/incorrect).
- **Data:** pin dataset names, splits (e.g., validation/held-out subsets), and versions; record per-task item counts. No training or tuning on these splits — zero-shot only (F3).

## 4. Controls
- **Single evaluation code path:** one pinned harness version (e.g., lm-eval-harness @ commit with recorded hash) and one config file used for every arm; both arms evaluated with the same Python environment and backend flags.
- **Checkpoint integrity:** each model pinned by repository/commit/checkpoint-ID/SHA-256; load path identical.
- **Identical prompts/decoding/scoring** across arms (see §3); task template and max_new_tokens fixed before evaluation.
- **Determinism:** greedy decoding; any residual backend nondeterminism documented via a re-run of one model on one small task (determinism sanity check), not a full re-run.
- **Data isolation:** no contamination checks required beyond using the standard held-out splits; no few-shot examples injected in the primary protocol (F3).
- **Output audit:** store complete per-item outputs; malformed/parse-failure outputs counted as incorrect and reported, not silently dropped.
- **Pre-registration artifact:** this design doc (metrics + decision rule) is the locked analysis specification; all results are written to a results manifest before interpretation.

## 5. Analysis plan
**Descriptive:** per-task table — task, item count n, accuracy(FuseLLM), accuracy(Llama-2), Δ, and per-task winner.

**Primary metric:** macro-average accuracy over the CS suite = mean of per-task accuracies (equal task weight), computed identically for both arms; Δ = macro(FuseLLM) − macro(Llama-2).

**Primary inference:**
- Two-stage bootstrap 95% CI on Δ: resample tasks (n=9) × resample items within tasks (per-task) to propagate both task-level and item-level variance.
- Paired per-task test: McNemar's test on the item level within each task (over the discordant pairs only).
- Overall paired permutation test on pooled items, stratified by task (FuseLLM/Llama-2 pairing preserved), H0 of no difference.
- Sensitivity check: paired (two-sided) t-test over the 9 per-task accuracies (df=8).

**Pre-registered "outperform" decision rule (fixed before running):** declare *FuseLLM outperforms Llama-2 on zero-shot CS* iff **all** hold:
1. point estimate Δ > 0;
2. 95% bootstrap CI on Δ excludes 0 **and** its lower bound ≥ +1.0 accuracy point (a materiality floor to avoid declaring statistically significant but trivially small differences);
3. McNemar (on at least the majority of tasks) and/or the stratified permutation test gives p < 0.05.
Otherwise the conclusion is *"no evidence that FuseLLM outperforms Llama-2 on zero-shot CS."* Both the point estimate and the interval are always reported; the conclusion is stated as a statistical claim, not a claim that any experiment was run.

**Secondary analyses (only if permitted under F3/source protocol):**
- 5-shot contrast on a representative subset (e.g., HellaSwag, Winogrande, OpenBookQA) to test sensitivity of the conclusion to the zero-shot protocol.
- Teacher arms (OpenLLaMA-7B, Mistral-7B) reported for context to locate FuseLLM relative to its teachers and backbone.

## 6. Feasibility and resource envelope (constraints, not blockers)
- **This deliverable requires no execution** (F4). Nothing here describes a run; results are prospective.
- If ever executed, the environment imposes: **CPU-only** (224 cores; `nvidia-smi` absent; no GPU), **network disabled** (HuggingFace unreachable → checkpoints/datasets must be materialized offline or preplaced), **no ML packages preinstalled** (no torch/transformers/lm-eval-harness/datasets in `pip list` → offline wheel installation required), and **~39GB free disk** on the /workspace NFS volume (97% used). Two ~13.5GB 7B checkpoints plus eval caches are marginal on that disk — a stated constraint; mitigations: bf16/quantized checkpoint loading, streaming dataset access, or a scratch volume with more headroom.
- Time bound: a 7B greedy CPU eval over ~9 tasks (~10–20k items total) is tractable with 224-core batching but will take many wall-clock hours; this is an operational note only and does not affect the design's validity.

## 7. Explicit list of assumptions (proposed choices, NOT confirmed facts)
1. CS suite = the 9-task list in §3 (HellaSwag, PIQA, Winogrande, OpenBookQA, ARC-easy/ARC-challenge, BoolQ, SIQA, COPA) — pending source confirmation (`setup_2`/`setup_9`).
2. Baseline = Llama-2-7B **base** (non-chat), matched to the FuseLLM backbone.
3. FuseLLM-7B = official released fused checkpoint (backbone Llama-2-7B; teachers OpenLLaMA-7B + Mistral-7B; probability-matrix fusion per paper); re-fusion documented only as fallback provenance.
4. Zero-shot protocol = lm-eval-harness-style fixed templates, greedy decoding, per-task max_new_tokens, no demonstrations.
5. Primary metric = macro-average accuracy across the CS suite; "outperform" per the §5 decision rule.
6. Secondary arms (teachers, chat, 5-shot) permissible provided the primary stays strict 0-shot CS FuseLLM-vs-Llama-2.

## 8. Uncertainties to resolve at execution time
- Exact source-defined CS task list and zero-shot prompt protocol (topics `iclr2024/18013/1:setup_2`, `setup_9`) — if they define anything different, §3 substitution rule applies.
- Availability of the official FuseLLM checkpoint offline (vs. required local re-fusion, which changes provenance and adds compute).
- Whether the intended baseline is 7B base, 13B, or chat — 7B base is the working assumption because FuseLLM is 7B-class.
- Whether "outperform" tolerates the materiality floor in the decision rule; the rule is stated and can be relaxed only by design revision, not post-hoc.
- Statistical power: with n=9 tasks and per-task samples in the hundreds to thousands, the design's bootstrap/McNemar machinery is well-powered to detect ≥1-point macro-average gaps; small per-task samples (e.g., COPA n≈100) are handled via two-stage bootstrap rather than per-task testing alone.

**Bottom line:** the design answers "will FuseLLM outperform Llama-2 on CS (zero-shot)?" by pre-registering a matched two-arm evaluation (FuseLLM-7B vs Llama-2-7B) on a standard zero-shot CS suite with fixed prompts/decoding, a macro-average primary metric, item-level records, bootstrap/McNemar/permutation inference, a materiality-aware decision rule, and explicit constraint-based feasibility — all under the fixed requirement that this is a design-only submission with no executed experiment.

## Proposed approach: MinED vs EM alignment criteria on BBH

**Core framing.** The two criteria are *judging/scoring functions* applied to the same generated model outputs — not training or prompting differences. So the cleanest apples-to-apples comparison is a two-stage pipeline where generation is held identical and only the scorer differs.

### 1. Concrete set-up

**Tasks:** the 27 BBH tasks as anchored by the study context — 23 multiple-choice (MC) tasks and 4 free-form generation tasks. (The identity of the 4 free-form tasks is flagged below as an assumption; all 27 are scored, so the comparison is complete either way.)

**Pipeline (two stages):**
- *Stage 1 — Generation (held fixed):* one LLM backbone (see assumptions) answers every example of every task under the standard BBH few-shot prompt setup, temperature 0, fixed seed. All raw outputs are **stored**.
- *Stage 2 — Alignment (the only thing that varies):* each stored raw output is scored twice — once by EM, once by MinED — via the same extraction + normalization code. Any accuracy difference is then attributable solely to the alignment criterion.

**Input/outputs under each criterion:**
- Shared preprocessing: extract candidate answer (MC → the chosen option letter A–E, or failing that the normalized response text; free-form → the generated string), then normalize (strip whitespace; lower-case for free-form; MC kept as letter after extraction).
- **EM (Exact Matching):** output counts as correct iff normalized extracted answer *exactly equals* the gold answer string. MC: letter equality. Free-form: exact string equality against the gold target (or any gold target in the accepted set). Empty/failed extraction → mismatch (0).
- **MinED (Minimum Edit Distance):** compute Levenshtein distance (pure-Python or `difflib.SequenceMatcher`, since no `Levenshtein`/`editdistance`/`numpy` packages are preinstalled in this environment) between the normalized output and each *candidate answer*; predicted answer = argmin over candidates; correct iff min distance normalized by `max(|output|,|candidate|) ≤ τ` (primary τ = 0.15, swept over {0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.15, 0.2, 0.3}). Candidates: MC → the 5 option strings (plus letter labels); free-form → the gold target set for that example (e.g., a valid Dyck string, a correctly sorted word list). **Tie-breaking:** if two candidates tie at the min distance, declared mismatch (conservative) in the primary spec; sensitivity runs the "pick lowest letter first" variant.

### 2. Comparison approach

- **Primary metric:** macro-average accuracy over the 27 tasks (each task weighted equally). Secondary: micro-average (over examples), per-task accuracy, and on the 4 free-form tasks a descriptive partial-credit score = 1 − normalized min edit distance.
- **Isolation of the criterion effect:** both criteria score the *same stored outputs*; extraction, normalization, prompt, decoding, and seed are bit-identical. This is a controlled post-hoc scoring experiment, so no model/prompt/decoding confound exists.
- **Primary decision rule — "MinED outperforms EM" holds iff all of:** (a) macro-accuracy(MinED) > macro-accuracy(EM); (b) on the 23 MC tasks aggregate accuracy does not drop below EM by more than a pre-registered epsilon (≈0, since MC should be near-insensitive to the criterion — this doubles as a placebo check); (c) MinED ≥ EM on a large majority of tasks (pre-registered: ≥ 24 of 27, with the gain concentrated on the 4 free-form tasks); (d) paired-signal significance: a sign test across the 27 tasks and a paired bootstrap 95% CI on the aggregate difference exclude 0.

### 3. Controls and safeguards

- **Held fixed across conditions:** model + weights, prompt template and few-shot exemplars, decoding params, seed, task ordering, dataset split, and the extraction/normalization routine. Only the matching function (exact vs min-edit-distance) varies.
- **Leakage guard:** gold candidate sets for MinED are built from gold labels only, never from model outputs; no test output ever informs scoring structure; exemplars disjoint from test examples.
- **Free-form inflation guard:** τ chosen a priori and swept; EM reported on the same 4 free-form tasks so nothing is "hidden"; report a false-accept rate (MinED-accepted-but-EM-rejected examples that are genuinely wrong after manual spot-check) so a lenient τ cannot masquerade as improvement.
- **Placebo/sanity check:** on 23 MC tasks MinED and EM should nearly coincide (both reduce to letter selection); a large MC divergence signals a pipeline/extraction bug, not an effect.
- **Prompt-order effects:** single-pass generation; scoring is deterministic and order-independent; no sequential interaction between conditions.

### 4. Analysis plan

- Per-task table: accuracy(EM), accuracy(MinED), Δ, direction of change across all 27 tasks (grouped MC vs free-form).
- Aggregate macro/micro accuracy with paired bootstrap CIs; sign test and McNemar-style paired per-example tests per task where applicable; wins/losses/ties count.
- Sensitivity: τ sweep; character- vs word-token-level edit distance; tie-breaking variants; normalization on/off — report that the MinED conclusion holds over the plausible τ range.
- Subgroup: MC-only (23) vs free-form-only (4) summaries to locate where any advantage comes from.

### 5. Consequential assumptions (flagged, not facts)

- **Backbone model unspecified** (e.g., PaLM/code-davinci-002 as in the original BBH paper vs a current open-weights model). Material for absolute accuracy and generalizability but not for the relative criterion comparison, because scoring is post-hoc on identical outputs.
- **Identity of the 4 free-form tasks** not visible in this workspace — assumed from the anchored scope (candidates like dyck_languages / word_sorting / multistep_arithmetic / etc.).
- **MinED threshold τ, tie-breaking rule, and whether normalization precedes distance** are not pinned by sources — handled via sensitivity sweep.
- **Number of runs:** temperature-0 makes generation deterministic; if sampling is allowed, seed count becomes an assumption.
- **"Outperform" read as higher accuracy** (not efficiency/robustness-only) — assumed for the decision rule.
- **EM for MC defined as letter equality** after extraction (not full-string equality) — assumed to be the standard BBH scoring.

Please confirm this direction (especially the two-stage post-hoc scoring framing, the aggregate metric + decision rule, and the τ sweep), and I will expand it into the full experiment design with pseudocode-level detail, controls, and exact analysis steps.

# Experiment Design (final deliverable, design-only — no execution)

## Title
Do the proposed **MinED (Minimum Edit Distance)** and **EM (Exact Matching)** alignment criteria differ in measured accuracy, and does MinED outperform EM, on the BBH benchmark (23 multiple-choice + 4 free-form tasks)?

## Fixed requirements honored from the study context
1. **Task set:** BBH benchmark, 27 tasks — 23 multiple-choice (MC) + 4 free-form generation tasks (scope anchored by the researcher).
2. **Comparison object:** two alignment (judging/scoring) criteria — MinED vs EM — applied to judge model outputs on those tasks.
3. **Framing:** the criteria are scoring functions, not model/prompting/training differences.
4. **Deliverable is a design only:** no execution, no fabricated or claimed results; the environment note ("repositories and compute not required") is honored.
5. **Environment constraint honored:** stdlib-only Python (verified Python 3.14.4; `Levenshtein`, `editdistance`, `numpy`, `scipy` NOT available; `difflib` is). All scoring is specifiable as pure-Python.

---

## 1. Rationale — why this design isolates the alignment-criterion effect

**The claim being tested is about the judging function, not the model.** In BBH-style evaluation, measured accuracy = alignment(output, gold). EM returns a match only on exact string equality after extraction/normalization; this is brittle to benign surface variation (extra whitespace, casing, trailing tokens, punctuation, near-miss spellings in generated free-form strings). MinED instead computes the normalized Levenshtein distance from the output to each candidate answer, selects the nearest candidate, and accepts if the distance is within a threshold τ — designed to rescue free-form generation tasks where the model emits a valid-but-not-canonically-formatted answer.

**Why the two-stage post-hoc framing cleanly isolates the effect.** All outputs are generated **once** by an identical pipeline, stored, and then scored **twice** (EM and MinED) by the same extraction/normalization/decoding-independent judges. By construction, every variable except the matching function — model, prompt template, few-shot exemplars, decoding parameters, seed, task ordering, split, extraction code — is bit-identical across the two conditions. Any accuracy difference is therefore attributable to the alignment criterion alone. This is strictly stronger than running two separate end-to-end evaluations that differ only in judge, because those could differ spuriously via generation nondeterminism or pipeline drift; here there is a single artifact set.

**What the design can support:** a precisely scoped claim — "under the specified τ, tie-break, and normalization choices, MinED reports a higher alignment accuracy than EM on these 27 BBH tasks (aggregate / per-task breakdown), and the effect is/is not robust across τ and consistent across tasks."
**What it cannot support:** any claim about the generative quality of the backbone; any claim generalizable to other tasks/models/outputs beyond the stored artifact set; claims that a criterion makes a model "better" at solving BBH in some intrinsic sense. The verdict is conditional on the specific outputs on which the criteria are applied.

---

## 2. Setup (pseudocode-level detail)

### 2.1 Stage 1 — Generation (held FIXED, executed once, outputs stored)
```
FIXED = { model=MODEL            # ASSUMPTION: unspecified backbone (see §6)
          temperature=0.0, seed=SEED, max_tokens=MAX_TOKENS,
          prompt_template=TPL, few_shot_exemplars=EX, split='test' }

raw = {}                                 # single source of truth for scoring
for task in BBH_TASKS:                   # 27 tasks = 23 MC + 4 free-form (ASSUMPTION on identity)
    prompts = build_prompts(task, EX, TPL)
    for ex in load(task, 'test'):
        raw[task][ex.id] = model.generate(prompts[ex.id], **FIXED)

save(raw)                                # BOTH criteria later read exactly this store
```
No sampling; temperature 0 → deterministic generation (ASSUMPTION; if sampling is allowed, replicate over K seeds and pool stored outputs — flagged in §6).

### 2.2 Shared extraction + normalization (FIXED, applied identically BEFORE both criteria)
```
def normalize_freeform(t):             # free-form tasks
    t = t.strip()
    t = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', t)
    if NORM_LOWER: t = t.lower()       # NORM_LOWER=True for primary run (sensitivity on/off)
    if NORM_PUNCT: t = t.translate(remove_punct)   # sensitivity on/off
    return t

def preprocess(raw_out, task_type):
    if task_type == 'MC':
        letter = extract_answer_letter(raw_out)   # regexes for "Answer: C", "(C)", "C" at end
        return (letter if letter else normalize_freeform(raw_out)), 'letter'
    else:
        return normalize_freeform(raw_out), 'text'
```
**Key control:** `preprocess` is a single shared function executed identically for the EM and MinED conditions; it cannot favor one criterion.

### 2.3 EM — Exact Matching (reference criterion)
```
def EM(pred, gold):
    if pred is None or pred == '':      # failed/empty extraction -> mismatch
        return 0.0
    return 1.0 if pred == gold else 0.0
```
- MC: `pred` and `gold` are option letters (letter equality — ASSUMPTION, §6); EM here is the standard BBH letter-match convention.
- Free-form: exact string equality between normalized predicted text and the gold target string.

### 2.4 MinED — Minimum Edit Distance (proposed criterion)
```
def levenshtein(a, b):                  # pure-Python DP; primary = char-level
    # standard O(|a|·|b|) dynamic program over characters
    # (stdlib-only; difflib.SequenceMatcher allowed as an alternative distance source)

def min_edit_distance(pred, candidates):
    ds = [levenshtein(pred, c) for c in candidates]
    dn = [d / max(len(pred), len(c), 1) for d, c in zip(ds, candidates)]
    i_min = min(range(len(dn)), key=lambda i: (dn[i], i))  # first-lowest canonical order
    unique = (sorted(dn)[0] < sorted(dn)[1]) if len(dn) > 1 else True   # tie detection
    return i_min, dn[i_min], unique

def MinED(pred, candidates, τ):
    if pred is None or pred == '': return 0.0                    # same failed-extraction rule as EM
    i, d_norm, unique = min_edit_distance(pred, candidates)
    if TIE_RULE == 'conservative' and not unique:
        return 0.0                                               # ambiguous nearest -> reject
    if TIE_RULE == 'first':
        pass                                                     # keep i_min
    return 1.0 if d_norm <= τ else 0.0
```
- **Candidate enumeration**
  - *MC (23 tasks):* candidates = the 5 option strings `{A: opt_A, …, E: opt_E}`; the predicted letter is the option minimizing distance; correctness = `d_norm ≤ τ` (letter label matches option text internally, so on near-identical option text MinED converges to letter selection — the placebo property, §3).
  - *Free-form (4 tasks):* candidates = the gold target set(s) for that example. If an example has **multiple valid gold targets** (e.g., any valid Dyck string of length n; a correctly sorted word list), correctness = `min over all gold targets of d_norm ≤ τ`. Candidate sets are built from gold labels only (§3 leakage guard).
- **τ sweep grid (sensitivity):** `τ ∈ {0.0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.15 (primary), 0.2, 0.3}`. τ = 0 with exact equality ≡ EM, giving a continuity/self-consistency check that the two implementations agree when they should.
- **Distance-variant sweep (sensitivity):** char-level Levenshtein (primary) vs word-token-level Levenshtein (split on whitespace) vs a `difflib.SequenceMatcher` ratio-based closeness ≥ ρ (mapped to a distance).

### 2.5 Hyperparameters — fixed vs swept (explicit)
**Fixed:** model, prompt template + exemplars, decoding (temp 0, seed, max tokens), task ordering, split, shared extraction/normalization, primary τ=0.15, char-level Levenshtein, conservative tie-break, NORM_LOWER=True/NORM_PUNCT=False.
**Swept (sensitivity only, never alters the shared generation):** τ ∈ grid; char-vs-word-vs-difflib distance; tie-break (conservative vs first); NORM_LOWER / NORM_PUNCT on/off.

---

## 3. Controls and safeguards

1. **Held identical across conditions (bit-for-bit):** the stored raw outputs (one artifact set), the shared `preprocess`/normalization function, gold answer sets, task ordering, dataset split. Only `EM()` vs `MinED()` differ. Any implementation bug is thereby symmetric unless it is inside the matching function itself.
2. **Leakage guards:** MinED candidate sets are constructed **from gold labels only** (option text for MC; gold targets for free-form) — never from any model output or from other examples; few-shot exemplars disjoint from test examples; scorers see one example at a time (no cross-example information).
3. **MC placebo check (sanity of the pipeline):** on the 23 MC tasks MinED and EM should produce near-identical aggregate accuracy (both collapse to letter selection). **Pre-registered rule:** if |macro(MC, MinED) − macro(MC, EM)| > ε = 1 accuracy point, flag a pipeline/extraction bug and do not issue a clean verdict until resolved.
4. **Free-form false-accept guard:** enumerate examples MinED accepts but EM rejects; manually spot-check the first ~50 (sorted by distance) and classify each as (a) genuine near-miss that an expert would credit vs (b) genuinely wrong answer let in by a lenient τ. Report the **false-accept rate** = fraction of (b). If the false-accept rate is high (e.g., >20% of MinED-only accepts), the free-form "gain" is discounted in the verdict.
5. **τ-inflation guard:** the verdict must hold at the primary τ=0.15 and remain directionally stable across the plausible τ range; a win that exists only at τ ≥ 0.2 is reported as non-robust (§4 partial-branch b).
6. **Prompt-order / carry-over:** single-pass generation with no sequential dependency between conditions; scoring is deterministic and order-independent.

---

## 4. Analysis plan

### 4.1 Outputs
- **Per-task table (primary result artifact):** rows = 27 tasks grouped MC (23) then free-form (4); columns = `EM_acc`, `MinED_acc`, `Δ`, direction (MinED wins / loses / ties). Plus the manual spot-check classification for the free-form false-accept guard.
- **Aggregates:** **macro-average** accuracy (mean of 27 per-task accuracies) = primary aggregate; micro-average (all examples pooled) reported secondarily; both for EM and MinED.
- **Paired inference (all on the identical artifact set, so paired by construction):**
  - *Paired bootstrap CI:* resample the 27 tasks with replacement (10,000 resamples, pure-stdlib `random`), CI on macro(MinED)−macro(EM); report that CI excludes 0 or not.
  - *Sign test* across the 27 tasks (MinED>EM / MinED<EM / ties), both-sided p-value.
  - *McNemar-style per-example test:* per task, 2×2 contingency (correct under EM-only vs MinED-only vs both vs neither); aggregate McNemar over pooled examples as a secondary signal.
- **Sensitivity:** repeat aggregate + per-task under (i) τ grid, (ii) char-vs-word-vs-difflib distance, (iii) tie-break variants, (iv) normalization on/off. Report whether the primary verdict survives the plausible hyperparameter range.

### 4.2 Pre-registered verdict rules (incl. partial conditions)
Define `G = macro(MinED) − macro(EM)` at primary τ=0.15.

- **Full "MinED outperforms EM":** all of — (a) G > 0; (b) bootstrap 95% CI on G excludes 0; (c) MinED ≥ EM on ≥ 24/27 tasks (sign-test consistency); (d) MC placebo holds (|ΔMC| ≤ ε); (e) free-form gain survives the false-accept spot-check.
- **Partial branches (how the verdict is worded when only some conditions hold):**
  - *a) Aggregate gain, weaker consistency:* (a)(b) hold but task majority < 24/27 → "MinED outperforms EM **on aggregate**, but the advantage is **not consistent across tasks**; it is concentrated in {list of tasks with Δ>0}."
  - *b) Threshold-dependence:* gain exists but only at τ ≥ 0.2 → "MinED outperforms EM **only under a lenient threshold**; not robust at primary τ."
  - *c) Free-form-only:* gain located entirely in the 4 free-form tasks with ΔMC ≈ 0 → "MinED outperforms EM **on the free-form tasks** and is **neutral** on MC tasks."
  - *d) False-accept contamination:* free-form gain coincides with high false-accept rate → the gain is **not credited**; verdict downgraded to "no evidence MinED improves **measured correctness** (it improves lenient acceptance)."
  - *e) No gain or CI includes 0* → "MinED **does not outperform** EM under this design."
These branches make the verdict falsifiable and force an explicit statement of *where* any advantage comes from (MC vs free-form) rather than a single opaque number.

---

## 5. Feasibility

- **Fully feasible as a design in this environment.** The deliverable requires no execution, and the study context explicitly waives repositories and compute. Runtimes/compute are not required and none are claimed.
- **Implementation feasibility of the spec is verified conceptually against the environment:** the environment is stdlib-only (confirmed: no `numpy`/`scipy`/`Levenshtein`/`editdistance`; `difflib` available; Python 3.14.4). The design therefore specifies a pure-Python DP Levenshtein and `difflib.SequenceMatcher` alternatives, and bootstrap/sign-test/McNemar computations are expressible with `random`/`math`/`statistics` alone. A smoke check that the *scoring functions* compile and yield sane distances on toy strings could be run in an optional scaffolding step but would be a feasibility sanity check only — **not** an experiment and **not** evidence of any BBH result.
- **Remaining external dependency:** generating the 27-task BBH outputs requires model access and the BBH dataset, which are out of scope for this design-only task and explicitly not required; the design assumes their availability at execution time (flagged as an assumption).

---

## 6. Assumptions and uncertainties (explicitly labeled, not facts)

**Assumptions (may materially affect the verdict):**
1. **Backbone model unspecified** (e.g., PaLM/code-davinci-002 as in the original BBH paper vs a current open-weights model). Affects absolute accuracy and generalizability; does **not** compromise the relative criterion comparison because scoring is post-hoc on identical outputs.
2. **Identity of the 4 free-form tasks** not visible in this workspace (e.g., candidates like dyck_languages, word_sorting, multistep_arithmetic). Affects candidate enumeration and, potentially, the size of the free-form effect.
3. **EM-for-MC = option-letter equality** after extraction (standard BBH convention), not full-string equality. Affects the MC placebo baseline.
4. **"Outperforms" = higher alignment accuracy** (not efficiency/robustness-only).
5. **τ=0.15 and the conservative tie-break as primary choices** (not source-specified); their effect is bounded by the sensitivity sweep.
6. **Single-pass, temperature-0 generation**; if sampling at execution time, this becomes K seeded passes and an extra seed-sensitivity analysis.

**Uncertainties (design handles but cannot resolve from available sources):**
- Whether the source defines MinED as *thresholded acceptance* (this design) vs *argmin-only without threshold* — changes the false-accept profile on free-form tasks.
- Whether free-form gold answers are single or multiple valid targets per example — handled by "min over gold set" candidate enumeration, but the multiplicity itself is unverified.
- Exact normalization convention (lowercase/punctuation) not pinned by sources — covered by the on/off sensitivity.
- Power of a 27-task sign test with ties — why the design adds per-example McNemar and the bootstrap CI as co-signals.

---

## Summary of the experimental protocol (one-paragraph executable spec)
Generate all 27 BBH test outputs once with a fixed, deterministic pipeline and store them; apply a single shared extraction/normalization; score every stored example twice — EM (exact equality; letter equality on the 23 MC tasks) and MinED (normalized Levenshtein to the gold/option candidate set, nearest-candidate acceptance at τ=0.15, conservative tie-break) — while holding everything else bit-identical; report per-task accuracy, macro/micro aggregates, paired-bootstrap CI, sign test, and per-example McNemar; sweep τ ∈ {0,…,0.3}, char-vs-word distance, tie-break, and normalization to establish robustness; enforce the MC placebo check and free-form false-accept spot-check; and emit the verdict via the pre-registered full/partial-branch rules. Execution is out of scope for this deliverable.

## 1. Результат инспекции

**Доступно:** только `/workspace/task.json` — вопрос *"does the proposed MinED method outperforms EM method, on benchmark BBH?"*, контекст *"Design an experiment… Do not claim that an experiment was run"*, и пометка `track.md` → *"Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required."* Физического файла `track.md`, репозиториев, датасетов и артефактов нет. Сеть отключена, GPU нет, системный Python 3.14.4, среда bubblewrap с пометкой, что exploratory команды не являются доказательством проведённого эксперимента.

**Подтверждаю:** это чисто design-only задача. Зафиксированные setup-факты (BBH = 27 задач: 23 MCQ + 4 free-form; MinED vs EM; покрытие algorithmic reasoning, arithmetic reasoning, NLU, world knowledge, multilingual) я принимаю из источника iclr2024/18013; в workspace они не представлены, так что их источник — ваша спецификация (см. assumptions).

## 2. Конспект proposed approach (скелет)

Интерпретация терминов. EM (baseline, self-consistency): сгенерированные ответы группируются только по точному совпадению строк; ответом берётся представитель самой частой группы. MinED (proposed, аналог Universal Self-Consistency): ответы группируются по попарной мере минимального редактирования (normalized Levenshtein similarity), кластеризация (connected components/MST по порогу τ), ответ = представитель наибольшего кластера (с confidence/tie-breaking правилом). Оба критерия применяются к **одним и тем же** сгенерированным outputs — единственный варьируемый фактор это scoring/alignment, что изолирует эффект критерия.

Компоненты эксперимента:
- **Inputs**: BBH, 27 задач × N dev/test инстансов; 3-shot CoT промпты из канонического BBH (SuZgun et al.), единый prompt template для обоих плеч.
- **Generation model**: одна публичная LLM (для дизайна укажем конкретную, см. feasibility), sampling decoding с фиксированным temperature и seed; k=40 генераций на инстанс (как в оригинальной постановке Uging); единый cache outputs для двух плеч.
- **Preprocessing/extraction**: для 23 MCQ — извлечение лейбла (A/B/C/D/E) и нормализация (trim, lowercase, убрать пунктуацию, варианты "(A)", "A)", "A."); для 4 free-form — извлечение финального ответа (разделение CoT и ответа) + та же нормализация.
- **Two arms on identical outputs**: Arm EM vs Arm MinED(τ). MinED настраивается по validation split (выбор τ и схемы length-normalization), затем фиксируется на test.
- **Метрики**: aggregate accuracy (macro-avg по 27 задачам), per-task accuracy, per-task win rate (MinED>EM), среднее/медиана разницы по задачам.
- **Статистика**: по 27 задачам — парный Wilcoxon signed-rank и sign test на per-task accuracy; по инстансам — McNemar (paired на бинарных исходах инстансов). Отчёт: table accuracy × arm, win rate, p-value, effect size; baseline EM на уровне published SC.

## 3. Assumptions и uncertainties (зафиксировать до финального дизайна)

(a) "outperforms" = aggregate accuracy И/ИЛИ per-task win rate — нужна явная primary метрика. Предложение: primary = mean per-task accuracy с Wilcoxon по 27 задачам; secondary = win-rate и McNemar.
(b) Точное определение MinED: normalization (case/whitespace/punctuation), normalized edit distance (Levenshtein / max(len_a,len_b)), порог τ (допустимое расстояние, по умолчанию τ=0.4-0.5 как в Uging), и правило выбора представителя кластера (самый частый? максимальная суммарная близость?).
(c) 4 free-form против 23 MCQ: разные extraction pipelines; длина ответов (free-form длиннее) влияет на Levenshtein — нужно решение по length-normalization; отчёт отдельно для двух групп задач (sanity check, что эффект не сконцентрирован в одном типе).
(d) Выбор генеративной модели и N; критично: outputs обоих плеч идентичны (cache), чтобы разница была только в критерии; параметры декодирования фиксированы.
(e) Feasibility: BBH публичный (HuggingFace/Google), для дизайна compute не нужен. При гипотетическом исполнении: одна модель × 27 задач × ~250 инстансов × 40 генераций ≈ 270k генераций; дизайн допускает уменьшение (подвыборка задач/инстансов, k=5) без потери структуры сравнения.

Дополнительные uncertainties: применяется ли MinED как критерий матчинга к gold или как критерий кластеризации (у меня предположение — кластеризация/агрегация); tie-breaking; какой model-сет; воспроизводимость (seed, temperature). Жду подтверждения этих пунктов (и вашу спецификацию по primary metric и τ), после чего разворачиваю полный дизайн.

payload.answer:
# Experimental Design — Does MinED outperform EM as an alignment criterion on BBH?

Design-only specification. Nothing was executed; no results are claimed. All numeric examples (sizes, latencies, effects) are parameter estimates for a hypothetical run, not observations.

---

## 0. Scope and interpretation (fixed by researcher)

- **MinED** = aggregation criterion: edit-distance–based clustering of sampled outputs (analogous to Universal Self-Consistency / "Uging"); **EM** = exact-match grouping (classical self-consistency, "SC"). Both are applied to the **same cached generations**; the *only* varied factor is scoring/alignment.
- This interpretation is an **explicit assumption** (source intent for "alignment criterion" is not independently known). **Alternative reading noted (one line, does not change the scheme):** if MinED instead meant *matching a prediction to the gold answer* (greedy best-correction), the experiment would become a *scoring-against-gold* comparison rather than an *aggregation* comparison; the current design targets the aggregation reading.
- Primary metric **fixed**: mean per-task accuracy (macro-average over 27 tasks), with paired one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank as the primary test; report Δ = MinED − EM with 95% CI. Secondaries: per-task win rate, McNemar on pooled instances, MCQ vs free-form breakdown.

---

## (i) Rationale and hypothesis

**Research question.** In a few-shot CoT setup on BBH, a model samples several candidate answers per instance; an *alignment criterion* selects the final answer. EM (exact-match majority) discards near-identical but not byte-identical answers, which is brittle to surface variation (spacing, casing, punctuation, paraphrase) — especially for free-form outputs. MinED (edit-distance clustering) groups by normalized string similarity, recovering votes lost by EM while remaining deterministic and label-free. Question: does the aggregate accuracy improve?

**Hypotheses** (pre-registered):
- H0: μ(MinED) − μ(EM) ≤ 0, where μ = mean per-task accuracy over the 27 BBH tasks.
- H1: μ(MinED) − μ(EM) > 0.

Primary test statistic: paired one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank over the 27 per-task accuracy deltas Δ_t = acc_t(MinED) − acc_t(EM), at α = 0.05. Direction and test are fixed *before* seeing results.

---

## (ii) Data / inputs and prompt scheme

- **Benchmark**: BBH (Suzgun et al., 2022), 27 tasks — 23 multiple-choice (letter A–E) + 4 free-form, covering algorithmic reasoning, arithmetic reasoning, NLU, world knowledge, multilingual (facts taken from researcher's source; see Assumptions A2).
- **Splits**: official *test* split used for evaluation. For τ tuning: use a *held-out validation split* if the release provides one (e.g., the official train split); **if no validation exists**, hold out a fixed random 20% of test instances per task for τ tuning (seeded) and evaluate on the remaining 80% — this is the standard dev/test protocol and is stated explicitly in the report. Fallback when neither is acceptable: a-priori τ = 0.5 with full sensitivity analysis (see (vi)). **No τ is ever tuned on the evaluation split.**
- **Prompts**: canonical 3-shot CoT exemplar texts published with BBH, one template per task (exemplar = question + step-by-step reasoning + final answer in the dataset's own format, e.g., "... So the answer is X."). Test instance appended identically. Identical prompts/exemplars for both arms.

---

## (iii) Generation and extraction procedure

1. **Generator (example parameter)**: one public instruct LLM, e.g., PaLM 2‑L / GPT‑4‑class / Llama‑3‑70B — configurable; the choice is a *parameter*, not a structural dependency (rationale: relative comparison of two scoring rules on identical outputs is model-agnostic in design).
2. **Decoding**: temperature T = 0.7, top‑p = 0.9, max_new_tokens set per task (longer for free-form), all runs for an arm share fixed RNG seed(s). k = 40 generations per instance (k ∈ {5,10,20,40} ablated, see (vi)).
3. **Caching**: all generations written once to a JSON manifest `{task, instance_id, seed, generated_texts[k]}`. **Both arms read only this manifest** — this is the core isolation control.
4. **Extraction** (applied identically to predictions and golds, per task):
   - Free-form: split CoT from final answer (delimiter / trailing-answer pattern per task, e.g., text after "So the answer is"); fallback: last non-empty line.
   - MCQ: extract answer token, map to letter A–E (recover "(A)", "A)", "A." variants).
5. **Normalization** (applied per task, identical to both arms): trim; lowercase; collapse whitespace; task-specific punctuation removal (MCQ: keep only the letter; free-form: strip punctuation/symbols but keep alphanumerics). Any task-specific normalization rule is registered in a config table *before* evaluation to avoid post-hoc fitting.

---

## (iv) Method specifications with pseudocode

```python
# Shared pre-processing
normalize(s, task)          # (iii)-(5); same for preds and golds
answers[i] = normalize(extract_final(gen_i), task)   # i = 1..k

#---------------- Arm EM: exact-match grouping (self-consistency) ----------------
def EM(answers):
    groups = {}                     # key: normalized string
    for a in answers: groups[a] += 1
    rep = argmax_sorted(groups, key=(count desc, lexicographic asc))
    return rep                      # deterministic

#---------------- Arm MinED: edit-distance clustering -----------------------------
def sim(a, b):                      # normalized Levenshtein similarity, fixed spec
    d = Levenshtein(a, b)           # standard DP, O(|a|·|b|)
    return 1.0 - d / max(len(a), len(b), 1)   # length-normalized; sim(a,a)=1

def MinED(answers, tau=0.5):
    # 1) connected-components clustering on threshold graph
    comps = union_find(range(k))
    for i, j in pairs(i<j):
        if sim(answers[i], answers[j]) >= tau:      # edge kept
            union(i, j)
    # 2) component score = total within-component similarity to other members
    for each component C:
        score(C, m) = sum(sim(answers[m], answers[n]) for n in C, n != m)
        freq(C, m)  = count of answers[m] in C
    # 3) select component maximizing (total-sim, then size, then lexicographic rep)
    C* = max(C, key=(sum(score(C,m)), |C|))
    rep = max(C*, key=(score(C*,m), freq(C*,m), lexicographic(answers[m])))
    return rep                      # deterministic
```

τ is tuned **globally (one shared τ)** on validation over {0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9} by validation mean per-task accuracy — a single global τ is chosen to avoid per-task overfitting; the chosen τ is then frozen and applied to the evaluation split.

Decision rule for accuracy (both arms): final answer (normalized) is correct iff it equals the normalized gold (exact string/letter equality). If a generation fails extraction (no parseable answer), it is dropped from clustering and the instance is scored using remaining answers; instances with 0 parseable answers in an arm are marked as "unanswerable" and counted incorrect (recorded separately for transparency). This drop rule is applied **identically to both arms** on the *same* cached outputs, so it cannot bias one arm against the other.

---

## (v) Metrics, statistical plan, sample size/power

**Per-instance outcome**: binary correct/incorrect under each arm → per-task accuracy acc_t.

**Primary**:
- μ_EM = mean_t acc_t(EM), μ_MinED = mean_t acc_t(MinED); Δ = μ_MinED − μ_EM.
- 95% CI for Δ: bootstrap over *tasks* (re-sample 27 tasks, 10k reps, percentile CI) — tasks are the sampling units, preserving the paired structure.
- Paired one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank on Δ_t (n = 27), H1: MinED > EM. Report W, effect size (rank-biserial r and/or median Δ), p-value.

**Secondary**:
- Per-task win rate = fraction of tasks with Δ_t > 0; binomial exact 95% CI; sign test p-value.
- McNemar (exact binomial version) on pooled instances: 2×2 table of (EM wrong/MCED right), (both correct), (both wrong), (EM right/MCED wrong) over all test instances of the 27 tasks.
- Breakdown: mean accuracy and Δ for the 23 MCQ tasks and the 4 free-form tasks **reported separately** (see Limitations L3).
- Robustness report: Δ across seeds (mean ± std over ≥3 seeds at each k).

**Sample size / power (design-level, pre-specified, not computed)**: the benchmark fixes n = 27 tasks, so power is bounded; a pre-specified power curve is computed by simulation *before* running the experiment: sample per-task Δ_t from a distribution calibrated to a plausible effect (e.g., prior Uging-style report of ~+1–2 aggregate points and a task-level win-rate p ∈ {0.6, 0.7, 0.8}), run one-sided Wilcoxon on 27 re-sampled tasks, report P(reject) for each (p, effect) cell. This yields a decision rule: a non-significant Wilcoxon with a small Δ is reported as "no evidence of improvement" rather than "no improvement". Because n=27 cannot be increased, the report prioritizes effect size + CI over the binary p-value.

---

## (vi) Controls and ablations

1. **Core isolation**: both arms on identical cached outputs; identical prompts, decode params, extraction, normalization, drop rule. Only the scoring step differs. (If any of these cannot be shared, the design is invalid — checked during scaffolding.)
2. **τ sensitivity**: on validation sweep {0.3…0.9}; on evaluation, plot acc(τ) for both arms to show robustness around the chosen τ (report chosen τ and the range of Δ over the sweep).
3. **Representative-rule ablations**: (a) total-within-cluster similarity (fixed primary); (b) frequency-only (ties lexicographic); (c) median string (min max-sim). Report Δ under each to show the choice is not load-bearing (if it is, flag as a limitation).
4. **Normalization ablations**: on/off lowercase, on/off punctuation removal — for MCQ and free-form separately — verify conclusions aren't artifacts of normalization.
5. **k ablation**: k ∈ {5, 10, 20, 40} × {EM, MinED}; report Δ(k) — checks whether any advantage appears already at small k and how it scales (stability check).
6. **Anchor control**: k=1 (no aggregation, single greedy/sampled answer per instance) as a floor for both arms' added value; report macro-accuracy of each arm relative to it.
7. **Reproducibility**: ≥3 independent seeds per (k) cell; report mean ± std; determinism of EM and MinED ensures within-seed reproducibility given cached outputs.
8. **Data-hygiene**: official test split only; no τ/rule tuning on evaluation; all config tables (normalization, extraction, τ grid) locked before running evaluation.

---

## (vii) Feasibility and resource estimate (hypothetical execution)

- **Data**: BBH is public (canonical release with 3-shot exemplars + test gold labels); download required only if the experiment were executed (this sandbox has network disabled; execution is out of scope).
- **Inference volume**: 27 tasks × ≈250 test instances/task ≈ 6.8k instances. At k=40 → ≈ **270k generations**; at k=10 → ≈ 68k generations (the sensible default for cost).
- **Compute** (example): a modern single GPU (~Llama-3-70B-class FP16) at ≈0.5–1 s/gen → ≈1–2 days at k=40, ≈5–8 h at k=10 (batched). Parallelize across tasks if more nodes available.
- **Evaluation**: Levenshtein is the only non-trivial cost: 40×40 ≈ 1600 string-pairs per instance → ≈11M pairs total at k=40; pure-Python/NumPy or `python-Levenshtein` handles this in well under an hour (free-form strings are short). Storage of cached generations ≈ 100–500 MB JSON.
- **Cost reduction options** (do not change structure): k=10 default; restrict the τ sweep to {0.4,0.5,0.6}; use 1 seed at the chosen k with 3 seeds on a 5-task subsample for variance attestation.
- No model training, no additional data collection; the design is fully reproducible from the public dataset + fixed config.

---

## (viii) Assumptions and limitations

**Assumptions (fixed task requirements marked F):**
- A1 (F): MinED = edit-distance aggregation clustering (Uging-style); EM = exact-match grouping. *Explicit assumption* — source intent unknown; alternative reading (scoring against gold) noted; would change the experiment, not adopted here.
- A2 (F): BBH = 27 tasks (23 MCQ + 4 free-form) with the stated coverage — accepted from the researcher's source; not independently verifiable in the workspace (no dataset present).
- A3 (F): Both arms share identical cached outputs; only scoring differs.
- A4 (F): MinED = normalized Levenshtein similarity 1 − d/max(|a|,|b|), connected-components clustering at global τ, default τ=0.5, tuned on validation / a-priori with sensitivity fallback; representative = max total within-cluster similarity, tie-break frequency then lexicographic.
- A5 (F): Primary = mean per-task accuracy, paired one-sided Wilcoxon (n=27); secondaries = win rate, McNemar, MCQ/free-form breakdown.
- A6: Generator model is an example parameter; no structural dependency on the choice.
- A7: A single parsed final answer per generation (deterministic extraction per task) is attainable with the specified patterns; unresolvable outputs handled by the drop rule applied equally to both arms.

**Limitations:**
- L1: A1 is an interpretation, not a verified intent; the result is conditional on the aggregation reading.
- L2: The generator choice may affect absolute/relative effect magnitude; conclusions are model-specific (design gives a fair within-model comparison, not cross-model generalization).
- L3: The 4 free-form tasks give very low statistical power in the breakdown; the primary conclusion rests on the n=27 Wilcoxon, with free-form reported as descriptive only.
- L4: n=27 limits power of the primary test; hence effect size + CI are co-primary reporting, with a pre-specified power/sensitivity simulation to interpret non-significance.
- L5: Task-specific normalization/extraction choices could influence results; mitigated by locked config tables + normalization ablations (vi-4).
- L6: If the release lacks a usable validation split, τ must be fixed a-priori (0.5) or tuned on a seeded 20% hold-out with the 80% evaluation reported — a design decision, not a hidden failure mode.
