payload.answer:
# Финальный дизайн эксперимента: QuaRot generalization на Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct — RTN vs GPTQ при 4/6/8 бит

## 1. Рациональность

Вопрос — насколько weight-квантизация пайплайна QuaRot обобщается на не-LLaMA модель (Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct): выигрывает ли GPTQ у RTN в PPL и zero-shot accuracy при битности 4/6/8.

Дизайн изолирует ЕДИНЫЙ фактор — тип весового квантизатора — на фоне фиксированной ротации Хадамара. Все 6 ячеек идут с включённой ротацией (`--rotate --perhead`), активации и KV НЕ квантуются (weight-only). **Это осознанная изоляция сравнения весовых квантизаторов: полное QuaRot-квантование (a/v/k-биты + KV-кэш) — отдельная ось, вне рамок вопроса, в дизайн не вносится и в таблицу не добавляется.** Такой выбор позволяет ответить «что именно ломается/побеждает на Phi-3» без спутывания с эффектами активационной квантизации.

Второй слой валидности — контроль процедуры через LLaMA-2-7B: воспроизведение табличных чисел бумаги QuaRot (оборудованный control, не основная ось). Третий слой — FP16-ротационный контроль, ловящий численные поломки ротации на Phi-3 (sliding-window/Hadamard) ДО чтения дельта-квантизации.

## 2. Окружение и пины (договорённость №3)

| Компонент | Пин / значение | Примечание |
|---|---|---|
| Среда | GPU ≥40 ГБ, Linux, Python 3.10/3.11 venv, CUDA-рантайм | НЕ песочница (здесь GPU нет, сеть выключена) |
| QuaRot | spcl/QuaRot, **заморозить конкретный commit-hash при первом доступе** (текущий HEAD записать в протокол) | Доступ к коду недоступен локально — хэш фиксируется на этапе bootstrap |
| transformers | **≥4.40 с `Phi3ForCausalLM`** (+ pin), совместим с загруженным из QuaRot | Если QuaRot-pinned transformers не содержит Phi3 — минимально нужный апгрейд с фиксацией, отклонение записать |
| torch | из requirements QuaRot, pin версии+cuXX | |
| datasets | wikitext2, c4 (allenai/c4, en, «realnewslike» как в QuaRot), pin revision | Кэш локальный, хэши датасетов записать |
| lm-eval-harness | **pin commit** (совместимый с QuaRot-скриптом eval) | Установка vendor без сети (в целевом образе) |
| Модель | `microsoft/Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct`, pin HF-revision/tag | |
| Семена | **seed=2** везде (квантизация + loaders + eval) | |
| Группировка весов | `--w_groupsize 128` во всех 6 ячейках | Вне ячеек: INT8-ref с `--w_groupsize -1` |
| Имена флагов квантизатора | `{gptq, rtn}` — **сверяются при первом доступе к репозиторию**, в командах ниже указаны как контракт-плейсхолдеры | Локально непроверяемо (нет сети/кода) |

## 3. Матрица условий, таблица результатов

Ячейки (все weight-only, `--rotate --perhead`, w_groupsize=128, seed=2):

| # | Условие | Обозначение |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | RTN-4 | PPL w2 / PPL c4 / mean acc + 7 per-task |
| A2 | RTN-6 (разведочная) | … |
| A3 | RTN-8 | … |
| B1 | GPTQ-4 | … |
| B2 | GPTQ-6 (разведочная) | … |
| B3 | GPTQ-8 | … |
| Б1 | **FP16-vanilla** (без ротации, без квант.) — главный reference | … |
| Б2 | FP16-rotated (ротация, без квант.) — контроль численности ротации | … |
| Б3 | INT8-граница: wbits=8, groupsize=-1 (per-channel) | … |

Колонки таблицы: `PPL(wikitext2)`, `PPL(c4)`, `mean zero-shot acc`, затем отдельными колонками `arc_easy, arc_challenge, hellaswag, piqa, winogrande, openbookqa, boolq`, плюс `ΔPPL vs FP16-vanilla` и `Δacc(pp) vs FP16-vanilla`.
LLaMA-2-7B-контроль прогоняется по тем же колонкам (только PPL + mean), не входит в таблицу Phi-3.

## 4. Полный протокол

### Фаза 0 — Bootstrap (в целевой среде: GPU + сеть)
1. venv (Python 3.10/3.11), клон/чек-аут QuaRot по пину, установка requirements (torch, transformers, datasets, sentencepiece, einops, accelerate, lm-eval по пину), vendor установочных артефактов.
2. Смоук-тест: `AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("microsoft/Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct")` загружается; прямой проход 8 токенов с патчем ротации QuaRot не падает; `RotaryEmbedding`/`head_dim=96` подхватываются.
3. Скачать и зафиксировать датасеты (c4, wikitext2) и модель в кэше; записать хэши.

### Фаза 1 — Контроль процедуры LLaMA-2-7B (оборудованный)
Воспроизвести бумажные числа LLaMA-2-7B: fp16, GPTQ-4(g128), RTN-4, 8-бит; сравнить с таблицей QuaRot. **Критерий прохождения:** PPL совпадает с таблицей в пределах допуска (например ±0.1; точное значение зафиксировать по таблице бумаги). Непрохождение → починить пайплайн до Phi-3. Это необходимое условие, чтобы деградацию на Phi-3 относить к модели, а не к процедуре.

### Фаза 2 — Квантизация Phi-3 (6 ячеек + INT8-ref)
Единый `quantize.py` QuaRot (контракт-плейсхолдеры флагов; сверка при первом доступе):
```
python quantize.py \
  --model microsoft/Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct \
  --dataset c4 --nsamples 128 --seed 2 \
  --rotate --perhead \
  --quantizer {gptq|rtn} \
  --wbits {4|6|8} --w_groupsize 128 \
  --save out/phi3_{quant}_{bits}.h5
```
RTN-ячейки: та же команда с `--quantizer rtn`, тот же `nsamples/seed` (калибровочных данных не требует — данные прогоняются тем же пайплайном для симметрии).
**Одинаковый калибровочный сэмпл для RTN и GPTQ:** калибровочные данные грузятся через `datautils.get_loaders(..., seed=2)`, берётся срез первых `nsamples`; ТОТ ЖЕ тензор подаётся в GPTQ и RTN-пути; хэш среза записывается в протокол. GPTQ-калибровка — на C4 (стандарт QuaRot). `--save/--load` фиксирует квантизованные веса для оценки.
INT8-ref: та же команда, `--wbits 8 --w_groupsize -1`.

### Фаза 3 — Оценка
Perplexity (одинаковые сиквенсы и stride для всех):
```
python eval/get_ppl.py --model <cell|fp16> --dataset wikitext2 --seqlen 2048 --stride 512 --seed 2
python eval/get_ppl.py --model <cell|fp16> --dataset c4 --seqlen 2048 --stride 512 --seed 2
```
Zero-shot (lm-eval-harness по пину, float16, seed=2):
```
lm_eval --model hf --model_args pretrained=<path>,dtype=float16 \
  --tasks arc_easy,arc_challenge,hellaswag,piqa,winogrande,openbookqa,boolq \
  --batch_size auto --seed 2
```
**Формат промпта для instruct-модели фиксируется как переменная протокола:** основной прогон — native-формат harness (без chat-template; измеряет базовые способности поверх instruct-весов); дополнительный контроль чувствительности — один лёгкий таск (arc_easy) с `--apply_chat_template` для количественной оценки влияния формата. Значение фиксируется на весь эксперимент, не меняется по ходу.

### Фаза 4 — Контроли (сводно)
- seed=2 во всех компонентах; один и тот же калибровочный срез (хэш) для RTN и GPTQ;
- одинаковые eval-сиквенсы, seqlen 2048, stride 512;
- одинаковый w_groupsize=128 в ячейках; одинаковые пины версий/железа;
- FP16-vanilla и FP16-rotated как пара контролей ротации;
- воспроизведение LLaMA-2-7B (Фаза 1);
- одинаковый формат промпта zero-shot.

## 5. План анализа (как читаем результат)

1. **Контроль валидности ротации на Phi-3:** если `PPL(FP16-rotated) − PPL(FP16-vanilla) > допуск` (напр. 0.05 PPL или 0.5 п.п. acc) — ротация/патч attention нечисленно безопасен на Phi-3 (подозрение: sliding-window/head_dim 96); тогда дельты квантизации не интерпретируем, требуется разборка пайплайна. Сработал ли контроль — первая строка вывода.
2. **Главное чтение — delta vs FP16:** `ΔPPL = PPL(cell) − PPL(FP16-vanilla)`, `Δacc = mean_acc(cell) − mean_acc(FP16-vanilla) в п.п.` для каждой ячейки. FP16-vanilla — главный reference, INT8-граница — ориентир «безболезненного» квантования.
3. **Правило решения «выигрывает ли GPTQ на Phi-3» (pre-registered):**
   - смотрим попарно по битности: GPTQ выигрывает у RTN на битности w, если `ΔPPL(GPTQ-w) < ΔPPL(RTN-w)` И `Δacc(GPTQ-w) ≥ Δacc(RTN-w)`;
   - итог «GPTQ ≥ RTN на Phi-3» — если GPTQ не хуже RTN по обеим метрикам минимум на 2 из 3 битностей; иначе «преимущество не подтверждено» (в т.ч. если 6-бит недоступна — решаем по 4 и 8).
4. **Sensitivity-кривая:** монотонность `Δ(4-bit) > Δ(6-bit) > Δ(8-bit)` (ожидание: 4-бит хуже всех, 8-бит ~ без потерь; близость 8-бит к INT8-границе — sanity). 4-бит — стресс-тест обобщения (в LLaMA GPTQ-4 работает; вопрос — сохраняется ли на Phi-3 с меньшим hidden_size).
5. **6-бит — разведочные ячейки (асимметрия с бумагой):** упаковка 6-бит в QuantLinear и числовая стабильность не валидированы авторами. Если ячейка 6-бит не собирается/не грузится (несовместимая упаковка в пине) → фиксируем «unsupported в данном пине», ячейка = N/A с явной отметкой в протоколе (не молчаливый пропуск). Отмечаем риск потери точности при 6-бит де-квантовании и проверяем близость к ожидаемой гладкой кривой.
6. **Интерпретация:** вывод строится качественно — сохраняется ли порядок GPTQ>RTN на Phi-3 относительно LLaMA-2-7B-контроля, устойчиво ли по битностям. Числа LLaMA-контроля используются как калибр масштаба (насколько велики дельты «нормально»).

## 6. Feasibility

- **Запуск требует:** GPU ≥40 ГБ (батч eval + GPTQ-калибровка; веса Phi-3 fp16 ≈ 8 ГБ), сеть для кода/модели/датасетов/harness, pin-совместимый стек. Ожидаемый бюджет: LLaMA-контроль + 6 ячеек + бейзлайны ≈ < 1 GPU-day.
- **В текущей песочнице ничего не выполняется** — это дизайн: /workspace пуст (только task.json), ML-стека нет, GPU-драйвера нет, сети нет, системный Python 3.14; ресурсы — 224 CPU / 2 TiB RAM (CPU-прогон возможен только как отложенный fallback для PPL, но не для zero-shot/GPTQ-калибровки в разумные сроки). Все численные ориентиры — ожидания/из бумаги, не из прогонов.
- **Непроверяемое локально:** точные имена CLI-флагов квантизатора, поведение Хадамара для hidden 3072/head_dim 96, упаковка 6-бит — сверяются при первом доступе к репозиторию (зафиксировано в п.2 и разведочных оговорках).

## 7. Отчётная форма
Таблица 9 строк (6 ячеек + FP16-vanilla, FP16-rotated, INT8-ref) × (PPL-w2, PPL-c4, mean acc, 7 per-task accs, ΔPPL, Δacc) + строка контроля LLaMA-2-7B + итоговая качественная формулировка по правилу решения + список N/A и технических оговорок (6-бит, формат промпта, пины).

**Experiment design plan — QuaRot generalization to Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct (RTN vs GPTQ at 4/6/8-bit)**

## 1. Inspection findings (workspace)
- /workspace contains only `task.json` (question + context, design-only) and a `track.md` note that repositories/compute are not required. No project notes, no source files, no datasets present.
- Environment: no network, no GPU (224 CPU cores), system Python 3.14 with no torch/transformers/datasets/lm-eval installed. → Confirms this is a **design-only** task: the design must be specified from researcher clarifications on the six setup topics (setup_1, 3, 4, 6, 8, 11) plus established QuaRot conventions.

## 2. Proposed approach

**Fixed variables (independent settings)**
- Target model: `microsoft/Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct` (3.8B, instruct variant, 4k context).
- Bit-widths: **4, 6, 8** (weight-only quantization).
- Quantization pipelines: **QuaRot** (Hadamard rotations of residual stream + attention QK/PV) applied identically to BOTH methods, then weight quantization with:
  - **RTN** (round-to-nearest, per-channel weights, group size 128),
  - **GPTQ** (calibrated, group size 128, symmetric, 128×2048-token sequences from C4, seed-fixed).
- Controls:
  - **Primary baseline:** same checkpoint in FP16 (no rotation, no quantization) for both metrics — anchors "generalization" as degradation vs unquantized.
  - **Secondary control (optional, if budget allows):** RTN/GPTQ *without* rotations at each width, to isolate whether QuaRot's rotation benefit transfers to a non-LLAMA arch.

**Metrics (dependent variables)**
- **Perplexity:** WikiText-2 (test), non-sliding 2048-token context (per QuaRot convention), lower-is-better.
- **Zero-shot accuracy:** EleutherAI lm-eval harness over the QuaRot core set — **PIQA, ARC-easy, ARC-challenge, HellaSwag, Winogrande** — reported per-task + mean accuracy; optionally extended with LAMBADA, RTE, MathQA, if the researcher's source notes include them. For the instruct variant, use the chat template / multiturn mode as in the Phi-3 model card.

**Experimental matrix (7 conditions)**
`{FP16 baseline} ∪ {RTN, GPTQ} × {4, 6, 8}`.
Each condition: WikiText-2 PPL + zero-shot mean & per-task accuracy. GPTQ calibration run 2-3× with different seeds to report calibration-induced spread; RTN and baseline are deterministic single runs.

**Comparative analysis plan**
- Full results table (conditions × metrics).
- Per bit-width: ΔPPL and Δzero-shot (RTN vs GPTQ), identifying the better method and where they converge (expected larger spread at 4-bit, near-parity at 8-bit).
- Generalization index vs FP16 baseline: PPL-ratio (PPL_quant/PPL_fp16) and zero-shot accuracy drop (acc_fp16 − acc_quant), used to state how much quality Phi-3 loses at each width/method.
- External anchor: qualitatively compare these degradation ratios with published QuaRot numbers on Llama-2/3 to judge "does QuaRot generalize as well to Phi-3 as to LLAMA models".
- Feasibility checks noted in the design: Phi-3 config-name support in QuaRot rotation hooks, and GPTQ support at 6-bit (4/6/8-bit group-128 GPTQ is standard in gptqmodel/auto-gptq).

## 3. Assumptions
- One comparison per method/bit-width (no hyperparameter sweep beyond the fixed defaults above).
- Perplexity is measured on raw text (no chat template); chat templating only for zero-shot tasks.
- QuaRot rotation hyperparameters follow the paper defaults (Hadamard rotations, block size, etc.) to be confirmed against the setup topics.
- GPTQ calibration set = C4 (128 sequences × 2048 tokens), as in QuaRot/GPTQ; seed-fixed for reproducibility.

## 4. Uncertainties / questions to confirm via the six setup topics
1. (setup_1) Does the source fix a single model (Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct) or a multi-model sweep? Also confirm exact HF model ID and dtype.
2. (setup_3) What rotation configuration is fixed (Hadamard dimension, per-layer/global rotation, attention QK-PV handling) and is it shared verbatim across RTN and GPTQ?
3. (setup_4) Exact weight-quantization config: RTN (per-channel? group size?), GPTQ (group size 128? symmetric? blocksize? calibration n_samples/seq_len?).
4. (setup_6) Perplexity setup: dataset/split (WikiText-2 vs C4), context length, sliding vs non-sliding window.
5. (setup_8) Zero-shot config: which task set, lm-eval version, chat-template/multiturn handling for the instruct model, and whether to report mean of N tasks.
6. (setup_11) Any constraint on calibration data, seeds, or an instruction about reporting per-bit-width single method (RTN-XOR-GPTQ) that the design must respect?

I will finalize the full design after you confirm/correct these points.

payload.answer:
# Final Design — QuaRot Generalization to Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct: RTN vs GPTQ at INT4/INT6/INT8

## 0. Scope and design/execution boundary
This is a **design specification only**. No experiment has been run and no results are claimed. Every number from the QuaRot paper (Ashkboos et al., NeurIPS 2024) or model cards used below is a **published external reference**, employed solely as a qualitative/literary anchor — never as a measured output of this design. The document distinguishes design (what will be run and how analyzed) from execution (nothing run yet).

## 1. Research question (operationalized)
*How well does QuaRot generalize to a non-LLAMA model (Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct), and how do QuaRot-RTN and QuaRot-GPTQ compare in perplexity and zero-shot accuracy at 4-, 6-, and 8-bit?*

Operational definition: quantify per-condition **degradation against the FP16 baseline** (PPL-ratio and zero-shot accuracy drop) and compute **Δ-metrics between methods per bit-width**. Answer the question in terms of (a) absolute quality per method×width, (b) method ordering (which is better, and where they converge), and (c) whether the rotation benefit transfers to a non-LLAMA architecturally (via the optional non-rotated control and the literary comparison with published Llama results).

## 2. Fixed/independent variables
- **Model (single):** `microsoft/Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct` (3.8B, 4k context, instruct/chat variant). No multi-model sweep.
- **Precisions:** INT4, INT6, INT8 — weight-only quantization (activations kept FP16; QuaRot rotations already handle activation outliers).
- **Quantization pipelines:** **QuaRot-RTN** and **QuaRot-GPTQ**, with one **identical shared rotation configuration** applied to both methods (residual-stream rotation + attention QK/PV rotations, Hadamard, per source setup). The only difference between the two arms is the weight quantizer (RTN vs GPTQ).

## 3. Controls
- **Primary control (mandatory):** FP16 unquantized **same-checkpoint** model — no rotation, no quantization — evaluated identically on both metrics. This anchors "generalization" as degradation vs unquantized.
- **Secondary control (optional, conditional on budget, NOT mandatory):** RTN and GPTQ **without rotations** at each bit-width, to isolate the contribution of QuaRot's rotations for a non-LLAMA arch. If computed, placed in an appendix; its absence does not invalidate the core matrix.

## 4. Metrics protocol (confirmed)
- **Perplexity:** WikiText-2 **test** split, **no chat template**, **no sliding window**, **sequence length 2048** tokens. Compute mean tokenwise negative log-likelihood → exp(PPL). Lower is better.
- **Zero-shot accuracy:** EleutherAI **lm-eval** harness over the core set — **PIQA, ARC-easy, ARC-challenge, HellaSwag, Winogrande** — run in **chat/multiturn mode** for the instruct variant (per Phi-3 model-card convention / source setup). Report **per-task accuracy + mean accuracy** across the 5 tasks. Exact-match accuracy.

## 5. Experimental matrix and replication
- **7 core conditions:** `FP16` ∪ `{RTN, GPTQ} × {4,6,8}`.
- **GPTQ calibration:** C4, **128 sequences × 2048 tokens**, group size 128, symmetric, fixed quantizer hyperparameters; repeated with **2–3 calibration seeds**.
- **Per-seed recorded metrics (for GPTQ):** WikiText-2 PPL and each of the five zero-shot accuracies plus the 5-task mean. Thus every seed yields a full `{PPL, per-task acc, mean acc}` vector.
- **Summary rules:**
  - GPTQ cells report **mean ± range** across seeds for every metric (PPL and each accuracy).
  - RTN and FP16 are deterministic → single values.
- Resulting master table: rows = 7 conditions; columns = PPL, 5 per-task accuracies, mean accuracy (GPTQ rows show mean±range).

## 6. Comparative analysis plan
1. **Full results table** (Section 5) + condition-level PPL and mean-accuracy columns.
2. **Δ-metrics per bit-width (RTN vs GPTQ):**
   - ΔPPL = PPL_method(bit) − PPL_baseline (and PPL-ratio = PPL_quant/PPL_fp16);
   - Δzero-shot = acc_baseline − acc_method(bit);
   - state which method wins at each width, where they converge (expected: larger RTN/GPTQ gap at 4-bit, near-parity at 8-bit — stated as a hypothesis to test, not a result).
3. **Calibration-sensitivity:** use the GPTQ mean±range to judge whether seed spread is material at each bit-width (narrow at 8-bit, wider at 4-bit expected).
4. **Degradation indices (generalization indicators):** PPL-ratio and zero-shot accuracy drop vs FP16; lower ratio / smaller drop = better generalization of QuaRot to Phi-3 at that method×width.
5. **External anchor (qualitative, literary only):** compare derived degradation ratios and method ordering with **published QuaRot results on Llama-2/3** (papers/leaderboards). Frame strictly as "how Phi-3 behaves relative to published LLAMA trends"; never presented as measured data in this design.
6. **Optional appendix:** non-rotated control and chat-template sensitivity (single canonical template vs model-card default).

## 7. Feasibility / design notes (not execution)

Design assumes one suitable GPU or the CPU fallback noted; no runtime is executed here.

1. Master results table (7 conditions × PPL / per-task / mean metrics; GPTQ with mean±range).

# 实验设计方案（plan 阶段）

## 1. 仓库 / 输入检查结果

- `/workspace` 中**只有** `task.json`；`track.md` 明确指出"Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required"。**仓库中没有任何源码**（无 QuaRot 实现、无 RTN/GPTQ 脚本、无模型或数据），无 `/home/actor` 之外的内容。
- 运行环境事实：Python 3.14.4、pip 25.1.1；**未安装** torch/transformers/datasets/lm-eval-harness（`import torch` 失败）；**无 GPU**（nvidia-smi 无法连接驱动）；**network=disabled**；224 核 CPU、约 2TB 内存。
- 结论：本任务为纯设计任务。设计必须**明确指定**实验时要拉取的工程与依赖（QuaRot 官方仓库 `spcl/QuaRot`、`IST-DASLab/gptq`、`EleutherAI/lm-evaluation-harness`、HuggingFace Transformers），并需在联网环境中先行下载 `microsoft/Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct` 与评测/校准数据集并缓存（HF_HOME / 离线缓存），再在具备 ≥1 块 A100-40GB（或等效显存≥24GB）的 GPU 环境执行。

## 2. 方案概述（对比 RTN vs GPTQ，4/6/8-bit，QuaRot 泛化到 Phi-3）

**核心思路**：以 Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct 为被测模型，在 QuaRot 旋转框架下做权重量化；因子为
`方法{RTN, GPTQ} × 位宽{4,6,8} × 旋转{有 QuaRot, 无 QuaRot}` → 12 个量化配置 + FP16 全精度对照 = **13 个配置**（每配置 3 个量化随机种子）。

**（a）QuaRot 在 Phi-3 上的适配三步**：
1. 把 QuaRot 对 modeling 文件的修改移植到 `modeling_phi3.py`：残差流 Hadamard 旋转（嵌入输出、QKV/up/gate 输入融合、out_proj 与 lm_head 逆旋转、层内残差 R4 补偿块）、注意力 QK 的随机 Hadamard（RoPE 之后运行时施加）、V/PV 旋转。
2. **旋转正确性门控（关键内部对照）**：量化前先验证"旋转后 FP 输出"与原始 FP16 输出数值一致（容差 ~1e-3 NLL/逐层 cosine），证明移植正确 —— 这本身就是对"QuaRot 是否泛化到 Phi-3"在数值正确性层面的直接回答。
3. 再在旋转后的权重上运行 RTN / GPTQ。

**（b）量化与评测协议**：
- 权重量化：权重专用（weight-only，激活保持 FP16，便于隔离权重量化效应；此为口径选择，详见不确定性）；分组 per-group size=128、组内对称 signed 量化；GPTQ 用同样的分组与 bits（b=4/6/8，逐层 Hessian 校准）。
- GPTQ（及 QuaRot 若有旋转选择校准）校准集：C4（`allenai/c4`，English）子集 **128 条 × 2048 tokens**（与 QuaRot 论文默认一致），固定种子切分。
- 困惑度评测：WikiText-2 test 与 C4 held-out（1024/2048 token, stride，报告 tokenized PPL）。
- 零样本准确率：lm-eval-harness（0.4.x、确定性 seed）任务集取 **HellaSwag、ARC-easy、ARC-challenge、WinoGrande、PIQA、OpenbookQA**（QuaRot 论文同款子集），0-shot；instruct 模型按普通补全评测、不加对话模板。
- 批次：GPTQ 校准前向 batch=1（seqlen 2048）；PPL 评测 batch ≤4；lm-eval `--batch_size auto`。
- 随机种子：torch/numpy/校准数据顺序均固定；每配置 3 个量化种子取均值±std。

**（c）回答"泛化"的对照设计**：同样协议跑一个 **Llama-2-7B 控制模型**（或在报告中对齐 QuaRot 论文已发表的 Llama 数值），用"旋转带来 ΔPPL/Δacc 收益在 Phi-3 与 Llama 上的差距"来直接回答泛化性，而非只看 Phi-3 绝对数值。

**（d）报告口径**：13 配置的 PPL 表与各任务 acc 表；每配置附 4-bit 相对 FP16 的 ΔPPL 与 acc-drop；注明每个配置的显存与时间预算。

## 3. 关键假设与不确定性（需在完整设计里显式写出）

- **假设 A**：Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct 的组件（RMSNorm、RoPE 类旋转、SiLU、GQA、tied embedding）与 QuaRot 的旋转方案兼容 —— 这需在下载 config 时核实。
- **不确定性 1（架构细节）**：`num_key_value_heads`（疑为 4）、`tie_word_embeddings`（疑为 true）、激活函数（silu vs gelu）、以及 **Phi-3 的 RoPE 是否带 `rope_scaling(longrope)`**（128k 变体必有，4k-instruct 的 config 也需核实）—— 直接决定 QuaRot 的 QK Hadamard 与旋转融合代码能否照搬。以上需以 HF registry 的 config 为准。
- **不确定性 2（工程泛化性）**：QuaRot 官仓只带 Llama/Mistral 修改文件，**移植到 Phi-3 是需要写代码的真工程步骤**，也是"泛化"问题的真正载体；旋转正确性门控正是为它设计的。
- **不确定性 3（指标口径）**：是否仅权重量化（vs QuaRot 论文的权重+KV/激活量化）；PPL 的 stride/seqlen；是否对 instruct 模型使用对话模板。设计中选择"权重-only、普通补全、无模板"，与问题"RTN vs GPTQ 的位宽对比"对齐。
- **不确定性 4（校准集选择）**：选择 C4（与 QuaRot 一致）而非 WikiText/RedPajama；需在报告中说明校准集与评测集重合度风险。
- **不确定性 5（计算预算）**：当前环境无 GPU/网络，最终实验必须在具备 A100-40GB 类硬件且联网的环境运行；设计需给出每配置预算。

1) 口径：明确本设计为权重专用（weight-only）量化协议，激活/KV 保持 FP16；并说明这是隔离"RTN vs GPTQ 的位宽效应"的有意选择，而非 QuaRot 原生"权重+激活/KV 全量化"口径——后者超出本问题范围。
2) 旋转正确性门控：将"旋转后 FP 输出与原始 FP16 输出数值一致（如逐层 cosine≥阈值、NLL 差≤1e-3）"作为移植成功的接受标准；若门控失败，则视为 QuaRot 对 Phi-3 不适配的直接证据，并记录故障点。
3) 架构核验：把 num_key_value_heads、tie_word_embeddings、激活函数、是否含 longrope rope_scaling 列为"以下载到的 HF config 为准"的运行时核实项；INT6 的具体实现机制（分组对称手写量化，非 bitsandbytes 原生）需写明。
4) 可行性：为每个配置给出 A100-40GB 下的显存与时间预算；说明 Phi-3-mini（约3.8B）与 Llama-2-7B 控制组存在规模差异，ΔPPL/Δacc 的比较需标注这一点；Llama 控制组可依据 QuaRot 已发表数值对比，全量重跑为可选。
5) 分析计划：给出 13 配置的汇总表格式、Δ 指标定义、3 种子均值±std、以及 GPTQ 校准集（C4, 128×2048）与评测集重叠风险的说明。

请按交付物要求产出最终实验设计（含 rationale、controls、analysis plan、feasibility），不虚构任何已执行实验。

payload.answer:
# 最终实验设计：QuaRot 对非 Llama 模型（Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct）的泛化性 —— RTN vs GPTQ 在 4/6/8-bit 下的困惑度与零样本准确率

> 本文件为**实验设计文档**，未执行任何实验，未虚构任何结果。设计与固定要求对应：setup_1（模型 = Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct）、setup_6（权重位宽 = INT4/INT6/INT8）、setup_8/setup_11（对比 QuaRot-RTN 与 QuaRot-GPTQ）。

---

## 1. 研究问题与目标

Q：QuaRot 的"旋转+量化"方案在非 Llama 架构（Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct）上能否同样生效？在 4/6/8-bit 下，RTN 与 GPTQ 的困惑度（PPL）和零样本准确率如何对比？

设计目标（按可验证性拆分）：
- **G1（正确性/泛化门控）**：旋转本身在 Phi-3 上是否数值正确（量化前 FP 输出不变）。
- **G2（位宽效应）**：权重-only 下 INT4/6/8 的 PPL 与零样本 acc。
- **G3（方法对比）**：同一旋转与位宽下 RTN vs GPTQ 的差异。
- **G4（旋转收益）**：有/无旋转两臂的差异量（QuaRot 在 Phi-3 上的增益），并对照 Llama-2 已发表数值回答"泛化到非 Llama 模型的强弱"。

---

## 2. 固定口径（第 1 项固定要求）

- **权重专用（weight-only）量化协议**：仅对线性层权重（q/k/v/o_proj、up/gate/down_proj、lm_head）做分组整数量化；**激活与 KV 缓存全程保持 FP16**。
- 这是**有意的口径选择**，用于隔离"RTN vs GPTQ 在位宽下的量化质量"这一自变量，避免把"激活/KV 量化噪声"与"权重位宽效应"混淆。QuaRot 论文原生采用的"权重+激活/KV 全量化"口径（含 4-bit KV、4-bit 激活）**超出本问题范围**，故不采用；本设计只在权重维度检验 QuaRot 旋转的收益。此口径在结论中不得回推成 QuaRot 全量化端到端性能。

### 2.1 量化实现（含 INT6 机制，第 3 项固定要求）

**统一的分组对称整数方案（RTN 与 GPTQ 共用，保证可比）**：
- 分组 size `g = 128`（沿输入通道方向每组 128 个权重）；`per-channel=True`（每输出通道一个 scale）之外的组内尺度为 `scale = absmax / (2^(b-1) − 1)`，**对称、无零点（zero-point=0）**。
- 量化/反量化在 **PyTorch 纯张量算子**中手写实现（向量化按组计算 scale → `round(w/scale)` → `w_q*scale`），**INT6 与 INT8 均不依赖 bitsandbytes**（其原生仅支持 4/8），采用同一条手写分组对称路径，仅 `b ∈ {4,6,8}` 不同。这保证 6-bit 与 4/8-bit 机制完全一致、可复现。
- **RTN**：直接 round-to-nearest，无需校准。
- **GPTQ**：采用 IST-DASLab/gptq 实现，固定 `bits ∈ {4,6,8}`、`groupsize=128`、`sym=True`、`perchannel=True`、`desc_act=True`（与 QuaRot 默认一致）；逐层、用校准集 Hessian 与误差补偿。同一位宽下 RTN/GPTQ 的组结构与位宽口径完全一致。

---

## 3. QuaRot 适配与"旋转正确性门控"（第 2 项固定要求）

### 3.1 适配步骤
1. 从 `spcl/QuaRot` 官仓获取旋转插入逻辑，移植到 `modeling_phi3.py`：残差流 Hadamard 旋转（嵌入输出融合、QKV/up/gate 输入侧融合权重、out_proj 与 lm_head 逆旋转、层内残差方向 R4 补偿块）、注意力 QK 随机 Hadamard（RoPE **之后**运行时施加）、V/PV 侧 Hadamard。
2. 若 Phi-3 config 含 `rope_scaling(longrope)`，按长 rope 实现校验 QK Hadamard 的插入位置与该 RoPE 变体是否兼容（见 §4 核实项）。
3. **旋转正确性门控（量化前的接受标准）**，在独立于校准的 32 条 C4 序列上比较"旋转后 FP 模型"与"原始 FP16 模型"：
   - 逐 transformer 层输出余弦相似度 **≥ 0.999**；
   - 末端 NLL 差 **≤ 1e-3**。
   - **若门控失败 → 直接判定 QuaRot 对 Phi-3 不适配**，记录首个失败层/模块（如 RoPE/QK 插入点、tied embedding 旋转、R4 残差补偿）作为"非泛化"证据，并**停止**该旋转臂的量化评测（在报告中以"adapter failed + 故障点"呈现，不产生量化数值）。
   - 门控通过 → 继续量化；量化噪声造成的数值差异与门控差异严格区分开。

### 3.2 架构核实清单（第 3 项固定要求，以下载到的 HF config 为准）
运行时从 `microsoft/Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct/config.json` 与 `modeling_phi3.py` 逐一核实并写入报告：
- `num_key_value_heads`（GQA 头数，疑为 4）；
- `tie_word_embeddings`（疑为 true，影响嵌入/lm_head 联动旋转）；
- 激活函数（silu vs gelu）；
- 是否存在 `rope_scaling`（如 `longrope`，128k 变体必有，4k 变体待核实）；
- 附带：`hidden_size=3072`、`intermediate_size=8192`、`num_hidden_layers=32`、`num_attention_heads=32`、`head_dim`、`rms_norm_eps`、全连接无 bias。

---

## 4. 评测协议

- **困惑度**：WikiText-2 test（tokenized，seqlen=2048，stride=2048）；C4 held-out（从 C4 train 取与校准**不相交**的 1000 条 × 2048 tokens，stride=2048）。
- **零样本准确率**：lm-eval-harness（0.4.x，确定性 seed）0-shot，任务 = **HellaSwag、ARC-easy、ARC-challenge、WinoGrande、PIQA、OpenbookQA**；instruct 模型按普通补全评测，**不加对话模板**（口径统一，避免模板引入额外方差）。
- **校准集（GPTQ）**：C4（`allenai/c4`，English）subset **128 条 × 2048 tokens**，按量化种子固定切分（seed 0/1/42 对应不同偏移块）。
- **随机性与批次**：torch/numpy/校准序列顺序均固定；GPTQ 校准前向 batch=1（seqlen 2048）；PPL 评测 batch≤4；lm-eval `--batch_size auto`。量化种子 3 个（0,1,42）。

---

## 5. 配置表（13 个，第 5 项固定要求的分析基础）

| # | 配置 | 旋转 | 位宽 | 说明 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | FP16 | — | 16 | 天花板参考 |
| 2–4 | RTN-4/6/8 | 无 | 4/6/8 | 无旋转臂（隔离旋转收益） |
| 5–7 | GPTQ-4/6/8 | 无 | 4/6/8 | 无旋转臂 |
| 8–10 | **QuaRot+RTN-4/6/8** | 有 | 4/6/8 | 主臂（setup_8） |
| 11–13 | **QuaRot+GPTQ-4/6/8** | 有 | 4/6/8 | 主臂（setup_11） |

每个量化配置×3 个量化种子；旋转数值门控只做一次（确定性操作）。若门控失败，仅报告故障点（§3.1）。

---

## 6. 指标与 Δ 定义（第 5 项固定要求）

- `PPL(c)`：tokenized 困惑度（WikiText-2 与 C4 分开）。
- `acc(c)`：每任务准确率及 6 任务均值 `mean_acc(c)`。
- `ΔPPL_c(c) = PPL(c) − PPL(FP16)`（另报相对百分比 `(PPL(c)−PPL(FP16))/PPL(FP16)`）。
- `Δacc(c) = mean_acc(FP16) − mean_acc(c)`。
- 旋转收益：`RotΔPPL(m,b) = PPL(QuaRot+m-b) − PPL(m-b 无旋转)`；`RotΔacc` 同理（**泛化性的核心指标**）。
- 方法对比：同一旋转+位宽下 `PPL(RTN-b) − PPL(GPTQ-b)` 等。
- 每组 `mean ± std`（3 种子）；lm-eval 任务级也报 3 种子间 std。
- 13 行 × (PPL_wiki, PPL_c4, 6×acc, mean_acc, ΔPPL, Δacc, 显存GB, 耗时min) 汇总表。

### 校准/评测集重叠风险（明确说明）
- C4 评测块与 GPTQ 校准块在**样本索引上不相交**（校准取 seed 对应块、评测取固定偏移块 [10000:10000+1000]），并将重叠检查（索引交集=∅）计入校验脚本。
- 残余风险：C4 评测与 C4 校准**同分布**（同数据集两段），可能轻微高估"旋转+校准"在 C4 上的表现；故以 **WikiText-2（分布外）为主指标**，C4 held-out 为辅助，报告同时给两者并说明此风险。

---

## 7. 分析计划（第 5 项固定要求）

1. **门控报告**：旋转后逐层 cosine、NLL 差；通过/失败及故障点。
2. **主表**：§6 汇总表（13 配置 × 3 种子均值±std）。
3. **位宽趋势**：INT4→6→8 的 ΔPPL/Δacc 单调性（RTN 与 GPTQ 分别）。
4. **方法对比**：QuaRot 下 GPTQ vs RTN 在各位宽的差距及 4-bit 时是否显著（种子间 std 是否重叠）。
5. **旋转收益**：`RotΔPPL/RotΔacc`；与 Llama-2-7B 的 QuaRot 论文发表值对比，**显式标注两模型规模差（~3.8B vs 7B）**，只作定性趋势对照；Llama 全量重跑为可选增强（可加一列同协议 Llama-2-7B 数值，成本约 2–3×）。
6. **结论口径**：分别回答 G1–G4；明确 weight-only 口径的边界（不推及 QuaRot 全量化）。

---

## 8. 可行性（A100-40GB 单卡预算，第 4 项固定要求）

- 模型规模：Phi-3-mini ~3.8B → FP16 权重 ~7.6GB；weight-only 下推理时反量化回 FP16，激活仍 FP16，**权重驻留显存约 8/6/4-bit 分别为 ~3.8/2.9/1.9GB（压缩）+ 前向激活开销**；GPTQ 逐层校准（batch1×2048）Hessian 与层权重均在单层规模，A100-40GB 全程充裕。
- 每配置耗时（单卡 A100-40GB，估算上限）：门控一次 ~15min；RTN 量化 ~5min；GPTQ 校准 ~40–60min；PPL（Wiki+C4）~20–30min；lm-eval 6 任务 ~30–45min。**单配置 ≤ ~2h，13 配置 × 每配置 3 种子（量化种子仅影响量化与 PPL/acc 评测，需重复评测）合计约 1.5–2 个 GPU·日**（门控与校准数据准备不计入重复）。
- 当前本机环境（Python 3.14.4、无 torch、无 GPU、network disabled、无现成源码/模型/数据）**不能运行**本设计；执行需在联网 + A100-40GB 类环境，先下载并缓存模型、C4/WikiText-2、lm-eval 数据集。**本任务仅交付设计，未运行任何实验。**

---

## 9. Rationale（设计理由）
- **weight-only**：让"RTN vs GPTQ 的位宽效应"成为唯一量化自变量，避免激活/KV 量化混淆主对比；
- **有/无旋转双臂**：把"旋转是否正确（泛化性）"与"位宽量化质量"解耦，前者由 G1 门控、后者由 G2/G3 量化对比回答；
- **旋转数值门控**：若不做，则"旋转破坏数值"与"量化劣化"无法区分——门控是泛化性判断的必要内部对照；
- **C4 128×2048 校准 + WikiText-2/C4 评测**：与 QuaRot/GPTQ 论文惯例一致，才能与 Llama 已发表数字直接对照；
- **GPTQ/RTN 同组结构（groupsize=128, sym）**：消除实现差异，使方法间对比归因于"是否有 Hessian 校准与误差补偿"。

## 10. Controls（对照设计）
- FP16 天花板（上限参考）；
- 旋转数值门控（正确性内部对照）；
- 无旋转臂（旋转收益归因）；
- Llama-2-7B 已发表 QuaRot 数值作为外部基准（可选同协议重跑）；
- 无对话模板、固定种子、校准/评测 C4 段不相交、两方法同 `groupsize=128/sym` 口径。

=========================================================================
EXPERIMENT DESIGN (FINAL, DESIGN-ONLY)
Title: Evaluating QuaRot Generalization to Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct:
Comparing QuaRot-RTN vs QuaRot-GPTQ at INT4/INT6/INT8
=========================================================================

0. DOCUMENT STATUS (honesty clause)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
This is a DESIGN-ONLY submission. No experiment was executed in the
sandbox, no results are reported, and no claim of completed runs is made.
The sandbox contains only task.json (track.md: "Design-only task;
repositories and compute are not required"); verified repository findings
and environment facts are stated in Section 2, and every repo-specific
detail is explicitly flagged as an ASSUMPTION TO VERIFY, never as an
observed fact.

=========================================================================
1. RESEARCH QUESTION AND RATIONALE
=========================================================================
Question (fixed by brief):
"HOW WELL DOES QUAROT GENERALIZE TO NON-LLAMA MODELS LIKE
Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct? How do RTN and GPTQ compare in perplexity and
zero-shot accuracy across 4-bit, 6-bit, and 8-bit quantization?"

Rationale: QuaRot (NeurIPS 2024) removes activation/weight outliers by
applying random Hadamard rotations to the input/weight subspaces before
quantization, then produces quantized weights. Its published validation
is on LLaMA-class models, whose architecture (rotary embedding layout,
QKV head structure, hidden sizes) is a known precondition for the
rotation placement. Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct (3.8B, Phi3ForCausalLM) is a
non-LLaMA model: it shares a similar overall decoder design but has its
own rotary-embedding implementation, QK-norm, different head/hidden
dims (hidden 3072, 32 heads, 64 head_dim) and vocabulary (32064). The
design therefore tests two things in one experiment:
  (a) GENERALIZATION: does QuaRot's rotation+quantizer pipeline transfer
      to a model it was not validated on, measured against an FP16
      reference and against NON-rotated (plain) quantizers?
  (b) QUANTIZER COMPARISON: within the QuaRot pipeline, is the weight
      quantizer (RTN vs GPTQ) still the main accuracy driver, and does
      the gap behave systematically across INT4/INT6/INT8?

By holding rotation configuration and activation precision fixed, the
RTN-vs-GPTQ comparison isolates the weight-quantization choice,
which is exactly the contrast the question asks about.

=========================================================================
2. VERIFIED REPOSITORY & ENVIRONMENT STATE (OBSERVED FACTS ONLY)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
From direct inspection of the sandbox:
  - /workspace contains exactly one file: task.json. There is NO QuaRot
    codebase, README, config, script, or dataset artifact present.
  - Searches for "94328", "*qua*", ".git" directories, and Python files
    outside system libs found nothing relevant. No model/dataset caches.
  - Environment: Python 3.14.4; NO torch/transformers/datasets/
    accelerate/lm-eval-harness/GPTQ packages installed.
  - No GPU (gpu_enabled=false; 224 CPU cores); network unreachable
    (/dev/tcp to 8.8.8.8 failed: "Network is unreachable").
Consequence (already accepted by the researcher): the design below is
written for a provisioning environment; all specifics of the real
spcl/QuaRot repo are ASSUMPTIONS (Section 8) to be verified against the
official repository when it is available, not observed facts.

=========================================================================
3. FIXED REQUIREMENTS vs PROPOSED CHOICES
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
FIXED BY THE BRIEF (not negotiable):
  F1  Model: Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct
  F2  Precisions: INT4, INT6, INT8
  F3  Methods: QuaRot-RTN, QuaRot-GPTQ
  F4  Metrics: perplexity and zero-shot accuracy

PROPOSED BY THIS DESIGN (researcher-adjustable, stated explicitly):
  P1  6+2 zero-shot tasks: ARC-easy, ARC-challenge, HellaSwag, PIQA,
      Winogrande, BoolQ (task accuracy + macro-average).
  P2  PPL corpus: WikiText-2 test (sliding-window stride, seqlen 2048).
  P3  Calibration: fixed 128-sample/2048-token subset, seeded document
      selection, percdamp 0.01, groupsize 128; corpus matched to the
      target repo's datautils loader (C4 'en' default, else WikiText-2
      train split) — and NEVER the same split used for PPL evaluation.
  P4  Replication: >=3 seeds per target cell (GPTQ is order/seed
      dependent; RTN is deterministic but run under matched seed parity).
  P5  Primary comparison is WEIGHT-ONLY (activations full precision):
      this isolates the weight quantizer. W8A8 (QuaRot activation
      quantization) is a clearly SECONDARY, optional robustness layer,
      not part of the headline claim.
  P6  Group size 128, true-sequential (repo default) quantization order.

=========================================================================
4. EXPERIMENTAL CONDITIONS AND CONTROLS
=========================================================================
4.1 Conditions table
  ID   | Type                       | Method            | Bits | Notes
  -----|----------------------------|-------------------|------|-------
  R0   | Reference (control)        | None (FP16)      | 16   | upper bound
  C4-R | Target cell (fixed req.)   | QuaRot-RTN        | 4    | rot+RTN
  C6-R | Target cell (fixed req.)   | QuaRot-RTN        | 6    | rot+RTN
  C8-R | Target cell (fixed req.)   | QuaRot-RTN        | 8    | rot+RTN
  C4-G | Target cell (fixed req.)   | QuaRot-GPTQ       | 4    | rot+GPTQ
  C6-G | Target cell (fixed req.)   | QuaRot-GPTQ       | 6    | rot+GPTQ
  C8-G | Target cell (fixed req.)   | QuaRot-GPTQ       | 8    | rot+GPTQ
  P4-R | Rotation-isolation control | Plain-RTN   (no rot) | 4 | proposed
  P8-R | Rotation-isolation control | Plain-RTN   (no rot) | 8 | proposed
  P4-G | Rotation-isolation control | Plain-GPTQ  (no rot) | 4 | proposed
  P8-G | Rotation-isolation control | Plain-GPTQ  (no rot) | 8 | proposed

  6 target cells (F2,F3) + FP16 reference (P-baseline) + 4 plain-quantizer
  controls (P-controls). Plain controls at 6-bit are redundant for the
  isolation question (rotation benefit is demonstrated at 4-bit and 8-bit),
  so they are omitted to save compute; this is a proposed scope decision.

4.2 Controls logic
  - FP16 reference (R0): every metric is expressed relative to R0, which
    neutralizes instruct-checkpoint quirks (instruct PPL runs slightly
    higher than base-ckpt PPL; all conditions share this constant).
  - Rotation-isolation controls (P4/8-*): identical quantizer configs with
    --rotate OFF. The delta (QuaRot - plain) at the same bitwidth isolates
    the value-add of Hadamard rotation; this is a sanity check that the
    4-bit headline numbers are not driven purely by the quantizer.
  - Protocol controls: identical calibration documents/order, identical
    seeds, identical eval scripts, identical lm-eval harness version,
    identical seqlen/stride, same GPU + torch settings across ALL rows.

4.3 Activation quantization scope (secondary layer)
  - Headline claim is derived from the weight-only table above (P5).
  - Optionally, repeat the 6 target cells + R0 with QuaRot's 8-bit
    activation quantization (W4A8/W6A8/W8A8), reported in a separate
    appendix table and NEVER merged into the headline RTN-vs-GPTQ claim.

=========================================================================
5. CALIBRATION PROTOCOL (GPTQ path; RTN for parity)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
  - Corpus: MUST match the target repo's datautils loader. Default
    expectation: C4 'en' (the GPTQ/QuaRot default); fallback: WikiText-2
    train split. Confirm which the repo uses (ASSUMPTION A3).
  - Size: fixed subset of 128 sequences, truncated/padded to seqlen 2048
    tokens (repo --nsamples 128, --seqlen 2048 conventions).
  - Seeded document selection: shuffle the corpus index with torch.Generator
    seeded by the replication seed BEFORE slicing the 128 docs, so each
    GPTQ seed quantizes a different-but-reproducible doc subset (order is
    what drives GPTQ variance).
  - Quantizer hyperparameters (fixed): --wbits 4|6|8, --groupsize 128,
    --percdamp 0.01, --true-sequential on (repo default), rotation ON for
    target cells, OFF for plain controls.
  - RTN parity: RTN is data-independent, but each R-cell is launched under
    the SAME process/seed initialization as its G-cell counterpart so that
    RNG state differences cannot confound paired comparisons.
  - Split hygiene: calibration split (C4 'en' or WikiText-2 TRAIN) must be
    disjoint from the PPL evaluation split (WikiText-2 TEST). If the repo
    defaults calibration to Wikitext-2, calibration must use the train
    split only; the test split is reserved strictly for evaluation.
  - Reproducibility record: log exact calibration corpus, doc indices,
    seed, percdamp, groupsize, seqlen, and the repo commit hash.

=========================================================================
6. EVALUATION PROTOCOL
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
6.1 Perplexity
  - Corpus: WikiText-2 TEST split (P2).
  - Method: standard GPTQ/HF sliding-window evaluation, seqlen 2048,
    stride such that documents are evaluated with overlapping windows
    (e.g., stride = seqlen - 256; the exact repo convention is used);
    report token-normalized model loss converted to PPL = exp(loss).
  - Output: single mean PPL per (condition, seed).

6.2 Zero-shot accuracy
  - Harness: lm-eval-harness, PINNED version (proposed 0.4.x line; the
    pinned version must match whatever the repo declares — ASSUMPTION A4).
  - Tasks (P1): ARC-easy, ARC-challenge, HellaSwag, PIQA, Winogrande,
    BoolQ. Report each task's standard accuracy metric (and acc_norm where
    the harness defines it: HellaSwag, Winogrande, ARC).
  - Instruct-model handling: NO chat template; plain causal-LM
    continuation via HF AutoTokenizer, as in QuaRot's own eval.
  - Output: per-task accuracy per (condition, seed) + macro-average across
    the 6 tasks.

6.3 Shared harness/eval settings across ALL conditions (including FP16)
  - Same harness version, same task configs, same batch/tokenizer,
    same seqlen; only the checkpoint differs. This makes all comparisons
    relative-safe even if absolute numbers differ from published ones.

=========================================================================
7. ANALYSIS AND AGGREGATION PLAN
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
7.1 Per-cell summary
  - For each cell: mean and SD over >=3 seeds of (a) WikiText-2 PPL,
    (b) per-task accuracy, (c) task macro-average.
7.2 Primary comparisons (weight-only table)
  - Delta PPL:  dPPL(cell) = PPL(cell) - PPL(FP16);
    relative increase rPPL(cell) = PPL(cell)/PPL(FP16) - 1. Lower is better.
  - Accuracy: report per-task accuracy and macro-average; higher is better.
7.3 Paired RTN vs GPTQ (matched seeds)
  - For each bit b in {4,6,8}: paired difference (QuaRot-RTN - QuaRot-GPTQ)
    over the same seeds for PPL (lower RTN = better) and for accuracy.
    Report mean paired delta and, with n>=3 seeds, a paired t-test or
    Wilcoxon signed-rank as an EXPLORATORY statistic (small n; interpret
    cautiously, treat as descriptive evidence, not a definitive NHST).
7.4 Monotonicity check across bits
  - Verify, within each method, that rPPL decreases and macro-accuracy
    increases (or is flat) as bits go 4 -> 6 -> 8, converging to the FP16
    reference. The 6-bit point is the informative intermediate: it tests
    whether 6-bit closes most of the 4-bit gap and whether RTN at 6-bit
    approaches GPTQ at 6-bit.
7.5 Rotation sanity check
  - Compare QuaRot-* vs plain-* at 4-bit and 8-bit for both PPL and
    accuracy. Expectation to be tested (not assumed as result): rotation
    improves 4-bit PPL/accuracy substantially, more for RTN than GPTQ
    (GPTQ already handles outliers better), and the benefit shrinks at

9. FEASIBILITY AND RUNTIME REQUIREMENTS (PROVISIONED ENVIRONMENT)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
Required runtime (the design targets this; it does NOT run in this sandbox):
  - GPU: >=24GB VRAM (Phi-3-mini fp16 weights ~7.6GB + calibration

payload.answer:
PLAN — "Using autocorrelation (ACF) to identify the optimal cycle length P for CycleNet time series forecasting"

1) REPO FINDINGS
- /workspace contains only task.json (the question + a note that this is design-only; track.md is referenced but not present).
- No datasets in the workspace, no network, and NO scientific Python packages installed (numpy/scipy/pandas/torch/statsmodels all missing; Python 3.14.4 system only, 224 CPUs, no GPU). Any future execution therefore requires either a pre-provisioned environment + datasets or a decision to rely on synthetic data. This design is written to be executable in principle under those conditions.

2) PROPOSED APPROACH OUTLINE (answer = does ACF-picked P match the best-performing P)
The hypothesis has two coupled claims: (a) ACF identifies the true dominant periodicity P* of the data; (b) running CycleNet with P=P* is optimal (or near-optimal) on held-out forecasting error. The experiment tests both in sequence:

Step A — Automatic cycle detection (pure ACF, no model):
- For each training series, compute the sample autocorrelation at lags 1..L (L = lookback, capped ~200 for speed), on detrended/differenced data to make periodicity the dominant stationary signal.
- Identify candidate cycle lengths as lags where ACF is a local maximum AND exceeds a significance band (Bartlett 95% CI ≈ ±1.96/sqrt(n)); the smallest such lag is the fundamental period; integer multiples appear as secondary peaks.
- Aggregate across series: average per-lag ACF across all series (and across variates) → dataset-level ACF profile; pick the top-k candidate lags (e.g., k=5) per dataset, ranked by mean ACF.
- Sanity check against ground truth: for data with known periodicity (synthetic + real benchmarks with documented seasonal periods), verify the top candidate matches P*.

Step B — Model validation (CycleNet with chosen P vs. alternatives):
- For each dataset, run CycleNet with:
   (i)  P = autocorrelation-derived candidate (top-1),
   (ii) P = default frequency-based value (e.g., 24 hourly, 24 traffic, 24 weather-10min... i.e., the paper's convention),
   (iii) a sweep over a P-range (e.g., all integer candidates around the ACF peak: P ∈ {P*-2..P*+2} plus common alternatives like daily vs weekly 168) to build a performance-vs-P curve,
   (iv) a non-cycle control (RCF disabled / P=0) to show the cycle module itself helps.
- Compare held-out MSE/MAE across multiple seeds; check that the ACF-picked P sits at/near the minimum of the P-sweep curve (i.e., ACF ranks candidates in the same order as test error). Report rank-correlation (Kendall's tau) between ACF magnitude at lag P and CycleNet error at P as a quantitative "does ACF predict the best P" measure.
- Statistical check: ACF-P vs default-P via paired comparison across seeds (e.g., Wilcoxon signed-rank) when differences are small.

3) KEY DESIGN CHOICES
- Data: (a) synthetic controllable series — AR + sinusoids + noise with known true P (validates the ACF→P* recovery step unambiguously); (b) 2–3 real benchmark datasets with known dominant periodicities: e.g., ETTh1 (hourly, daily P=24 / weekly 168), ETTm1 (15-min, daily P=96), Electricity (hourly, day+week), and optionally M4 subsets (daily/monthly/quarterly) to cover multiple frequencies. Choice matters because the ACF method is only meaningful where seasonality dominates; we deliberately pick such data.
- Horizon: the CycleNet benchmark suite: {96, 192, 336, 720} for ETT/Electricity; fixed short horizons for M4. Lookback L=336 (needs L ≥ 2·P to support RCF, and also L ≥ max candidate P).
- How P feeds the model: P is the integer cycle length of the Residual Cycle Forecasting (RCF) module — a shared learnable cycle token of length P indexed by (t mod P); residual target y_t − y_{t−P}. So P must be an integer ≥1, must satisfy L ≥ 2P, and must be constant per dataset (one P per dataset, not per series).
- Evaluation metric: MSE and MAE (the standard CycleNet metrics); optionally symmetric-MAPE for M4. Report mean±std over 3–5 seeds.
- Baselines: CycleNet(default P) and CycleNet(ACF P) as the head-to-head; P-sweep as the landscape; RCF-off as the ablation control; report against published CycleNet numbers as an external sanity anchor if datasets permit.
- Controls: identical seeds, lookback, horizon, optimiser and epoch budget for all P variants so the only differing variable is P.

4) KEY ASSUMPTIONS & UNCERTAINTIES
- A1 (fixed-P): CycleNet expects ONE fixed integer cycle length per dataset; our design must pick a single P, and RCF constrains L ≥ 2P. Multiple periodicities (e.g., 24 vs 168 for ETT) force a choice — we define "optimal" as the P minimising held-out error, and test whether ACF ranks 24 vs 168 correctly.
- A2 (dominant seasonality): ACF-based detection assumes the data is periodic/stationary enough that the dominant ACF peak is the driving pattern; heavily trend/non-stationary or noisy data breaks recovery (mitigated by detrending/differencing and by choosing seasonal benchmark data).
- A3 (aggregation): pooling ACF across variates assumes the dataset shares one dominant period; per-series heterogeneity within a multivariate set is a source of error (uncertainty, to be reported per dataset).
- U1 (resources): no GPU, no installed deps, no network, no datasets — actual execution is infeasible in this exact environment. Design assumes a provisioned runtime with torch + datasets, or falls back to a fully synthetic proof-of-concept runnable with pure-Python/pip-installed numpy. Runtime is the main constraint: full ETTh/Electricity training with multiple P values × seeds is expensive on CPU; mitigate with epoch limits, single-seed sweeps + 3-seed head-to-head, and subsampled training sets.
- U2 (ACF vs other signals): the question restricts the method to autocorrelation; FFT/periodogram is a possible cross-check but not required for the core answer.
- U3 (definition of "optimal"): "optimal cycle length" is measured as best held-out MSE/MAE; if ties are common, we evaluate whether the ACF-picked P lands within the statistical-noise band of the best P rather than exactly at the argmin.

FINAL DESIGN DOCUMENT
====================================================================
Title: Using autocorrelation (ACF) analysis to identify the optimal cycle length P for CycleNet in time series forecasting
Status: Design-only deliverable (no execution performed)

====================================================================
1. OBJECTIVES AND HYPOTHESIS
====================================================================
Primary objective: Determine whether, and how reliably, sample autocorrelation analysis can select the cycle length P for CycleNet that produces the best (lowest) held-out forecast error, where "optimal cycle length" is *operationally defined* as the P minimising validation MSE/MAE.

The question decomposes into two coupled hypotheses that the design tests separately:
  H1 (detection): The dominant peak(s) of the sample autocorrelation function (ACF) recover the true dominant periodicity P* of a dataset. Validated against synthetic data with KNOWN P (unambiguous ground truth) and against benchmarks with documented seasonal periods.
  H2 (optimality): Running CycleNet with P = ACF-derived candidate yields held-out error that is statistically indistinguishable from (within a noise band of) the best P found by a full P-sweep, and is no worse than the default frequency-based P. Quantified via a P-sweep error curve plus a rank-correlation check that ACF magnitude order predicts error order.
  H3 (mechanism/ablation): The cycle module itself is what delivers the improvement (RCF-on vs RCF-off), so that attributing the result to a correctly chosen P is valid.

Success criteria (pre-registered, per dataset):
  S1. ACF-picked P equals the true P* on synthetic data in ≥ 95% of generated datasets.
  S2. ACF-picked P has validation MSE/MAE within the noise band (mean ± 1 SE over seeds) of the sweep argmin, AND beats or ties default-P with error reduction ≥ 1% on average.
  S3. Kendall's tau_b between (ACF magnitude at P) and (CycleNet error at P) is negative and significant at p<0.05, or at minimum the ACF-picked P is among the top-2 ranked candidates by error.
  S4. RCF-on beats RCF-off on the same data/horizon (isolating the value of the cycle module).

====================================================================
2. DATA SELECTION AND RATIONALE
====================================================================
Rationale: ACF-based detection is only meaningful when periodicity dominates any trend/irregular component, so we deliberately select (a) synthetic data with known ground-truth P, and (b) real benchmarks with documented seasonal periods.

2.1 Synthetic data (validates H1 unambiguously)
Generators (seeded, 10 replicates per configuration, ~2000–10000 points each, univariate):
  - Seasonal AR/pseudo-AR: x_t = c + Σ_j a_j·sin(2π·t/P_j + φ_j) + ε_t, noise levels ε ~ N(0, σ²) with SNR ∈ {2, 5, 10}.
  - Deterministic seasonal with trend: x_t = linear trend + seasonal + AR(2) noise.
  - Stochastic seasonal (SAR-like): x_t = φ·x_{t−P} + ε_t.
  Configurations with single period P ∈ {6, 12, 24, 48, 96, 168} (to span daily/weekly patterns) and double-period variants (e.g., P1=24 with P2=168) to test multiple-periodicity ranking.
Role: the ONLY place where "true P" is known exactly; isolates claim H1 from H2.

2.2 Real benchmark datasets (validates H2/H3)
  - ETTh1 (hourly): known daily P=24 and weekly P=168 periods → tests multi-period selection.
  - ETTm1 (15-min): 4 series, daily P=96 → cross-frequency check vs ETTh1.
  - Electricity (ECL, 321 series, hourly): daily 24 + weekly 168 → tests per-variate ACF pooling on a wide multivariate set.
  - Weather (21 series, 10-min): daily P=144.
  - M4 subset (daily/weekly/monthly/quarterly, univariate, many series): covers low-frequency periods (P=7 / 7 / 12 / 4) and gives a many-dataset aggregation for the rank-correlation check.
Optional external anchor: compare with reported CycleNet numbers from the paper for the same datasets/horizons to sanity-check our implementation.

2.3 Preprocessing & splits (identical for all configs to keep P as the only variable)
  - Remove NaNs/inf, no global normalisation before ACF (but use per-series standardisation for detection); for the model, apply per-variate standardisation (mean/std) as in the CycleNet pipeline.
  - Split: chronological 60/20/20 train/val/test (no random shuffle — respects temporal order). ACF computed on TRAIN segment only (avoids information leakage from test into the P choice).

====================================================================
3. FULL ACF DETECTION PROCEDURE
====================================================================
Goal: convert each series into a small ranked set of candidate cycle lengths, with a single per-dataset recommendation.

3.1 Preprocessing per series (train segment only)
  a) Detrend: subtract OLS linear trend (a quadratic variant as sensitivity check). This removes the trend that in real data can otherwise be the dominant low-frequency ACF mass.
  b) Variance stabilisation: optional log transform if variance grows with level (checked via coefficient of variation per block).
  c) Stationarity guard: first-difference if the Augmented-Dickey-Fuller-style check indicates strong non-stationarity persists after detrending; re-run ACF on the differenced series and report both (differencing preserves periodicity at lag P but adds a −1 at lag 1 and reduces low-lag mass, so we note this in interpretation).
  d) Centre to zero mean.

3.2 Sample ACF
  For lag k = 1..K (K = min(L_lookback, 200)):
      r_k = [ Σ_{t} (z_t − z̄)(z_{t+k} − z̄) ] / [ Σ_t (z_t − z̄)² ],  z = preprocessed series.
  Use the standard estimator with N_T − k terms; require sufficient overlap (skip series with fewer than ~4·max candidate points).

3.3 Significance band
  Under white-noise null, r_k ≈ N(0, 1/N_eff); 95% Bartlett band = ±1.96/√N_eff, N_eff = length of z.
  Practical threshold: r_k must exceed max(1.96/√N_eff, 0.15) to count as a candidate — this filters spurious small peaks while staying generous for noisy real data.

3.4 Candidate extraction (per series)
  A lag k* is a candidate if:
    (i)  r_{k*−1} < r_{k*} ≥ r_{k*+1}   (local maximum),
    (ii) r_{k*} above the threshold in 3.3,
    (iii) k* ≥ 2 (lag-1 structure is AR not periodicity).
  Fundamental period = the SMALLEST such k* (integer multiples reappear as secondary peaks). To avoid double counting harmonics, we de-duplicate lags that are integer multiples/divisors of a smaller strong candidate (keep the smaller, but record the multiple as a secondary ranked option). Ties within ±1 lag (e.g., 23 vs 24 from noise) are merged to the mean.

3.5 Aggregation across series and variates (dataset-level)
  Two complementary rankings per dataset:
   (a) Magnitude ranking: average per-lag r_k across all series/variates → mean ACF profile; extract candidates as in 3.4 on the mean profile.
   (b) Vote ranking: for each lag, count the fraction of series where that lag is a candidate; rank by vote fraction.
  Final candidate list = top-k (k=5) lags from (a), re-ranked by (b) to break magnitude-ties. The top-1 becomes the recommended P_ACF for that dataset. Report both rankings; disagreement (>1 position shift) flags a heterogeneous-period dataset (handled in §4.3 and §5).

3.6 Ground-truth recovery check (H1) on synthetic data
  P_ACF == true P* (or its smallest harmonic) per replicate; report recovery rate and the full candidate list to show how far the "true" P ranks when not top-1.

3.7 Optional cross-check (not part of the core answer)
  FFT periodogram peak as a one-line corroboration only; the answer is ACF-based by task definition.

====================================================================
4. CYCLENET SETUP
====================================================================
4.1 How P enters the model (Residual Cycle Forecasting, RCF)
  CycleNet (Lin et al., NeurIPS 2024) augments a backbone forecaster (e.g., a linear/DLinear head) with an RCF module that holds a LEARNABLE cycle token of length P shared across time steps (per variate for multivariate data). For time step t the model emits a cycle component ŷ^cycle_t = token[t mod P]; the backbone is trained on residuals y_t − ŷ^cycle_{t−P} (cycle-to-cycle differences); forecast = backbone residual output + cycle component. Consequences that constrain our design:
   - P must be a single fixed positive integer per dataset (one cycle token, one period). This is why §3 aggregates to one P per dataset rather than per series.
   - RCF needs the lag-P history within the receptive window: lookback L must satisfy L ≥ 2·P (else the model cannot reference the previous cycle for early in-window steps). With L=336 this caps P ≤ 168, which comfortably covers all daily/weekly periods in our data while ruling out unrealistically long P (e.g., yearly for hourly data).

4.2 Model protocol (fixed across all P variants so P is the ONLY variable)
  - Backbone: DLinear-style head (the CycleNet default) for a lean, CPU-friendly baseline; note that the same protocol generalises to any backbone.
  - Lookback L = 336; horizons H ∈ {96, 192, 336, 720} for ETT/ECL/Weather; {24, 48, 168} or the M4 short-term horizons for M4 subsets.
  - Optimiser: Adam, lr 1e-3 (cosine decay), batch 32, MSE loss, early stopping on validation loss (patience 10).
  - Data normalisation per variate (standardisation) identical across variants.
  - Seeds: 3 seeds minimum, up to 5 if budget allows, identical seeds across all P variants of the same dataset/horizon (enables paired tests).

4.3 P-sweep range (per dataset)
  Let p1 = top ACF candidate, p2..p5 = the rest. Sweep set = {max(1, p1−2)…p1+2} ∪ {p2..p5} ∪ {default P by data frequency} ∪ {known alternates, e.g., 24 AND 168 for hourly data}. Clamp any candidate P to ≤ L/2 (=168) to respect the L ≥ 2P RCF constraint. This yields ~8–12 P values per dataset. Rationale: the sweep builds the error-vs-P landscape on which "optimal" is operationally defined, and tests whether the ACF picks a point on/near its minimum.

4.4 Baselines and controls, each tied to a specific claim it isolates
  C1 — CycleNet(P_ACF) vs CycleNet(P_default): the core head-to-head for H2's "at least as good as convention". P_default = {24 hourly, 96 for 15-min, 144 for 10-min, 7 weekly, 12 monthly, 4 quarterly} (the paper's frequency heuristic).
  C2 — CycleNet(P) for every P in the sweep: the error-vs-P curve; isolates H2's "optimality" (is P_ACF within the noise band of the argmin?) and supplies the rank-correlation input for H2.
  C3 — CycleNet with RCF module disabled (P=0 / no cycle token, same backbone, same everything else): the ablation isolating H3 (the cycle mechanism itself must pay off, so the P choice is not a free lunch on a useless module).
  C4 — Published CycleNet/other-paper numbers on the same dataset+horizon (external anchor): sanity-check that our implementation reproduces the ballpark; it does not participate in hypothesis tests.

4.5 Evaluation metrics
  MSE and MAE averaged over all forecast steps and variates (the standard CycleNet reporting); symmetric-MAPE as a secondary metric for M4 subsets. Report mean ± std across seeds. Each claim uses test-set metrics; C2/C3 use validation for early stopping and TEST for the reported comparison.

====================================================================
5. ANALYSIS PLAN
====================================================================
5.1 Head-to-head — ACF-P vs default-P (C1)
  For each dataset×horizon: difference Δ = MAE(P_default) − MAE(P_ACF) per seed. Paired test across seeds: with ≥5 seeds use paired t-test; with 3 seeds use Wilcoxon signed-rank (acknowledge low power) and, crucially, report the DIRECTIONAL CONSISTENCY (how many seeds show Δ>0) and effect size (mean relative error reduction %). Success = Δ ≥ 0 (tie or win) with ≥ 2/3 seeds consistent, or a significant paired test.

5.2 P-sweep landscape (C2)
  Plot/table MAE(P) across the sweep per dataset. Report:
   (i)   argmin P*_err and its noise band [best ± 1 SE(seeds)],
   (ii)  whether P_ACF ∈ band (success = within band, or P_ACF is the band's argmin),
   (iii) whether P_default also ∈ band (to characterise when ACF adds nothing because defaults already tie).

5.3 Rank-correlation check (the headline "ACF predicts optimality" metric)
  For each dataset: order sweep candidates by mean ACF magnitude (descending) and by test MAE (ascending) → Kendall's tau_b and Spearman rho between ACF-rank and error-rank (expect negative correlation: high ACF ⇒ low error). Aggregate tau across the M4 many-dataset family (one point per dataset) to gain statistical power. Positive/near-zero tau = the ACF signal does NOT track performance and the method fails.

5.4 Tie handling / noise band
  Because multiple P can be statistically tied, "optimal" is not a single point. Definition: the optimal set = {P : MAE(P) within band of argmin}. Success is that P_ACF belongs to this set. This avoids over-claiming when a 24-vs-168 choice does not change error; in that case we report that ACF and default agree within the band and the ranking is stable.

5.5 Attributing performance (C3)
  RCF-on(P_ACF) vs RCF-off on identical protocol: paired comparison as in 5.1. If the module gives ≤0 gain, the whole "optimal P" question is vacuous on that dataset and it is flagged rather than counted as evidence.

5.6 Interpretation output per dataset
  A small table: dataset | true/documented periods | P_ACF (with vote+magnitude ranking) | P_default | sweep argmin (band) | ACF∈band? | Δ vs default | tau_b | RCF-on vs off gain. A cross-dataset summary of S1–S4 closes the answer to the research question.

====================================================================
6. FEASIBILITY, RUNTIME AND FALLBACKS
====================================================================
6.1 Current environment reality
  /workspace is empty (only task.json); Python 3.14.4 system-only; NO numpy/scipy/pandas/torch installed; network disabled; CPU-only (224 cores), no GPU. Therefore the full experiment is NOT runnable as-is. Concrete prerequisites to actually execute: pip-installable scientific stack (numpy, scipy, torch, pandas) and the datasets (§2.2). These are provisioning items outside the design, stated as assumptions, not solved here.

6.2 Runtime & scaling budget (if provisioned on the 224-CPU node)
  Dominant cost is CycleNet training across the P-sweep × horizons × seeds.
  - Per run: ETTh1 L=336 H=96, ~8.6k train pts, batch 32, 30–60 epochs (early stop): roughly minutes on GPU / tens of minutes on 224 CPU threads if the model is the lean DLinear-backbone variant. Multiply by (datasets ~5) × (sweep ~10) × (horizons up to 4) × (seeds 3) → the FULL grid is heavy (hundreds of runs). Mitigations, applied cumulatively until in budget:
    a) Epoch cap 40 + early stopping; batch 64.
    b) 3 seeds for head-to-head/ablation, 1–2 seeds for the sweep landscape (sweep is used for argmin/noise-band plus tau, which tolerates single-seed estimates).
    c) Subsampling: for ECL/Weather train on a random ~50% variate subset (reports per-variate-pooled behaviour on a subset; flagged as a limitation).
    d) Limit horizons to {96, 336} for the sweep, add {192, 720} only for the head-to-head if budget allows.
  - ACF step is near-free (O(N·K) per series) and the synthetic recovery study is cheap — this part runs even without heavy compute.

6.3 Fallback: synthetic-only proof-of-concept (runnable with minimal deps)
  If provisioning of real data fails, the design degrades gracefully to a self-contained PoC that still answers the question's core logically:
  - Generate synthetic series with known P (§2.1), run §3 ACF detection, confirm recovery (S1). 
  - Replace real CycleNet with a cheap reference forecaster that depends explicitly on P (e.g., seasonal-naive: ŷ_{t+h} = x_{t+h−P}, and seasonal-auto: ŷ using lag-P differenced linear fit) to demonstrate that P chosen by ACF attains near-minimal error over a P-sweep (mirrors S2/S3 without training a neural net). This preserves the experimental LOGIC (ACF-picked P ≈ best P on held-out error) when GPUs/torch/data are unavailable; it is clearly labelled as a fallback proxy, not the full CycleNet result.

6.4 What is NOT claimed
  No experiment has been run; this document specifies the design, controls, metrics and decision rules such that executing it (under the provisioning in 6.1) would concretely answer the research question with pre-registered success criteria.

====================================================================
DECISION RULES SUMMARY (for later execution)
- H1 accepted if synthetic recovery rate ≥ 95%.
- H2 accepted per dataset if P_ACF ∈ noise band of sweep argmin AND Δ vs default ≥ 0 (majority of seeds consistent) AND tau_b < 0 with p<0.05 (aggregated for M4).
- H3 accepted if RCF-on beats RCF-off (paired test or ≥2/3 seeds positive) on at least the synthetic and one real dataset.
- Any dataset breaking an assumption (dominant seasonality, shared periodicity) is reported and excluded from aggregate success, not silently adjusted.

payload.answer:
## 1) Input inspection — the repository is EMPTY

`/workspace` contains only `task.json` (no CycleNet code, configs, docs, or datasets). System Python 3.14 has no numpy/scipy; network is disabled. `track.md` explicitly says "Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required." **Conclusion: there is no usable local CycleNet implementation; the design must rely on the public description (arXiv 2402.10322).** Any numbers I quote for the mechanism are from the paper's public description and must be re-verified against the paper's appendix during implementation; I flag the uncertain ones below.

### CycleNet mechanism (as per public description)
- **Core module** — RCF (Residual Cycle Forecasting): a Transformer encoder–decoder whose input is first *detrended by a cycle baseline* and whose output is re-augmented by it.
- **Cycle length hyperparameter p** → (a) the dimension of a per-step **cycle embedding** and (b) the length of a learnable **cycle-trend vector** c ∈ R^p (per target channel).
- **How p becomes an input**: for every time step t (in *both* lookback and forecast windows) the model computes the **cycle index** s = (t − t₀) mod p, forms a **one-hot vector** of length p (equivalently an index into a learnable `d_model × p` embedding table), and injects this as the positional/periodic embedding added to the token representation. Lookback steps also subtract c[s] from the input (residual = x_t − c[s]); forecast steps add c[t mod p] back to the decoder output. So the model **must know the absolute calendar time** of every step (the embedding does not reset per window), and p sets how far back in calendar time the model can "align" its periodic memory.
- **Encoder/decoder use of the cycle dimension**: the cycle embedding replaces/augments absolute positional encoding in both encoder (lookback tokens) and decoder (target tokens); the residual (cycle-subtracted) sequence is what the attention layers actually model, and the cycle trend is added on top of the decoder output. In short, p controls "how many discrete phases the periodic memory distinguishes"; choosing p wrong (e.g., 24 vs 168 vs 96) changes both the detrending baseline and the phase-alignment of forecast steps.

### Datasets and periodicities (standard long-horizon benchmark set, evaluated on 8 sets)
- **Electricity (ECL)**: hourly, 321 vars, strong daily (24h) + weekly (168h); horizons {96,192,336,720}.
- **Traffic**: hourly, 862 vars, daily + weekly (168h); same horizons.
- **Weather**: 10-min sampling, 21 vars, daily cycle = 144 steps (weekly = 1008); same horizons.
- **Solar-Energy**: 10-min, 137 vars, strong daily (144) cycle; same horizons.
- **ETTh1/ETTh2**: hourly, 7 vars, daily (24) / weekly (168); ETTh series are shorter, so **168h and especially 8760h (yearly) may not be estimable** from the ~2-year span — a key feasibility constraint.
- **ETTm1/ETTm2**: 15-min, 7 vars, daily = 96, weekly = 672.
- Paper-reported nominal p values per dataset (e.g., 24 daily vs 168 weekly for hourly sets; 144 for 10-min sets) exist in the appendix but I cannot verify them offline — **all such per-dataset numbers are marked uncertain**.

## 2) Proposed approach (sketch)

**Period estimation (per training series):**
- Compute the sample **autocorrelation function** (ACF) r_k on the training portion of each channel.
- Also compute a **Fourier periodogram** (period = 1/argmax-frequency) as a complementary view.
- Candidate cycle-length sets are dataset-dependent and derived from **sampling resolution** × natural period:
  - hourly → {24, 168, 8760}
  - 15-min (ETTm) → {96, 672}
  - 10-min (Weather/Solar) → {144, 1008}
- **Estimator**: dominant period = argmax over lags of r_k (with local-maximum/peak detection), then map to the nearest candidate; equivalently take the top-k periodogram peaks. Candidate score = r_{p} (lag-p autocorrelation) or normalized top-k periodogram mass at frequency 1/p.

**Selection rule (two levels, both tested):**
- *Per-series*: estimate a period per channel → assign each channel its own cycle length (mixture of cycles per dataset) vs. a **majority vote** for a single dataset-level p.
- *Dataset-level*: average the autocorrelograms across channels, pick the candidate with the largest mean r_p, **with a threshold** (e.g., require r_p > 0.2, or > 2/√n statistical significance) — if no candidate passes, fall back to the no-cycle baseline (p = none, i.e. skip the RCF cycle branch).

**Evaluation protocol (to be run after design approval, not run now):**
- **Controls/baselines**: (i) no-cycle baseline (RCF residuals only, no cycle embedding/trend), (ii) each individual candidate p (24/168 or 96/672 or 144/1008), (iii) the ACF-chosen p, (iv) the paper-reported nominal p.
- **Metrics**: MAE and MSE (standard for these datasets), reported on channels normalized the usual way.
- **Splits**: fixed standard conventions — ETT train/val/test ≈ 12/4/4 months (6:2:2); ECL ≈ 15/3/6 months; Traffic ≈ 7:1:2; Weather/Solar per README fractions; forecast horizons {96,192,336,720}. Cycle is chosen on the **validation** split only; test metrics reported for the chosen p; also a small sensitivity pane showing metric for each candidate p.
- **Consistency check**: the ACF-estimated p should reproduce the known natural periodicity of each dataset (sanity gate); report agreement rate and the threshold sensitivity.

The toy test I already ran (pure-Python ACF, synthetic hourly 24-period series + trend + noise) showed a clean peak at lag 24 (r≈0.89), confirming the estimator's discriminative power and the harmonic at lag 48 — and exposing that **first-difference detrending shifts the argmax (25 vs 24)**, so detrending choice is material.

## 3) Consequential assumptions & uncertainties (mine to surface)

**Assumptions:**
- The public description of CycleNet (one-hot/embedding cycle index + per-channel cycle-trend vector + RCF residual architecture) is accurate, since no local code exists to verify against.
- ACF on the raw training series is informative enough to recover the dominant period despite trend/drift (my toy test supports this for a mild linear trend).
- Dataset-level (single p) selection is the primary operating point — per-series assignment is a secondary, optional variant.
- The paper-reported nominal p values are a reasonable "best-known" reference that ACF should reproduce.
- Validation-based metric choice (best val MAE) is the operational definition of "optimal", even when it disagrees with the true periodicity.

**Uncertainties:**
- Actual per-dataset p values and exact split fractions in CycleNet's configs (cannot verify offline; appendix values vs my memory may differ).
- Whether the paper's p is chosen by dataset (single) or per-series; and whether lookback length is fixed at 336 or varies (my assumption: fixed 336 for long-horizon sets, unverified).
- Detrending method for ACF — raw vs detrended vs seasonally adjusted; first-difference shifts argmax (observed in toy test); need a rule (e.g., fit polynomial trend → remove, or use raw ACF, or use Lomb-Scargle).
- **Lag scan range**: which lags to scan (e.g., 1..720, vs only candidates); short series (ETTh ~2yr) cannot reliably support lag 8760 (only ~2 full periods), so yearly candidates are statistically weak there.
- **Mixed/missing periodicity**: some channels have both daily+weekly (two strong peaks) or none (traffic on holidays, weather noise); need a tie-break rule (favor lower harmonic = shorter period? favor strongest peak?) and a fallback to no-cycle.
- Whether r_k threshold for "significant" cycle should be statistical (2/√n) or heuristic (0.2/0.3).
- Whether the same p must serve both detrending (cycle trend vector) and positional embedding — in the paper they are tied, so the estimator must produce one p per series/dataset.
- Operational definition of "optimal cycle length": best val metric vs. faithfulness to true seasonality may disagree; I will treat val MAE as the ground truth for recommendation and report both.

Mechanism, dataset list, periodicities, and nominal cycle lengths are reconstructed from the public CycleNet description (arXiv 2402.10322) and standard long-horizon benchmark conventions (Electricity, Traffic, Weather, Solar, ETTh/m).

Standard benchmark set is 8 long-horizon datasets (ECL, Traffic, Weather, Solar, ETTh1/2, ETTm1/2) with natural daily/weekly cycles and horizons {96,192,336,720}.
Dataset-level single cycle length is the primary operating point; per-series assignment is a secondary variant.
