---

## 10. Допущения и неопределённости (явный список)

**Допущения (зафиксированы как требования дизайна):**
- A1. Источник истины по архитектуре — внешние статья/репо CycleNet (ACAT-SCUT/CycleNet, ICLR 2025); локальных исходников в workspace нет (проверено). Точные дефолты (`r_cycle`, `n_cycles`, `lr`, scheduler) переиспользуются из reference как задокументированные значения.
- A2. Исполнение происходит в среде с установленными numpy/torch и доступом к датасетам; в текущей песочнице зависимостей и сети нет — дизайн не претендует на запуск здесь.
- A3. Модель малая, CPU-only (224 CPU), GPU не требуется.
- A4. Основной вариант — residual CycleNet (канонический); vanilla — опциональная абляция.
- A5. Агрегация метрик — per-point (стандарт LTSF).
- A6. Критерий успеха — пре-регистрированный (см. §6.2), допускает отрицательный исход.

**Неопределённости (решения экспериментатора, с обоснованием):**
- U1. Дефолтные гиперпараметры reference-репо не проверяемы без доступа к сети — фиксируются из статьи и явно помечаются в конфиге; верификация — эмпирическая (A4/A5).
- U2. Точный период `r_cycle` на реальных датасетах (24/96/144/168) — задаётся доменно, затем подтверждается FFT/автокорреляцией на train (не на тесте).
- U3. Бюджет вычислений (число сидов = 5, подмножество горизонтов для Solar/Exchange) — компромисс между статистической надёжностью и CPU-временем.
- U4. Унивариатный протокол выбран базовым (детерминированность и простота fair comparison); мультивариантный — опциональное расширение, не входит в критерий успеха.
- U5. Порог R2 («≥3 из 4 датасетов», «≥2 со значимой разницей») — экспертное решение для баланса между жёсткостью и чувствительностью.

payload.answer:
Enfoque bosquejado para diseñar el experimento CycleNet (predicción de series con patrones periódicos):

**0. Insumos reales para el diseño (confirmado por inspección):** solo `task.json` (+ contenido de `track.md`: tarea de solo diseño, sin repos/repos ni cómputo). No hay datasets ni dependencias instaladas. El diseño descansa en: (i) conocimiento del paper CycleNet (NeurIPS 2024), y (ii) datos sintéticos que el propio experimento generaría (no hay datos pre-existentes).

**1. Mecanismo del modelo — "Residual Cycle Forecasting":**
- Período: conocido a priori (p.ej. P=7 semanal, P=24 horario, P=365 anual) o estimado por autocorrelación/FFT sobre la porción de entrenamiento. En diseño: usar P conocido para los experimentos principales y un experimento de robustez con P estimado.
- Componente cíclico aprendido: buffer c ∈ R^{P} (por serie o compartido), entrada en fase c[t mod P]. Se aprende end-to-end como parámetro.
- Substracción del ciclo: residual r_t = x_t − c[t mod P]; la red residual recibe r.
- Red residual liviana (MLP de 2–3 capas, o capas lineales/conv1d con conexiones residuales) que predice el residual en el horizonte H.
- Predicción con "cycle reuse": para t futuros (L,…,L+H−1), el componente cíclico se obtiene reusando c en fases deslizantes c[(L+i) mod P] (la ventana del período se repite hacia adelante). Salida final: ŷ = ciclo_reuso + residual_pred.

**2. Datos (sintéticos + opcional público):**
- Sintéticos con periodicidad conocida: series diarias con estacionalidad semanal (P=7) y/o anual (P=365), combinadas con tendencia suave y ruido gaussiano (p.ej. x_t = A·sin(2πt/P) + tendencia + ε). Ground-truth del período permite validar la estimación de P, la ablatión y la interpretabilidad del buffer aprendido.
- Opcional, si estuviera disponible (no está en este entorno): un dataset público estándar (p.ej. M4-M5, Electricity, Traffic, ETT) para generalización.
- Por qué sintéticos: control total de la periódica, repeticiones múltiples, bajo costo, y permite aislar el aporte del ciclo (factor de ablatión controlado).

**3. Entrenamiento (sin fuga):**
- Split contiguo en el tiempo: train/val/test 70/15/15 (en ese orden cronológico); prohibido shuffling entre splits.
- Muestreo de ventanas dentro de train: entradas x[L] → objetivo x[L+1:L+H+1], con ventana L ≥ 2P para que el ciclo sea visible.
- Pérdida: MSE como principal; MAE como secundaria (robustez a outliers). Optimizador Adam (lr ≈ 1e−3, batch pequeño). Parada por early stopping en val (patience) + tope de épocas.

**4. Controles y baselines (aislar el aporte del ciclo):**
- Naive estacional: ŷ_{t} = x_{t−P} (repite el patrón) — baseline más directo del período.
- ARIMA o ETS simple sobre la serie cruda.
- Lineal/MLP entrenado sobre la serie **cruda** (sin componente cíclico) — control del aporte del ciclo.
- Ablación decisiva: CycleNet con el bloque cíclico **desactivado** (solo la red residual sobre x cruda) vs. CycleNet completo. Si el ciclo no aporta, ambos deben dar lo mismo.

**5. Análisis de resultados:**
- Métricas en test: MSE y MAE por horizonte (y agregadas); mejora relativa (%) vs. cada baseline.
- Tabla de comparación: CycleNet vs. baselines vs. ablatión.
- Verificación de interpretabilidad: comparar el buffer c aprendido contra el patrón sintético real del período.
- Sensibilidad: variar P estimado y el largo de ventana L (¿estabilidad?).

**6. Viabilidad:**
- CycleNet es liviano (paper: <1% de parámetros/FLOPs de PatchTST, entrenable en CPU) → factible sin GPU.
- Requisitos que el diseño debe controlar: período conocido o estimable; patrón aproximadamente periódico/estacionario (un solo patrón estable); ventana ≥ 1–2 períodos; el ciclo asume periodicidad estable que no cambia dentro del horizonte.

**3. Supuestos e incertidumbres consecuentes (para resolver en esta revisión del enfoque):**
- (S) Período: asumo conocido a priori (P=7/365) para el experimento principal; la estimación por autocorrelación es un experimento secundario.
- (S) Tamaño de la serie sintética: no fijo aún (p.ej. 1000–5000 pasos); ¿preferís longitud larga (estabilidad) o corta (más realista)?
- (S) Presupuesto de cómputo: asumo CPU con presupuesto moderado (serie y modelo pequeños); si querés escala mayor (p.ej. M4 completo), habría que acotar.
- (S) Versión/implementación exacta de CycleNet: sin acceso a red no puedo verificar el código oficial; asumo la arquitectura del paper (buffer de ciclo + red residual + cycle reuse). Detalle a confirmar: si se usa RevIN (normalización reversible) o solo la sustracción del ciclo.
- (I) Si la implementación requiriera el código oficial del paper, no está disponible offline; el diseño lo dejará especificado como pseudodiseño reproducible.
- (I) El tipo de estacionalidad (aditiva vs. multiplicativa) y la presencia de tendencia/deriva afectan cuán separable es el ciclo; el diseño podrá elegir el régimen aditivo (más favorable) y reportar la limitación.

payload.answer:
# Diseño final del experimento: CycleNet para series temporales con patrones periódicos

**Naturaleza de la tarea:** solo diseño reproducible (confirmado: `track.md` en `task.json` dice "Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required."; datasets `[]`, sin deps instaladas, sin GPU). No se ejecuta nada; se especifica el protocolo completo para que un futuro agente pueda implementarlo sin ambigüedad. Ningún resultado aquí reportado es observado.

---

## 1. Pregunta y racional

¿Cómo implementar y entrenar un modelo CycleNet (residual cycle forecasting) para pronosticar series con patrones periódicos, y cómo aislar experimentalmente el aporte de su componente cíclico?

**Racional del enfoque:** CycleNet separa la señal en (i) un componente cíclico periódico aprendido (buffer `c ∈ ℝ^P`) y (ii) un residual, modelado por una red liviana. Su ventaja frente a redes que modelan todo a la vez es que la periodicidad se extrapola de forma exacta vía *cycle reuse* (repetición deslizante del período), lo cual es barato y robusto en CPU. Para validar que este mecanismo funciona y que aporta, comparamos contra baselines que también explotan la periodicidad (Naive estacional, ETS/ARIMA estacional) y contra la **ablatión del propio modelo sin el ciclo** — el control diferenciador.

---

## 2. Arquitectura del modelo (especificación)

Componentes (basados en el paper CycleNet, NeurIPS 2024; implementación propia reproducible, sin depender de código oficial offline):

1. **Período P:** conocido a priori en el experimento principal (P=7 semanal; P=365 anual); secundariamente estimado por autocorrelación/FFT sobre el bloque de train.
2. **Buffer de ciclo aprendido:** `C ∈ ℝ^(M×P)` (ver §5). Índice de fase `phase(t) = t mod P`; valor cíclico `c[t] = C[m, phase(t)]`.
3. **Sustracción del ciclo:** residual de entrada `r_t = x_t − c[t]` (régimen aditivo).
4. **Red residual liviana `f_θ`:** mapea la ventana `r[1..L] ∈ ℝ^L → residual futuro `ℝ^H`. Concretamente un MLP de 2 capas `L→128→64→H` con GELU + LayerNorm (para el escenario anual, capa de entrada 730→128 → ~95k parámetros, viable en CPU). Es la única parte parametrizada junto con `C`.
5. **Cycle reuse (predicción hacia adelante):** para los pasos futuros `t = L+1..L+H`, el componente cíclico es `c[t] = C[m, (L+i) mod P] ` (la ventana del período se desliza y repite). Salida final:
   `ŷ[L+i] = C[m, (L+i) mod P] + f_θ(r)[i]`.

Entrenamiento conjunto end-to-end de `{C, θ}` con la pérdida en §4.

---

## 3. Datos sintéticos (generados por el diseño, no preexistentes)

Regla común: régimen **aditivo** `x_t = c_true(t mod P) + tendencia + ε`, `ε ~ N(0, σ²)`, para que el ciclo sea separable y la sustracción tenga sentido.

- **Escenario A — semana (P=7):** patrón verdadero `c_true` de 7 fases (p.ej. `[0.5, 0.3, 0.1, −0.2, −0.4, −0.1, 0.2]`, escalado al nivel de la serie), tendencia pequeña (pendiente ≈ 0.001/paso), ruido σ con SNR razonable (σ ≈ 0.2). Longitud **n = 1,500** pasos (≈214 semanas, ~4 años diarios).
- **Escenario B — año (P=365):** serie diaria con estacionalidad anual suave (p.ej. sinusoide `A·sin(2π t/365 + φ)` o patrón `c_true[365]` de curva suave), misma tendencia/ruido. Longitud **n = 3,000** pasos (~8.2 años).
- **Múltiples series:** **M = 4** series por escenario (misma P y forma de patrón, distinto ruido/semilla) para poder agregar métricas y dar estabilidad estadística.

**Por qué sintéticos:** el ground-truth del período permite (i) validar la recuperación del patrón por el buffer aprendido, (ii) realizar la ablatión de forma controlada, (iii) medir la sensibilidad a la estimación de P, y (iv) es barato y repetible.

---

## 4. Protocolo de entrenamiento (sin fuga)

- **Split contiguo en el tiempo:** train/val/test **70/15/15** en orden cronológico (A: train 1,050 / val 225 / test 225; B: 2,100/450/450). Prohibido barajar entre splits.
- **Ventanas de entrenamiento:** entradas de longitud **L = 2P** (A: L=14; B: L=730), objetivo `x[L+1..L+H]`, extraídas del bloque de train con stride 1 (posible submuestreo para acelerar). ~1,000 ventanas (A) / ~1,350 (B) por época.
- **Horizonte:** **H = P** (principal: 7 / 365) y **H = 2P** (sensibilidad; A: 14; B: no se repite por costo, se reduce a sensibilidad sobre P estimado).
- **Pérdida:** MSE principal; MAE secundaria (reporte de robustez).
- **Optimizador:** Adam, lr = 1e−3, weight decay 1e−4, batch = 32.
- **Paradas:** tope de **200 épocas** + **early stopping en val (MSE)** con patience = 20; se guarda el mejor checkpoint por val.
- **Reproducibilidad:** semillas fijas (p.ej. 42, 43, 44) para 3 réplicas y reporte con media ± desviación.
- **Evaluación en test:** ventanas **no solapadas** para evitar correlación/sobreconteo en las métricas.

---

## 5. Decisión sobre el buffer: compartido vs. por serie

**Decisión: buffer por serie (`C ∈ ℝ^(M×P)`).** Justificación: en CycleNet el ciclo se guarda por canal/serie; las series sintéticas comparten período y forma pero difieren en realizaciones de ruido y, opcionalmente, en desfase de fase; un buffer compartido exigiría alineación de fases que los datos reales no garantizan. El buffer compartido se deja como **variante secundaria de sensibilidad** (solo si todas las series se generan fase-alineadas). Parámetros del ciclo: A → 4×7 = 28; B → 4×365 = 1,460; despreciables frente a los de `f_θ`.

---

## 6. Controles y baselines (aislar el aporte del ciclo)

1. **Naive estacional:** `ŷ_{t+k} = x_{t+k−P}` — explota el mismo período, sin aprendizaje. Control directo del valor del ciclo.
2. **Naive último valor:** `ŷ = x_t` — cota inferior de referencia.
3. **ETS estacional** con período fijo; para el escenario anual (P=365) se usan **órdenes estacionales fijos** (p.ej. SARIMA(1,0,1)(1,1,1)₃₆₅ o ETS con seasonal period fijado), **evitando auto-selección costosa** (resolución pedida: sin búsqueda automática de órdenes).
4. **Ablación decisiva (control diferenciador):** la misma red residual (mismos `f_θ` e hiperparámetros) aplicada a la serie **cruda** `x` — es decir, CycleNet con el buffer de ciclo **desactivado/eliminado**. Diferencia respecto a CycleNet completo = aporte puro del componente cíclico con capacidad de red idéntica. También se reporta la variante con `C` congelado en inicialización (verificar que el aprendizaje del ciclo importa).

---

## 7. Plan de análisis (resultados esperados del protocolo, no observados)

- **Métricas en test:** MSE y MAE agregadas y **por horizonte** (paso 1..H); comparación de CycleNet vs. cada baseline con **mejora relativa (%)** y desviación entre semillas.
- **Tabla 1:** (escenario × modelo: CycleNet, Naive estacional, Naive último, ETS/SARIMA, Ablatión) — MSE/MAE.
- **Tabla 2:** mejoras relativas (%) de CycleNet vs. cada baseline y vs. ablatión, con CI por semilla.
- **Sanity de interpretabilidad:** correlación/RMSE entre el buffer aprendido `C[m,:]` y el patrón `c_true` sintético — valida que el modelo *aprende* el ciclo real y no un artefacto.
- **Sensibilidad:** (i) P estimado por autocorrelación vs. P conocido; (ii) H = P vs. 2P; (iii) L = P vs. 2P (verificar que L ≥ 1–2 períodos importa); (iv) buffer compartido vs. por-serie. Se reportará estabilidad de las conclusiones.
- **Criterio de hipótesis esperado:** CycleNet debe ganar vs. baselines y superar (o igualar a lo sumo) a la ablatión; si la ablatión igualara o superara, el diseño concluiría que el ciclo no aporta en ese régimen.

---

## 8. Viabilidad

- **Cómputo:** modelo liviano (papel: <1% parámetros/FLOPs de PatchTST). A: ~11k params (MLP 14→128→64→7 + C 28); B: ~95k params (730→128→7 + C 1,460). ~1,000–1,350 ventanas/época × ≤200 épocas → **minutos en CPU** (224 cores disponibles). No requiere GPU.
- **Dependencias:** solo numpy/pandas (generación sintética, métricas, baselines Naive); opcional torch/pandas para el modelo y ETS. No están instaladas ahora; es un paso de implementación (fuera del alcance de diseño).
- **Requisitos del mecanismo (deben controlarse en el diseño):** período conocido o estimable; patrón estable/estacionario en el régimen aditivo; ventana L ≥ 1–2 períodos. Estas condiciones están garantizadas por la generación sintética.

---

## 9. Supuestos e incertidumbres con mitigación

## 一、输入与仓库检查结论
- /workspace 只有 task.json；无 CycleNet 骨架代码、无数据集、无说明文档 → **仓库为空白**。以下设计全部内容均需「新建/假定」，不依赖任何现存文件。
- 本任务为设计型（track.md: "Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required"），因此交付物是**可执行实验设计文档**（架构规约 + 伪代码 + 实验矩阵），不要求实际训练或联网。

## 二、实验设计框架（总体思路，细节留待批准后展开）
**A. 数据与周期特征**
- 主数据源：**合成周期性时序**（可控 ground-truth）。生成器模型 = 趋势项 + 多个正弦季节分量（周期 w ∈ {24, 168}，可多分量叠加）+ 噪声（多档 SNR，如 0.1/0.5/1.0），支持单/多变量、非平稳漂移变体。优势：周期已知可验证、可精确做周期匹配与敏感性消融、无需网络下载。
- 备选数据（设计预留接口，若数据可得）：公共基准 ETTh1/ETTm1/Weather/Traffic/Electricity，其周期为领域已知（24/24/24/168/24），作为真实数据验证集。脚本与预处理（缺失值、重采样、train/val/test 划分）写入设计。
- 周期特征：CycleNet 用**按相位索引的可学习查找表**（每通道 w 个 bias 参数）+ 残差抽取，周期长度 w 由领域知识给定（合成数据即 ground-truth），不把自动周期估计作为主流程，仅列为扩展项。

**B. 模型结构（CycleNet 规格）与训练方案**
- 结构：输入 P 步历史 → 按相位（含 lag 偏移）查表得循环特征 c → 残差 r = x − c → 骨干网络（默认**线性 Residual-Backbone，可选 DLinear**）预测未来残差 → 对预测区间相位查表得未来循环特征 → 最终预测 = 骨干输出 + 循环特征。w、lag、P、H 为核心超参。
- 训练：时序不乱序的滚动窗口切分 train/val/test；损失 MSE（另报 MAE）；Adam + 学习率调度 + 早停；每序列 z-score 归一化、评估时反归一化；多 seed 取均值±std。骨干只取线性/浅层，保证 CPU 可运行、算力可控。

**C. 基线与评价指标**
- 基线：①同骨架但**去掉/冻结循环项**（即 cycle-free 消融对照）；②Seasonal-naive（重复上一周期）；③普通线性回归/DLinear；④可选持久化（naive last）。
- 指标：MSE、MAE（论文口径，归一化与原始尺度均报）；相对提升率；预测区间 [H<w 与 H>w] 两种口径分别报告，考察「周期长度与预测时长匹配」的影响。

**D. 消融与控制变量**
- 消融1: 有无循环残差（删除 vs 冻结循环表）；消融2: 周期长度敏感性（w 正确 / w−Δ / w∕2 / 2w）；消融3: 骨干替换（线性 vs DLinear）；消融4: lag 偏移取值。
- 控制变量：固定全局随机种子、**完全相同**的 train/val/test 划分、相同归一化与损失、相同优化器与超参、同一套指标计算代码，保证除目标变量外一切不变。

## 三、关键假设与不确定项（按三类区分）

**（1）可从资料确认的事实（文献层面）**
- CycleNet 的核心结构定义（ICLR 2025: 周期残差 + 可学习循环查找表 + 骨干叠加）属于公开文献描述。
- 公共基准数据集及各自领域已知周期（24/168 等）与基准指标口径（MSE/MAE、预测长度 96–720）有公开惯例可循。

**（2）需作合理假设之处**
- 数据不可得 → 主实验采用合成数据；公共基准仅作可选扩展。
- 任务为设计型 → 假设「实现代码按设计规约可运行」，不实际执行。
- 若未来需要真实运行，假设可将 numpy/torch 预装（当前环境网络关闭且无包），模型规模按 CPU 友好设计。

**（3）存在不确定之处**
- CycleNet 复现细节（lag 相位计算的确切公式、循环特征与归一化的交互）无法离线核实，需以公开论文一般描述为默认并纳入消融。
- 合成数据能否代表真实时序的噪声与非平稳结构存在偏差，结论外推需谨慎（用备选公共数据缓解）。
- 无 GPU 时若真要训练，线性骨干可行但深度骨干（PatchTST 级别）不可行，设计以线性/DLinear 为限。

以上为框架汇报，未展开完整实验矩阵与伪代码；待确认后我再产出完整设计（stage=result）。

1. 主实验数据采用**合成周期时序**（因为仓库无数据、网络关闭），周期 w 即 ground-truth。
2. 周期长度由领域知识给定（含合成数据的已知值），自动周期估计仅作可选扩展（O6）。
3. 实现按本文档规约可运行；若运行环境需预装 numpy/torch（当前环境缺失且无法联网安装），由执行方满足。
4. 模型规模按 CPU 友好设计（骨干仅 linear/DLinear），不追求论文级大模型。

**C. 确定的不确定项**
1. CycleNet 的 lag 相位计算、循环特征与归一化交互的复现细节无法离线核实 → 以本文档默认值（L=0）为基并纳入敏感性实验（AB2）。
2. 合成数据（正弦+高斯噪声）不能完全代表真实时序的异方差噪声/日历效应 → 结论外推边界见 §10。
3. 公共基准数据是否可得未定 → O4 为可选验证分支。
4. 无 GPU 时深度骨干（PatchTST 级）不可行，可能低估 CycleNet 与强骨干结合的增益。

## 2. 研究问题与目标
- **RQ1**：CycleNet 是否能比无显式周期建模的基线更准确地预测周期时序？（主对照）
- **RQ2**：预测时长 H 与周期长度 w 的关系（H<w vs H>w）如何影响 CycleNet 相对基线的优势？
- **RQ3**：循环特征是否必须可学习/联合训练？周期长度、lag 等超参的敏感性如何？
- 成功标准：在合成数据上，CycleNet 的 test MSE/MAE 在多数单元格低于 NoCycle 骨干、DLinear、Seasonal-naive、Persistent，且 w 正确时最优；稳定性用多 seed 的均值±std 判断。

## 3. 数据设计（合成生成器规格）

### 3.1 记号（全文一致）
- 单条时序长度 T；周期长度 w；输入长度 P；预测时长 H；通道数 D。
- 绝对时间 n∈{0,…,T−1}；当前最后观测时刻 t；未来索引 j=1..H（对应时刻 t+j）。
- 相位函数 φ(n) = (n + L) mod w，L 为 lag 偏移，默认 L=0。
- 归一化：每条序列取其 **train 段**的 μ,σ 做 z-score；预测反归一化回原尺度再算指标。

### 3.2 生成器伪代码（实现语言无关，Python 约定）
```
def gen_series(seed, w, n_cycles, D, SNR, multi, drift, rng):
    T = n_cycles * w                       # 例如 w=24→2880，w=168→4032
    n = arange(T)
    X = zeros(T, D)
    for c in range(D if multi else 1):
        phase  = rng.uniform(0, w)                         # 每通道随机相位
        amp    = rng.uniform(0.5, 1.5)
        trend  = 0.0
        if drift: trend = slope * n                        # 线性漂移，slope∈{0.001,0.01}(归一化后)
        X[:,c] = amp * sin(2*pi*(n + phase)/w) \
               + (0.3*amp)*sin(4*pi*(n+phase)/w)           # 基频+一次谐波
        if not multi: break                                # 单变量 D=1
    noise = rng.normal(0, amp, (T,D)) / SNR                 # SNR=信号幅度/噪声σ
    return X + noise
```
- 因子：w∈{24,168}；SNR∈{0.1,1.0}（`SNR=信号幅度/噪声σ`，0.1 高噪声、1.0 低噪声）；多变量 D∈{1,8}；drift∈{False,True}。
- 数据质量检查（设计规约）：生成后做一次 FFT 峰值验证周期≈w，确保生成器正确（检查项，不构成实验结论）。

### 3.3 划分（无泄漏、所有方法共用）
- 按时间顺序：train 段 70%（用于 μ,σ 与训练）、val 段 10%（选模/早停）、test 段 20%（仅最终评估）。
- 训练窗口：在 train 段内按 **stride=H** 滑动取 (输入 P, 标签 H)，输入 `x_{t-P+1:t}`、标签 `x_{t+1:t+H}`；任何窗口不跨段边界。
- P 设定：P = max(2w, 256)（w=24→P=256；w=168→P=336），保证至少含两个完整周期。

## 4. 模型规格（CycleNet）
### 4.1 组件
- 循环查找表 C∈R^{w×D}（可学习，用 φ 索引；D 通道各自一个 bias 向量）。
- 骨干 B：默认**线性残差骨干**（B_lin：`R_future = W@R + b`，W∈R^{H×P}，按通道共享，记作 linear），变体 **DLinear**（B_DL：对 R 做均值移动平均分解为趋势+季节，各接一个线性层后相加）。
### 4.2 前向伪代码
```
# 输入: 归一化历史 X_hist = x_{t-P+1:t}  (shape P×D)；返回预测 \hat{X}_{t+1:t+H}
def forward(X_hist, t, C, backbone, w, L):
    idx_hist = arange(t-P+1, t+1)
    c_hist   = C[(idx_hist + L) % w]              # 按相位查表（含 L 偏移，见 φ）
    R        = X_hist - c_hist                    # 周期残差 r = x − c
    R_fut    = backbone(R)                        # 预测未来残差 (H×D)
    idx_fut  = arange(t+1, t+H+1)
    c_fut    = C[(idx_fut + L) % w]               # 未来相位循环特征
    return R_fut + c_fut                          # 叠加输出
```
- 训练损失：MSE（归一化尺度，见 §6）；MAE 同步记录。
### 4.3 训练循环伪代码
```
for seed in [0,1,2,3,4]:
    set_seed(seed)
    for each series:
        mu,sig = mean/std(train_portion); Xnorm = (X-mu)/sig     # 每序列独立 z-score
        build train/val windows from Xnorm                      # §3.3 划分，stride=H
    model = CycleNet(w, D, backbone=linear|DLinear)
    opt = Adam(model.params, lr=1e-3, weight_decay=1e-5)
    sched = CosineAnnealingLR(opt, T_max=100)
    for epoch in 1..100:
        for batch in train_windows: loss = MSE(model(batch.x), batch.y); opt.step()
        val_mse = MSE on val_windows（归一化尺度）
        if val_mse best: 保存 best.pt
        if no improve 10 epochs: break
    # 评估: 用 best.pt 在 test 段逐窗口预测 → 反归一化 \hat{x}=(\hat{x}_norm*sig+mu)
    # 记录 test MSE/MAE（原始尺度，见 §6）
report mean±std over 5 seeds for every metric
```

## 5. 基线定义（精确）
1. **NoCycle（cycle-free 消融/基线）**：与 CycleNet 同骨干、同训练协议，但**去掉循环表与残差环节**：`hat_x = B(X_hist)`（骨干直接预测归一化序列）。隔离「显式周期建模」的贡献。
2. **DLinear（独立基线）**：标准 DLinear，历史窗（非残差）分解为趋势/季节并预测；训练协议、种子与 CycleNet 全同。
3. **Seasonal-naive（非参数）**：模板=最近一个周期 `x_{t-w+1:t}`，预测 `\hat{x}_{t+j} = template[(j-1) mod w]`（j=1..H；H>w 时循环复制模板）。
4. **Persistent（非参数）**：`\hat{x}_{t+j} = x_t`（最后值重复）。
- 附加消融 **FrozenCycle**：保留残差管线，但 **C 冻结为随机初始化**（不参与梯度更新，仅骨干训练）→ 验证循环特征必须联合学习。

## 6. 评价指标（一致口径）
- 先对每个测试窗口预测反归一化到原尺度，再计算：`MSE = mean_{t,j,c}(x_tj − xhat_tj)^2`，`MAE = mean|x_tj − xhat_tj|`。
- 报告：原始尺度 MSE/MAE（主报告）+ 归一化尺度 MSE（跨序列可比副表）。多 seed 给 mean±std。相对提升 `(MSE_base − MSE_CN)/MSE_base×100%`。

## 7. 控制变量清单（强制，所有方法/种子完全一致）
- 同一 train/val/test 划分；同一 μ,σ；同一 MSE 损失；同一优化器(Adam lr=1e-3, wd=1e-5)与调度(Cosine 100)、早停(patience=10)；同一 batch size(128) 与输入 P/H；同一随机种子集 {0,1,2,3,4}；同一指标实现代码；模型选择严格基于 val，test 仅评估一次。
- 注：非参数基线（Seasonal-naive/Persistent）无训练，但用同一划分与同一指标代码；"同优化器"条款仅约束可训练模型。

## 8. 消融与敏感性（预期解读逻辑 → 均为待验证假设）
在代表单元格（w=24, SNR=1.0, 单变量, 平稳, H=48, seed 固定为 0 外加 5-seed 复核）上执行：
- **AB1 周期长度偏差**：w' ∈ {w−Δ, w, w+Δ, 2w, w/2}（Δ=4）。解读假设：w'=w 时 test MSE 应最低（残差中残留周期性最少）；w/2 把两相位合并导致最差；2w 因谐波结构（基频+一次谐波）可能近乎等价或略差。此为机制验证，非结论。
- **AB2 lag 偏移**：L ∈ {0, +1, −1, +w/2, −w/2}。解读假设：合成数据相位已知且平稳，L 影响应小；若漂移/相位错位数据（drift=True）出现，则 L 可能显著 → 用于判断相位对齐敏感性。
- **AB3 骨干替换**：linear vs DLinear 分别包在 CycleNet 里，对照组为对应 NoCycle 骨干 → 分离「周期模块增益」与「骨干能力增益」（RQ1/RQ3 归因）。
- **AB4 FrozenCycle**：C 是否必须可学习（联合训练的必要性）。

## 9. 完整实验矩阵（M=必做，O=可选分支）
**主对照矩阵（必做 M1–M16）**：因子 = w{24,168} × SNR{0.1,1.0} × H 关系{H<w, H>w} × {单变量, 平稳} = 2×2×2×2=16 单元格；每格方法 = {CycleNet(linear, w 正确), NoCycle-linear, DLinear, Seasonal-naive, Persistent} × 5 seeds。H 取值：w=24 → H∈{12(H<w), 48(H>w)}；w=168 → H∈{48(H<w), 336(H>w)}。
**消融矩阵（必做）**：AB1×5、AB2×5、AB3（linear/DLinear 各 ×[CycleNet, NoCycle]×5 seeds）、AB4×5，均在代表单元格。
**可选扩展（O）**：
- O1 多变量（D=8）重跑 M 的 4 个代表格；
- O2 非平稳漂移（drift=True）重跑 M 子集；
- O3 中间噪声 SNR=0.5；
- O4 真实基准验证：ETTh1/ETTm1/Weather/Traffic/Electricity（若数据可得，使用 §1-A 已知周期，协议同上）；
- O5 CycleNet+DLinear 骨干对比（补强 AB3）；
- O6 自动周期估计扩展（FFT/ACF 估计 w 后喂给模型）→ 解除「w 已知」假设的验证。

## 10. 可行性与限制
- **参数规模（CPU 可行）**：CycleNet-linear 单变量约 `w + P×H` ≈ 168+336×48≈20k 参数（w=168) / 24+256×48≈12k（w=24）；DLinear 同量级（约 2×P×H）。骨干仅 1 层线性或 DLinear（各 2 个线性层）。
- **训练开销（估计）**：每条序列 T≈2.9k–4k 点，stride=H 得约 60–140 窗口/epoch；100 epoch 早停约 10；单模型 CPU 上约数秒–数分钟。主矩阵约 16 格 × 5 方法 × 5 seeds ≈ 400 次训练（其中非参数无训练），加消融约再 100 次；估计 **224 核 CPU 环境下一日内可完成**。若运行端资源紧张，可降级为 seeds={0,1,2}、stride=2H（该降级属执行期决定，不影响设计逻辑）。
- **无 GPU 的限制**：只有 linear/DLinear 级骨干可训练；PatchTST/Transformer 级骨干与论文原始量级实验不在本设计范围 → 明确标注为「机制/可行性验证」，不构成对真实世界 SOTA 的复现主张。
- **合成数据外推边界**：正弦+高斯噪声+可选线性漂移不能覆盖真实数据的异方差噪声、缺失、日历/节假日效应；因此主结论限于「机制成立性与相对收益排序」，真实基准结论仅当 O4 执行后才可获得。

## 11. 分析方案（结果呈现）
1. 主表：每单元格各方法 test MSE/MAE（mean±std over 5 seeds）+ CycleNet 相对各基线提升%；单元格 × 方法的二维热力图。
2. RQ2 对比：w 固定时，横向比较 H<w 与 H>w 两格的相对提升率趋势。
3. 敏感性图：test MSE vs w'（AB1）、vs L（AB2），x 轴刻度标出 w=24 正确位置。
4. 消融归因：CycleNet vs NoCycle（周期增益）、vs FrozenCycle（可学习性）、linear vs DLinear（骨干增益）。
5. 所有表格注明「待验证假设/预测顺序，非实验结果」；配 5-seed 波动（±std）而非只报单点。

## 12. 交付物清单（落地所需）
1. `config.yaml`：因子取值、P/H/stride、优化器/调度/早停、seeds 列表（本设计 §3–§5 数值即其默认值）。
2. `gen_series.py`（§3.2 生成器 + FFT 校验）、`model.py`（§4.2 前向）、`train.py`（§4.3 循环）、`baselines.py`（§5）、`metrics.py`（§6）、`run_matrix.py`（§9 矩阵编排）。
3. `report.py`：主表/提升率/敏感性图/消融表（§11）。

—— 文档结束；除环境探测命令外，本设计未运行任何训练/评估实验。

## 1. What input/repository material exists

- The workspace contains **only** `/workspace/task.json`. Its `documents.track.md` explicitly says: *"Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required."*
- **No** code stubs, notes, docs, datasets, or references related to CycleNet or time-series forecasting exist in the repository.
- Environment facts I confirmed with exploratory commands:
  - Python 3.14.4, 224 CPU cores, **no GPU** (`gpu_enabled: false`).
  - **No** numpy, torch, pandas, scipy, sklearn, statsmodels, or any scientific ML stack installed (checked `site-packages`, `pip list`, and `pip cache`); only the system Python and pip/setuptools wheels are present.
  - **Network is disabled** (DNS resolution fails), so packages cannot be downloaded and public datasets (ETTh1, Weather, Electricity, Traffic, etc.) cannot be fetched.
  - No dataset files (csv/npz/pt) anywhere in the sandbox.
- Since no source material exists, the CycleNet design must be reconstructed from the published method (Linli Zhang et al., "CycleNet: Enhancing Time Series Forecasting through Modeling Periodic Patterns", NeurIPS 2024), and any details I cannot verify offline must be flagged as assumptions.

## 2. Proposed shape of the design (high level)

**Goal.** Implement and train a CycleNet-style forecast model and show it exploits periodic structure: implement Residual Cycle Forecasting (RCF) with a learnable periodic (cycle) component, evaluate on synthetic periodic data, and quantify gains vs. non-periodic baselines and ablations.

**Model (CycleNet-style core).**
- **Phase/cycle encoding:** known period length `p` (e.g., 24 for daily, 168 for weekly); a time-stamp encoder maps each time step to a phase index `r = t mod p`.
- **CycleNet block / learnable periodic weight:** a parameter matrix `W ∈ R^(p x d)` whose row `W[r]` is the phase's periodic embedding; the cycle component for any window is the gather `C[t] = W[r_t]`.
- **RCF residual framework:** (encoder) subtract the cycle component of the lookback window from the input so the sequence backbone models only the *residual*; (decoder) output = backbone's residual prediction + the cycle component of forecast timestamps `C_dec`.
- **Backbone:** a compact sequence model (e.g., a small Transformer encoder, or a DLinear-style linear head) that maps lookback residuals to multi-step residuals (direct multi-horizon, non-autoregressive).

**Data.** Primary: synthetic periodic multivariate series (sum of sinusoids with known daily/weekly cycles + trend + noise, with timestamp grid), generated in-repo so it is fully reproducible and offline-safe. Secondary (described but not executed unless obtainable): standard public benchmarks (ETT, Weather, Electricity) as an optional arm.

**Training/eval.** Temporal train/val/test split (no shuffling leakage); per-channel normalization (train-stat z-score); MSE loss + Adam + LR schedule + early stopping; direct multi-horizon prediction; metrics MSE/MAE overall and per-horizon. Baselines/controls: (a) seasonal-naive / mean-of-cycle forecast, (b) same model *without* the cycle component (RCF ablation), (c) the cycle-component-only forecaster (no residual backbone). Analysis: convergence, per-horizon errors, sensitivity to period misspecification (wrong `p`) and to noise level.

**Feasibility note.** Actual execution is explicitly not required and is *not* feasible here as-is (no numpy/torch and no network to install them), so the deliverable is a complete, self-contained design with pseudocode, hyperparameters, evaluation protocol, and an analysis plan. If execution were required, a minimal pure-Python/numpy implementation would run comfortably on 224 CPUs with a small synthetic dataset.

## 3. Key assumptions & uncertainties to pin down (before full design)
1. **Backbone architecture in the official CycleNet** — likely a compact Transformer encoder inside the RCF wrapper; I treat this as replaceable/optional (any residual-sequence model), to be stated as a design choice rather than a hard requirement.
2. **Exact CycleNet block internals** — whether the block adds an extra channel-mixing 1×1 conv on top of the row-lookup (`W[r]`) as part of the period network; the safe core is "learnable per-phase weight + gather," and the conv is an optional refinement.
3. **Data set selection** — no offline data exists, so synthetic generated data is the only executably available source; whether the design should also specify real-benchmark arms (for potential future execution) is open.
4. **Multivariate vs univariate** — official CycleNet is multivariate (channel-wise); I propose multivariate synthetic channels with a clear primary/secondary metric convention (MSE/MAE normalized, consistent with the paper).
5. **Periodicity knowledge** — the method assumes the period is known a priori; design must state the known-period assumption and the sensitivity arm for misspecified `p`.
6. **Environment constraints** — no GPU, no numpy/torch, no network; execution cannot be validated in this sandbox, so "feasible checks" are limited to syntax/logic-level pseudocode verification, not trained results.

Please approve this direction (or request adjustments to the model scope, data strategy, or metrics) and I will produce the full experiment design for the result handoff.

payload.answer:
# Final Experiment Design
## Implementing and training a CycleNet-style forecaster for periodic time series

**Deliverable type:** design + executable pseudocode + evaluation/analysis plan. **No experiment was run** and none is claimed. The design is reconstructed from the published CycleNet method (NeurIPS 2024, Zhang et al., "CycleNet: Enhancing Time Series Forecasting through Modeling Periodic Patterns") because the workspace contains no source material (verified: `/workspace` holds only `task.json`; `track.md` explicitly states "Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required"). Reconstruction-dependent details are explicitly labeled **[ASSUMPTION]**.

---

### 0. Fixed requirements vs. assumptions

**Fixed task requirements**
- Provide an experiment design for implementing and training a CycleNet-style model that forecasts periodic time series.
- Deliverable is a design; no execution, no claimed results.
- Design must include rationale, model spec, data spec, training/inference protocol, controls/ablations, analysis plan, and feasibility.

**[ASSUMPTION]s (labeled throughout)**
- A1. CycleNet is reconstructed from the published paper; its core invariant is the **Residual Cycle Forecasting (RCF)** framework with a **learnable per-phase periodic weight matrix**. Fine-grained implementation details of the official code are treated as design choices, not facts.
- A2. The model assumes a **known period length p** a priori (the paper's setting); the design adds a dedicated sensitivity arm for misspecified `p`.
- A3. **Synthetic, offline-generated data is the only executable data source** in this sandbox (no datasets present; network disabled). Real benchmarks are optional future arms only.
- A4. The backbone is **pluggable**; only the cycle mechanism is invariant. A lightweight default is chosen for CPU feasibility.

---

### 1. Rationale

**Objective.** Quantify whether a CycleNet-style model improves multi-horizon forecasts of periodic series, and isolate *which* design element drives the gain.

**Why this setup isolates the periodic contribution.** By using synthetic data with a *known ground-truth period*, we control exactly what the signal looks like. We can then ask four crisp questions, each answered by one control:
1. Does the learnable cycle component add value over the same backbone without it? → **M2 (no-cycle ablation)**.
2. Does the full model beat a classical seasonal baseline? → **M3 (seasonal-naive)**.
3. Is the residual-sequence backbone needed at all, or is the cycle component alone sufficient? → **M4 (cycle-only)**.
4. Does the model actually *use* periodicity correctly? → **sensitivity to misspecified `p` and to noise** (Section 6).

On real datasets (if ever available) these questions are confounded by unknown periodicity and other structure; the synthetic control design removes that ambiguity, making the periodic-modeling hypothesis directly testable.

---

### 2. Model specification (CycleNet-style)

#### 2.1 Notation
- `L` = lookback length, `H` = forecast horizon (e.g., `L=96`, `H=24`).
- `C0` = number of channels (multivariate), `d` = model/hidden width, `p` = known cycle length in samples (e.g., `p=24` hourly-daily, or `p=168` hourly-weekly).
- Inputs windows `x ∈ R^(B,L,C0)`; timestamp phase maps `r ∈ Z^(B,L+H)` giving per-step phase index.

#### 2.2 Timestamp → phase encoding
Given an hourly timestamp grid, phase index `r_t = t mod p`. For a second period (e.g., weekly in addition to daily), stack a second weight matrix; primary experiments use a **single dominant period** to keep interpretation clean **[ASSUMPTION A2]**. The encoder is a pure integer mapping (gather index), so it is deterministic and differentiable with respect to `W` via the gather.

#### 2.3 CycleNet block (learnable per-phase cycle component)
- Parameter `W ∈ R^(p × d)`; row `W[r]` is the learned periodic embedding for phase `r`.
- Cycle component for any window with phases `r[0:T]`: `C[t] = W[r_t]` (a batched gather), shape `(B, T, d)`.
- **Refinement (optional, [ASSUMPTION A1]):** a pointwise (1×1) channel-mixing projection applied to the gathered rows before/after addition. Default: include a `d×d` linear so the cycle component can mix features; this is a tunable and is *not* part of the invariant.

#### 2.4 RCF residual framework (the invariant)
- **Encoder (residualization):** `R_enc[t] = x_enc[t] − Proj_in(C_enc[t])` for `t` in the lookback window — the backbone never sees the raw periodic signal, only the residual.
- **Backbone:** `f_θ` maps `(R_enc, auxiliary features)` → residual forecast `R̂ ∈ R^(H, C0)`. Direct multi-horizon, non-autoregressive output.
- **Decoder (re-injection):** `y_hat[t] = R̂[t] + Proj_out(C_dec[t])` for `t` in the forecast window, where `C_dec` is gathered from the *forecast timestamps' phases*.

Pseudocode (single forward pass):

```
def forward(x_enc, r_enc, r_dec):
    C_enc = W[r_enc]                        # (B, L, d) cycle component of lookback
    R_enc = x_enc - lin_in(C_enc)           # residualize input
    R_hat = backbone(R_enc)                 # (B, H, C0) residual forecasts
    C_dec = W[r_dec]                        # gather cycle component at forecast phases
    return R_hat + lin_out(C_dec)           # (B, H, C0) final forecast
```

#### 2.5 Backbone (pluggable default)
- Default: a **compact Transformer encoder** (2 layers, `d=64–128`, 4 heads, MLP ratio 4, ~50–100k params) reading the residualized lookback and emitting `H` residual steps via a linear head. **[ASSUMPTION A4]**
- Lightweight alternative (fast CPU fallback): a **DLinear-style** linear decomposition head (two linear layers over `L→H` per channel). Because only the cycle mechanism is invariant, the design reports the backbone as a hyperparameter sweep over {Transformer, DLinear}; any backbone may be substituted without changing the RCF structure.

#### 2.6 Input/output shaping
- Input tensor `(B, L, C0)`; phase maps `(B, L)` and `(B, H)`; output `(B, H, C0)`.
- Training uses random contiguous windows of length `L+H` drawn from the train split (no cross-split windows).

---

### 3. Data specification (synthetic, offline, reproducible)

**Generator recipe (deterministic seed).** Hourly synthetic multivariate series, `C0=8` channels, total length `T = 3 years ≈ 26,304` points (or `T = 1 year` for the 224-CPU fast sweep):

```
t = arange(T), hours since epoch
for channel c in 0..C0-1:
    a_c, phi_c = per-channel amplitude/phase (random, fixed seed)
    b_c, psi_c = per-channel weekly amplitude/phase
    y_c(t) = a_c * sin(2π t/24  + phi_c)     # daily cycle, ground-truth p=24
           + b_c * sin(2π t/168 + psi_c)     # weekly cycle
           + beta_c * (t/T)                  # mild linear drift
           + sigma * eps_c(t)                # Gaussian noise, eps ~ N(0,1)
```

- **Split (strict temporal order, no leakage):** train = first 70%, val = next 15%, test = last 15%. Normalization statistics (per-channel z-score mean/std) computed **on train only** and applied to all splits.
- **Design variants** (created by re-running the generator):
  - Noise level `sigma ∈ {0.05, 0.2, 0.5}` (relative to median per-channel signal amplitude).
  - Misspecified period `p ∈ {23, 24, 25, 12}` for the sensitivity arm (true p = 24).
  - Optional irregular-sampling variant **[ASSUMPTION A3]** if irregular-data behavior is to be probed; not in the primary protocol.

**Real public benchmarks (ETT, Weather, Electricity, Traffic)** are **[ASSUMPTION A3] optional future arms only** — they cannot be obtained or executed in this sandbox (no network, no data files). The design is structured so the same `data → windows → model → metrics` pipeline accepts a `(values, timestamps)` interface, making a later real-data swap a drop-in change; the synthetic pipeline is the only executed/validated path.

---

### 4. Training / inference protocol

- **Loss:** MSE on raw (denormalized) scale during training; report **MSE and MAE** overall and per-horizon (paper convention). Optional normalized (per-channel variance) versions for cross-channel comparability.
- **Optimizer:** Adam, `lr=1e-3` (with `lr=1e-4` for the Transformer arm), weight decay `1e-4`; cosine or StepLR decay.
- **Batching:** window-based sampling, batch size 64–128, `L=96`, `H=24` primary; an `H∈{48,96}` horizon sweep for per-horizon analysis.
- **Early stopping:** monitor val MSE, patience 10 epochs, restore best-val checkpoint. Cap at ~100 epochs.
- **Statistical stability:** 5 independent training runs per configuration with distinct seeds; report **mean ± std** over seeds. All randomness (data generator, init, batching, optimizer) seeded.
- **Inference:** deterministic single forward pass over test windows; windows stride `H` over the test split to cover it densely; aggregate metrics over all forecast steps, and per-horizon `h=1..H` separately.

---

### 5. Controls / ablations (each answers a specific question)

| ID | Model | Change vs. full | Question it answers |
|----|-------|-----------------|---------------------|
| M1 | **CycleNet (full: RCF + backbone)** | — | Baseline method; the claim being tested. |
| M2 | **Backbone-only (no cycle)** | RCF disabled; backbone sees raw `x` | Does the learnable cycle component add value over the same capacity without it? |
| M3 | **Seasonal-naive** | statistical baseline: forecast = per-phase mean computed from train (or the learned `W` applied to forecast phases) | Does the learned model beat a classical seasonal baseline? |
| M4 | **Cycle-only** | residual backbone removed; `y_hat = C_dec` | Is residual-sequence modeling needed at all, or is the cycle component alone sufficient? |

Expected discriminating outcomes (stated as hypotheses, **not results**): M1 ≲ M3 in the noiseless low-trend case but should improve in noisy/trendy regimes; M1 < M2 is required to justify the cycle block; M1 < M4 (i.e., M4 alone insufficient) when trend/interaction structure exists beyond the pure period.

---

### 6. Analysis plan

- **Convergence:** per-seed train/val loss curves for M1 vs M2 (does residualization train faster/more stably?).
- **Per-horizon errors:** MSE/MAE table by horizon `h=1..H` for M1–M4 (is the benefit concentrated at certain horizons?).
- **Sensitivity to period misspecification:** run full model with `p∈{23,24,25,12}`; expect best at `p=24`, degradation at wrong `p` — demonstrating the model genuinely uses `p`. **[ASSUMPTION A2-derived test]**
- **Sensitivity to noise:** repeat M1/M2 at `sigma∈{0.05,0.2,0.5}`; check that the cycle component's advantage grows as noise drops (when periodicity is discernible).
- **Cycle-component inspection:** plot learned `W[r]` rows vs. the true sinusoid's phase, as a sanity check that the model recovers the ground-truth period shape.

**Results table template (to be filled only if ever executed):**

| Config | Model | p | σ | seed | Overall MSE | Overall MAE | MSE@h=1 | MSE@h=H | val loss (final) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | M1 | 24 | 0.2 | 0–4 | mean±std | mean±std | … | … | … |
| C2 | M2 | 24 | 0.2 | 0–4 | … | … | … | … | … |
| … | M3/M4, p-sweep, σ-sweep | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … |

---

### 7. Feasibility

- **This deliverable is a design + verified-for-logical-completeness pseudocode, not an executed experiment.** The sandbox has **no numpy/torch/scipy/pandas** (verified via `pip list`, `site-packages`, and `pip cache`), **no network** (DNS resolution fails, so packages cannot be installed), and **no GPU** (224 CPU cores only). Therefore no training run can be performed here, and no results are claimed.
- **If execution were later required**: a minimal **pure-Python/numpy** implementation is sufficient because the entire periodic mechanism is a gather (`W[r]`) plus elementwise residual subtraction/addition — no specialized ops. Requirements for a feasible run on these 224 CPUs: install numpy (single CPU suffices for a toy run), use small sizes (`L=96–168`, `H=24–96`, `C0=4–8`, `d=64–128`, Transformer with 2 layers, or DLinear), 1-year synthetic set, ~50–100 epochs; expected wall-clock on the order of minutes to a few hours on CPU. Vectorizing window batching and using the DLinear fallback makes it comfortably CPU-feasible.
- **Validation without execution:** the pseudocode can be statically checked for shape consistency and the RCF invariant (residualization before backbone, re-injection after); the evaluation protocol uses standard, reproducible definitions (temporal splits, per-channel train-stat normalization, fixed seeds, per-horizon metrics). These checks are part of the design, not executed experiments.

---

### Assumptions explicitly restated
- A1: CycleNet internals reconstructed from the paper; RCF + per-phase weight is the invariant; extra 1×1 mixing is optional.
- A2: known period `p` assumed a priori, with a misspecification sensitivity arm.
- A3: synthetic offline data is the only executable source; real benchmarks are optional future arms that cannot run in this sandbox.
- A4: the residual backbone is pluggable (Transformer default / DLinear fallback); the cycle mechanism is fixed.

**Uncertainties still open (non-blocking):** exact official block layout (A1), preferred default backbone (A4), single vs. multi-period encoding, and whether a future real-data arm is wanted. None of these require execution to be resolved.

Let's nail down the design before committing. I need three things from you, and none of them is the full plan yet.

1) INPUT / REPOSITORY INSPECTION. Give me a tight summary of InfLLM's mechanism straight from the paper/repo: (a) what the "dynamic context memory" actually does — how the context is segmented into blocks, what triggers block-level retrieval, and how retrieved blocks enter attention beyond the sliding window; and (b) what "unit representations" means in their setup — context units vs memory units, how units are encoded, and how attention is computed over units versus tokens.

2) PROPOSED APPROACH (sketch only). The question is about causal importance, so sketch a controlled ablation design across two factors: (i) dynamic context memory lookup ON vs OFF — where OFF means a fair alternative like standard recent-sliding-window attention or a fixed-size full-context attention within budget; and (ii) unit representation choices — e.g., unit granularity/size, how unit embeddings are derived, or unit-level vs token-level attention. Indicate a base model, matched parameter/flops budget, control conditions, candidate long-context tasks that stress retrieval (needle-in-haystack style, multi-hop/reasoning, QA, summarization), plus short-context counterparts, and an analysis plan (main effects, interaction, error and retrieval-success analysis). This is design-only — do NOT claim any experiment was run.

3) ASSUMPTIONS AND UNCERTAINTIES. The paper text is the source of truth, not memory. Flag explicitly every assumption: what "unit representations" refers to, whether dropping dynamic lookup is a fair control, benchmark choice, and any compute/runtime budget we cannot verify. Don't present the full solution yet — I'll review the approach next turn before we move to the main work.

PLAN (sketch — no experiment run)

Environment check first: /workspace contains only task.json; no InfLLM repo, no datasets, torch absent, network disabled. So the mechanism summary below is reconstructed from the published paper (arXiv 2402.04617, Xiao et al. 2024) from memory and must be treated as to-be-verified against the paper text where I flag it. Python 3.14 present; no compute. This is a design deliverable only.

=========================================
1) INPUT / REPOSITORY INSPECTION (from paper, since no repo present)
=========================================
(a) Dynamic context memory — what it does
• The long prefix is segmented into fixed-size blocks called context units (size c tokens, typically c≈128).
• For each unit the model keeps a compact "unit representation" (see (b)) in a memory store; the full token-level K/V states of the unit are kept in an external cache, not in the running attention.
• A "lookup" step runs per forward pass: the current query (plus attention-sink tokens) attends to the unit representations in memory, scores them, and retrieves the top-k most relevant units — this is the block-level retrieval trigger (attention over compressed units, not tokens).
• The retrieved units' token-level K/V states are then loaded and attended at token granularity together with the attention sink and the recent sliding-window tokens. So "entry into attention beyond the window" is exactly: retrieved-unit token KVs are appended to the window context.
• Memory is dynamic because it grows/shrinks over the sequence: when tokens slide out of the recent window they are compacted into units and written to memory/disk cache, and a lookup is re-run at each step to keep the selected units fresh.

(b) Unit representations
• Context units = the blocks of c consecutive tokens (the segmentation).
• Memory units = the stored compressed representations (plus their cached token KVs).
• Encoding of a unit: mean-pooling the key states of its tokens (my recollection; see Assumption U1 — the paper may additionally refine these with a contrastive objective while keeping the LLM frozen — must be verified).
• Two attention granularities: coarse attention over unit representations during lookup (selects top-k), and fine token-level attention over sink+window+retrieved-unit tokens during actual generation.

=========================================
2) PROPOSED APPROACH (sketch)
=========================================
Experiment: 2-factor controlled ablation on causal importance.

Base model: Llama-2-7B/4K (the paper's primary model). Note: this environment has no GPU; the design assumes external GPU execution. A smaller sanity-check model (e.g., Llama-2-7B or Mistral-7B) with the same protocol is acceptable if budget is thin; the base model must be identical across all arms.

Factor A — dynamic context memory lookup: ON vs OFF
• A-ON (treatment): full InfLLM — attention sink + sliding window + top-k retrieved units (unit-level lookup then token-level attention).
• A-OFF (active control, budget-matched): same attended-token budget W + k·c but selection is NOT dynamic — e.g., (i) StreamingLLM-style sink+recent-window-only, and (ii) fixed/static block selection (first-N blocks or uniformly strided blocks) replacing the lookup. This isolates the "dynamic lookup" component per se.
• Reference arms (not factors): (R1) full-context attention on the full long input (upper-bound oracle, only feasible on moderate lengths), (R2) truncate-to-window (lower bound). These give the performance envelope but are not treated as factors.
• Budget control: fix W (sliding window), k (retrieved units) and c so every ON/OFF arm attends to the same number of tokens per query ⇒ differences are attributable to mechanism, not compute. Attended-token/FLOPs per query is constant across arms.

Factor B — unit representation choice (tested at lookup ON, and also crossed with factor A where sensible):
• B1 unit granularity c ∈ {64, 128, 256} tokens.
• B2 unit encoding: (i) mean-pooled keys (paper default, pending verification), (ii) last-token key, (iii) a small learned projection (contrastive-style refinement if the paper supports it), (iv) raw token-KV proxy (no compression) as an upper probe.
• B3 selection granularity: top-k unit-level (compressed) attention vs a token-level soft-attention routing for the same budget.

Design shape: factorial table — A {ON, OFF-dynamic, OFF-memory} × B {c × encoding × granularity}, plus R1/R2 references. Randomized/NIAH-style trials repeated with multiple needles, positions, distractors, seeds.

Tasks (long-context, retrieval-stressing):
• Retri: needle-in-haystack / passkey / synthetic NIAH with varied needle depth and distance.
• Multi-hop: long-context multi-hop reasoning where evidence spans are far apart (distant-span retrieval + composition).
• QA: long-doc QA (LongBench-family / LooGLE-style where a specific distant passage answers).
• Summ: long-document summarization (faithfulness/ROUGE) — stresses whether lookup selects the informative units vs generic text.
• Short-context counterparts: the same task families at short length (within 4K) to (i) confirm the base model isn't degraded by our scaffolding and (ii) establish the "no long-context burden" baseline.

Analysis plan:
• Main effects: paired mean differences with CIs — Δ(lookup ON vs OFF) across tasks; Δ(unit variants) within lookup ON.
• Interaction: two-way (task × lookup) and (lookup × unit representation) — e.g., does unit representation matter more when lookup is ON? Does lookup help more on retrieval-heavy vs summarization tasks?
• Error analysis: post-hoc classification of failures (retrieval miss — correct unit not in top-k but token-level attention would have found it vs reasoning failure after correct retrieval vs local-answer failure).
• Retrieval-success analysis: unit-level recall@k (does the ground-truth answer span's unit enter the top-k?) plotted against downstream accuracy and correlated with lookup ON arms; this directly isolates lookup quality from downstream reasoning.
• Efficiency sanity-check (descriptive): attended tokens/query and runtime for the budget-matched arms, only to confirm the budget match is honored — not a headline claim.

=========================================
3) ASSUMPTIONS AND UNCERTAINTIES (explicit)
=========================================
Assumptions:
• A1: The paper (arXiv 2402.04617) is the source of truth; I could NOT open it offline — the mechanism summary (unit size ≈128, mean-pooled key encoding, attention-sink+window+top-k retrieved units) is from memory and must be re-verified against the actual paper text/code before the results stage.
• A2: "Unit representations" refers to the compressed per-block (per-unit) representations used by the lookup, distinct from the token KVs; encoding = mean-pooled keys (pending A1 verification of any contrastive refinement).
• A3: Dropping dynamic lookup is a fair control only if the attended-token budget (W + k·c per query) is matched across ON/OFF arms and the base model is identical; otherwise ON would confound compute with mechanism.
• A4: Benchmark choice (NIAH, LongBench/LooGLE-style QA+mul-hop+summ, short counterparts) is my selection, not mandated by the task/repo.
• A5: Base model Llama-2-7B is assumed acceptable; requires an external GPU environment (this one has none) — if no GPU is available the design cannot be executed as specified.
• A6: Attention-sink + sliding-window is treated as the "OFF" scaffold inherited from InfLLM; I assume the paper itself contains this scaffold.

Uncertainties:
• U1: Exact InfLLM hyperparameters (c, k, W, whether lookup uses attention-sink queries too) — unverified.
• U2: Whether the paper trains/refines unit representations (contrastive objective with frozen LLM) vs pure mean-pooling — impacts Factor B design; verify before finalizing.
• U3: Whether "OFF = standard recent-sliding-window attention within budget" is a fair/meaningful counterfactual for the causal question, or whether reviewers require both a fixed-block and a random-block control.
• U4: Runtime/memory budget for Llama-2-7B inference on 128K–1M inputs — cannot be estimated reliably here (no GPU); needs calibration on the target hardware.
• U5: Metric choice for retrieval success (unit recall@k) assumes we can locate the ground-truth answer span in the input — easy for NIAH, harder for LongBench-style QA.
• U6: How to define "within budget" for the fixed full-context reference arm at the longest lengths (full attention is infeasible there) — may need to cap the oracle arm at moderate lengths.

No experiment was run. Next step: your review of this sketch; I will then produce the full step-by-step design (conditions table, per-task protocols, metrics, controls, budget model, and a feasibility check list).

आपका प्रस्ताव मंज़ूर है — दृष्टिकोण मुद्दे के केंद्र को सही पकड़ता है। मुख्य विकल्पों पर मेरी बात:

1) बजट-मिलान ही इस प्रयोग का दिल है। हर ON/OFF हाथ में प्रति-क्वेरी attended tokens (W + k·c) और base model बिल्कुल समान रहें, वरना तुलना compute को mechanism से अलग नहीं कर सकती। OFF के लिए दोनों नियंत्रण रखें — (i) sink+sliding-window मात्र और (ii) static/नियत block selection (पहले-N या strided) — ताकि U3 की अस्पष्टता दूर रहे।

2) unit representation के विकल्पों (c ∈ {64,128,256}, encoding, selection granularity) का पूरा factorial बहुत सारी कोशिकाएँ बनाएगा, और GPU न होने से runtime अनिश्चित है। यह सुझाव है, अनिवार्य नहीं: चरणबद्ध तरीका रखें — पहले lookup ON/OFF का core crossover न्यूनतम cell पर, फिर unit variants का profile झुकाव-विश्लेषण, और full factorial सिर्फ एक उपसमुच्चय पर। अंतिम design में cell count स्पष्ट बताइए।

3) retrieval-success विश्लेषण (unit recall@k) को मुख्य मीट्रिकों में रखें — यही lookup quality को downstream reasoning से अलग करता है। NIAH में needle depth × position × distractor को चरणबद्ध रखें।

4) full-attention oracle (R1) को केवल मध्यम लंबाई तक कैप करें, और short-context arms को sanity baseline रूप में रखें।

5) तथ्य-पक्ष: जब तक कागज़/कोड offline उपलब्ध नहीं है, unit size (लगभग 128), mean-pooled key encoding आदि assumption ही हैं — अंतिम design में इन्हें "verification pending" के रूप में चिह्नित करें और U1/U2 से जोड़ें।

payload.answer:
FULL DESIGN (deliverable) — stage=result. Design-only; no experiment run, no results invented.

========================================================================
0. DESIGN PRINCIPLES
========================================================================
• Head-to-head comparisons hold base model, prompts, seeds, and per-query attended-token budget (W + k·c + s) constant across ON and OFF arms, so differences are attributable to mechanism not compute.
• Staged to keep GPU-unknown: Phase 1 core crossover on minimal cells → Phase 2 unit-profile (one-factor-at-a-time at A=ON) → Phase 3 factorial on a small core subset. Full factorial run only if Phase 0 shows budget headroom.
• Retrieval-success (unit recall@k) is a first-class metric tier, splitting lookup quality from downstream reasoning.
• Placeholder defaults below (c≈128, k≈3, W≈1024, sink s≈4) are marked VERIFICATION PENDING (U1) — they must be confirmed from the paper/code before building anything.

Notation: W = sliding-window size, k = retrieved units, c = tokens/unit, s = attention-sink tokens. Default (pending) B: c=128, mean-pooled-key encoding, unit-level top-k selection, k=3.

========================================================================
1. CONDITIONS TABLE (full cell count)
========================================================================
FACTOR A — lookup mechanism (3 levels):
  A_ON        : dynamic unit-level lookup → top-k units' token KVs enter attention with sink+window.
  A_OFF_WIN   : active control — sink + window ONLY, window enlarged to W + k·c so per-query attended tokens match A_ON; no memory/lookup.
  A_OFF_STATIC: active control — sink + window (W) + fixed k·c tokens selected statically (variant a: first-N blocks; variant b: strided blocks), matched budget.
References (not factors): R1 full-context attention (oracle) capped at moderate length (default L_cap = 32K, fixed in Phase 0); R2 truncate-to-first-V-tokens (lower bound, V = W + k·c).

FACTOR B — unit representation:
  Bc granularity   : {64, 128, 256}
  Be encoding      : {mean-pooled keys (default), last-token key, learned/contrastive-refined (ONLY if the paper supports it — U2; else this level is dropped)}
  Bs selection     : {unit-level top-k (default), token-level routing}
  → full B grid = 3 × 3 × 2 = 18 (or 3×2×2 = 12 if learned encoding unsupported).

TASK SET (5 families):
  T1 NIAH (needle-in-haystack, staged) | T2 long-context multi-hop reasoning | T3 long-doc QA | T4 long-document summarization | T5 short-context counterparts of T1–T3 (length ≤ 4K, sanity baseline).

STAGE CELL COUNTS (unique treatment cells):
  Phase 1  core crossover: A{ON, OFF_WIN, OFF_STATIC} × B_default = 3 cells, run on all 5 families (+R1 at L_cap on T1–T3, R2 on all).
  Phase 2  unit-profile at A=ON: Bc{64,256} + Be_last-token (+Be_learned if supported) + Bs_token-routing = 4–5 unique cells, run on all 5 families.
  Phase 3  interaction subset (core tasks T1, T2, T3): A{ON, OFF_STATIC} × B_subset{mean/c128, mean/c256, last/c128, last/c256} → 8 cells; minus 5 already run in Ph1–2 ⇒ ~3 new cells; extends to A(3)×B_subset(4)=12 if budget allows.
  TOTAL: ≈ 11 core cells + (optional) up to 18-cell full B factorial on the core-task subset; each cell = (tasks × trials × seeds) repeated measures for CIs.

========================================================================
2. PER-TASK PROTOCOLS
========================================================================
Common: greedy decoding (temperature 0) OR seed-locked per instance across cells; identical prompt templates across all arms (no per-arm prompt tuning); ≥5 seeds per condition; report mean ± 95% CI.

T1 NIAH (staged): synthetic long documents with embedded needles.
  • Trial factors: needle depth d ∈ {0.05, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 0.95}; needle position ∈ {front, middle, back}; distractor count ∈ {0, 5, 20} needles; context length ∈ {8K, 32K, 128K} (longest only if Phase-0 GPU budget allows).
  • Metrics: needle-answer accuracy; UNIT_RECALL@k = did the unit containing the needle enter the top-k retrieved set?; depth×position error curves.

T2 Multi-hop: long-context reasoning with two evidence spans in distant units (separation controlled, e.g., ≥ 50% of context apart).
  • Metrics: final-answer EM; UNIT_RECALL@{k} over BOTH gold units.

T3 Long-doc QA: LongBench/LooGLE-style long-document QA with gold support passages.
  • Metrics: answer EM/F1; UNIT_RECALL@k w.r.t. the gold-support unit.

T4 Summarization: long-document summarization.
  • Metrics: faithfulness (NLI/FactScore-style) and ROUGE-L; UNIT_RECALL@k = coverage of manually-marked salient units (whether lookup selects informative units).

T5 Short counterparts (≤4K): same families at short length → sanity that the scaffolding (sink+window+our OFF/ON code paths) does not degrade short-context capability vs the base model; isolates "long-context burden".

========================================================================
3. METRICS AND ERROR TAXONOMY
========================================================================
Metric tiers:
  M1 primary: task accuracy (EM/F1/faithfulness) + UNIT_RECALL@k (retrieval-success as a matched, per-trial measurement).
  M2 efficiency (descriptive, to confirm budget match only): measured attended tokens/query, per-query wall-clock, KV memory — a check that the budget constraint holds, NOT a headline claim.
  M3 error attribution.

Error taxonomy (per failed trial, one label):
  E1 RETRIEVAL MISS   : correct unit not in top-k (unit recall@k fails) → failure attributable to lookup.
  E2 RETRIEVAL OK/REASON FAIL: unit retrieved, token attention saw it, downstream reasoning wrong.
  E3 LOCAL FAILURE    : required info inside the window and attended, yet wrong → base-model/capability limit.
  E4 SETUP FAILURE    : decode/format/parse errors (excluded from accuracy, reported separately).
Marginal-claim rule: E1 dominating the ON-vs-OFF gap ⇒ lookup critical; E2 dominating ⇒ unit coverage/representation critical; E3 dominating ⇒ the factor matters little (capability bottleneck). This is the experiment's core inference.

========================================================================
4. ANALYSIS PLAN
========================================================================
• Main effects: paired differences with CIs — (Δ ON vs OFF_WIN), (Δ ON vs OFF_STATIC) per task; (Δ unit variants) at A=ON.
• Interactions: two-way task × A (does lookup matter more on retrieval-heavy NIAH/QA than on summarization?); A × B in Phase 3 (does representation matter only when lookup is ON?).
• Retrieval-success mediation: plot accuracy vs UNIT_RECALL@k across cells; decompose the ON-vs-OFF gap into E1 vs E2 vs E3 shares.
• NIAH curve analysis: accuracy across depth × position × distractor; identify lookup-specific failure bands (deep/back needles, high distractors) vs uniform degradation.
• Robustness: Phase-2 profile (c, encoding, selection) reported as effect sizes with multiple-seed CIs, not only significance.

========================================================================
5. BUDGET MODEL (per query, matched across ON and OFF cells)
========================================================================
attended_tokens (per query, per layer):
  A_ON        : s + W + k·c          (lookup adds +m unit-representation scores, m = block count)
  A_OFF_WIN   : s + (W + k·c)        ← same total, enlarged window
  A_OFF_STATIC: s + W + k·c          ← same total, fixed blocks
  R1 (oracle) : L (capped at L_cap)  ← reference only
  R2 (trunc.) : V = W + k·c
Matching: the dominant attention term (QKᵀ + PV over attended tokens) is equal across A_ON/A_OFF_WIN/A_OFF_STATIC. A_ON adds only the cheap lookup over m compressed units (m ≪ m·c); Phase 0 MEASURES actual per-query FLOPs/wall-clock, and if the lookup term exceeds ~10% of per-query attention cost the matched-budget claim is weakened and reported as a caveat. KV memory is NOT matched across arms (inherent to the methods) — documented, kept out of the causal claim.

========================================================================
6. CONTROLS
========================================================================
C1 Budget + base-model match (Section 5). C2 Identical prompts/templates across all arms. C3 Multiple seeds + CIs; greedy/seed-locked decoding. C4 Oracle (R1, capped) and truncation (R2) envelope. C5 Short-context sanity (T5). C6 Static-block control covers both first-N and strided variants (resolves U3). C7 Lookup-quality confound excluded by measuring UNIT_RECALL@k separately from accuracy.

========================================================================
7. FEASIBILITY CHECKLIST
========================================================================
 [ ] Verify paper/code text for c, k, W, sink, unit encoding, and any contrastive refinement (A1/U1/U2) — FIRST action; update all "pending" placeholders before building.
 [ ] Confirm GPU availability & memory for cached per-unit KVs and retrieved-unit attention at target L (this environment has none — execution must move to a GPU cluster; Phase 0 calibrates).
 [ ] Confirm weights (Llama-2-7B) and datasets (synthetic NIAH generator, LongBench/LooGLE splits, summarization corpus) accessible.
 [ ] Phase 0: measure per-query FLOPs/wall-clock for A_ON vs A_OFF arms at one length; confirm budget match within tolerance; fix L_cap ≥ max{32K, feasible} for R1; fix max context length (8K/32K/128K) affordable.
 [ ] Smoke test: unit-encoding implementation reproduces paper defaults (mean-pooled keys) on a 5-instance run before staged execution.
 [ ] Decide learned-encoding level inclusion based on U2 outcome.
 [ ] Pre-register metrics, error taxonomy, and marginal-claim rules before Phase 1.

========================================================================
8. ASSUMPTIONS (verification pending) & UNCERTAINTIES
========================================================================
Carried from the approved sketch and now resolved: two OFF controls kept (U3 closed); retrieval-success as a primary metric tier; R1 capped at L_cap and short arms kept as sanity; c≈128 / mean-pool etc. remain verification-pending and wired to U1/U2. Full structured lists passed separately as fields: 7 assumptions and 6 uncertainties, the salient ones being — the paper/code is the source of truth and all placeholder hyperparameters/mechanism details are pending confirmation (A1/A2/U1); unit-representation encoding may be contrastively refined rather than pure mean-pooling (U2); GPU runtime at 8K/32K/128K is unverifiable here and Phase 0 calibrates it (U4); gold-span localization drives the QA/summ recall@k quality (U5).

payload.answer:
## 0. Инспекция исходных материалов (что реально есть)

- /workspace содержит **только** task.json. Файла track.md и какого-либо кода/репозитория по InfLLM **нет** (проверено find по всему дереву: InfLLM/track не найдены).
- В task.json: documents.track.md = "Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required." → это подтверждает design-only статус.
- Сеть отключена (network: disabled) → скачать статью/код InfLLM прямо отсюда нельзя. **По InfLLM в рабочей среде есть только описание в вопросе; код недоступен.** Архитектура InfLLM используется как допущение на основе статьи (см. §«Допущения»).
- Среда: python3, системные зависимости без проектных пакетов, нет GPU, 224 CPU. Реальный прогон не требуется и не заявлен.

## 1. Постановка: два причинных фактора, один вопрос «насколько критичны»

Вопрос решается как оценка **главных эффектов и их взаимодействия** двух факторов на скор длинноконтекстных задач.

**Фактор A — механизм lookup контекстной памяти** (сколько уровней описано в §2):
- A1 *dynamic retrieval* (InfLLM-style): query → attention по unit-репрезентациям → selection top-k юнитов → decode-attention по токенам выбранных юнитов + недавнее окно;
- A2 *фиксированное скользящее окно* (только последние S токенов, никакого обращения к памяти; S так, чтобы бюджет токенов совпадал с A1/A3);
- A3 *случайные блоки* (те же k юнитов, тот же бюджет, но выбор без запроса — рандом, засеянный; изолирует «умный выбор» от «факта существования памяти»);
- A4 *full attention по всей памяти* (потолок/ceil-референс, не бюджет-сматчен).

**Фактор B — представление единиц памяти** (способ сжатия блока в то, по чему считается lookup-внимание; только для A1/A3/A4-подобных, см. §2):
- B1 representative-token hidden state (дефолт InfLLM: выделенный токен-представитель блока);
- B2 mean-pooling токенов блока;
- B3 max-pooling;
- B4 первый токен блока как представитель (без доп. токена);
- B5 «кэш всех токенов блока» (без сжатия в вектор — lookup по всем ключам блока).

## 2. Структура дизайна: факторный 2×K + два референсных «плеча»

A2 и A4 не используют unit-репрезентации, поэтому их нельзя вписать в полное пересечение A×B (B там вакуумно). Поэтому:

- **Основная сетка (факторный 2×K):** A ∈ {A1 dynamic, A3 random} × B ∈ {B1…B5} → 2×5 = 10 ячеек, все на одном наборе инстансов (within-subject, paired).
- **Референсные ячейки вне сетки:** A2 (окно, B не применяется) и A4 (full attention, B не применяется, не budget-matched). Они дают нижнюю и верхнюю границы шкалы.

Почему факторный 2×K уместен:
- Исследовательский вопрос — это два главных эффекта + взаимодействие. Пересечённая сетка оценивает: (1) насколько сильно падает скор при замене dynamic→random при каждом B (критичность lookup); (2) насколько вариация по B двигает скор при фиксированном lookup (критичность представления); (3) взаимодействие (например, плохие репрезентации B «ломают» dynamic сильнее, чем random — тогда представление критично только в связке с умным lookup);
- Сетка мала (2×5), полный факторный дизайн выполним; дробный факторный (например, свёрнутый fold-over или латинский квадрат по задачам) — только резерв, если бюджет жёсткий;
- B почти вычислительно-нейтрален для основной метрики (меняется лишь дешёвый lookup по репрезентациям, а не число attend-токенов) — это идеальное свойство независимой переменной: мы измеряем цену качества «сжатия», а не цену флопов.

## 3. Зависимые переменные и набор задач (стратификация по потребности в удалённой памяти)

**Первичные (accuracy-класс):**
- **Passkey / needle-in-a-haystack:** accuracy и median-error-distance; сетка длин контекста (например, 4K/8K/16K/32K/64K/128K) × глубины иглы (early/mid/late → early = требует удалённого lookup; late = покрывается окном, контроль на «recent bias»).
- **LongBench-класс метрик,** стратифицированные подзадачи по удалённости знания: single-doc QA (NarrativeQA, Qasper), multi-doc QA (MultiFieldQA, HotpotQA), summarization, few-shot, code completion; плюс синтетические «∞Bench-стиль» задачи с известным местоположением факта (для них известен «ground-truth unit» — это даёт процессную метрику ниже).
- При необходимости — **perplexity** на длинных документах (PG-19-класс) по позиции контекста как sanity-check (не как основной довод, т.к. PPL слабый прокси длинных рассуждений).

**Вторичные/процессные (объясняющие «почему»):**
- **Top-k unit retrieval hit-rate** — попадание ground-truth юнита в выбранные top-k (на синтетике иглу мы знаем точно); прямая связка «качество представления → правильность выбора → итоговый скор».
- Латентность, FLOPs, размер буфера памяти (чтобы отделить «качество выбора» от «эффективности»).

## 4. Контроли

- Фиксированный backbone и фиксированная длина контекста на ячейку; фикс. decoding (greedy/фикс. beam, температура 0; при стохастике — повтор по нескольким сидам с усреднением);
- Одинаковая сегментация контекста на юниты (фикс. размер блока, например, 128 токенов, контигуальные блоки) во всех A1/A3/B-ячейках;
- Одинаковые промпты/шаблоны/инстансы и сиды (та же последовательность задач, тот же порядок предъявления);
- Единый evaluation harness: одни и те же скрипты скорения и определения метрик на все условия;
- Бюджет-матчинг: A1/A3/A2 attend одинаковое число токенов (W недавних + k·u токенов юнитов); A4 — отдельный не-матченный потолок;
- Симметрия по вычислительным ресурсам (одна машина/конфиг), случайные абляции A3 — 5 сидов с усреднением и разбросом;
- Процедура «одной папки логов»: единый формат вывода моделей, единый парсер.

## 5. Конфаунды и как их учесть

- **Recent bias / локальность:** иглы late решаются даже без lookup → их отдельно выделяем как контроль, основной сигнал — early/mid иглы; отчёт отдельно по глубинам.
- **Размер юнита × представление:** mean/max/rep по-разному ведут себя при крупных блоках → фикс. размер блока на основной сетке + малая robustness-прогонка (2 размера блока) для B-фактора.
- **Top-k взаимозависимость:** random и dynamic чувствительны к k по-разному → фикс. k и u на основной сетке, чувствительность по k как второстепенный подпрогон.
- **Разнокалиберность LongBench:** скор не агрегировать вслепую → отчёт по подзадачам + взвешенная агрегация; стратификация по «удалённости» факта.
- **Форматные шорткаты в passkey:** несколько стилей/несколько игл, вариация форматов.
- **Знакомство backbone с задачами (data contamination):** использовать hold-out семейства/недавние задачи; зафиксировать как остаточный конфаунд.
- **Имплементационные различия arms** (masks, KV-кэширование, порядок стека токенов): унифицировать код вокруг общего интерфейса декодирования, diff-проверка масок.
- **Асимметрия бюджета** (A4 и частично A2): отчёт в двух системах координат — «при равном бюджете» (основной) и «потолок/без ограничения бюджета» (вторичный).

## 6. Анализ и метрика «критичности»

- На сетке 2×K: repeated-measures ANOVA / mixed-effects (условия — фикс. эффекты, инстансы — случайные) по ячейкам задач; главные эффекты A, B и взаимодействие; эффекты стандартизовать (partial η², абсолютный Δ скоров).
- Сравнение с референсами: парные тесты (paired t/Wilcoxon) сетки против A2 (вниз) и A4 (вверх) — это помещает все 10 ячеек на шкалу «окно ↔ потолок»; «критичность lookup» = Δ(A1−A3), «критичность представления» = размах по B при A1.
- Процессная медиация: hit-rate как объясняющая переменная для скоров (регрессия/медиация), чтобы отличить «выбор не тот» от «представление потеряно».

## 7. Ключевые допущения

1. **Архитектура InfLLM по статье (код недоступен):** токены сегментируются на фикс. юниты; у каждого юнита есть репрезентация (по умолчанию — hidden state выделенного токена-представителя); lookup = attention запроса по репрезентациям юнитов → top-k; декодинг attends недавнее окно + токены выбранных юнитов; без обучения (training-free).
2. «Dynamic context memory lookup» операционализирован как top-k выбор по unit-репрезентациям; «unit representations» — как перечень B1…B5 (от сжатия к полному кэшу токенов блока).
3. Backbone и бенчмарки (LLaMA-класс или меньшая открытая модель, LongBench, passkey-генератор) доступны в целевой среде выполнения; сейчас сеть выключена, но design-only это не блокирует.
4. Вычисления — только инференс (InfLLM training-free), поэтому каждая ячейка ограничена стоимостью forward на евал-сетах; для бюджета допустим малый/средний backbone (например, 1–8B, CPU fp16 или fp8 как запасной вариант).
5. Метрики стандартизованы; выбор exact-match vs LLM-судья — отдельное решение eval harness.

## 8. Существенные неопределённости (нужны уточнения при полном дизайне)

1. Точный дефолт InfLLM: размер юнита, способ репрезентативного токена, на каких слоях берётся репрезентация, учитывается ли всегда недавнее окно (нужно сверить со статьёй/кодом, когда появится доступ к сети).
2. Что автор вопроса вкладывает в «unit representations» (сжатие в вектор vs кэш всех токенов) — дизайн перекрывает оба конца спектра (B1…B5).
3. Доступность/лицензии LongBench и подзадач; формат passkey-генерации; нужен ли LLM-судья (доп. модель = доп. дисперсия).
4. Бюджет прогона полной сетки (10 ячеек + 2 референса + N задач × L длин × K глубин) — при жёстком бюджете переход на дробный факторный/меньший backbone; но это design-only, потому вопрос отложен.
5. Определение «честного» budget-матчинга A2 (S недавних токенов vs k удалённых юнитов) — операционализация нетривиальна, нужно зафиксировать заранее.
6. Переносимость выводов на разные backbone-семейства (эффект может зависеть от модели) — рассматривается как обобщаемость, а не конфаунд основной сетки.

## 9. Что уточнить у исследователя для полного дизайна (приоритетно)

- (1) фиксировать ли backbone 7B/8B-класс или разрешён малый прокси; (2) нужен ли полноценный LongBench или достаточно синтетики (passkey + ∞Bench-стиль), где известен ground-truth unit; (3) считать ли A4/full attention обязательным потолком; (4) приемлем ли LLM-судья для LongBench-класса метрик.

Кода InfLLM в среде нет — архитектура берётся как допущение из статьи.

payload.message:
План подхода одобряю — он отвечает вопросу «насколько критичны» через факторную сетку (главные эффекты + взаимодействие lookup×представление), бюджет-матчинг, референсные плечи (окно / full attention) и процессные метрики (top-k hit-rate) для объяснения механизма. Ниже фиксирую твои открытые пункты как решения дизайнера, чтобы финал не застрял на уточнениях (это assumptions, не факты).

(1) Backbone: фиксируем ОДИН открытый backbone ~7–8B класса (например, LLaMA-3-8B/аналог) как основное условие; чувствительность на малом backbone (1–3B) — опциональный вторичный прогон для обобщения, не обязательный. Все 10 ячеек + 2 референса гонятся на одном бэкбоне.
(2) Задачи: ядро вывода — синтетика с известным ground-truth unit (passkey/needle-сетка по длине 4K–128K и глубине early/mid/late + ∞Bench-стиль задачи с известным местом факта); LongBench-класс — вторичный реалистичный набор (одиночный/мультидок QA, summarization, few-shot) для внешней валидности. Полный LongBench не обязателен; отчёт по подзадачам без слепой агрегации.
(3) A4 full attention — включаем как потолок (не budget-matched), A2 окно — низ референсной шкалы. Это нужно для калибровки «критичности».
(4) Метрики: primary — exact/normalized match на passkey/синтетике (детерминировано); LLM-judge — только secondary для open-ended LongBench QA, один и тот же judge-модель и фиксированный промпт на всех ячейках (доп. дисперсия одинакова).
(5) Статистика: mixed-effects/repeated-measures (условия — фикс., инстансы — случайные), partial η² + абсолютные Δ, парные тесты ячеек против A2/A4; hit-rate как медиатор.

Теперь соберёшь финальный deliverable — полный дизайн эксперимента с (а) рациональностью/гипотезами, (б) всеми условиями и их обоснованием, (в) контролами и конфаундами, (г) планом анализа, (д) оценкой выполнимости (инференс-only, порядок величин по forward-прогонам). Эксперимент НЕ запускать и результатов не выдумывать — только дизайн. В конце явно перечисли assumptions и unresolved uncertainties. Это design-only; код/запуск не нужны.
