# Diseño experimental final (sin ejecución)

**Estado declarativo.** No se ha ejecutado ningún experimento. Este documento es el plan pre-registrado. Los únicos datos de la fuente son: la pregunta, el contexto ("design an experiment; researcher can clarify setup by topic") y el placeholder track.md ("Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required"). Todo lo demás referente a WorkArena++, el framework, el modelo, la métrica y el presupuesto es **decisión de diseño o conocimiento general externo a verificar al implementar** — así etiquetado en §6.

---

## 1) Hipótesis y definición operativa de "mejorar"

**Hipótesis nula (confirmatoria, pareada):** para una misma instancia de tarea, la probabilidad de éxito con prompting CoT iguala a la del control de próxima acción: P(success_CoT) = P(success_Ctrl). En términos de McNemar: entre pares discordantes, la dirección no es sistemática (P(control ok, CoT fail) = P(CoT ok, control fail)).

**Hipótesis alternativa:** CoT produce una tasa de éxito por episodio mayor que el control.

**Definición operativa de "mejorar" (regla de decisión pre-registrada):** se declara mejora **solo si se cumplen las tres condiciones** sobre la muestra pareada completa:
1. Test de McNemar exacto bilateral: p < 0.05.
2. Estimación puntual de la diferencia pareada (tasa CoT − tasa control) ≥ δ_min = **+5 puntos porcentuales** absolutos.
3. El límite inferior del IC bootstrap (percentil, 10 000 remuestras de clusters de instancias tarea) de la diferencia pareada es **> 0**.

**Umbral de significancia fijo:** α = 0.05 para el análisis confirmatorio (un único test sobre la muestra combinada, sin corrección necesaria).

**Corrección por comparaciones múltiples:** los análisis por categoría/Workflow y por tramo de horizonte son **exploratorios**. Se aplica FDR de Benjamini–Hochberg con q = 0.05 al conjunto de tests estratificados, y Bonferroni (k categorías ≈ 5) como análisis de robustez. Solo el resultado confirmatorio combinado gobierna la conclusión de "mejora".

**Efecto mínimo detectable (MDE):** se potencia el estudio para detectar δ = +5 pp con potencia 80% al 5% bilateral. Como se muestra en §3, con tasas base bajas esto exige el benchmark completo. Si el presupuesto obliga a un subconjunto menor, el MDE se amplía explícitamente (δ = +8 pp para N ≈ 300) y los tamaños inferiores se interpretan como "evidencia insuficiente", no como "sin efecto".

---

## 2) Especificación exacta del prompting y mecánica de CoT

**Ciclo de agente común (idéntico en A y B).** Por paso: (1) recibir observación de browserGym = goal + URL + árbol de accesibilidad (axtree) + last_action + last_action_error; (2) construir el prompt según condición; (3) llamada LLM; (4) parsear la acción (JSON con `name` del FunctionCall de browserGym y `args`); (5) ejecutarla; repetir hasta éxito, tope de pasos o fallo. Historial de conversación idéntico en ambas condiciones, recortado a las últimas **H = 8** etapas (política fija idéntica) para igualar el coste de contexto.

**Condición A — Control (próxima acción, sin razonamiento).**
```
System: You are a helpful AI assistant operating a web browser to complete a user task.
You will receive a textual rendering of the current page (accessibility tree) and the task goal.
Choose ONE next action from the available action functions and reply with a single JSON object:
{"name": "<function_name>", "args": {...}}
Output ONLY the JSON action object; do not add any other text.
Available actions: {action_signatures}
```
```
User: Task: {goal}
URL: {url}
Last action: {last_action}
Last action error: {last_action_error}
Page (accessibility tree):
{obs}
Next action:
```

**Condición B — CoT por-paso (primaria).** Idéntica plantilla a A salvo el bloque de razonamiento en System:
```
System: ... [mismo texto que A] ...
Before choosing your action, reason step by step:
- Briefly summarize the current page state and what still remains to complete the task.
- Explain which element or navigation is needed next and why.
- Select the single next action consistent with that reasoning.
Then reply with a JSON object:
{"reasoning": "<your step-by-step reasoning>", "name": "<function_name>", "args": {...}}
The "reasoning" field is for internal deliberation and will be recorded; only "name" and "args" will be executed.
Available actions: {action_signatures}
```
El mensaje User es **idéntico** al de A. La diferencia entre A y B es únicamente la instrucción de razonar (diferencia mínima de prompt, control de confusión).

**Por qué CoT por-paso como mecánica primaria (justificación).** WorkArena++ penaliza errores compuestos a lo largo de horizontes largos; el benchmark documenta el fracaso de agentes avaros que eligen la acción sin deliberación. El prompting CoT por-paso (Wei et al., 2022) inserta la deliberación justo en el punto de decisión — la operacionalización más fiel y mínima de "mecanismo de prompting de cadena de pensamiento" — y mantiene la comparación limpia con el control: mismo presupuesto de pasos, misma observación, misma historia, mismo formato de salida (JSON), cambiando solo el razonamiento. El "plan-first/scratchpad persistente" es una mecánica distinta (planificación) que se evalúa aparte (Condición D), para no confundir CoT con planificación.

**Condición C — Control de verbosidad (secundario).** Igual que A pero pidiendo una frase corta sin razonamiento antes del JSON:
```
System: ... Before choosing your action, restate the current page state in one sentence (no reasoning or analysis), then reply with the JSON action: {"summary": "...", "name": "...", "args": {...}} ...
```
Separa el efecto "longitud/tokens extra" del efecto "razonamiento".

**Condición D — Plan-first (secundario).** En el paso 1 el modelo emite un plan de todo el episodio; luego actúa por-paso. Aísla el componente de planificación.

**Parseo y robustez de formato (crítico para igualdad entre condiciones).** Se usa salida estructurada / tool-calling del proveedor si está disponible (o JSON mode), igual en todas las condiciones, para que la mayor longitud de la salida CoT no genere más fallos de parseo. Política de reintento: máximo 2 reparaciones de JSON; si falla, acción = `noop` y se registra; tasa de malparseo se reporta por condición (diagnóstico, ver §5) y debe ser < 5% y balanceada, si no, se marca como riesgo de interpretación.

---

## 3) Muestreo de tareas y tamaño de muestra (con potencia)

**Marco y exclusión.** WorkArena++ expone un conjunto de tareas procedimentales sobre ServiceNow vía browserGym (conocimiento externo, a confirmar al enumerar; se usa la lista oficial de tareas del repo). Plan: **enumerar todas las tareas del benchmark**, asignar a cada una una semilla de instancia s fija, estratificar por categoría de Workflow, y aplicar criterios de exclusión pre-registrados (nulos): cualquier tarea que falle al cargar o produzca observación vacía se reintenta una vez y, si persiste, se descarta **en ambas condiciones** (para preservar el pareo), registrando la gota.

**Justificación de tamaño con simulación de potencia (Monte Carlo, 3000 datasets por celda, McNemar con corrección de continuidad; modelo de umbral latente con correlación de pareo ρ):**

| pA (control) | δ | ρ | N=200 | N=300 | N=400 | N=682 (todo) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.12 | 0.05 | 0.5 | 0.30 | 0.48 | 0.60 | **0.85** |
| 0.12 | 0.08 | 0.5 | 0.68 | 0.85 | 0.94 | 0.997 |
| 0.20 | 0.05 | 0.5 | 0.25 | 0.37 | 0.48 | 0.73 |
| 0.12 | 0.05 | 0.3 | 0.27 | 0.42 | 0.54 | 0.79 |

**Decisión de muestreo principal:** usar **el benchmark completo pareado (N ≈ 682 tareas)** en la comparación A vs B. Es la única configuración que alcanza ≥ 80% de potencia para el MDE de +5 pp con tasas base realistas (≈12%) y correlación moderada de pareo (ρ≈0.5). La baja tasa base hace que el test pareado necesite casi todo el conjunto (es una consecuencia estadística directa, no un capricho de presupuesto).

**Plan de contingencia pre-registrado:** si el presupuesto no admite 682 pares, se ejecuta **N = 300 pares** (mínimo aceptable), declarando explícitamente el MDE ampliado a +8 pp (potencia ≈0.85) y advirtiendo que diferencias de +5 pp quedarán por debajo de la potencia (IC anchos). No se usa parada opcional ni ampliación condicional de N que infle el error tipo I.

**Condiciones secundarias (C, D) y robustez:** submuestra de **N = 150 tareas** (estratificada) para C y D, y **M = 40 tareas × K = 5 repeticiones** para el estudio de robustez (§4, §5). Solo se interpretan las secundarias si la primaria es significativa.

---

## 4) Protocolo de ejecución

**Modelo y versión de API.** Primario: **un único LLM frontera accesible** (p. ej., GPT-4o o equivalente disponible; no lo fija la fuente → decisión). Se fija: nombre exacto del modelo, fecha/versión de la API y configuración de servidor, registrados como artefactos. Modelo secundario opcional (p. ej., Claude Sonnet) solo para generalidad. **Temperatura:** principal T = 0 (decodificación greedy) para minimizar varianza intra-condición; subestudio de robustez añade T = 0.7 (§5). Mismo max_tokens y mismo conjunto de herramientas en A y B.

**Versión de WorkArena++ / entorno (decisión, no dada por la fuente):** pin del commit exacto del repo WorkArena++ y de browserGym, hash lock de dependencias (requirements con hashes), Python versionado y reproducción por contenedor/Makefile. La versión de ServiceNow (instancia) se fija y se registra su health-check previo.

**Instancia y semillas.** Una semilla de instancia `s` por tarea (fija en el registro); se generan las instancias con el mecanismo oficial del benchmark. **Orden de condiciones:** para cada tarea, el orden A/B se aleatoriza (semilla fija del asignador) para controlar deriva temporal del modelo/API; cada instancia se ejecuta una vez por condición (K = 1 con T = 0) → par de resultados pareados.

**Repeticiones K:** principal K = 1 (T = 0). Subestudio de robustez: M = 40 tareas × K = 5 a T = 0 (para cuantificar no-determinismo residual y estabilidad de la tasa) y otra tanda × K = 5 a T = 0.7 (para robustez a temperatura).

**Límite de pasos por episodio.** Tope uniforme **máx_steps = 30** en ambas condiciones (si el benchmark define su propio default, se usa el del benchmark pero idéntico en A y B; se registra cuál). Los episodios que alcanzan el tope sin terminar se cuentan como fallo y se registran; si una tarea requiere una trayectoria de referencia > 30 pasos, se loguea y se marca en incertidumbres (no se excluye, para no sesgar el pareo).

**Presupuesto paramétrico (estimación, no dato de fuente).** Estimación por episodio: entrada ≈ 6k tokens/paso (axtree + goal + historial recortado H=8) × ≈ 12 pasos ≈ 72k tokens de entrada; salida ≈ 40 (A) vs ≈ 250 (B, razonamiento incluido) tokens por paso. Para los 682 pares: entrada ≈ 98M tokens, salida ≈ 1.6M (B) extra; con tarifas de referencia (≈ $2.5/M entrada, ≈ $10/M salida) ≈ **$250–350** para la primaria completa; C/D/robustez suman ≈ 25%. Se añade un límite duro de coste (contador de episodios/pasos) pre-registrado y un tope de ventana temporal (p. ej., resultados en una semana de cómputo) que solo se declara, nunca se usa para parar selectivamente.

---

## 5) Plan de análisis e informes de diagnóstico

**Paso 0 — Diagnósticos de calidad (antes de la inferencia):**
- Tasa de parseo de JSON por condición (< 5%, balanceada entre A y B); tasa de acciones `noop`; tasa de episodios que tocan el tope de pasos.
- Tasa de descarte de tareas (debe ser baja y simétrica; cualquier descarte se elimina del par completo).
- No-determinismo: éxito de A/B en repeticiones T=0 del subestudio de 40 tareas (si K=1 no se repite el episodio principal, se usa el subestudio para cuantificar).
- Adecuación del test: número de pares discordantes b+c (con pA≈0.12/ρ≈0.5 esperamos ≈13% discordancia ≈ 89 pares sobre 682); si b+c < 20, el test es poco informativo y se reporta explícitamente.

**Paso 1 — Confirmatorio (combinado):** McNemar exacto bilateral (y χ² con corrección de continuidad como robustez) sobre los pares; tablas 2×2 de concordancia; diferencia pareada puntual con IC bootstrap por clusters de tarea (percentil, 10k). Regla de decisión de §1.

**Paso 2 — Estratificado/exploratorio (con BH-FDR q=0.05 + Bonferroni como robustez):** diferencias por categoría de Workflow y por tramo de horizonte (≤6, 7–14, >14 pasos); tablas de tasa de éxito por condición y por estrato con IC (Clopper–Pearson).

**Paso 3 — Métricas secundarias (solo interpretadas si la primaria es significativa):**
- Eficiencia: pasos-hasta-completar entre condiciones (Wilcoxon pareado sobre pares donde ambas condiciones tienen éxito; ojo al techo del tope de 30).
- Coste: tokens de entrada/salida por episodio y por éxito; "éxito por dólar" (trade-off explícito, ya que CoT añade tokens).
- Robustez: estabilidad de la tasa de éxito entre K repeticiones (desviación estándar intra-tarea); comparación T=0 vs T=0.7.
- Condiciones C (verbosidad) y D (plan-first) sobre la submuestra de 150: si B > A pero C ≈ A, el efecto es razonamiento, no longitud; si D ≈ B, parte del beneficio es planificación.

**Informe final:** tabla de resultados por condición y estrato, IC, discordancia, coste, diagnósticos, configs con hash, prompts exactos y código como artefactos versionados.

---

## 6) Supuestos, riesgos y factibilidad/reproducibilidad

**Qué es dato de la fuente vs. supuesto:**
- *Fuente:* solo la pregunta, el contexto y track.md ("design-only"). Nada sobre WorkArena++, framework, modelo, métrica o presupuesto.
- *Conocimiento externo a verificar al implementar (tratado como supuesto operativo):* WorkArena++ = benchmark sobre ServiceNow con 682 tareas, observación vía axtree en browserGym, éxito binario por validadores deterministas, agentes que emiten una acción por paso, y tasas de éxito bajas (≈12–20%) con LLMs frontera. Si al enumerar el repo el número/estructura difiere, se re-calcula la potencia con el mismo procedimiento (script de potencia incluido como artefacto).
- *Decisiones de diseño (nuestras, explícitas):* modelo(s) y fecha de API, temperatura 0, prompts exactos de §2, δ_min = 5 pp, α = 0.05, FDR = 0.05, N ≈ 682 (o 300 en contingencia), K, tope 30 pasos, historial H = 8, presupuesto paramétrico.

**Riesgos y mitigaciones:**
1. **Deriva/no-determinismo de API** → pin de versión, T=0, subestudio K=5, registro de fecha.
2. **Parsing sesgado por condición** (salida CoT más larga) → salida estructurada/tool-calling en todas, diagnóstico y umbral < 5%.
3. **Potencia insuficiente con subconjunto** → se usan los 682 pares; si no, MDE ampliado declarado y regla de interpretación "evidencia insuficiente" (nunca "sin efecto").
4. **Confusión por verbosidad/coste** → Condición C y métricas de coste/tokens.
5. **Confusión prompter/versión de instancia ServiceNow** → misma instancia, health-check, registro de versión, descartes simétricos.
6. **Multi-comparaciones en estratos** → solo el test combinado es confirmatorio; FDR+Bonferroni en estratos.
7. **Coste/tiempo** → topes duros pre-registrados, presupuesto paramétrico, sin parada opcional.

**Factibilidad y reproducibilidad del entorno real.** El sandbox actual no puede ejecutarlo (red deshabilitada, sin GPU, sin paquetes de benchmark/agente). El experimento real corre en infraestructura con red: la API del LLM y un navegador headless (Playwright) sobre la instancia ServiceNow de WorkArena++; **no requiere GPU** (los pasos son llamadas a API + navegador). Para reproducibilidad: commit fijo de WorkArena++/browserGym, requirements lockeados, seeds fijas, prompts como archivos, script de potencia versionado, Makefile/runcbook, e informe con hashes de entorno. No se afirmará que el experimento se ejecutó si no se ejecuta.

---

## Resumen de decisiones fijas
Pareado por instancia; primaria A (próxima acción) vs B (CoT por-paso) con prompts de §2; éxito binario vía validadores del benchmark; confirmatorio = McNemar exacto + IC bootstrap + δ_min = 5 pp; N = 682 pares (contingencia 300); modelo/temperatura/prompts/versionado fijados y registrados; secundarias = pasos, tokens, robustez, verbosidad (C) y plan-first (D); todo pre-registrado y etiquetado fuente-vs-supuesto.

## 一、输入与资料检查结果（如实说明）

**已确认的事实（来自实际检查）：**
- `/workspace` 目录中**只有一个文件** `task.json`，无任何 WorkArena++、代理框架、提示词模板或数据集文件。
- `task.json` 内容为：研究问题（CoT 提示机制能否提升 LLM 代理在 WorkArena++ 中的任务解决能力）、背景说明、以及 `documents.track.md = "Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required."`（即**本任务为纯设计任务，不需要运行实验**，也不要求下载代码库）。
- 环境检查：Python 3.14.4、pip 25.1.1、git/curl/wget 可用；224 核 CPU、约 2TB 内存；`nvidia-smi` 存在但**无法与驱动通信（实际无可用 GPU）**；**网络禁用**；无预装项目依赖、无数据集。

**推论（标注为推断，非实测）：**
- 由于网络禁用且无 GPU/无模型 API 凭证，本环境**无法**真正运行 WorkArena++（其需要浏览器环境＋LLM API）。因此本任务的交付物只能是**一份完整、可执行的实验设计方案**，而非实际实验运行结果。
- "researcher_topics: neurips2024/97713/3:setup_1" 疑似指某个来源中的 setup 描述，但工作区内无对应文件，**无法据此确认任何设定**。

## 二、拟议实验设计框架（核心内容）

### 1. 研究问题 → 可检验假设
- **H0（零假设）**：在保持任务实例、基础模型、代理框架、评分器一致的前提下，采用 CoT 提示 vs 基线提示（无 CoT）所解决的任务比例**无显著差异**（平均成功率之差 = 0）。
- **H1（研究假设，备择）**：CoT 提示组在 WorkArena++ 选中任务子集上的**成功率显著高于**基线组（平均成功率之差 > 0，单侧；或 ≠ 0，双侧）。
- **探索性假设**（不预先承诺显著性）：CoT 的增益对**多步骤、规划密集型**任务（如复杂工作流）大于对简单单步任务；不同 CoT 变体（零样本／少样本／隐式 CoT）之间存在增益差异。

### 2. 自变量操作化（CoT 提示的有无及变体）
采用**单因子、多水平**受试内（paired / within-task）设计，核心因子为"提示条件"：
- **A（对照，基线）**：零样本直接提示——只给任务描述与可用动作，要求代理直接行动，**不含任何推理指引**。
- **B（处理1，零样本 CoT）**：在行动前显式要求"逐步推理"（如 "Let's think step by step" 或等价中文指令），推理文本作为附加输出后接行动。
- **C（处理2，少样本 CoT）**：在系统/用户提示中追加 2–3 个"任务描述→推理轨迹→正确行动"示范样例（exemplars）。
- **D（可选项，处理3，隐式/内部 CoT）**：推理在内部完成、不把推理文本暴露给环境（用于分离"文本可见性"与"推理机制"两个维度）。
- **E（可选项，对照 B'）**：少样本**无** CoT（与 C 相同数量的示范但示范中不含推理）——用于把"更多示范"与"CoT 推理"的效果区分开。

> 该因子结构天然支持两个对比：**主效应**（含 CoT vs 不含 CoT 的 B/C/D/B' 与 A 的组合对比）与**变体间对比**（B vs C vs D；C vs B'）。

### 3. 因变量操作化与指标定义
- **主指标（Primary）**：**任务成功率（Success Rate, SR）** = 得分为"通过"的任务实例占比。通过判定取 WorkArena++ 评分器分数 ≥ 预注册阈值（如连续奖励 ≥ 0.9 或等价二值化），阈值事先固定。
- **辅助指标（Secondary）**：
  - 平均连续性奖励分数（judge 输出，[0,1] 连续分）；
  - 任务完成率（到达终止状态的比例，不论对错）；
  - 步骤效率：成功任务的平均动作步数与**步数中位数**；
  - 标记/成本效率：每任务平均总 token 数与估算 API 成本；
  - 成功任务的平均墙钟时间；
  - 失败模式分类（规划错误、界面误解、过早终止等，由评分器日志人工抽样编码）。
- 所有指标在"任务实例 × 条件"配对层面计算差异（paired），以消除任务难度个体差异。

### 4. 实验组与对照组设置（配对 / 受试内）
- 每组（A–E）在**完全相同的任务实例集合**上运行（同一 seed、同一环境初始状态），只有提示文本不同。
- 条件顺序做随机化/轮转（counterbalancing），避免运行批次效应。

### 5. WorkArena++ 任务子集选取原则
- **分层抽样**覆盖 WorkArena++ 的几大基准族（new features / update pages / workday 等），每族按难度分层抽选；
- **只选用有金标/参考解的任务实例**（WorkArena++ 中无参考解的任务无法可靠判定成功，一律排除）；
- **剔除天花板/地板效应任务**：用基线条件预筛，"所有基线都成功"或"所有基线都失败"的任务按预注册规则处理（保留但单独报告，或按难度权重报告）；
- 目标规模：每族 50–100 个实例，总计约 200–300 个任务实例/条件（在成本预算内取较大值）。

### 6. 样本量与重复次数
- 每个（实例, 条件）重复 **R = 3–5 次**（不同随机种子）以覆盖 LLM 采样随机性与评分器随机性；每条件总运行数 = 实例数 × R。
- 功效设计：配对二值结局按 **McNemar 检验**功效计算，双侧 α=0.05、power=0.80，若预期配对不一致比例约 15–25% 且最小可检出效应 ~5–10 个百分点，则约需 150–250 个配对实例（即符合上面 200–300 的规模）；此功效估算**属于假设**（基线差异率未知），需在试点（pilot，约 20 实例/条件）后复核。

### 7. 数据分析与统计计划（预注册）
- **主分析**：配对二值成功率 → **McNemar 检验**（含近似与精确版），报告配对不一致表与匹配比值比（matched odds ratio）、Cohen's h 效应量；同时报告**双侧 95% bootstrap 置信区间**（按实例分层重采样）。
- **辅助分析**：连续奖励差 → 配对 t 检验与 Wilcoxon 符号秩检验；步数/token → 同为配对检验。
- **多重比较**：多个 CoT 变体对基线、以及变体间两两对比时，采用 **Holm/Bonferroni 校正**并在预注册中固定对比集合。
- **亚组分析（探索性）**：按基准族、任务难度分层报告平均处理效应，检查 H-探索性假设。
- **稳健性**：① 评分器温度/随机性——对每个输出重复评分取均值或多数投票；② 温度敏感性——在固定温度（如 0）主分析之外，加一组温度 > 0 的敏感性分析；③ 排除评分器偏差——评分器提示中**隐藏条件标签**（盲评），避免识别出 CoT 文本而影响打分。
- **失败分析**：抽样人工标注失败模式，量化"规划失败"类别的占比是否因 CoT 下降。

### 8. 拟议实施路径（讨论用，非最终）
1. 确认或修订上述假设与设计参数（模型、CoT 变体集合、阈值、子集规模）→ 2. 起草预注册方案（含判定规则、排除规则、多重比较方案）→ 3. 试点 20 实例核对功效与成本 → 4. 正式运行（需网络+LLM API+BrowserGym，见约束）→ 5. 分析、稳健性与失败归类 → 6. 产出完整设计文档与结果报告。

## 三、关键假设与不确定性（未在文件中确认，一律视为假设）

**必须标注为假设、待来源确认的设定：**
1. **基础模型**：假设为 GPT-4o（WorkArena++ 论文所用主模型）；备选/敏感性模型可加 GPT-4o-mini 或开源模型。**未经 task.json 确认**，且沙盒无 API。

4. **CoT 变体集合**：假设至少覆盖"零样本 CoT""少样本 CoT""隐式 CoT"三变体（见第二部分），具体纳入哪些变体待定。
5. **任务实例集合与规模**：假设 WorkArena++ 有 ~1,000+ 已发布任务可抽，选取 200–300；**具体实例清单取决于实际下载到的版本**。
6. **功效估算中的效应量与基线成功率**（基线 SR 约 12–22% 来自公开文献记忆，**非本环境实测**）。
7. **计算/时间与可重复性约束**：网络禁用、无可用 GPU、无 API 凭证——**真实运行必须在本沙盒之外**（或在开通网络/API 后进行）；运行成本（每次调用按 token 计费）需按试点实测估算；可重复性依赖固定 seed 与固定 WorkArena++ 版本/提交（需锁定版本号）。

# 实验设计方案文档（Design Document）

> **声明：本文件为纯设计文档。** 本任务为 design-only task（`task.json` 中 `track.md` 明确 "Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required."）。**未运行任何实验**，下文所有"将执行/拟运行"均为设计预设，不声称已产生结果。研究范围锚点为固定事实：`fact: neurips2024/97713/3:setup_1`——即评估 CoT 提示机制对 LLM 代理在 WorkArena++ 中任务解决能力的有效性。除该锚点外，一切未被源文件确认的设定一律标注为**假设（assumption）**。

---

## 1. 研究问题与假设

**研究问题（RQ）**：链式思考（CoT）提示机制能否提升 LLM 代理在 WorkArena++ 中的任务解决能力？

**假设（可检验、预注册）：**
- **H0**：在任务实例集、基础模型、代理框架、评分器与解码参数全部对齐的前提下，主条件对（C-B-A-E 组合对比见 §2.2）的平均任务成功率之差为 0（无显著差异）。
- **H1（主假设）**：至少一个 CoT 主条件（B 零样本 CoT 或 C 少样本 CoT）的任务成功率显著高于其对应无 CoT 对照（A 或 E）。预注册主对比集合：B vs A，C vs E；C vs A 为支持性对比。
- **H2（探索性子假设，预注册分组）**：CoT 增益随任务复杂度增加而增大（"多步/规划密集任务获益更大"）。**复杂度代理在分析前预先选定**（见 §4.3），不做事后分组。
- **H3（机制性探索）**：CoT 降低"规划失败"类失败的比例（见 §7 失败归类）。

---

## 2. 实验设计

### 2.1 设计类型
配对（受试内 / within-task）设计：同一任务实例集 × 全部提示条件，仅提示文本不同，其余完全一致。条件运行顺序随机轮转（counterbalance）。

### 2.2 自变量操作化与条件集（含修订 R1：精简核心条件 + 优先级）
因子：**提示条件**，一个五条件集合，其中前四个为核心（主分析），后两个为可选。

**核心条件（主分析，预算内优先）：**
| 条件 | 定义 | 定位 |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | 基线：零样本直接提示。仅给任务描述与可用动作，直接输出行动，无任何推理指引 | 对照组 |
| **B** | 零样本 CoT：每个决策步先输出推理文本，再输出行动（见 §2.3） | 处理1 |
| **C** | 少样本 CoT：追加 k=2–3 个"任务→推理→行动"示范，随后逐决策步 CoT | 处理2 |
| **E** | 少样本无 CoT 对照：示范**数量与 C 相同**（k 相同），但示范仅含行动、不含推理；逐决策步仅输出行动 | 控制"示范数量"混淆 |

**可选条件（敏感性/延伸分析，低优先级，按剩余预算执行）：**
- **D**：隐式 CoT（推理在内部完成、不向环境暴露推理文本）——用于分离"推理机制"与"文本可见性"两个维度。
- **M2**：第二基础模型（GPT-4o-mini 或开源模型，如 Qwen 2.5–72B，经本地/API 运行）——用于验证效应跨模型稳健性。**（注意：开源模型本地推理需 GPU 或 CPU-only 的量化方案，均为假设。）**

**预算内优先级顺序（预算不足时依次裁剪）：** A=B=C=E（必须完整）> 重复次数 R 保底 > D > M2。优先保证核心四条件的主分析效力，其次才做可选条件。

### 2.3 CoT 施用粒度（修订 R2）
- **主设定**：**逐决策步 CoT**——代理在每个决策步先产生一段推理（当前状态摘要 → 计划 → 目标选择理由），再输出结构化行动。
- **敏感性变体（可选条件，标注为 sensitivity）**：**"先规划后行动"**——仅在任务起始做一次全任务规划，其后逐决策步直接行动。此变体纳入敏感性分析，用于检验 CoT 增益是来自"全局规划"还是"逐步行推理"。
- **输出格式对齐（硬性约束）**：全部条件使用**同一结构化 JSON 输出信封**：
  ```
  {"reasoning": "<可选，A/E 为空或省略>", "action": "<action_name>", "args": {...}}
  ```
  即 A 与 E 也使用相同 JSON schema（`reasoning` 字段置空），仅内容不同。这保证"输出格式差异"不作为混淆变量。C 与 E 的示范数量、示范任务类型、长度分布一致。

### 2.4 因变量操作化与指标
- **主指标（Primary）**：**任务成功率 SR** = 判定为"通过"的任务实例占比。通过判据预注册（见 §5.1 二值化）。
- **辅助指标（Secondary）**：
  - 平均连续性评审奖励（judge 输出，[0,1]）；
  - 任务完成率（到达终止状态比例，不论对错）；
  - 步骤效率（成功任务的平均/中位动作步数）；
  - Token 与成本效率（每任务总 token、估算 API 成本）；
  - 成功任务平均墙钟时长；
  - 失败模式分布（见 §7）。
- 所有指标在"任务实例 × 条件"配对层面计算差异。

### 2.5 任务子集选取原则
- **候选池**：WorkArena++ 已发布任务族（new features / update pages / workday 等）。**【假设：具体族与版本以实际锁定的仓库为准，见 §8。】**
- **强制纳入规则**：仅选取**有官方金标/参考解**的任务实例（无参考解则无法可靠判定成功，一律排除）。
- **分层抽样**：按基准族分层，每族内按 §4.3 预注册的复杂度代理分层，随机抽取（固定随机种子）。
- **剔除/标记规则（预注册）**：若基线 A 在某实例上"全 N 个重复均成功"或"全失败"，则标记为天花板/地板实例；**不删除**，但在主报告与按难度分组报告中分别呈现，避免选择性剔除。
- **目标规模**：每族 50–100 实例，总计 **200–300 任务实例/条件**（受预算约束，最终值以试点功效复核为准，见 §6）。

---

## 3. 基础模型与代理框架（假设，非文件确认）
- **基础模型（主）**：**假设** 为 GPT-4o（WorkArena++ 论文主模型）；温度固定（主分析 temperature=0；敏感性分析 temperature=0.5）。
- **代理框架（主）**：**假设** 为 **BrowserGym**（WorkArena++ 官方环境接口）及基准随附代理脚手架；行动空间与观察表示采用该框架默认接口。
- 上述二者的版本与 commit 在正式运行前锁定（见 §8）。

---

## 4. 样本量与功效估算

### 4.1 配对结构与重复次数
- 每（实例, 条件）重复 **R=3 次**（3 个固定随机种子），预算允许则 R=5。
- 每条件运行数 = 实例数 × R；主对比 B vs A 与 C vs E 为配对。

### 4.2 功效估算（以试点复核为准，当前为假设计算）
方法：配对二值结局 **McNemar 检验**，α=0.05（双侧），power=0.80。
- **假设** 配对不一致比例 p10（基线失败/CoT 成功）≈ 15%，p01（基线成功/CoT 失败）≈ 5%（净增益 ~10pp）；据此约需 **200 个配对实例**。
- 若试点显示净增益仅 ~5pp，则需提高实例数或接受较低 power；**最终以试点实测 p10/p01 重新计算**。

### 4.3 复杂度代理（修订 R4，预注册，用于 H2 分层与功效/分组）
复杂度代理在**分析前唯一指定并写入预注册**，选其一为主、其余为稳健备用：
1. **参考轨迹最小步数**（官方金标参考解的动作步数，取多参考解中位数）；
2. 若基准元数据含**人工难度评级**则并列采用；
3. 规划密度（参考解中涉及状态改变的关键决策数）。

按代理值将任务集三等分（低/中/高复杂度）作为 H2 的预注册分层变量；**不做事后重分组**。H2 检验为条件 × 复杂度分层的交互项（见 §5.4）。

### 4.4 试点（pilot）设计
- 规模：约 **20 实例/条件**（每实例 R=3），仅核心四条件。
- 目标：① 校准功效参数 p10/p01；② 实测每任务 token 与成本（预算核算）；③ 检验环境/渲染与 verifier 判据与锁定版本的兼容性；④ 校验输出格式在全部条件下的解析一致性。
- 试点结果仅用于修订参数，不进入正式结果统计。

---

## 5. 数据分析与统计计划（修订 R3：判定细节预注册）

### 5.1 评分与二值化（预注册、固定）
- **评分器**：WorkArena++ 官方 LLM 评审器（verifier）。**【假设：verifier 为 GPT-4o，实际以锁定版本为准。】**
- **连续分**：verifier 输出 [0,1] 连续奖励。
- **二值化阈值（方向写死）**：**success ⟺ 评分 ≥ 0.9**（在锁定官方 verifier 后，若其自带判据与 0.9 不一致，则以官方判据为准并记录偏差；>0.9 与 ≥0.9 的区别在预注册中一次性定死为 ≥0.9，避免临场调整）。
- **judge 温度**：固定 **temperature=0.0**。
- **重复评分次数**：每个 (任务, 条件, 重复) 的轨迹评分 **Nr=3** 次；通过判定 = **3 次评分的均值 ≥ 0.9**（连续指标用均值；若预注册改为多数投票则用多数票）。
- **盲评**：评分提示**不含条件标签**，verifier 只看（任务条件描述、金标判据、代理轨迹），不被告知该轨迹来自哪一提示条件，杜绝条件识别偏差。
- **阈值稳健性**：预注册的敏感性报告 0.8/0.9/0.95 三档阈值下 SR 变化，作为稳健性而非主判据。

### 5.2 主分析
- 主对比：B vs A、C vs E（McNemar 检验，含精确二项版），报告配对不一致表、匹配比值比、Agresti 校正 CI、效应量 Cohen's h。
- C vs A 为支持性对比。
- 连续奖励：配对 t 检验 + Wilcoxon 符号秩；步数/token/时长：配对检验。

### 5.3 多重比较校正
- 预注册固定对比集合：{B vs A, C vs E, C vs A}。
- 采用 **Holm 校正**（α=0.05）。可选条件 D、M2 及敏感性变体的对比为探索性，结果标注为"未校正的探索性证据"。

### 5.4 H2（复杂度交互）分析
- 用 §4.3 的三分层，拟合混合效应逻辑回归：`success ~ condition + complexity + condition×complexity + (1|task_instance)`；
- 报告各复杂度层的平均处理效应与交互项显著性；该分析为**探索性**，结论以估计值与 CI 为主，不依赖单一 p 值。

### 5.5 稳健性计划
- 分层 bootstrap（按实例，1000 次）给出主对比的 bootstrap CI，与 McNemar 结论交叉验证；
- 温度敏感性：temperature=0.5 下复跑主对比（若预算允许）；
- 阈值敏感性（§5.1）；
- 排除 outlier 实例（如 token 超限被截断的轨迹）后重跑；
- 缺失/超时实例处理：预注册"轨迹未终止达 max-steps 即算失败"。

---

## 6. 可行性 / 前置条件（修订 R5 的外部执行要求）

**当前沙盒环境的硬约束（已实测确认）：**
- `/workspace` 仅含 `task.json`，无任何基准/框架文件；网络禁用；GPU 驱动不可用（`nvidia-smi` 无法与驱动通信）；无预装依赖与数据集。**因此本设计无法在当前沙盒内运行。**
- **前置条件（正式运行前必须满足，逐条核验）：**
  1. **网络开通 + LLM API 凭证**（GPT-4o 等）；
  2. **锁定版本**的 WorkArena++（含金标参考解的任务版本）与 BrowserGym（记录仓库 commit hash、依赖 lockfile 并归档）；
  3. 实例选取 seed、运行 seed、judge 运行 seed 全部固定并记录；
  4. 全部提示文本（A/B/C/E/D 完整模板）在预注册仓库中冻结为版本化文件；
  5. 解码参数（temperature、max_tokens、top_p=1、stop 条件）全条件一致；
  6. 计算资源：BrowserGym 需浏览器自动化能力（依赖网络/环境），LLM 调用按 token 计费——每任务成本在试点中实测并据此核定总预算。

**可复现性要求（写入交付物）：** 版本锁定、seed 清单、完整轨迹日志（含每步观察/推理/行动 JSON）、评分记录、分析脚本与随机种子、预注册文件与任何偏差记录（deviations log）一并归档。

**预算核算方式：** 总成本 ≈ 实例数 × 条件数 × R × Nr(评分) × 每任务平均 token 成本；其中每任务平均 token 成本由试点实测。

---

## 7. 失败归类（预注册分类方案）
- 取样：失败轨迹**全量或每条件随机 50 条**（取较大者）。
- 互斥、优先顺序判定的**类别**：
  1. **规划失败**：界面操作正确但动作序列逻辑错误/顺序不当；
  2. **界面感知失败**：读错/定位错页面元素；
  3. **动作执行失败**：action/args 格式或控件错误；
  4. **过早终止**：在完成前自行宣布完成；
  5. **循环/停滞**：重复动作或达 max-steps 超时；
  6. **最终状态核验不符**：自认为完成但 verifier 判定条件未满足；
  7. **其他**（附自由文本）。
- 编码：两位标注者独立编码，目标 Cohen's κ ≥ 0.8，分歧由第三人裁定；按条件报告类别占比，重点检验 H3（规划失败占比在 B/C 中是否低于 A/E）。

---

## 8. 完整假设清单（一切未经源文件确认者）
1. **基础模型**＝GPT-4o（主），GPT-4o-mini/开源模型（可选 M2）——假设，未在文件中确认；
2. **代理框架**＝BrowserGym 及基准随附脚手架——假设；
3. **task.json 中 track.md 的 "design-only；不需运行"**——已确认事实；
4. **WorkArena++ 族/版本/任务池**（new features / update pages / workday 等族与 ~1,000+ 任务量、金标参考解可用性）——假设，待锁定版本核验；
5. **评分器＝官方 verifier（GPT-4o），输出 [0,1]**——假设，阈值 ≥0.9、judge 温度 0、Nr=3 为预注册设定；
6. **功效参数**（基线 SR、p10/p01、净增益 ~10pp）——假设，以试点（20 实例/条件）实测复核为准；
7. **CoT 增益对复杂任务更大（H2）**——探索性假设；
8. **浏览器自动化与 LLM API 在沙盒外可用**——假设的前置条件；当前沙盒内**已实测**不可用（网络禁用、GPU 驱动失效）；
9. **温度=0 下的可复现性、格式一致性**——实现假设，需正式运行验证；
10. **成本/token 估算**——假设，待试点实测。

**硬性事实（与假设区分）**：本任务为纯设计任务；`/workspace` 仅有 `task.json`；网络禁用；GPU 实际不可用；Python 3.14.4 与 git/curl/wget 存在。研究范围锚点 `fact: neurips2024/97713/3:setup_1` 已确认，但**不携带任何源文件级的配置细节**。

## 9. 待议 / 需确认事项（供研究者下一步决策）
- CoT 示范 k 的确切取值（2 或 3）与示范任务来源；
- verifier 官方判据是否与 ≥0.9 一致；
- 每条件正式实例数（200 vs 300）在预算约束下的最终取值；
- 是否在正式运行中纳入"先规划后行动"敏感性变体。

payload.answer:
Proposed approach outline for testing whether CoT prompting improves LLM-agent task solving in WorkArena++.

**Target construct:** "CoT prompting" = adding an explicit prompt-internal instruction that makes the LLM generate intermediate reasoning (a written plan/state-assessment) immediately before choosing each web action, versus a baseline where the same agent is instructed to emit the next action directly without such reasoning. "Task-solving ability" = official per-task success rate (environment oracle) on WorkArena++ tasks.

**1. Benchmarking setup (WorkArena++)**
- Environment: official WorkArena++ suite, built on BrowserGym (ServiceNow-backed UI), driven by Playwright. Tasks are parameterized instances organized into task families (e.g., Knowledge, Service Catalog, Order Management, ...); each instance is a unique configuration (randomization seed).
- Task selection: a defined subset to bound cost — ideally a stratified sample (K instances per family, e.g., 40–100 instances total) rather than the full suite, with the chosen subset registered/locked before running. Full suite optional if budget allows.
- Evaluation: per-episode binary success from the environment's success checker; primary aggregate = mean success rate over the matched task-instance set (plus per-family rates). Secondary metrics: steps-to-completion, invalid-action rate, token/cost per episode, and exact-match accuracy for WorkArena++ answer/instruction families where applicable.
- Runner: standard BrowserGym agent loop — LLM receives the AOM accessibility tree + task instruction + prior actions, emits the next action in the agent action space (click/fill/type/submit/...); a reasoning field is used for CoT where the scaffold exposes one.

**2. Agent architecture and conditions**
- Single fixed model/checkpoint for all arms, identical observation formatting, identical action schema, identical prompt scaffold — the ONLY textual difference between arms is the reasoning instruction block.
- Baseline (no-CoT): instruction says to return the action JSON directly, no extra commentary ("do not explain your reasoning").
- CoT (treatment): same instruction plus a reasoning directive placed in the same prompt position, e.g. "Before choosing the action, think step by step: what is the goal, what has been done, what remains, which action is best next; write your reasoning in the reasoning field, then output the action."
- Optionally a third length-matched control arm: emit a fixed-length, task-irrelevant commentary (e.g., "describe the visible screen" without planning) so any effect of added tokens/attention is separated from genuine CoT. This is the strongest guard against the "CoT just adds text" confound but ~50% more cost.
- Counterbalancing: only the reasoning directive differs; shared prompt text, position, task order, and instance order identical across arms.

**3. IV/DV and controls**
- IV: CoT prompting (binary; optionally ordinal: none / free-form "think step by step" / structured plan-then-act / length-matched filler).
- DV: binary per-task success; aggregate success rate; secondary step count, cost, invalid-action rate.
- Controls: pinned model + snapshot date; temperature fixed (T=0 with seeds; if sampling, fixed T + seed and multiple repeats); max output tokens fixed; identical instance seeds generated from a master seed so each task instance runs under both arms (paired design); fixed episode cap (e.g., max steps) applied identically.

**4. Analysis plan**
- Primary: paired per-task comparison — McNemar's test on matched binary outcomes; 95% CI on the success-rate difference (Wilson/bootstrap); effect size (Δ in SR, or Cohen's h / odds ratio).
- Secondary: per-family breakdowns; mixed-effects logistic regression (success ~ condition + (1|task family) + (1|instance id)) to account for clustering; step/cost comparisons via paired tests (dependent t / Wilcoxon).
- Robustness: replicate the CoT instruction with 2 phrasings; option to repeat the head model with a second LLM; report per-cell repeat counts and confirm no instruction leakage between arms.
- Sample-size framing: with ~50–100 paired instances and per-cell repeats, design should detect a ≈10-point SR difference at α=0.05, two-sided, at reasonable power; provide explicit power estimate.

**5. Feasibility**
This workspace is design-only: /workspace contains only task.json (project brief: "Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required"); no WorkArena++ code, datasets, or packages are present; network is disabled. The actual run would occur elsewhere using the official WorkArena++/BrowserGym stack, a provisioned ServiceNow environment, and an LLM API with a pinned version. All benchmark-specific numbers in the final design must be grounded in the researcher's source-supported facts before the run.

**Open decisions needed before finalizing (see also assumptions/uncertainties):**
1. Task subset + sample size given the available runtime/cost budget (stratified subset vs. full suite).

payload.answer:
# Experiment Design — Does Chain-of-Thought (CoT) Prompting Improve Task-Solving Ability of LLM-Based Agents in WorkArena++?

**Status: DESIGN ONLY. No experiment has been run; no results are claimed.** This document is a decision-complete plan intended to be executed elsewhere. All benchmark-specific details are tagged **[ASSUMPTION]** where they come from domain knowledge and could not be verified in this workspace (which contains only the project brief `task.json`, no repositories, no datasets, no network, and no relevant installed packages).

---

## 1. Research question and hypotheses

- **RQ:** Does adding a chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting mechanism — an explicit prompt directive that makes the LLM produce intermediate reasoning before each web action — improve the task-solving ability of an LLM-based agent on WorkArena++?
- **Primary hypothesis (H1):** Mean task success rate under the CoT-prompted condition is higher than under the no-CoT baseline, on a matched set of WorkArena++ task instances.
- **Secondary hypotheses:** (H2) Any observed advantage persists when the CoT arm is compared against a length-matched "verbosity" control that adds the same quota of extra text without task-relevant reasoning — i.e., the effect is attributable to reasoning *content*, not merely to additional tokens or instruction salience. (H3, exploratory) The effect of CoT varies by task family and difficulty (e.g., larger gains on multi-step knowledge/order-management tasks than on single-step form-fill).
- **Operational definitions:** *CoT* = model-generated intermediate reasoning text, elicited by a prompt directive placed in a fixed position in the context before each action, distinct from the action itself. *Task-solving ability* = environment-oracle per-task binary success; aggregated as mean success rate over matched instances.

## 2. Benchmark setup — WorkArena++

- **Environment [ASSUMPTION]:** Official WorkArena++ suite built on **BrowserGym**, driving a ServiceNow-backed application UI via **Playwright**. WorkArena++ extends the WorkArena benchmark (ICLR 2024) with additional/harder task families; run through `browsergym`-style environments exposing tasks as (template, parameter set) pairs. Family taxonomy assumed ~20–30 families (e.g., Knowledge, Service Catalog, Order Management, Software, Sales, ...); exact count/taxonomy to be confirmed from the pinned repo at execution time and recorded verbatim.
- **Agent loop [ASSUMPTION]:** Standard BrowserGym agent scaffold. At each step the model receives (i) the task instruction, (ii) a serialized AOM accessibility tree of the current page, (iii) the action history (truncated window), and emits an action in the agent action space (`click`, `fill`, `select_option`, `type`/`press_enter`, `hover`, `scroll`, `submit`, `goto`, `close`, `go_back`, etc.). **A reasoning/`think` field is assumed available in the action schema (§3/§9); fallback defined below if not.**
- **Scoring [ASSUMPTION]:** Binary per-episode success from the environment's automated success checker (oracle) verifying ServiceNow state against the goal; for answer/instruction-following families, success is exact-match on the produced answer, judged by the official checker. No human evaluation in the primary loop.
- **Episodes/caps [ASSUMPTION]:** Max 20 environment steps per episode; 60 s per step; applied identically to all arms. Episodes exceeding the cap count as failures.
- **Environment provisioning [ASSUMPTION]:** Self-hosted ServiceNow via the official dockerized setup, pinned to a fixed version/commit; instance state reset to a clean baseline before every episode; repo commit SHA, instance version, and any observed UI drift (DOM hash + screenshot) logged per episode for reproducibility.

## 3. Conditions and agent architecture

Three arms (same scaffold, same observation format, same action schema, same model/checkpoint; **the only textual difference across arms is the reasoning-directive block in the system prompt, in a fixed position**):

| Arm | System-prompt directive (diff line) | Role |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Baseline (no-CoT)** | *"Choose the single best next action and output its JSON. Do not write any commentary or explanation."* If the scaffold has a reasoning field, it is suppressed/forbidden. | Reference |
| **B. CoT (free-form)** | *"Before choosing the action, think step by step: restate the goal, assess what has been done, identify what remains, and justify the best next action; write this reasoning in the reasoning field, then output the action JSON."* | Treatment |
| **C. Length-matched verbosity control** | *"Before outputting the action, write exactly N tokens of commentary that describes the visible page layout in plain words (no planning, no goal analysis), then output the action JSON."* N matched to arm B's realized median reasoning length in tokens. | Confound guard |

- **Pairing/counterbalancing:** Arms share all other prompt text verbatim, prompt position of the directive block, task ordering, and instance ordering. Arm order per instance is randomized (balanced) across instances; a fresh session/episode is used per arm per instance (episodes are independent, so no within-episode contamination).
- **Fallback (if scaffold exposes no reasoning field):** Arm B emits CoT as ordinary assistant text preceding a JSON action line; Arm C emits the length-matched filler text similarly; baseline emits only the JSON. Preserves the three-arm contrast.
- **Robustness phrasing:** A **structured plan-then-act** variant of Arm B (explicit "Plan: <decomposed goal> / State: <progress> / Next: <action>") is run as a second CoT phrasing on the head model only (§7.4).

## 4. Sample design and power

- **Design:** Paired within-subject design. A stratified sample of **~80 task instances** is drawn from WorkArena++: ~K instances per family (e.g., ~4–8 × 15–20 families to reach 80), stratified to cover representative families and difficulty (single-step vs. multi-step). Each instance is parameterized by an RNG seed derived from a **master seed** (e.g., `master_seed = 20261022`; instance seeds = `hash(family, instance_index, arm_order)`) so the identical task configuration is presented to every arm. **Full suite is noted only as a budget-permitting extension**, not part of the primary analysis.
- **Repeats [ASSUMPTION]:** Primary paired analysis uses 1 episode per (instance, arm) cell under temperature 0 (matched seeds). Up to 3 repeats per cell (head-model arms) are used for variance estimation and determinism checks; §7 states exactly how repeats enter.
- **Power calculation (design-time, α=0.05, two-sided, McNemar):** paired-binary sample size `n = [z_{α/2}·√ψ + z_{1-β}·√(ψ−δ²)]² / δ²`, where ψ = discordant proportion and δ = marginal success-rate difference. Using baseline SR ≈ 0.40, δ = 0.10, ψ = 0.15 (CoT flips ~12.5% of tasks, rarely hurts ~2.5%): **n ≈ 116 instances → 80% power**. At the cost-driven default n = 80, power ≈ 0.64 for δ = 0.10 (≈ 0.80 for δ = 0.13). **Decision: default 80 paired instances (~64% power at δ=0.10), extended toward n ≈ 116 as budget allows; power table and ψ/δ assumptions recorded before data collection.** The supplementary mixed-effects model is more efficient under clustering and mitigates the power cost.
- **Registration:** master seed, instance-subset list, family mapping, and analysis script are frozen (pre-registered) before any rollout.

## 5. Variables and controls

- **Independent variable:** CoT prompting — 3-level arm (baseline / free-form CoT / length-matched filler); ordinal extension (free-form vs. structured) used only in robustness.
- **Dependent variables:** primary = binary per-episode success; aggregate = mean success rate over matched instances. Secondary = steps-to-completion, invalid-action rate (steps rejected by env/parser), token and USD cost per episode, per-family success rate, exact-match accuracy on answer families.
- **Fixed controls (all arms):** pinned model + checkpoint snapshot date; temperature 0 (base policy) with matched seeds; max output tokens fixed; identical AOM formatting, context window/truncation, action schema, step cap, and prompt scaffolding; identical retry/timeout policy. **Sampling fallback:** if the API cannot guarantee T=0 determinism, use fixed T ≈ 0.2 with seeded sampling and **3 repeats per cell**, per-cell success aggregated as modal outcome for the primary paired comparison (first repeat per cell for McNemar; repeats drive variance in the mixed-effects model) — documented contingency, not the default.
- **Blinding:** The evaluator (oracle) is automated and arm-agnostic; instance set and seeds identical across arms, so no re-sampling can favor one arm.

## 6. Execution protocol

1. Freeze and record: WorkArena++/repo commit, ServiceNow instance version, model ID + snapshot, seeds, subset list, prompts (three arms + structured variant), step caps, analysis script.
2. Provision self-hosted ServiceNow; sanity-run 2 demo instances per arm to validate the scaffold and parser.
3. Roll out episodes in randomized order (averaging out time drift), logging per step: full prompt, reasoning/action text, AOM snapshot, env response, DOM hash, latency, token counts.
4. Reset environment state before each episode; log git SHA + instance version + DOM hash for drift detection.
5. Store raw logs immutably; run the frozen analysis script.

## 7. Analysis plan

1. **Primary paired comparison (H1):** On the 80 matched instances (1 episode per cell), ΔSR = SR_B − SR_A with a bootstrap 95% CI (block bootstrap by family); test with **McNemar's test** (exact or normal-approximation, two-sided, α=0.05). Effect sizes: Cohen's h for the SR difference and the discordant-pair odds ratio (n_{B-pass,A-fail} / n_{A-pass,B-fail}).
2. **Pre-registered robustness of primary result:** ΔSR also reported with per-arm SR over repeats (modal outcome) if the T>0 fallback is triggered; report n, power table, and observed discordance structure (ψ).
3. **Confound guard (H2):** Compare Arm B vs Arm C (and B vs C vs A jointly). Evidence that B's advantage over A remains when B is contrasted with the length-matched control supports the reasoning-specific explanation; a null B-vs-C difference would caution that CoT's benefit is not attributable to extra text alone. Report Δ and CI; interpret cautiously given modest power.
4. **Efficiency & clustering (H3):** Mixed-effects logistic regression — `success ~ arm + (1 | family) + (1 | instance)` — reporting the arm fixed-effect OR and 95% CI; per-family SR tables with exact CIs; steps-to-completion via paired Wilcoxon signed-rank (and paired t on log steps), restricted to successful episodes for "efficiency" interpretation; invalid-action rate and cost per arm as descriptive comparisons with paired tests.
5. **Robustness replications:** (a) structured plan-then-act CoT phrasing vs. free-form CoT (same model) — consistency of ΔSR; (b) optional second LLM on a reduced 20-instance subset for cross-model generalizability; (c) determinism sanity check (T=0 same cell twice → identical trajectory); (d) per-family consistency, flagged if gains concentrate in one family.
6. **Reporting:** per-task outcome matrix (80×3), arm-level SRs with CIs, McNemar table, model output, and full prompt/log provenance. Conclusions on H1 stated conditional on effect size and CI, not only on the point estimate.

## 8. Feasibility and compute budget

- **Cost model [ASSUMPTION]:** ~80 instances × 3 arms × (1–3 repeats) ≈ 240–720 episodes; ~5–20 steps/episode → ~2,400–7,200 LLM calls; ~5k–20k input tokens/step (AOM can be large) → ~30–90M input tokens total on the head model; estimated cost low hundreds–~2k USD depending on model; wall-clock tens of hours on one worker, parallelizable across multiple Playwright workers.
- **This workspace:** cannot run the experiment (design-only, no network, no packages, no browser/ServiceNow). Execution requires an external environment with the official WorkArena++/BrowserGym stack, a provisioned ServiceNow instance, and the pinned LLM API.

## 9. Assumptions and uncertainties (dedicated section)

**[ASSUMPTION] Benchmark:** official WorkArena++ on BrowserGym/ServiceNow; ~20–30 families; instance parameterization from a master seed; environment-oracle success scoring with exact-match for answer families (~29-family taxonomy in WorkArena, extended in WorkArena++) — exact counts/semantics confirmed from the pinned repo at run time.
**[ASSUMPTION] Scaffold:** AOM accessibility-tree observation; JSON action space incl. `click/fill/select/type/submit/...`; a reasoning/`think` field available (fallback in §3 if not).
**[ASSUMPTION] Model/sampling:** pinned API model/checkpoint; temperature-0 determinism achievable (contingency fallback in §5); token/cost budget as estimated.
**[ASSUMPTION] Environment:** self-hosted ServiceNow, pinned commit, clean reset per episode; drift logged via DOM hash + screenshots; step cap 20.
**[ASSUMPTION] Statistics:** two-sided α=0.05; McNemar normal approximation valid at n≈80+; discordance assumptions (ψ≈0.15, δ≈0.10) used only for planning power.
**[UNCERTAINTY]** Exact family list/count and per-family difficulty mix at execution time; whether the scaffold's reasoning field is exposed as assumed; whether T=0 is truly deterministic on the chosen API; realized token cost vs. estimate; extent of cross-task correlation reducing effective sample size (partially absorbed by the mixed-effects model); possible model-internal (non-prompted) reasoning in the baseline arm — an inherent limitation of "no-CoT" as an instruction-level construct, acknowledged and mitigated by the length-matched arm, not fully eliminable.

## 10. Limitations (candid)

- 80 paired instances give ≈64% power at δ=0.10; smaller effects may be missed, and the B-vs-C contrast is underpowered by design.
- In-prompt CoT cannot fully silence a model's latent reasoning in the baseline; results read as "explicitly-prompted CoT vs. not," not as evidence about the mechanism of deliberation.
- All benchmark-specific numbers are assumptions pending verification against the pinned WorkArena++ repository at execution time.

- Runtime: Python 3.14.4; **no ML/causal packages preinstalled** (pip list empty for numpy/scipy/sklearn/lingam/tigramite/dowhy/etc.); network disabled.
- Consequence: the experiment is **design-only / source-supported**. The design will describe the CAMUV algorithm and its evaluation as a specification derived from the published method (Sharma, Ravikumar & Zhang, "Causal Discovery using Additive Noise Models with Unobserved Variables"), NOT as a run claim, and will list exactly which libraries an eventual implementation would need (numpy, scipy, scikit-learn for GP/random-forest regression + a kernel-based independence test such as HSIC, optionally graphviz for plotting). No official CAMUV package was verified present, so the design should treat "implementation" as a faithful re-implementation from the paper description, not a wrapper of an existing library.

## 2. Proposed approach (high-level experiment design)

**Question being answered:** Can CAMUV-style additive-noise reasoning correctly recover direct causal relationships among observed variables when latent confounders exist, and how does it compare to baselines that do not handle latents (pairwise ANM) or that handle latents via constraint-based reasoning (FCI/PC)?

CAMUV core idea (as I understand it, to be stated as an assumption): each observed variable is generated as an additive noise model from its direct causes, which may be observed or latent: X_j = f_j(Pa_j) + N_j, N_j ⟂ Pa_j. A directed test "X_i explains X_j" checks whether j's regression residual is independent of X_i (GP/random-forest fit + HSIC). The identifiable signal is the **asymmetry**:
- exactly one direction independent → directed edge X_i → X_j (direct cause);
- both directions dependent → the pair is confounded by a latent common cause (no direct edge);
- both independent → ambiguous/independent pair.
CAMUV then resolves which variables are *directly* linked among observed variables and leaves the graph over latent nodes agnostic.

**Experiment components:**
- (a) Data generation: latent confounders + additive noise, with ground-truth graphs over both observed and latent nodes:
  - S1: 2 observed vars + 1 latent pure confounder (V-structure, no direct edge) — the core distinguishing case;
  - S2: triangle (X→Y→Z, X→Z);
  - S3: confounded chain (X→Y→Z with latent H→Y,Y?/Z) ;
  - S4: 3-chain with a hidden confounder at one head;
  - S5 (scaling): 4–6 observed + 1–2 latent, randomized DAGs.
  - Functions: nonlinear (sine, quadratic, power) + linear cases; noise: Gaussian and uniform; latent strength (coefficient magnitude) varied to make confounding easy vs hard. Sample sizes e.g. 500 / 2000 / 10000. Fixed seeds, N=20–50 repetitions.
- (b) CAMUV implementation spec: per-pair regression (GP via sklearn `GaussianProcessRegressor`, or random-forest fallback) → residual independence via HSIC (custom kernel-based statistic or `scipy`-based implementation) with permutation/bootstrap p-values; decision rule as above; output a directed graph over observed nodes.
- (c) Baselines/controls (and why): 
  - **Pairwise ANM** (same regression+HSIC but no latent handling, i.e., treat "both fail" as "no relation") — shows the exact bias CAMUV is designed to fix (confounded pairs get no edge);
  - **PC** (no latent assumption) — constraint-based control;
  - **FCI** (explicitly handles latent confounders, PAG output) — the principled competitor; comparison against FCI's "definite direct edge" edges highlights the strength/weakness of CAMUV's pairwise approach;
  - naive co-occurrence baseline (correlation threshold) as a sanity low bar.
- (d) Evaluation metrics: SHD on the observed-only subgraph (undirected+directed decomposed), orientation accuracy on correctly detected edges, edge precision/recall/F1, and a specific "confounder-detection accuracy" metric = fraction of confounded pairs correctly left unconnected (CAMUV) vs incorrectly connected (ANM) vs represented with a latent (FCI).
- (e) Analysis plan: per-scenario mean±std over seeds; ablation by function nonlinearity / noise variance / latent strength / sample size; paired significance tests (e.g., McNemar on edge indicators) or bootstrap CIs comparing CAMUV vs ANM vs FCI; a "failure mode" section mapping which scenarios break CAMUV (e.g., strong/linear confounding, both directions independent, non-faithfulness).

## 3. Consequential assumptions & uncertainties

Assumptions (to be made explicit in the final design):
- Data-generating process is ANM with independent additive noise and a **directed acyclic graph** over observed+latent nodes.
- **Faithfulness** and the genericity assumptions needed for ANM identifiability at least approximately hold in simulated data (they will by construction in most simulated setups).
- Observed variables' parent sets may include latent nodes; we only seek identifiability of *direct edges among observed variables* and treat latent structure as a nuisance.
- My reconstruction of CAMUV's exact decision rule / pseudocode (asymmetry-based) is based on my understanding of the published method; if the researcher can confirm the paper's exact theorem/pseudocode (e.g., about resolving the "both-independence" ambiguity and the confounder criterion), I will lock it in.

Uncertainties / open items:
- Exact CAMUV pseudocode & identifiability theorem details (whether "both-independent → ambiguous" or handled via a multi-variable confounder test involving a third observed variable). This is the highest-impact uncertainty.
- Whether an official CAMUV reference implementation exists that should be the "library" baseline vs. a from-scratch re-implementation.
- FCI's computational cost and hyperparameter sensitivity (CI test choice) in the scaled scenarios; budget may require limiting FCI to small graphs.
- Performance metric for PAG-vs-DAG comparison (FCI outputs PAGs, not DAGs) — needs a defined projection rule.

Scope is exactly this: data generation spec, CAMUV implementation spec, baselines, metrics, analysis plan, assumptions — no run claims. Awaiting your approval before I produce the full detailed design (stage=result).

payload.answer:
# Experiment Design Document — Causal Discovery with Unobserved Common Causes via CAMUV

**Design-only deliverable. No experiment was run; all "would be / expected" statements are planning content and are explicitly not claims of execution.**

## 0. Task frame (fixed requirements)
Answer the question: *"How can you discover causal relationships in data with unobserved common causes using the CAMUV algorithm?"* by specifying a controlled experiment that (a) generates ANM data under latent confounders, (b) applies a CAMUV-style algorithm, (c) compares it against suitable baselines, and (d) quantifies discovery quality under defined metrics and an analysis plan. Environment: /workspace contains only task.json; network disabled; no ML/causal packages importable (verified: numpy/scipy/sklearn/networkx all raise ModuleNotFoundError).

---

## 1. CAMUV decision rule — explicit labelled assumption (point 1, locked)

The published paper (Sharma, Ravikumar & Zhang, "Causal Discovery using Additive Noise Models with Unobserved Variables") could **not** be verified against the actual text in this environment (no source material, network off). The following is therefore stated as our **reconstruction**, a working assumption the whole experiment is defined against — it must be treated in all interpretation as "CAMUV-as-reconstructed", not as a confirmed theorem. Its impact on evaluation is noted in §6 (metrics) and §7 (failure modes).

**Model class assumed (CAMUV DGP).** Each observed variable is an additive noise model over its direct causes, which may be observed or latent: X_j = f_j(Pa_j) + N_j, with N_j independent of Pa_j. The underlying causal graph over O ∪ L (observed O, latent L) is a DAG; faithfulness and generic ANM-identifiability conditions are assumed to hold in the simulated data (they hold by construction for most of our generator settings).

**Pairwise test.** For each ordered pair (i, j): fit f̂ via nonparametric regression (Gaussian Process with RBF kernel for n ≤ 3000, random forest for larger n), form residual R_{j|i} = X_j − f̂_j(X_i), and test independence of X_i and R_{j|i} with a kernel-based HSIC test (permutation p-value, n_perm ≈ 300, or Gamma-approximation asymptotic p-value for speed). "X_i explains X_j" ⇔ p_{i→j} > α (independence accepted), with α family-wise controlled via Benjamini–Hochberg over all pairs.

**Decision rule (reconstruction).** For each unordered observed pair {i, j}:
1. **Exactly one direction independent** (p_{i→j} > α, p_{j→i} ≤ α, or vice-versa) → infer **directed edge** i→j (the independent direction).
2. **Both directions dependent** (p_{i→j} ≤ α AND p_{j→i} ≤ α) → infer **latent common cause** present, no direct observed edge.
3. **Both directions independent** → **ambiguous**: output no edge, record in an explicit "ambiguity" bucket.

**Why this rule answers the question.** In a pure ANM (no latents), identifiability relies on the asymmetry of the residual-independence test. Under latent confounders the key additional fact this rule exploits is that a *confounded* pair with no direct edge is expected to fail *both* directions (the latent leaks into both residuals), whereas a genuine direct edge is expected to pass in its own direction absent a simultaneous confounder on the same tail. The pair whose both directions fail is exactly the "unobserved common cause" signature this experiment detects.

**Impact of the labelling on evaluation.** Because rule 3 is our choice, the "ambiguity rate" is reported as a first-class metric (§6) and the both-fail⇒latent interpretation is validated *empirically* only against confounded ground-truth pairs (S1/S3/S5), not asserted. All CAMUV results are contextualized as "CAMUV (reconstruction)".

---

## 2. Data generation (point 3 — full detail)

**Generator.** Generic ANM engine: input ground-truth DAG over V = O ∪ L; each node j gets f_j (family + parameters, seed-drawn) and noise N_j. Sample X_j = f_j(Pa_j) + N_j in topological order.

**Function families.** linear (a·x), sine (a·sin(b·x+φ)), quadratic (a·x²+b·x with centering), and cubic (a·x³ + b·x). Per edge, family drawn uniformly from the non-linear ones (linear only in dedicated ablation). Edge coefficients a ∈ {0.5, 1.0, 1.5}.

**Noise.** Gaussian σ ∈ {0.1, 0.5, 1.0} (relative to signal scale), and Uniform(−u, u) with matching scale (in the uniform ablation).

**Latent strength** (scale factor on all latent→observed edge coefficients): weak 0.3 / moderate 1.0 / strong 2.0.

**Sample sizes** n ∈ {500, 2000, 10000}. **Repetitions**: 20–50 fixed seeds (e.g., seeds 0..49), identical seed stream across methods so all comparisons are paired.

**Scenarios (ground-truth graphs over observed + latent nodes).**
- **S1 — pure confounder (the core case):** 2 observed X, Y; 1 latent H with H→X, H→Y; no direct edge between X, Y.
- **S2 — triangle (no latents):** X→Y, Y→Z, X→Z (3 observed) — sanity/control that the method still works with no latents.
- **S3 — confounded chain:** X→Y→Z (3 observed) plus latent H→Y and H→Z (a hidden confounder in the chain head). Mixes direct edges (X→Y, Y→Z) with a confounded pair (Y,Z).
- **S4 — direct edge + confounder on the same pair:** H→X, H→Y, and X→Y. Expected hard case for the pairwise rule (see §7, failure mode 1).
- **S5 — scaling:** 4–6 observed + 1–2 latent; random DAG (Erdős–Rényi, bounded fan-in, ~1.5× expected edges) with a random latent confounder attached to 2–3 observed nodes. ~30 random graphs × seeds.

**Data splits:** each generated dataset is used by every method (no independent re-fitting of the generator), keeping method comparisons paired.

---

## 3. CAMUV implementation spec (point 2 — libraries & steps)

No CAMUV/causal library is available or verifiable (workspace empty, network off, no `lingam`/`tigramite`/`dowhy`, and even numpy/scipy/sklearn/networkx are not importable now — see §9). Therefore the design specifies a **faithful re-implementation** of the method in §1.

- **Dependencies (if this were executed):** numpy, scipy, scikit-learn (`GaussianProcessRegressor` with RBF kernel; `RandomForestRegressor` fallback for n > 3000 to avoid O(n³) GP cost), networkx (graph bookkeeping, SHD computation). HSIC: custom implementation (standard kernel-based estimator HSIC = trace(K·H·L·H)/m² on standardized variables with RBF kernels; p-value via 300 permutations or via the Gamma-moment approximation for the independence asymptotic).
- **Pipeline steps:** (1) standardize each observed variable; (2) for all ordered pairs, regression → residual → HSIC p-value; (3) BH multiple-testing correction across pairs; (4) apply §1 decision rule; (5) write out directed graph over observed nodes + the latent/ambiguous bookkeeping; (6) save per-pair p-values to disk for post-hoc α-sweep analysis (optional ROC-style trade-off).

---

## 4. Baselines / controls and why (point 3)

1. **Pairwise ANM (no latent handling)** — the *critical control*: identical regression+HSIC machinery, but interprets "both directions fail" as "no relationship" and "both pass" as "unrelated" (never "latent"). Isolates the exact contribution the CAMUV rule adds; expected to (wrongly) leave confounded S1 pairs unconnected.
2. **PC (constraint-based, assumes no latents)** — standard non-ANM baseline; known to mis-handle latent confounders (over-connect / mis-orient), giving a reference point for the state-of-the-art without latent machinery.
3. **FCI (constraint-based, explicitly handles latents)** — the *principled competitor* for unobserved common causes; the fairest head-to-head. Output is a PAG, so §5's projection rule is mandatory.
4. **Correlation-threshold (|Pearson| > τ)** — low-bar sanity baseline.
All baselines restricted to the same observed-variable subspace as CAMUV.

---

## 5. FCI PAG → comparable metric projection rule (point 2 — concrete)

FCI returns a PAG over observed nodes with marks →, o→, o–o, ↔. We define a deterministic projection so SHD/orientation/precision-recall are comparable to the DAG-like output of CAMUV/ANM:

- **Adjacency projection (level L1):** a pair is "edge-present" in the FCI output if the mark is any of o–o, o→, ↔, →. (All are some kind of adjacency; ↔ explicitly encodes a latent common cause.)
- **Direction projection (level L2):** only an unambiguously directed mark **→** counts as an oriented directed edge for direction metrics. **o→** counts as adjacency but is *not* oriented (its head mark is unresolved); **↔** counts as a **latent-common-cause annotation** (feeds the confounder-detection metric, not the directed-edge metric).
- **Orientation-accuracy restriction:** orientation accuracy is computed only over pairs that are edge-adjacent *and* whose ground truth has a directed edge; unresolved o→ marks are counted as "not oriented" (neither correct nor wrong, but tracked separately to be fair to FCI).
- **SHD:** computed on (a) adjacency sets (additions/deletions) via L1, plus (b) a separate orientation-error count via L2 (reversals and directed-vs-undirected mismatches). This two-level SHD decomposition is reported for *all* methods so the comparison is apples-to-apples: CAMUV/ANM also contribute L1(adjacency) and L2(orientation) components.
- The rule is fixed *before* running (registered in the design), so it can't be tuned post-hoc on results.

---

## 6. Evaluation metrics (point 3)

All computed on the **observed-variable subgraph only** (latent structure is ground truth for generation, but we evaluate discovery of direct edges among observed variables; latent nodes never appear in metrics, only latent-*detection*).
- **SHD (adjacency level + orientation level, per §5):** total edge additions + deletions + reversals vs. ground-truth observed subgraph; report the three components separately.
- **Orientation accuracy:** fraction of inferred directed edges (among observed pairs) whose head direction matches ground truth, restricted to pairs with a ground-truth direct edge.
- **Edge precision / recall / F1:** on direct-edge presence between observed pairs (ground-truth adjacency restricted to observed subgraph).
- **Confounder-detection accuracy:** for pairs whose ground truth is "latent common cause, no direct edge" (S1, S3 Y–Z, S5 confounded pairs): fraction correctly left unconnected (CAMUV/ANM) or annotated with ↔ (FCI). This is the metric most directly answering *"data with unobserved common causes"*.
- **Ambiguity rate (CAMUV only):** fraction of observed pairs landing in rule-3 "both independent" bucket — reported explicitly because it is a consequence of our labelled reconstruction (§1).
- Baseline-comparison sanity: for S2 (no latents) all methods should perform well; degradation on S2 would signal a generator/metric bug.

---

## 7. Analysis plan (point 3)

- **Per-scenario summary:** for each scenario × configuration (function family, noise σ/distribution, latent strength, n): mean ± std (and median ± IQR) over the 20–50 seeds for every metric in §6.
- **Ablations:** (i) non-linear vs linear functions (ANM identifiability expectation: linear-Gaussian is non-identifiable → ambiguous bucket grows; document); (ii) Gaussian vs uniform noise; (iii) latent strength weak/moderate/strong (expectation: weak confounding → near-ANM behavior, strong → both-fail signature dominates); (iv) sample size 500/2000/10000 (power of the independence test); (v) scale S5.
- **Significance / pairwise tests:** because seeds are identical across methods, all comparisons are paired: for binary edge indicators use **McNemar's test** (CAMUV vs each baseline per pair, with BH correction); for continuous SHD differences use bootstrap 95% CIs on the paired difference.
- **Failure-mode section** (expected findings to report honestly, not hidden):
  1. **S4 (direct edge X→Y + latent confounding on the same tail):** residual of Y-on-X is not independent (the latent leaks into the residual) → the pairwise rule may report "both fail" → false "latent-only" conclusion. Expect lower recall for CAMUV in S4; report as documented limitation.
  2. **Linear-Gaussian data:** both directions often independent → ambiguity bucket rises; accuracy falls. Report.
  3. **Weak direct effect vs strong confounder:** direction may flip toward "latent-only".
  4. **Both-independent ambiguity:** reported, never silently dropped (rule 3 is ours).
  5. **FCI cost/coverage:** at p > 6 FCI's conditioning-set growth may force early stop; restrict FCI to p ≤ 6 and cap conditioning set size (documented as an FCI-budget caveat).
- **Deliverables shape:** per-scenario metric table; ablation grids; pairwise significance table; explicit failure-mode write-up; α-sweep curve (optional, from saved p-values) trading edge recall vs precision.

---

## 8. Rationale summary (why this design answers the question)
- The both-fail⇒latent signature is the *definitional* phenomenon of "data with unobserved common causes" under the ANM lens, so making S1 the headline scenario directly tests the algorithm's stated purpose.
- Pairing CAMUV against (a) its own machinery minus latent handling (ANM) and (b) the established latent-handling method (FCI) isolates the CAMUV rule's unique contribution and locates CAMUV relative to constraint-based methods.
- The fixed PAG projection (§5) and two-level SHD make cross-method metrics meaningful instead of ad hoc.
- Explicit labelling of the §1 rule as a reconstruction keeps claims honest given the offline environment.

---

## 9. Feasibility (design-only, honest) (point 4)
- **No experiment was run**; everything below is a planning specification, not evidence of execution. The workspace contains no code, and the current runtime cannot import numpy/scipy/sklearn/networkx (verified) — any future execution would require these to be installed at image-build time (network is disabled at runtime).
- **Implementation needs if executed:** numpy, scipy, scikit-learn (GP/RF regression), networkx; custom HSIC module only (~50 lines, kernel matrices + permutation/Gamma p-value). No CAMUV-specific package exists or is verifiable, so a from-scratch re-implementation per §3 is the design.
- **Approximate compute budget (planning estimate, not a run claim):** pairwise tests cost O(p²) fits per dataset. GP fits are O(n³) → cap GP at n ≤ 3000, switch to random forest for n = 10 000. HSIC with permutations adds O(n²·n_perm). Estimated a few minutes per dataset; the full grid (S1–S5 × function/noise/latent-strength/n ≈ 15 configs × 20–50 seeds) ≈ several hours to ~1–2 CPU-days on the available 224 cores, *dominated by FCI* (its independence tests explode with conditioning-set size) — the budget therefore caps FCI at p ≤ 6 and caps conditioning sets (documented caveat in §7.5).
- **Feasibility of the design itself:** everything required (generator, metrics, projection rule, analysis script skeleton) is fully specifiable today from first principles, which is exactly what this document does.

---

## 10. Assumptions vs fixed requirements, and uncertainties

**Fixed requirements (from task):** answer the question; design-only; source-supported claims only; no run claim (respected throughout).

**Assumptions (mine, explicit):**
1. DGP is ANM with independent additive noise over a DAG on O∪L; faithfulness + generic ANM identifiability hold in simulation.
2. §1's CAMUV decision rule is a labelled reconstruction (verifiable-unverifiable offline) — the single most consequential assumption.
3. Goal is directed-edge discovery among observed variables only; latent structure is a nuisance (except for the confounder-detection metric).
4. FCI projection rule (§5) and two-level SHD are our fixed conventions.
5. All method comparisons are paired on shared seeds.

**Uncertainties:**
- Exact CAMUV paper theorem/pseudocode unverifiable in this environment (highest impact; mitigated by labelling + explicit ambiguity/latent metrics that would surface any mismatch).
- Whether an official CAMUV reference implementation exists that a future run should use instead of §3's re-implementation.
- FCI's practical cost/power at p > 6 (mitigated by capping its scope).
- Interpretation dependence of SHD when comparing PAG-projected vs DAG outputs (mitigated by the pre-registered projection and two-level decomposition).

## 1. Input / repository inspection

Workspace findings (verified): `/workspace` contains exactly one file, `task.json`. The `documents.track.md` entry referenced there is NOT present on disk. There are no datasets, no code, no packages (`pip`/`pip3` unavailable; bare system Python 3.14; network disabled). Conclusion: **the task is fully self-contained as a written experimental design**; nothing in the workspace needs to be incorporated, and no execution/compute is required.

Source-supported separation (I could not re-fetch the CAM-UV paper with the network off, so "source-supported" below = from my prior knowledge of the published work and standard causal-discovery literature, to be re-validated against the paper before any execution):

- CAM-UV extends the Causal Additive Model (CAM, Bühlmann et al. 2014) to settings with unobserved common causes (latent variables that directly cause two or more observed variables). It takes **observed variables only** as input and returns (a) an estimated causal order/direction among observed variables and (b) detected unobserved common causes. [source-supported, high confidence]
- Core identification signal: under additive noise, if X → Y then the residual of Y's regression on X is **independent** of X; the reverse direction and true common-cause confounding produce **dependence**. This residual-independence asymmetry is the workhorse. [source-supported, high confidence]
- Identifiability rests on additive-noise structure, smooth (typically nonlinear) functions, non-Gaussianity of the disturbance terms, plus a faithfulness-type no-cancellation condition. [source-supported, high confidence in general, exact conditions = assumption]
- Exact search procedure, nonparametric mutual-information estimator, kernel/binning choices, and hyperparameters are implementation details I will treat as **working assumptions** (re-validated against the authors' reference implementation if ever executed).

## 2. Proposed approach

Goal of the experiment: demonstrate, on ground-truth generative models that contain unobserved common causes, that CAM-UV (run on observed variables only) recovers the correct causal order and correctly flags latent confounders, and quantify how this degrades with confounder strength and noise Gaussianity.

2a. Data-generating process (known ground truth). Draw a DAG over observed variables X_1..X_p and unobserved variables U_1..U_k, sample a fixed topological order, then generate:
`X_j = Σ_{i∈Pa_j} f_ij(X_i) + Σ_{u∈Conf_j} g_uj(U_u) + ε_j`, ε_j ~ non-Gaussian (e.g., Laplace) by default; `f,g` smooth nonlinear (e.g., polynomial deg 2–3, sigmoid, or spline terms), confounders U ~ some fixed distribution.
Four core ground-truth scenarios:
- S1 (single confounder): U → X1, U → X2, no observed edge. True answer: no X1–X2 directed edge; one latent common cause.
- S2 (multiple confounders): U1 → {X1,X2}, U2 → {X3,X4}.
- S3 (edge + confounder): U → X1, U → X2, AND X1 → X2. Tests whether CAM-UV still orients the direct edge while detecting U.
- S4 (structured): chain/confounded diamond, e.g., X1 → X2 → X3 plus U → X1, U → X3, or {X1,X2} → X3 with U1 → {X1,X2}. Tests recovery of partial order amid multiple latents.

2b. Applying CAM-UV. Feed only the observed data matrix (columns = observed variables, n rows) to the CAM-UV procedure. The algorithm uses the residual-independence signal: for candidate cause X and candidate effect Y it regresses Y on X and measures (nonparametrically) dependence between X and the residual; independence ⇒ direction X→Y permitted; dependence in both directions ⇒ flag a latent common cause rather than a directed edge. Estimated output: causal order over observed variables + detected unobserved common causes. (Exact subroutine = working assumption; the conceptual signal is source-supported.)

2c. Concrete knobs (a factorial design with the middle cell as the "default"):
- p observed variables: {4, 6, 10}
- k unobserved common causes: {1, 2, 3} matched to scenarios
- model family: nonlinear additive (default), nonlinear additive with Gaussian noise (robustness), near-linear non-Gaussian (to test agreement with LiNGAM)
- sample size n: {500, 1000, 2000, 5000}
- confounder strength: signal-to-noise ratio SNR_conf = Var(confounder contribution)/Var(noise) swept over {0.2, 1, 5} (low/med/high)
- seeds/runs: 50 replicates per cell, fixed seed registry for reproducibility

## 3. Controls and baselines

- **Standard CAM (no hidden-variable handling)** — the direct ablation: shows the bias/errors CAM-UV is designed to fix when latents are present (e.g., spurious direction decisions on confounded pairs).
- **LiNGAM / DirectLiNGAM** — additive-noise direction-finding under the linear-non-Gaussian model; meaningful control because it shares the residual-independence principle but assumes linearity, isolating where nonlinearity matters and cross-checking S3 and near-linear cells.
- **Naive correlation / lower-residual-variance baseline** — "direction" decided by sign/magnitude of correlation or lower regression residual variance; demonstrates why residual *independence* (not dependence strength or correlation) is the correct signal, and is the standard sanity baseline.
- Optional (state as optional to avoid over-scoping): **FCI** as a constraints-based latent-variable-aware family for a complementary conditional-independence view.

## 4. Analysis plan and metrics

- Primary metric A — **direction-recovery accuracy**: fraction of (i) directed observed edges whose orientation matches ground truth, and (ii) confounded pairs correctly labeled "no directed edge, latent present" (for S1/S2). This directly answers "how CAM-UV discovers causal relationships under unobserved common causes."
- Primary metric B — **causal-order accuracy**: fraction of correctly recovered topological ordering of observed variables (or Kendall-tau over recovered vs. true order) on S4-type graphs.
- Secondary: **latent-confounder detection** sensitivity/specificity (does CAM-UV flag the true U's without hallucinating); **edge precision/recall** (recovered vs. true directed edges and confounding relations).
- Robustness sweeps: performance vs. n (consistency scaling), vs. SNR_conf, and vs. noise distribution (non-Gaussian vs. Gaussian). Primary = direction accuracy in default cells and the SNR_conf sweep; secondary = precision/recall and the Gaussian-noise degradation.
- Aggregation/stats: mean ± 95% CI over 50 seeds per cell; report curves over the swept axis; paired comparison (same seeds) of CAM-UV vs. each baseline. Simple and reproducible; no exotic inference needed.

## 5. Assumptions and uncertainties

Assumptions I will carry (design assumptions, marked in final design): the residual-independence signal is the operative CAM-UV mechanism; the nonparametric dependence estimator details; the exact CAM-UV search/heuristic for grouping latent causes; the DGP families, SNR definition, and scenario set are my design choices; a no-execution deliverable is sufficient.

Identifiability/technical conditions CAM-UV relies on (I will state as conditions the design must satisfy, marking confirmed-fact vs. design-assumption): additive noise structure (source-supported); smooth nonlinear functions (source-supported); non-Gaussianity of observed-variable disturbance (source-supported core, but I will treat the minimal condition as a paper-dependent assumption since I could not re-fetch it); faithfulness/no-cancellation (assumption — I will design f,g generically and check residual independence empirically on noise-free ground truth); structural adequacy of the model (unobserved causes enter additively and are common causes of ≥2 observed vars) (assumption).

Key uncertainties: (1) CAM-UV paper specifics (exact identifiability theorem, estimator, hyperparameters) could not be re-verified offline — flagged for re-validation before execution; (2) this is a design-only deliverable — the design contains a feasibility/run-plan appendix describing what an execution would need (numpy/scipy/sklearn + authors' CAM-UV reference implementation; runtimes modest for p ≤ 10, n ≤ 5000) but we will NOT claim an experiment was run.

Open decisions for your review: (a) include FCI as an optional comparator or drop it; (b) p and n grid — keep the full factorial, or slim to focused cells? (c) should the Gaussian-noise cell be primary or clearly secondary?
